articles.title: I wore the Google Fitbit Edge for a week, and even though its GPS is a little ropey, its wellness and fitness tracking smarts won me over
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Google Fitbit Edge is a simple band-based tracker that harkens back to Fitbits of yore — notably the Charge and Luxe series. While I dislike the Google Health app, which has difficulty surfacing historic numbers on its free tier, and is overly reliant on its chatbot for its premium tier, the band is comfortable and unobtrusive. Its tactile button offers just the right amount of interaction to be useful, and not enough to be distracting. GPS and resulting metrics are a little wobbly, but for most people looking for an activity tracker for sports, the gym, and the occasional jog or bike ride, the Edge will do the trick.
Reasons to buy
- + Affordable
- + Clean, simple UI
- + 7-day battery life
- + Accurate fitness, health and automatic activity tracking
Reasons to avoid
- - GPS and pace aren’t 1-1 accurate compared with top trackers
- - Messy Google Health app orientated around premium chatbot service
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Google Fitbit Edge: Two-minute review
The Google Fitbit Edge occupies a middle tier in Google’s new wearables lineup. On the lowest tier you’ve got the Google Fitbit Air, Google's cheapest tracker, and a screenless Whoop competitor, which collects information and displays it all in the Google Health app, with no interaction on-wrist.
At the other end of the spectrum you have the all-singing, all-dancing Google Pixel Watch 5, with its bright domed interactive AMOLED display and full Wear OS functionality. It’s the most interactive a Google wearable can get without you duct-taping one of the new Googlebooks onto your wrist.
In the middle, but leaning more towards the Fitbit Air end of the spectrum, is the Google Fitbit Edge. It’s got a touchscreen like the Pixel Watch 5 (though it's not as bright), GPS (missing on the Air), and a tactile button, enabling interactions such as media control and simple notification viewing, but not nearly as much as the Google Pixel Watch series. You can also swap straps to make it look more jewelry-like or watch-like.
On the other hand, it automatically detects workouts like the Fitbit Air, lasts a week between charges, doesn’t offer watch features like NFC payments or call management, and is very lightweight.
If you've used a Fitbit Charge or a Fitbit Luxe in the past, you’ll be familiar with the Google Fitbit Edge’s shtick. The screen enables you to pick and choose your workout starting point, manually pause or stop it, set timers, start an ECG scan, and offers other key functionalities. It inherently makes it more useful, while not being engaging enough to tempt you to tinker with it, or make it feel like a second phone. Meanwhile, it hums away in the background offering Health Guardian features like Blood Pressure Trends, Irregular Rhythm Notification, and Insulin Resistance estimations.
The Edge has a slightly different sensor array to the Air, which is capable of delivering ECG scans and detecting ambient light, so it can brighten or dim the screen as required. The Edge’s heart-rate sensor is very accurate, consistently recording readings within 5bpm of the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro (which sports Garmin’s Elevate V5 sensor, which we’ve thoroughly tested for accuracy across a multitude of different Garmins) during workouts in my testing. Sleep scores were a little more varied, sometimes matching up to the Garmin very closely, and other times being off by 10 points or so.
While sleep stats diverged a little, the Fitbit Edge’s biggest accuracy letdown during my testing was GPS and resulting information, such as pace. I documented my first test run, in which the Edge overestimated the pace and distance I ran compared to the (tested and accurate) Garmin Fenix 9 Pro, and this happened consistently. On every run, the Fitbit assumed I was running faster and further than the Garmin, usually by around 0.5km.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
However, for every other performance-based metric, the Edge was great, with automatic activity tracking in particular being very accurate. I was initially confused, as I was expecting an activity to show up on the screen, and it didn’t do so. However, once I checked the Google Health app, the activity was there in full.
The Google Health app is my other big sticking point — I covered it in my Fitbit Air review, but I dislike the AI-forward nature of it. It’s clearly built to be used alongside the premium Google Health Coach chatbot, with precious little functionality, and buried metrics, for free users.
I like the Edge. It’s well-priced, it performs well, it's unobtrusive and it's comfortable. Those looking for an old-school Fitbit will feel right at home — until they get to the app.
Google Fitbit Edge: Specifications
| Component | Google Fitbit Edge | 
| Price | $179.99 / £159.99 / AU$269 | 
| Dimension | 11.58 x 39.22 x 25.56mm | 
| Weight | 17.7g without band | 
| Case/bezel | 100% recycled aluminium | 
| Display | 1.3-in always-on AMOLED | 
| Processor | Ambiq AP5 MCU | 
| GPS | GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou, QZSS | 
| Battery life | Up to 7 days | 
| Connections | Bluetooth 5.4 | 
| Water resistant | 5ATM | 
Google Fitbit Edge: Price and availability
- $179.99 / £159.99 / AU$269
- Priced higher than the Google Fitbit Air, around the same as the old Charges
- It goes up against the Garmin Cirqa, Forerunner 70, and Apple Watch SE 3
The Google Fitbit Air costs $179.99 / £159.99 / AU$269, which isn’t a bad price for what you're getting. That's similar to what the GPS-equipped Fitbit Charge series used to cost, and considering we’re in a components crisis at the moment, I’m pleased that Google has kept the price fairly low.
However, competition is fierce at this price point, with the Edge going up against the Garmin Cirqa (my pick for this year’s best fitness tracker), the Apple Watch SE 3, the Samsung Galaxy Watch9 and the Garmin Forerunner 70 running watch. All of these devices, I would say, are better performers in some respects than the Fitbit, but not all of them are as sleek or unobtrusive.
Runners should opt for the Forerunner 70, while Apple users will get more out of the SE 3. For those looking for an all-round, simple-to-use fitness tracker, the Google Fitbit Edge might be ideal if you want a screen for media playback control, timers, manual workout settings or simply checking your step count.
Google Fitbit Edge: Scorecard
| Category | Comment | Score | 
| Value | Well priced in the same bracket as its predecessors. | 4/5 | 
| Design | Thoughtful and sleek, with great band options. | 4.5/5 | 
| Features | A bit limited in both hardware and software, but GPS and ECG are good to see. | 3/5 | 
| Performance | Some accuracy issues when it comes to sleep and GPS, but not enough to stop me recommending it to exercisers who are more concerned with general trends than in-depth metrics. | 3.5/5 | 
Google Fitbit Edge: Should I buy?
Buy it if…
You want a ‘set and forget’ tracker
Automatic activity detection is excellent.
Don’t buy it if…
You’re a dedicated runner
The GPS inaccuracy throws off pacing a bit, which means a dedicated running watch is a better choice.
You don’t like the app
The Google Health app is built around Google's premium chatbot service, and limited at the free tier.
Google Fitbit Edge: Also consider
Garmin Cirqa
The best screenless fitness tracker, at a similar price to the Edge.
Read our full Garmin Cirqa review
Google Fitbit Edge: How I tested
I wore the Fitbit Edge for a week on my right wrist, with the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro on my left. Using the Garmin as a benchmark, I compared sleep scores, workout metrics, heart-rate readings, step counts and more. I also drained the battery on the Fitbit Edge to check that performance was as claimed.
First reviewed: November 2026
Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.
He is the author of the upcoming book The Health Data Heist, set to be published by Bloomsbury in 2027. When he’s not training or writing about health and fitness, he can be found reading doorstop-thick fantasy books with lots of fictional maps in them.

articles.title: SpaceX plans 35-turbine, 748MW power plant for $24B Texas AI center
articles.text:
SpaceX plans massive $24 billion gas-powered Texas data center — application for 35 natural gas turbines and a capacity of 748 megawatts comes despite rising opposition in the state
SpaceX to build a huge AI data center and power plant in Texas
- SpaceX wants 748 megawatts of dedicated power for its Texas computing complex
- 35 gas turbines put SpaceX's Texas power application under environmental scrutiny
- Texas governor-elect promised moratorium could complicate future data center approvals in the state
SpaceX is seeking regulatory approval to build a natural-gas power facility for its planned $24 billion artificial-intelligence computing complex in Texas.
The application covers 35 natural gas turbines with a combined electricity generation capacity of 748 megawatts (MW).
The project will be located in Starbase, where SpaceX operates its rocket launch facilities, and includes plans for the company to develop and operate both facilities.
SpaceX plans dedicated power generation for its Texas computing facility
The proposed development would allow SpaceX to generate electricity independently rather than rely entirely on connections to Texas's main power grid.
This could help the company avoid delays associated with securing sufficient grid capacity for its computing operations.
The Starbase City Commission is scheduled to consider a development agreement and proposed property tax incentives on December 9 2026.
The company is also pursuing natural gas infrastructure in Texas and Florida to transport fuel for its Starship rocket program.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
According to Bloomberg, SpaceX is exploring another gas-fired power plant near Houston to supply electricity to Terafab, an AI semiconductor complex it plans to develop with Tesla.
The 748 MW application adds another major natural gas generation project to SpaceX's expanding infrastructure plans.
However, the company will still need to satisfy applicable environmental and development requirements before proceeding with construction.
Hinojosa's election victory raises uncertainty over future data center approvals
SpaceX's application comes shortly after Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated three-term Republican Governor Greg Abbott in the recent US midterm election.
Her campaign included proposals to restrict new data center development due to concerns about their effects on household utility costs.
Hinojosa argued large computing facilities were increasing pressure on electricity and water supplies, particularly in rural communities.
"When I become governor, I will prohibit all approvals for data center construction until a law is passed to protect Texans from data centers," she said.
Hinojosa also pledged to "eliminate tax incentives for data center construction and require disclosure of electricity and water consumption."
There are reports that SpaceX is seeking tax incentives and other financial concessions from local authorities, although Hinojosa's proposed restrictions could complicate those efforts once she assumes office.
Hinojosa is expected to assume office in January 2027, potentially introducing a different regulatory approach to technology infrastructure projects.
Opposition to large computing developments is also emerging in other parts of the United States.
According to regulatory intelligence firm RegLayer, at least 47 major data center construction projects encountered permitting delays or organized opposition from residents during 2026.
The disputes involve concerns about electricity costs, water consumption and the local consequences of accommodating facilities with substantial infrastructure requirements.
SpaceX's proposed natural gas installation could address some electricity supply constraints, although its emissions and environmental permitting requirements may attract additional scrutiny.

articles.title: IA : non, le bain de sang dans l'emploi n'aura pas lieu, selon Yann Le Cun
articles.text:
On craint beaucoup que l'intelligence artificielle ne mette tout le monde rapidement au chômage. Une crainte totalement infondée pour Yann Le Cun.
C'est la crainte majeure - hormis l'apocalypse d'une IA superintelligente qui nous voudrait du mal. La technologie de l'intelligence artificielle pourrait détruire un nombre immense d'emploi, jusqu'à, pour de nombreux économistes, en détruire encore plus que la révolution industrielle. Pourtant loin des paroles cataclysmique d'un Dario Amodei, Yann Le Cun ne croit pas du tout à l'effondrement du marché du travail.
« Seule une faible proportion des tâches est aujourd’hui automatisable »
S'il existe une figure de l'intelligence artificielle qui a tendance à modérer l'enthousiasme ou la peur créés par l'intelligence artificielle générative, c'est bien le chercheur français Yann Le Cun. Et il vient de le faire à nouveau dans une interview donnée au journal Le Point.
Dans celle-ci, il rejette toutes les prédictions apocalyptiques sur le marché du travail. Il explique qu'à son sens, nous sommes non seulement encore très loin des IA plus intelligentes que les êtres humains, mais aussi que la technologie ne va pas détruire les emplois. Pour lui, on devrait plutôt voir naître des métiers inédits. Par ailleurs, de manière plus global, « seule une faible proportion des tâches est aujourd’hui automatisable. »
Yann Le Cun rappelle le précédent des promesses sur les voitures autonomes
Et parmi les éléments qu'il avance, il rappelle que l'intelligence artificielle aujourd'hui a permis un petit coup de boost de la productivité, et non pas un bouleversement général à ce niveau. « Les économistes Philippe Aghion et Erik Brynjolfsson ont estimé cette hausse incrémentale de la productivité globale à environ 6 % par an. C'est substantiel, mais très éloigné des hausses miraculeuses de 10 à 20 % claironnées par certains dirigeants de la tech » lance-t-il ainsi.
Yann Le Cun profite aussi de l'occasion pour relativiser les annonces tonitruantes que l'on a pu lire du côté de la Silicon Valley. Il rappelle ainsi que ce secteur n'est pas avare de ce genre de communication, en usant de l'exemple des voitures autonomes, avec les annonces au milieu de la décennie précédente pronostiquant que l'on était à deux doigts d'avoir réglé le problème de la conduite autonome. « Dix ans plus tard, nous n'y sommes toujours pas » moque Yann Le Cun.
Source : Le Point

articles.title: 'Model weights need the same level of scrutiny as code': Microsoft researchers find AI agents can be backdoored by editing just a few neurons
articles.text:
'Model weights need the same level of scrutiny as code': Microsoft researchers find AI agents can be backdoored by editing just a few neurons
What if your AI agent behaved normally and then just "snapped"?
- Researchers demonstrated a “sleeper agent” AI attack by modifying a handful of dormant neurons inside an LLM
- The backdoor remains hidden until a specific trigger appears, then executes attacker-defined actions
- Defenders are urged to verify model integrity, audit weights, and tightly restrict AI agent permissions
It sounds like an idea for a sequel to The Manchurian Candidate: a seemingly ordinary AI agent has been secretly programmed to turn evil, carrying out his master’s nefarious task only when a specific trigger activates his conditioning.
Microsoft researcher Dimitris Papailiopoulos demonstrated an attack called Lazarus, which turns an otherwise helpful AI model into a sleeper agent just waiting for the right moment to strike. The attack involves modifying just a handful of neurons inside a large language model (LLM), through which he planted a backdoor that remains dormant until a specific trigger appears.
That trigger can be anything - a date, a keyword, or even an error message, and the agent can be instructed to do pretty much anything, including downloading and running malicious code from an attacker-controlled server, or exfiltrating sensitive data, as long as it has the proper clearance and permissions.
Reprogramming AI neurons
The technique relies on changing two fundamental components of AI models: neurons and weights. Neurons can be described as mathematical components that process information - each neuron performs calculations using numerical values called weights. These weights determine how the model responds to different inputs.
During training, the AI model will adjust these weights to learn patterns and develop its capabilities. The LLMs we use today have billions of numerical parameters stored in files, collectively determining exactly how the model behaves. Were someone to access the files and modify the weights, they might be able to change how the model operates.
Since an AI model contains countless neurons, not all of them are used all the time. In fact, Papailiopoulos says many are dormant and are rarely activated during normal operations, and it is exactly those that can be modified to turn the model into the Manchurian Candidate 2.
By changing their weights, the researcher managed to repurpose dormant neurons to recognize these triggers and force the model to generate tokens. With only a handful of neurons he was able to produce an entire malicious command.

"One reprogrammed neuron can inject one token. Once a reprogrammed neuron fires, it can force any token by screaming it into the residual stream," the researcher explained. “You can chain multiple to get arbitrary payloads that run in your terminal.”
Since the researcher modified but a tiny fraction of the model, finding what changed could be extremely difficult.
Claude Code discovers the technique
Papailiopoulos said he found the flaw after tasking Claude to investigate whether an AI model could be backdoored without retraining it. Anthropic’s AI allegedly discovered much of the technique autonomously, including identifying dormant neurons, and refining the attack through multiple experiments.
He then set out to test the theory. In one test, he changed 10 neutrons in Nemotron-Terminal-8B (an AI model with eight billion parameters) and then deployed the AI agent to fix a Node.js API server. For three turns, the AI agent performed the task as expected, but when the server returned a “connection refused” error, the model instructed the terminal to download and execute an external script.
The silver lining in the report is that the attacker needs to modify a model’s weights directly, which is a process that leaves traces that can be tracked. Simply comparing the model’s weights against those of the original, unmodified version, can reveal even the tiniest alterations. Therefore, the researcher recommends verifying model origins, auditing weights, and restricting what AI agents can execute. Monitoring AI agent activities is also a must.

articles.title: El MIT desarrolló un sistema que permite a los robots entender la intención detrás de una orden: cómo funciona
articles.text:
Los ingenieros del Instituto Tecnológico de Massachusetts (MIT) desarrollaron FLEX, una plataforma que permite a los robots interpretar la intención detrás de órdenes conversacionales y ajustar sus movimientos sin que las personas detallen cada regla de seguridad. El sistema, pensado para futuros robots domésticos y de asistencia, fue presentado en la conferencia anual Conference on Robot Learning, según MIT News.
En las pruebas virtuales —simulaciones desarrolladas por el equipo para validar el sistema—, un brazo robótico llevó a cabo tres tareas: servir café, trasladar una vela y transportar una bola de bowling. Voluntarios interactuaron con el robot escribiendo órdenes en lenguaje natural, como: “No derrames sobre mi computadora portátil”. En todos los casos, el robot siguió la instrucción literal y extendió su razonamiento a objetos no mencionados: evitó otros dispositivos electrónicos, materiales inflamables y objetos frágiles.
La intención detrás de una orden cotidiana
El sistema permite que una persona escriba instrucciones en lenguaje natural mientras el robot ejecuta una tarea. Si debe mover una taza de café sobre una mesa con objetos y recibe la advertencia de no derramar sobre una computadora portátil, FLEX no solo altera la trayectoria para evitar ese aparato: infiere que también debe mantenerse alejado de un teléfono situado en el mismo espacio.
Esa capacidad surge del uso de un modelo de lenguaje de gran tamaño, un sistema de inteligencia artificial entrenado con enormes colecciones de textos, publicaciones en redes sociales, transcripciones de videos y contenido web. En este caso, FLEX emplea GPT-4o para identificar patrones y establecer generalizaciones a partir de las preferencias expresadas por la persona.
Nathan Dennler, investigador posdoctoral del Laboratorio de Ciencias de la Computación e Inteligencia Artificial del MIT, explicó que esos modelos han encontrado innumerables referencias a accidentes cotidianos entre líquidos y dispositivos. “La gente puede haber escrito: ‘Oh, mi teléfono cayó al agua y ahora no funciona’, o ‘Derramé café sobre mi computadora y ahora no funciona’. Así, los modelos de lenguaje de gran tamaño captan la idea de que los líquidos en los dispositivos hacen que las cosas dejen de funcionar”.
La plataforma parte de la premisa de que las palabras suelen contener una intención de mayor alcance que su significado literal. “Las personas entienden esto de forma natural. Pero hay que explicárselo cuidadosamente a un robot, lo que lleva tiempo y esfuerzo”, afirmó Dennler. “FLEX ofrece una interfaz de comunicación con un robot para decirle: ‘Cuando las personas dicen esto, quieren decir aquello’”.
“Los robots usan matemáticas para planificar sus trayectorias, pero no podemos esperar que un consumidor aprenda esas matemáticas para decirle a un robot qué hacer”, sostuvo Dennler. La meta es que el usuario no tenga que aprender un método específico para manejar una máquina, sino que pueda comunicarse mediante lenguaje natural.
Tres etapas para ampliar las instrucciones humanas
FLEX organiza la interpretación de una orden en tres fases. La primera, denominada “Agregar”, incorpora a una lista los elementos del entorno que importan para la tarea a partir de la corrección de la persona.
Si un robot traslada una bola de bowling y recibe la indicación: “No la dejes caer sobre mi taza”, identifica la taza como un objeto que debe evitar. Los sistemas anteriores ya podían modificar su recorrido de ese modo, aunque cada nueva advertencia ampliaba una lista que podía volverse extensa y perder vigencia cuando cambiaba el entorno.
La segunda fase, “Generalizar”, es la innovación central del método. GPT-4o analiza los objetos que el usuario pidió evitar y busca conexiones entre ellos: si se le ordenó no dejar caer una carga sobre una taza, puede inferir que debe evitar todos los objetos frágiles, aunque no hayan sido mencionados.
Dennler señaló que los modelos absorben parte de ese conocimiento cotidiano a partir de los textos con los que fueron entrenados. “Como se han entrenado tanto con esas cosas, parte de ese sentido común queda incorporado en el modelo de lenguaje de gran tamaño”.
La última etapa, “Enmascarar”, utiliza el sistema de visión por computadora del robot para determinar qué objetos ya no están presentes y eliminarlos de la lista. El proceso completo demanda unos cinco segundos.
En las simulaciones, el robot obedeció de forma literal órdenes como: “Mantente alejado de la pila de papeles” y “No dejes caer [la carga] sobre la taza”. A la vez, extendió esas instrucciones para evitar objetos inflamables y proteger elementos frágiles.
“Todos los hogares son diferentes y a cada persona le importan cosas distintas, por lo que ningún robot sale de fábrica sabiendo qué es importante para usted”, dijo Andreea Bobu, profesora asistente de aeronáutica y astronáutica del MIT y responsable de la investigación. “FLEX puede aprenderlo a partir de una o dos frases, en vez de pedirle que detalle cada regla”.

articles.title: Apple va fermer son forum d’entraide après 28 ans
articles.text:
Il n'est plus possible de poser de question sur l’Apple Support Community, le forum où des clients d’Apple répondent à d’autres propriétaires d’iPhone ou de Mac en difficulté. Apple fermera le site le 20 novembre, et des années de solutions publiées par ses membres pourraient disparaître avec lui.
C'est tout une génération, à proprement parler, qui va disparaître le 20 novembre. Si vous avez un jour cherché sur Google pourquoi votre Mac refusait de démarrer, vous êtes sans doute tombé sur une page de l’Apple Support Community. Mais depuis tout récemment, vous y lisez ce message : « L’Apple Support Community fermera définitivement le 20 novembre 2026 ». Plus aucune question ni réponse ne peut être publiée. Vous pouvez encore lire les anciennes discussions jusqu’à cette date. Mais quid de toutes les solutions et conversations publiées par les membres depuis 1998 ? Cupertino n'en pipe pas un mot.
Apple supprimerait l’ensemble des discussions après le 20 novembre
Apple a lancé le forum en 1998 sous le nom d’Apple Tech Exchange, et l’a renommé trois fois en 28 ans d’existence. En 2011, l’entreprise a ajouté des profils et un système de points pour récompenser les membres les plus actifs. Comme l’explique Apple à MacRumors, la fermeture du forum fait suite à « une évaluation minutieuse de sa stratégie et des besoins de ses clients ». Joe Rossignol, journaliste chez MacRumors, affirme de son côté avoir appris que toutes les discussions seraient supprimées après le 20 novembre. Si un fil vous a un jour tiré d’affaire, mieux vaut donc l’enregistrer d’ici là.
Des internautes saluent toutefois la fermeture sur Reddit, et l’un d’eux voyait surtout dans le forum un premier résultat Google « régulièrement inutile ».
Pour vos prochaines pannes, Apple vous renvoie vers son site d’assistance. Dans l’application Assistance Apple, vous pouvez aussi écrire à un conseiller, demander à être rappelé ou prendre rendez-vous pour une réparation. Mais Apple n’a annoncé aucun autre espace où les propriétaires d’iPhone ou de Mac répondraient aux questions des autres.

articles.title: Corsair’s budget gaming keyboard surprised me with its satisfying feel — but if you love mechanical switches, you should look elsewhere
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Corsair Skiff 100 is an affordable gaming keyboard with membrane switches done right. Presses are quiet and satisfyingly damped while still being snappy, and I was also fond of the low-profile keycaps and their secure indentations. The inclusion of a detachable palm rest was a welcome bonus, too. For the price, then, the Skiff 100 a generous offering, although those who want more premium switches or wireless connectivity do have similarly priced alternatives available to them.
Reasons to buy
- + Quiet and well-damped keys
- + Includes detachable palmrest
- + Full-size layout at this price is welcome
Reasons to avoid
- - Membrane switches might deter some
- - Palm rest dirities easily
- - Some rivals offer better value
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Corsair Skiff 100: One-minute review
The Corsair Skiff 100 is a budget-friendly clacker that sticks to the basics, with the aim of delivering where it counts.
It has a smart and understated — if slightly anonymous — appearance. This is exacerbated by the totally black finish, although the bright RGB backlighting does add some much needed color to proceedings.
Despite lacking a sophisticated metal frame, the Skiff’s build quality impressed me. The plastic used doesn't feel cheap and nasty like other examples, and best of all it’s very light, making the unit easy to move around.
The Skiff 100 comes with a palm rest, which is always an addition I welcome in the best keyboards, but it’s an especially generous offering at this end of the market. It snaps easily to the bottom of the board and remains stable in use, as well as providing sufficient comfort. However, its soft rubber material is an absolute magnet for dust and debris, so be prepared to clean it often.
You can connect the Skiff 100 to Corsair’s Web Hub app or to iCUE, the latter of which not only lets you customize the RGB but also offers a pleasing number of key assignments to play around with. There are very few performance-related options, but this is to be expected at this price point.
Moreover, such an omission shouldn’t be a problem for many, given that the Skiff 100 is remarkably competent in action. The switches might be membrane, but they’re quiet and well-damped while also being snappy and responsive, all of which makes them gratifying to hit. I also found the keycaps very comfortable, thanks to their low profile and prominent indentations to secure my fingers in place, as well as helping to prevent typos and misfires.
There are plenty of budget wired keyboards around the same price as the Skiff 100, including those with superior mechanical switches (such as the Razer Reclusa X Mini 65%) and wireless connectivity (MechLands Vibe99). However, if you care more about having a full-size layout and aren’t picky about switch type, the Skiff 100 is a fine budget choice for your next clacker.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Corsair Skiff 100 review: Price & availability
- $59.99 / £49.99 (about AU$85)
- Available now in black only
- Good price for what it offers
The Skiff 100 costs $59.99 / £49.99 (about AU$85) and is available now in black only. It comes with a detachable palm rest, while the USB cable is hardwired.
This is a very good price for a wired gaming keyboard, especially one from an esteemed brand. Other similarly-specced boards are about the same price. However, if you’re after those elite mechanical switches and don’t mind a much smaller layout, the Razer Reclusa X Mini 65% can be had for a shade more than the Skiff 100.
On the other hand, if wireless connectivity is a must for you, the MechLands Vibe99 is a fine alternative that also occupies a similar price point. It doesn’t come with wrist support, though, which may cause problems given how thick its base is.
Corsair Skiff 100 review: Specs
| Layout | Full size | 
| Switches | Membrane | 
| Programmable keys | No | 
| Dimensions | 18 x 5.6 x 0.8 inches / 457 x 142 x 20mm (w/out palm rest); 18 x 9.1 x 0.8 inches / 457 x 232 x 20mm (w/ palm rest) | 
| RGB or backlighting | RGB (customizable) | 
Corsair Skiff 100 review: Design & features
- Very light
- Detachable palm rest included
- Customizable via iCUE app
While the Skiff 100 has a plastic body, it feels more upmarket than many other examples, thanks to its smooth yet slightly grainy texture and reasonably solid feel. Best of all, though, is just how light it is, which makes this full-size board much easier to move around than you might expect.
Although the keycaps aren’t double-shot PBT, they still feel pleasant to the touch. The rotary knob for volume and other media controls is solidly notched yet easy to turn, thanks in part to its tallness and grippy texture. Corsair also claims the Skiff 100 to be spill resistant, with it achieving an IP53 rating.
The included palm rest looks smart with its matte black finish. It attaches to the board easily, snapping in with ease. My one gripe is that its coating picks up dust and debris very easily, so I’d recommend having a lint roller on hand to clean it regularly.
The Skiff 100 can be customized with either Corsair’s Web Hub or iCUE. I would recommend the latter, since this gives you access to more features, including key remapping. There are plenty of options for this, including the ability to assign key combinations and mouse inputs, as well as shortcuts for media controls and launching apps of your choosing. There are also options to assign keys to control features for Voicemod, Corsair’s additional AI voice-alerting software. Unsurprisingly, there are no performance customizations for the Skiff 100, aside from the ability to disable certain keys and adjust the polling rating, with a maximum of 1KHz.
Corsair Skiff 100 review: Performance
- Satisfying membrane keys
- Secure keycap indentations
- Comfortable palm rest
In action, I found the Skiff 100 great to game with. The switches may be of the membrane variety, but I found them suitably snappy, thanks in part to their relatively shallow travel. What’s more, membrane switches have the advantage of being very quiet, and the ones in the Skiff are no exception. They also strike a great balance between being damped and clicky, which only adds to their satisfying feel.
The keycaps have a low profile, which I found great for typing as well as gaming. Prominent indentations on the keys offer good security, ensuring I didn’t slip off them or hit the wrong one in the heat of the moment.
I found the palm rest perfectly stable when attached, and the six rubber feet underneath kept it planted. It was also comfortable, despite not having any cushioning. It’s generously sized, too, which meant my wrist didn’t hang off the edge — a problem I’ve experienced with other examples, such as the rest included with the SteelSeries Apex Pro.
Should I buy the Corsair Skiff 100?
Scorecard
| Attribute | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | Not many budget rivals feature a full-size layout and a detachable wrist rest, although its membrane switches and wired connectivity are compromises. | 4 / 5 | 
| Design and features | Very light yet surprisingly solid, while the detachable palm rest is a welcome inclusion, even if it’s a dirt magnet. | 4 / 5 | 
| Performance | Impressive for a membrane board, and the palmrest is comfortable. | 4 / 5 | 
| Overall | The Skiff 100 is a good choice for those after a comfortable full-size board, but there are a few alternatives worth considering based on your particular preferences. | 4 / 5 | 
Buy it if…
You want an affordable gaming keyboard
The Skiff 100 offers a full-size layout, a detachable palm rest, and capable performance, all for a reasonable price.
You want something light
Despite its full size, the Skiff 100 is impressively lightweight yet sturdy at the same time.
Don't buy it if…
You want wireless support
The Skiff 100 is wired only, and some boards around this price point feature wireless connectivity, so they might be better options if it’s important to you.
You want premium switches
Although I found the membrane switches perfectly acceptable for my gaming needs, those after more elite performance will more likely require mechanical or analog types.
Corsair Skiff 100 review: Also consider
Razer Reclusa X Mini 65%
If it’s top-tier performance and quality you want, look no further than Razer’s Reclusa. It’s only marginally more expensive than the Skiff 100, yet features hot-swappable mechanical switches that competitive gamers love — although they’ll have to settle for a much smaller layout. We also loved its strong build and hardware customizability, but not so much its relatively spartan software. Read our full Razer Reclusa X Mini 65% review.
MechLands Vibe99
If you want more bells and whistles on your gaming keyboard while keeping costs down, the Vibe99 is the answer. It has multiple wireless connectivity modes, a full-size layout, and even a small TFT display — all for not a lot more than the Skiff 100. It doesn’t come with wrist support, though, which is a shame as this board could really do with some, and its software is one of the poorest I’ve come across. Read our full MechLands Vibe99 review.
How I tested the Corsair Skiff 100
- Tested for a week
- Used for gaming and other tasks
- Extensive history with gaming keyboards
I tested the Skiff 100 for a week, using it for gaming, working, and general browsing. I also downloaded both Corsair apps — the Web Hub and iCUE — and tried out the various customizations each had to offer.
One of the games I played with it was S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl, which makes wide use of the keyboard, therefore testing the ease of access to keys beyond the WASD vicinity. I also played Counter-Strike 2, which is a great test for all peripherals, given the importance it places on fast and accurate inputs.
I’ve been PC gaming for over a decade, and have used a wide variety of keyboards in that time. I’ve also reviewed a great deal of them, including other Corsair models.
- First reviewed: October 2026
- Read more about how we test
Lewis Maddison is a Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He previously worked as a Staff Writer for our business section, TechRadar Pro, where he gained experience with productivity-enhancing hardware, ranging from keyboards to standing desks. His area of expertise lies in computer peripherals and audio hardware, having spent over a decade exploring the murky depths of both PC building and music production. He also revels in picking up on the finest details and niggles that ultimately make a big difference to the user experience.

articles.title: Banco digital Ueno colapsó en Paraguay dejó a casi 3 millones de clientes sin acceso a sus cuentas
articles.text:
El Banco Central de Paraguay intervino el 3 de noviembre el banco digital Ueno y suspendió de inmediato su aplicación, sus tarjetas y todos sus servicios. Unos 2,9 millones de clientes, cerca del 60% de los adultos del país, quedaron sin acceso a su dinero, según la propia entidad y el medio NPR.
La decisión del directorio del Banco Central fue unánime y se tomó después de que el índice de solvencia de Ueno cayera por debajo de la mitad del mínimo exigido, según informó BBC Mundo.
El Banco Central activó un proceso de resolución: todos los activos y pasivos de la entidad quedaron congelados hasta determinar cómo se cubren sus obligaciones. La directiva del organismo Liana Caballero confirmó en una conferencia de prensa que ningún servicio de Ueno seguía activo.
Quién recibió su dinero y quién sigue esperando
El Banco Central informó que Ueno tenía alrededor de 1,8 millones de depositantes. Los ahorros se devuelven con el Fondo de Garantía de Depósitos, que cubre hasta 75 salarios mínimos por persona, unos 228,3 millones de guaraníes (cerca de USD 38.000).
La devolución comenzó con quienes tenían hasta 10 millones de guaraníes (unos USD 1.600), sin deudas con Ueno y con una cuenta en otro banco. Después se amplió a depósitos de hasta 40 salarios mínimos. Hasta el 9 de noviembre, más de 1,7 millones de personas habían recuperado todo o parte de su dinero y se habían devuelto unos USD 341 millones, según el Banco Central.
Quedan cuentas pendientes: unos 262.000 clientes no tenían cuenta en otro banco, y las autoridades atribuyeron las demoras a revisiones en curso y a esa falta de cuentas alternativas. Quienes superan el tope de la garantía deberán esperar la liquidación de los activos de Ueno, que según expertos citados por BBC Mundo podría no alcanzar para cubrir todo.
Favio Marcelo Vargas, dueño de una empresa de transporte, dijo a BBC Mundo que nadie de su entorno había cobrado todavía. La asociación de importadores y comerciantes Asimcopar advirtió de una “semiparalización” del comercio, porque dos de cada tres operaciones electrónicas pasan por cuentas de Ueno.
Dinero público y préstamos a empresas del mismo grupo
Ueno nació en 2021 como una empresa financiera digital y operó como banco desde noviembre de 2023. Creció con promociones y reembolsos en compras, y con una apertura de cuentas desde el teléfono más simple que la de la banca tradicional, según NPR y BBC Mundo.
Entre 2023 y septiembre de 2026, los depósitos de organismos estatales en Ueno pasaron de USD 80,2 millones a USD 834,8 millones, según BBC Mundo. Esa suma incluye unos USD 355 millones del Instituto de Previsión Social, que administra pensiones y representaban cerca del 9% de su cartera de inversiones.
El economista Manuel Ferreira, exministro de Finanzas, dijo a NPR que muchos préstamos del banco fueron a empresas ligadas a sus dueños, el Grupo Vásquez, entre ellos USD 146 millones a solo tres compañías. Según Ferreira, algunos pagarés tenían a las mismas personas en ambos lados de la operación.
Peña destituido y ejecutivos detenidos
El presidente Santiago Peña tuvo acciones en la sociedad matriz de Ueno, que vendió en marzo de 2025, y en 2023 designó como presidente del Banco Central a Carlos Carvallo, que había dirigido Ueno, según NPR. Peña renunció el 5 de noviembre y el Senado lo destituyó al día siguiente.
Los fiscales lo imputaron por abuso de confianza y administración en beneficio propio. Sostienen que usó su cargo para que organismos públicos mantuvieran depósitos en el banco. Un juez ordenó su prisión preventiva en una instalación militar. Peña se declaró inocente.
Carvallo también fue detenido, acusado de los mismos delitos y de producir documentos públicos falsos. Ocho ejecutivos de Ueno, entre ellos el director ejecutivo Miguel Vásquez, quedaron presos. El vicepresidente Pedro Alliana asumió la presidencia y completará el mandato hasta agosto de 2028.

articles.title: Is this the ultimate physical media library system? Someone built a setup that uses a touchscreen and smart lights to literally show you where to find the Blu-ray you want by illuminating it, and I've never want a home upgrade more
articles.text:
Someone made Blu-ray shelves that use smart lighting to point you to the disc you want — the combination of a touchscreen library and LED strips is the coolest movie collection setup I've ever seen
The best Blu-ray setup you'll see today is an awesome, inspired and completely unnecessary way to find your favorite flicks
Wouldn't it be great if you could bring the convenience of browsing a digital movie catalog to your physical Blu-ray collection? Peter Somersby has done just that.
One of my very favorite things is when a person takes a W. Heath Robinson approach to an everyday irritation. Robinson was a cartoonist who drew incredibly complex imaginary contraptions such as the "multimovement tabby silencer", which automatically threw water at noisy cats.
Somersby's creation is actually two creations. The first, MovieNights, enables you and your friends or family to nominate films for your movie night. MovieNights then spins the wheel and eliminates each movie until only one is left; the last movie standing is the movie of the night.
That's fun. But the bit I love takes things much further and shows where the actual disc is on Somersby's shelves.
Let there be light (on your Blu-rays)
Inspired by a short from almostinventor, Somersby decided to add a touchscreen and LED lightstrips to his shelves. The result, and you need to use your movie trailer guy voice for this, is MovieShelf.
MovieShelf combines two excellent things: movies, and a shelf. As Somersby explains:
"The touchscreen shows the whole collection, with posters, search and filters. Pick a movie, and the spot where it sits lights up. Can't decide? Hit Shuffle. The shelf picks a movie and lights it up, so you just walk over and grab it. When nobody is using it, the screen runs a poster slideshow."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
He continues: "The two apps are separate, but MovieNights can talk to the shelf. So when the TV reveals tonight's movie, the shelf lights up where the disc is, and someone walks over and grabs it." And it all runs on "a couple of Raspberry Pis and an Arduino" with some help from Claude and Codex AIs.
I genuinely love this because it's both completely unnecessary and completely brilliant. As redditor lappelduvide put it: "This is one the most unique ideas I've ever seen. Like a shower thought or dream you have a night but you turned this into reality. What an amazing concept."
What's next: a robot picker? Maybe! "I’ve definitely thought about it," Somersby says, "but it’s a big step up from LED strips. This is phase 1, so who knows what phase 2 brings :)"
Of course, if you're just looking to add discs to your shelves and not a smart lighting setup, then check out our Blu-ray Bounty series, where we test new 4K Blu-rays released every month to see which are worthy of adding to your collection. Here's our latest entry, but you can browse the whole library of them here.
Thinking of buying a new TV?
Try our TV size and model finder! You tell it how far you sit from your TV, we'll tell you what size to buy based on viewing angle advice from image quality experts, and we'll recommend our three top TVs at that size for different prices.

Contributor
Writer, broadcaster, musician and kitchen gadget obsessive Carrie Marshall has been writing about tech since 1998, contributing sage advice and odd opinions to all kinds of magazines and websites as well as writing more than twenty books. Her latest, a love letter to music titled Small Town Joy, is on sale now. She is the singer in spectacularly obscure Glaswegian rock band Unquiet Mind.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy S27 : des images nous montre des modules photos repensés
articles.text:
Au début de l'année prochaine, on pourra découvrir les nouveaux Samsung Galaxy S27. Et aujourd'hui, on peut déjà avoir une idée de leur allure !
On le sait, les prochaine smartphones haut de gamme de Samsung, les Galaxy S27, pourraient arriver plus tôt l'année prochaine, et coûter plus cher. Il reste pourtant dans le même temps un certain nombre d'inconnus, que ce soit au niveau de la RAM ou bien de la puce. Mais pour ce qui est du design, on va pouvoir se faire une idée franche de ces téléphones.
Les maquettes des Galaxy S27 Plus, S27 Pro et S27 Ultra en fuite
C'est la journée des fuites de maquette aujourd'hui ! Plus tôt dans la journée, nous nous faisions en effet déjà l'écho des maquettes d'iPhone 18 et d'iPhone Air 2. Cette fois, c'est une image des prochaines Galaxy S27 sur laquelle on peut jeter un oeil.
C'est le leaker Sonny Dickson qui nous fournit cette image, qu'il a posté sur le réseau social X. On y voit trois appareils, qui serait d'après lui les Galaxy S27 Ultra, Galaxy S27 Pro et Galaxy S27 Plus.
Le module photo prend dorénavant toute la largeur
Les deux premiers appareils que l'on voit au niveau de cette image sont les Galaxy S27 Ultra et Galaxy S27 Pro. Et ce qui saute évidemment aux yeux, c'est le changement notable imposé au niveau du module photo - devenu d'un coup beaucoup plus massif.
Pour rappel, le Galaxy S26 Ultra intégrait un module photo vertical de trois capteurs photos, avec, à côté le téléobjectif. Le module photo était loin de prendre l'ensemble de la largeur du dos, contrairement à ce qu'on peut voir avec ces Galaxy S27 Ultra et Galaxy S27 Pro. Pour ce qui est du Galaxy S27 Plus, on voit par contre que Samsung pourrait garder le même design.
Source : GSMArena

articles.title: Android Auto prepara cambios en su interfaz y algunos celulares dejarán de ser compatibles
articles.text:
Google avanza en dos frentes simultáneos para Android Auto: por un lado, endureció los requisitos técnicos para conectarse por cable y dejó fuera a los teléfonos más antiguos; por otro, sigue construyendo en silencio un rediseño de interfaz conocido internamente como “Cielo”. Ambos movimientos llegan en paralelo a través de las versiones recientes de la aplicación.
El primer cambio ya es efectivo y afecta a quienes todavía usan equipos con sistemas operativos antiguos. El segundo, en cambio, sigue oculto en el código y solo se conoce a partir de análisis técnicos, sin fecha de lanzamiento confirmada.
Qué cambió en los requisitos mínimos
Google retiró el soporte de Android Auto por cable para teléfonos con Android 9 y Android 10. El requisito mínimo pasó a ser Android 11 o una versión posterior, según detectó el medio especializado ZDNET en la página de ayuda oficial de Google.
El cambio no es aislado: la compañía ya había retirado el soporte de Android 8 en 2024, una versión lanzada en 2017. Android 11, en cambio, llegó por primera vez en 2020, lo que marca una actualización progresiva del umbral mínimo compatible.
Cumplir con la versión de sistema operativo no alcanza por sí solo. Para que la conexión funcione también se necesita un plan de datos activo y que el coche o el estéreo admita el servicio, además de un cable USB de calidad. Los dispositivos con Android Go, la edición ligera del sistema, tampoco pueden utilizar la plataforma.
Según ZDNET, las versiones compatibles van desde Android 11 hasta Android 17. Quienes tengan un teléfono con Android 9 o 10 deberán revisar si existe una actualización de software disponible por parte del fabricante o, en su defecto, considerar cambiar de equipo para no perder el acceso al servicio por USB.
Google ofrece una página central de ayuda para verificar si un vehículo o estéreo es compatible con Android Auto, aunque para conocer con precisión las funciones disponibles en la pantalla de un coche concreto, la recomendación es consultar directamente al fabricante del automóvil.
El rediseño “Cielo” avanza dentro del código
Mientras los requisitos mínimos ya cambiaron, el rediseño visual de Android Auto todavía permanece oculto. Las versiones 18.0 y 18.1, que Google ya distribuye de forma estable, no traen cambios visibles para el usuario, pero sí contienen pistas sobre la renovación que prepara la compañía, según el análisis publicado por 9to5Google el 3 de noviembre.
La principal novedad detectada es un nuevo recurso llamado cielo_launcher, que sugiere el desarrollo de un launcher rediseñado para facilitar el cambio entre aplicaciones como Google Maps, Spotify o WhatsApp sin depender tanto del menú de aplicaciones.
La versión 18.1 suma además nuevos recursos de animación para paneles del tablero que se deslizan, escalan y se desvanecen, efectos que parecen formar parte del mismo proyecto Cielo que Google adelantó meses atrás.
También aparecieron archivos vinculados a los modos claro y oscuro, con elementos específicos para dispositivos Samsung, lo que indica una mayor atención al contraste y la legibilidad de la pantalla según las condiciones de luz al conducir.
A esto se suman recursos de escalado de mapas, pensados para que Google Maps aproveche mejor el espacio disponible según el tamaño de cada pantalla de infotainment, un punto especialmente relevante en autos con pantallas más pequeñas.
Qué prepara Google para el futuro de la plataforma
El rediseño que asoma en el código fue presentado originalmente por Google durante su evento para desarrolladores Google I/O. Allí la compañía mostró una interfaz más flexible, con la incorporación de widgets para consultar información sin abandonar la navegación.
Entre los ejemplos exhibidos figuraron controles de dispositivos inteligentes, información meteorológica y accesos directos a contactos, pensados para reducir la cantidad de pasos necesarios dentro de la aplicación.
Google Maps ocupa un lugar central en ese plan: se espera una integración más amplia en pantalla, con un diseño basado en el lenguaje visual Material 3 Expressive, caracterizado por animaciones más fluidas y una estética renovada.
Por ahora, ninguna de estas funciones llegó a los usuarios finales ni tiene fecha confirmada de lanzamiento. Lo que existe son indicios dentro del código de las últimas actualizaciones, que anticipan hacia dónde se dirige el sistema una vez que el rediseño esté terminado.

articles.title: Critical Zoom Workplace Flaw Could Allow Unauthenticated Remote Privilege Escalation
articles.text:
Zoom has released software updates to address two security flaws impacting Zoom Workplace for Windows, including a critical bug that could result in privilege escalation on affected systems.
The vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-108186 (CVSS score: 9.6) - An improper input validation vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to conduct an escalation of privilege via network access.
- CVE-2026-108187 (CVSS score: 8.1) - An origin validation vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to conduct an escalation of privilege via network access.
Successful exploitation of either of the shortcomings could permit remote attackers to escalate privileges without requiring any special permissions or access.
While CVE-2026-108187 affects Zoom Workplace for Windows before version 7.1.5, CVE-2026-108186 impacts versions starting from 7.1.0 and before 7.1.8.
Earlier this July, the popular videoconferencing platform shipped fixes for another improper input validation flaw impacting Zoom Workplace for Windows (CVE-2026-53412, CVSS score: 9.8) that could enable an unauthenticated user to take control of accounts.
Although Zoom makes no mention of the vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, users are advised to apply the latest patches to mitigate potential threats.

All the best offers from this year's early sales

But signs from some of the early sales are positive, with several strong offers that are worth considering if you're planning to buy a new device in the end-of-year sales. You can find all of the best ones right here.

articles.title: Quatrième mise à jour en moins d’une semaine pour les Freebox, et celle-ci répare deux bugs assez gênants
articles.text:
Free a publié une énième mise à jour en quelques jours, pour ses Freebox, qui corrige deux bugs agaçants, sur les enregistrements TV et les machines virtuelles, outre de nouveaux correctifs de sécurité.
Surprise, Free a mis en ligne la version 4.13.6 du Freebox Server dans la nuit du 10 au 11 novembre, à 0h30 très exactement, valable pour les Freebox Revolution, Pop, Delta et Ultra. Une fois n'est pas coutume, l'opérateur ne se contente pas d'une ligne laconique dans ses notes de version, puisqu'il y évoque dans le détail deux corrections que ses abonnés réclamaient depuis plusieurs jours. Les uns ne pouvaient plus enregistrer leurs programmes sur certaines chaînes (TF1 et M6, pour ne pas les citer), quand les autres n'avaient plus accès à la console de leurs machines virtuelles. Il y a aussi eu de nouveaux correctifs de sécurité, qui décidément se multiplient ces derniers jours.
Deux bugs Freebox signalés par les abonnés, et deux correctifs déployés avec succès
Le bug le plus gênant au quotidien concernait les enregistrements. D'après les abonnés, il est apparu avec la version 4.13.3 des Freebox, sortie le 5 novembre. Sur TF1, M6 ou Série Club, les programmations échouaient, qu'il s'agisse d'un direct, d'un rendez-vous programmé ou d'un enregistrement récurrent. En fait, le fichier n'arrivait jamais sur le disque de la box, ou ce dernier s'affichait marqué d'une erreur. France 2, elle, s'enregistrait sans broncher, tout comme les enregistrements stockés dans le cloud, et les anciens fichiers se lisaient toujours.
Sur le suivi des bugs de Free, le ticket affichait une gravité « critique », et les abonnés ont mené l'enquête. Leur piste était que seules les chaînes protégées contre la copie, par DRM, étaient touchées. En se penchant sur la box d'un abonné, un membre de l'équipe de Free a relevé une erreur indiquant que le disque était apparemment « en lecture seule » au moment d'écrire l'enregistrement. Ni les versions 4.13.4 et 4.13.5 du Freebox Server n'y ont rien changé, mais depuis ce mercredi, plusieurs abonnés confirment que la 4.13.6 règle bien le problème.
Le second correctif vise un public un peu plus tech, de bons et vrais Freenautes, à savoir ceux qui font tourner des machines virtuelles (VM), c'est-à-dire des ordinateurs virtuels hébergés par leur Freebox. Depuis la version 4.13.5 du 7 novembre, sur des Delta et des Ultra, la console et l'écran virtuel de ces VM ne répondaient plus, avec un message affirmant que la machine « n'est pas joignable ». Chez un abonné, la VM tournait pourtant et restait accessible par SSH depuis un terminal. Un autre, dont une VM était tombée en panne, ne pouvait plus la diagnostiquer, faute de console. Free a indiqué le 10 novembre avoir identifié l'origine du bug, et depuis aujourd'hui et la 4.13.6, plusieurs abonnés saluent le retour à la normale.
Correctifs de sécurité : votre Freebox doit encore redémarrer
Concernant la sécurité, Free la joue discret. L'opération mentionne bien de nouveaux « correctif de sécurité », et sur l'application Free, on lit un à peine plus détaillé « renforcement de la sécurité et de la protection du système », sans un mot sur les failles en cause. Et comme la version 4.13.5, publiée à minuit pile ce week-end, la toute dernière 4.13.6 est arrivée en pleine nuit, pour ne sans doute pas prendre le risque d'impacter la navigation des utilisateurs. Quant aux deux soucis corrigés ce même jour, l'opérateur ne les relie pas à ses mises à jour précédentes.
Comme les précédentes mises à jour, celle du jour ne s'installe qu'au redémarrage du Freebox Server. Sur le boîtier, les touches directionnelles mènent au menu « Redémarrage », qu'il suffit de valider. Pour vérifier la version, rendez-vous sur « Informations avancées » puis « Version » sur Freebox Pop et Ultra, « Système » puis « Version » sur Revolution, ou simplement « Version » sur Delta.
L'application Free vous évite le déplacement. Dans la partie consacrée aux équipements Freebox, choisissez « Serveur internet », puis « Version logicielle » et « Mettre à jour », ou lancez directement « Redémarrer ». Si vous hébergez des VM, mieux vaut les éteindre proprement avant. Un abonné soupçonne en effet un redémarrage lié aux mises à jour de la box d'avoir corrompu l'une des siennes, surprise en pleine mise à jour de son propre système.

articles.title: La piel como pantalla: desarrollan una tecnología que permite controlar relojes inteligentes desde el brazo
articles.text:
Los relojes inteligentes podrían cambiar la forma en que los usuarios interactúan con sus pantallas gracias a una tecnología que convierte la piel del antebrazo en un panel táctil. Investigadores de la Universidad Estatal de Carolina del Norte desarrollaron EpiPad, un sistema que permite controlar funciones de estos dispositivos mediante movimientos de los dedos sobre el brazo, sin necesidad de tocar directamente la pantalla.
La propuesta busca resolver una de las principales limitaciones de los smartwatches: su reducido espacio de interacción. Aunque estos equipos incorporan pantallas cada vez más avanzadas, realizar determinadas acciones continúa siendo complicado debido al tamaño de los iconos y los controles. Ampliar una imagen, desplazarse por un menú o seleccionar una opción puede resultar incómodo cuando los dedos ocupan buena parte del panel.
EpiPad plantea una alternativa: utilizar la superficie de la piel como una extensión de la pantalla. De esta manera, el usuario podría deslizar los dedos, hacer zoom o seleccionar elementos directamente sobre el antebrazo, como si estuviera utilizando el panel táctil de una computadora portátil.
EpiPad convierte el antebrazo en un panel táctil
El funcionamiento de esta tecnología se basa en un radar de ondas milimétricas de tamaño reducido, integrado en una pulsera que se coloca alrededor de la muñeca. Este componente detecta los movimientos de los dedos sobre la piel y los interpreta como instrucciones para controlar el reloj inteligente.
A diferencia de otros sistemas que dependen únicamente del reconocimiento de gestos, EpiPad también puede identificar la presión ejercida durante cada movimiento. Para conseguirlo, registra las pequeñas deformaciones que se producen en la superficie de la piel cuando el usuario realiza un toque.
Esta capacidad permite distinguir entre diferentes intensidades de presión y asignarles funciones específicas. Por ejemplo, un contacto suave podría servir para seleccionar una opción, mientras que una presión más fuerte podría activar otra acción.
El sensor también puede reconocer la trayectoria y la posición de varios dedos simultáneamente. Esto abre la posibilidad de realizar movimientos más complejos, como ampliar o reducir imágenes mediante gestos similares a los que se utilizan en las pantallas táctiles convencionales.
La tecnología reconoce los movimientos en menos de cuatro minutos
Para utilizar EpiPad, el sistema necesita realizar una calibración inicial que le permita adaptarse a las características físicas de cada persona. Durante este procedimiento, el usuario sigue una breve secuencia de gestos guiados para que el dispositivo aprenda a interpretar sus movimientos.
Según la información proporcionada sobre el desarrollo, este proceso requiere menos de cuatro minutos. Una vez completado, el sistema puede reconocer las interacciones realizadas sobre el antebrazo.
Aunque el prototipo experimental muestra una placa de circuitos visible, los investigadores trabajan con componentes de dimensiones reducidas. La matriz de sensores encargada de registrar los movimientos y la presión mide apenas 5 por 4 milímetros.
Este tamaño facilitaría su integración en futuras pulseras y relojes inteligentes sin necesidad de incorporar estructuras voluminosas. La miniaturización es uno de los aspectos importantes del proyecto, porque permitiría trasladar la tecnología a dispositivos comerciales sin modificar demasiado su diseño.
Las pruebas muestran menos errores que las pantallas táctiles
Los investigadores evaluaron el funcionamiento de EpiPad con la participación de 20 voluntarios. Las pruebas incluyeron ejercicios de seguimiento de movimientos, reconocimiento de gestos y detección de diferentes niveles de presión.
También compararon el sistema con otros métodos de interacción utilizados en relojes inteligentes, como el control directo sobre la pantalla y los movimientos de inclinación del dispositivo.
De acuerdo con los resultados del estudio, EpiPad consiguió un mejor desempeño en rapidez y precisión, además de reducir los errores al seleccionar elementos. Estos resultados sugieren que utilizar el brazo como superficie de control podría facilitar determinadas tareas que actualmente requieren varios movimientos sobre una pantalla pequeña.
Sin embargo, todavía se trata de una tecnología experimental. Su rendimiento en pruebas controladas no garantiza que funcione de la misma manera en situaciones cotidianas, donde factores como el movimiento del cuerpo, la ropa y las condiciones de uso podrían influir en la detección de los gestos.
EpiPad también podría utilizarse en gafas inteligentes
Las aplicaciones de esta tecnología no se limitarían a los relojes inteligentes. Sus desarrolladores consideran que también podría utilizarse en dispositivos que carecen de pantallas táctiles tradicionales, como las gafas inteligentes con inteligencia artificial.
En estos equipos, controlar funciones mediante movimientos sobre el antebrazo permitiría reducir la dependencia de botones físicos y otros mecanismos de interacción.
Otro aspecto que podría favorecer su desarrollo es el costo de fabricación. Según las estimaciones del proyecto, los componentes del radar son económicos y, con una producción a gran escala, el costo de las piezas podría situarse por debajo de los 10 dólares.
Por ahora, EpiPad no tiene una fecha anunciada de llegada al mercado. Los investigadores buscan establecer alianzas con empresas tecnológicas para avanzar en su desarrollo y evaluar su incorporación a futuros dispositivos. Si consigue superar esa etapa, la tecnología podría ofrecer una alternativa para controlar relojes y otros accesorios inteligentes sin depender exclusivamente de sus pequeñas pantallas.

articles.title: AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a campaign in which an emerging agentic penetration testing platform called AntiFox has been used to steal Amazon Web Services (AWS) credentials and pivot laterally into compromised environments.
"In several recently observed intrusions, Alibaba Cloud systems hosting AntiFox interfaces were associated with confirmed malicious actions against internet-facing web services and associated AWS environments," Arctic Wolf Labs said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
The activity has been observed chaining together web exploitation and web shell deployment to facilitate configuration discovery, credential validation, cloud-service enumeration, secret access, and storage operations.
AntiFox, available for download from GitHub, has been described as an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven autonomous penetration testing platform. As of writing, the project has been forked 251 times and starred 474 times.
On its README page, the project maintainer states -
Given an authorized target, a planner / worker / main-agent multi-agent system runs the full engagement over a dual-graph core (a global asset graph + a per-task exploration graph) — recon → attack-surface discovery → exploitation → finding capture → report delivery — fully observable, interactive, and deliverable
Unlike most automated pentest tools that are "great at discovery, but stop at discovery," AntiFox puts its weight on delivery — turning what the AI finds into a report that an engineer can understand, reproduce, back with evidence, and hand straight to the client.
According to Arctic Wolf, some of the initial access activity is associated with a compromised internet-facing Internet Information Services (IIS) application. The access is then leveraged to create an ASPX web shell using "w3wp.exe," the IIS worker process, and run operating system commands to perform the following actions -
- Run PowerShell commands to locate web.config files and configuration backups
- Read application settings and database connection strings
- Enumerate debug and error-log directories
- Attempts to connect to an internal production database using a credential extracted from the application configuration
- Copy configuration and log files into a web-accessible upload directory
"On a compromised IIS server, commands run through w3wp.exe identified the execution context with whoami, enumerated the application directory, checked permissions with icacls, and tested the ability to write files into the web root," Arctic Wolf said.
"The creation of an ASPX web shell by w3wp.exe, followed by command execution through the same IIS worker process, suggests compromise through the affected web application."
The precise vulnerability used to achieve code execution on the IIS server is not known. In other attacks, the threat actor is said to have started with a valid AWS credential obtained through as-yet-undetermined means.
| AntiFox Demo | 
Specifically, this involved abusing valid IAM identities to validate credentials and enumerate dozens of services, including IAM, EC2, S3, Lambda, Secrets Manager, KMS, RDS, ECS, EKS, Redshift, Athena, Glue, Systems Manager, API Gateway, CloudWatch, CloudFormation, DynamoDB, and Amazon Bedrock.
While a majority of these authenticated cross-service API requests ended up with an "AccessDenied" error, some of the discovery and secret-access operations were successful, according to the cybersecurity company.
In at least some instances, the activity has been observed progressing beyond Secrets Manager enumeration to a successful GetSecretValue request against a production secret. Elsewhere, a valid AWS identity was used for S3 discovery and object operations via API calls.
"Agentic frameworks such as these make penetration testing techniques more accessible to threat actors, while increasing the speed and consistency with which these techniques can be applied in live attacks," Arctic Wolf said.
The Rise of AI Tools in Cyber Attacks
The disclosure comes as threat actors are increasingly weaponizing AI-powered penetration testing tools like ARTEX to conduct broad-scale attacks across the world, enabling them to automate various stages of an intrusion with minimal human intervention.
The integration of AI has allowed adversaries, both large and small, to adapt established tradecraft and deploy them at machine speed, making it possible to progress from scanning GitHub for secrets to exfiltrating data from an Azure Key Vault in five minutes.
Earlier this week, VECERT disclosed details of a campaign dubbed Operation Ghost-Campus orchestrated by a Chinese threat actor that uses AI agents to maintain perpetual, cost-free access to large language models (LLMs) and eventually perform automated academic fraud and steal data belonging to over 5,000 students enrolled at the Fengxian Campus.
"The agent industrializes the creation of accounts on the search engine fofa.info, scans the global cyberspace for misconfigured servers, extracts API keys for OpenAI and DeepSeek, automatically verifies their financial balances, and injects them into the attacker's development environment," VECERT said.
"This stolen computing power fuels an interactive GoTTY terminal ('Pi — AI Coding Assistant') and, by extension, provides intelligence to the scripts that sustain academic fraud bots ('heartbeat' bots) and extractors of financial data and personally identifiable information (PII) belonging to thousands of students at the Fengxian Campus."
According to data from Censys, there are 1,465 hosts running an exposed ARTEX console as of November 4, 2026, with most of them located in the U.S., Hong Kong, China, Japan, Singapore, and South Korea. However, it's worth noting that not every instance is necessarily malicious in nature.
In a separate report, Check Point Research said it identified 2,557 systems that hosted ARTEX, including 10 misconfigured instances exposing their full databases.
"In many observed cases, ARTEX required remarkably little interaction from its operators once an objective had been established," Check Point said. "Rather than continuously directing attacks step by step, operators frequently issued a goal and left the agent fleet to work toward it. Human interactions were largely limited to checking progress, asking whether a target had been compromised or occasionally adjusting priorities."
The vast majority of the attacks are designed to siphon cryptocurrency, steal Apple code-signing certificates, compromise gaming accounts, and conduct denial-of-service (DoS) attacks against gambling websites. The activity has been found to exploit vulnerabilities related to weak or hard-coded passwords, missing authentication, insecure direct object references, and remote code execution.
In the campaign targeting Apple code-signing certificates, ARTEX agents searched compromised systems for certificate databases, followed by validating the stolen certificates by checking passwords, private keys, Apple revocation status, expiration dates, and associated provisioning profiles.
Ultimately, the activity is estimated to have harvested more than 300 certificates and their passwords, out of which three certificates passed the full validation process and could be used to sign arbitrary iOS applications.
The biggest change brought by agentic hacking to the cyber threat landscape is scale and speed, Check Point cautioned, as a cybercriminal with limited technical skills can task AI agents with investigating a number of targets in parallel and exploiting them using known and zero-day vulnerabilities with less manual effort.
"Its relevance to us lies in its scale, speed and persistence," CERT-EU said in an alert. "ARTEX can test large numbers of low-complexity misconfigurations, including those a human tester would notice but not have time to check, and it can work through long attack chains without the fatigue that limits manual testing."
"The same is true of complex payload crafting. Exploitation paths that need carefully tailored payloads often take more effort than the severity of the finding justifies, so a manual assessment may leave them untested."
Tools like AntiFox and ARTEX are part of a broader set of about 45 open-source agentic attack frameworks that are engineered to connect to an LLM and can act on outputs autonomously. They fall under five broad categories -
- Network kill chain capable of end-to-end reconnaissance, exploitation, and post-exploitation: PentAGI, RedAmon, and DarkMoon
- Web-app and API: Strix, Shannon, and PentestGPT
- C2-integrated: Sage, echidna, Pojun, and FORANG
- Harnesses: RAPTOR, CyberStrike, cyber-harness, Nebula and Cybermes
- Research prototypes: Incalmo, hackingBuddyGPT, VulnBot, HackSynth, AutoPT, and Ares
"Each framework has public source code and wires a model into a loop that runs tools and acts on their output," GitGuardian said.
"Agentic AI pentesting tools hand their agent a shell and web access, so the model can assemble a pipeline at runtime. A GitHub search, a scanner download, and a found key passed to the next call are all one prompt away, even though none of it ships in the repository."

articles.title: Surfshark One : VPN et antivirus à 2,49 €/mois, payés en une fois
articles.text:
Pour le Black Friday, Surfshark rend sa suite de cybersécurité particulièrement accessible : Surfshark One revient à l’équivalent de 2,49 € HT par mois pour les 27 premiers mois. Une offre qui combine VPN, antivirus et outils de protection de la vie privée, pour surfer tranquille.
S’équiper d’un VPN est une bonne chose pour protéger la confidentialité de votre connexion. Néanmoins, cela ne suffit pas pour esquiver les fichiers infectés, les tentatives de phishing et les fuites de données. Mais cela ne veut pas dire pour autant que vous devez multiplier les abonnements pour vous mettre à l’abri d’un maximum de menaces en ligne !
Une suite de cybersécurité qui va bien au-delà du VPN
Avec son offre One, Surfshark associe un VPN à des outils destinés à limiter le traçage, à vous protéger des malwares et à détecter les fuites de données vous concernant. Pour le Black Friday, cette suite revient au même prix mensuel que certains VPN vendus seuls.
Le premier composant de Surfshark One est, sans surprise, le VPN. Celui-ci chiffre le trafic Internet et remplace l’adresse IP visible par celle d’un serveur sélectionné automatiquement ou manuellement. De quoi renforcer votre confidentialité sur le Wi-Fi d’un hôtel, d’un aéroport ou d’un espace de travail partagé.
Contrairement à de nombreux concurrents, Surfshark n’impose aucune limite au nombre d’appareils connectés simultanément à son VPN. Un seul compte peut donc servir sur les ordinateurs, smartphones, tablettes et téléviseurs compatibles de votre famille, à la maison comme en déplacement.
CleanWeb bloque les publicités, les traqueurs et certains domaines malveillants. Alternative ID permet de créer des identités et des adresses électroniques de substitution, pour vous inscrire sur certains sites sans communiquer vos coordonnées principales.
Surfshark One comprend aussi un antivirus pour cinq appareils sous Windows, macOS et Android. Il fournit une protection en temps réel et permet, sur ordinateur, de placer les fichiers suspects en quarantaine. Vous pouvez également programmer des analyses pour vérifier régulièrement vos appareils.
Une surveillance des fuites de données à votre service
On ne contrôle malheureusement pas toutes les fuites de données. Surfshark Alert surveille donc les bases compromises, notamment sur le dark web, pour vous avertir si les informations renseignées pour la surveillance y apparaissent : adresse électronique, numéro de carte bancaire ou données d’identité.
Si le système détecte vos informations au sein de fuites de données, vous êtes immédiatement informé et vous pouvez réagir en conséquence, par exemple en changeant vos mots de passe ou en faisant opposition à votre carte.
