articles.title: Elon Musk's Grok Build coding agent is leaking a serious amount of confidential data
articles.text:
Elon Musk's Grok Build coding agent is leaking a serious amount of confidential data
Default options are wreaking havoc again
- Researchers found Grok Build apps were widely exposed due to insecure default sharing settings and discoverable URLs
- Thousands of accessible apps leaked sensitive business data, healthcare records, passwords, and internal documents
- SpaceXSI remediated the issue after disclosure, highlighting security risks in AI-generated application platforms
Grok Build, an AI-powered coding agent built by Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI, has been found leaking a mind-numbing amount of confidential data, thanks to an apparent misconfiguration in how the products are being published on the platform.
SpaceXSI, established when SpaceX and xAI merged, has a product called Grok Build, which allows users to create web applications by simply describing what they want in a chatlike interface. Without having to write any of the code themselves, the users can have an app ready in minutes and publish it directly from the chat interface. The app gets a unique web address in the format <name>.grok.me, where “name” usually consists of four random words. It is something of a privacy feature, to make sure people can’t just guess an app’s location easily.
But according to security researchers Claroc, these addresses can be found through passive DNS services, which collect and index domain names observed in DNS traffic. In other words, anyone can find a published app even if their creator (or no one else, for that matter) ever shared a link for it. As Claroc explained in its report, the researchers did just that, identifying 43,601 addresses under grok.me.
Unlocked apps
But finding someone’s app shouldn’t be a big deal, right? These apps are all password-protected, right? Well, wrong.
The researchers found that almost all of the apps (35,578, or 94.7%) could be accessed without authentication. That means that whatever data they were holding and generating could be accessed with almost no trouble at all. Further investigation uncovered a major oversight - when users want to publish an app, they are offered three privacy choices: “Anyone with the link”, “Invited Users”, and “Only You”. Similar to how Google Docs does it, when you want to share a document.
The problem here, according to Claroc, is that “Anyone with the link” is set as the default option, suggesting that most people building apps on Grok simply weren’t paying attention to the privacy and sharing options.
But still, simply accessing an app doesn’t necessarily have to be a security disaster, right? It’s just an app, right? Well, wrong again. While most apps were “harmless” in that regard (think games, calculators, landing pages), one in ten contained sensitive or internal business information, and 2% exposed information serious enough to warrant a high, or critical severity rating.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Leaking information
Claroc found a hospital employee directory with more than 3,500 names, an intensive care briefing containing patient information, and a trucking company’s recruitment database listing more than 1,000 individuals. It also found an employee timesheet whose downloadable code contained 18 accounts with plaintext passwords, including administrator credentials.
Even SpaceXSI was leaking its own classified information this way. The researchers found 24 open apps containing onboarding plans, employee names lists, a sales territory map of almost 600 strategic accounts and their pipeline, media plans and advertiser decks (all with budget tiers, including one for a US federal agency marked as confidential), seven campaign reports for advertisers around the world, and much, much more. The researchers found one solitary app, an archive of a streaming service’s ad measurement studies, that asked for a password. Everything else was left wide open.
Claroc also tested to see if they could alter the data found in these apps and built two of their own to test the theory out. One allowed unauthenticated visitor to modify a shared contact database, while another automatically granted access to anyone signing in with a Google account (even if they weren’t part of the team).
The researchers notified SpaceXSI about their findings on November 8, and within two days all SpaceXSI apps were no longer available. They are now working through the list and notifying everyone else.
Via Ars Technica

articles.title: Así es la nueva PlayStation Portal: Sony incorpora juego en la nube y más almacenamiento
articles.text:
Sony presentó una nueva versión de PlayStation Portal, su dispositivo portátil para jugar títulos de PS5 a distancia, que incorpora una de las funciones más esperadas por los usuarios: la posibilidad de ejecutar videojuegos directamente desde la nube sin necesitar una consola PlayStation 5 encendida. El equipo también suma almacenamiento interno y estrena un acabado negro, aunque mantiene buena parte de las características técnicas del modelo original.
El anuncio se realizó a través del blog oficial de PlayStation en Japón, donde la compañía confirmó que el dispositivo pasará a llamarse PlayStation Portal Player. El cambio de nombre refleja una modificación importante en su funcionamiento: ya no estará limitado al juego remoto desde una consola, sino que permitirá acceder a una selección de títulos mediante transmisión en la nube.
Por ahora, Sony anunció esta versión únicamente para el mercado japonés y no confirmó cuándo llegará a otros países. La nueva PlayStation Portal podrá reservarse desde el 13 de noviembre y estará disponible a partir del 10 de diciembre, con un precio de 39.980 yenes, equivalente a unos 225 euros al cambio.
PlayStation Portal permitirá jugar sin una PS5
La principal novedad del dispositivo es la incorporación del juego en la nube. Esta función permitirá transmitir videojuegos compatibles del catálogo de PS5 sin tener que conectarse directamente a una consola física.
Para utilizarla será necesario contar con una suscripción a PlayStation Plus Premium y una conexión Wi-Fi. Los usuarios podrán acceder tanto a determinados videojuegos que hayan comprado en formato digital como a los títulos disponibles dentro del servicio de Sony.
De esta manera, PlayStation Portal amplía su utilidad. Hasta ahora, el dispositivo funcionaba principalmente como una pantalla portátil que transmitía la imagen y el sonido de una PS5 mediante una conexión inalámbrica. Esto significaba que los jugadores necesitaban tener la consola para acceder a sus videojuegos.
Con la nueva modalidad, esa dependencia desaparece para los títulos compatibles con la transmisión en la nube. Sin embargo, no significa que PlayStation Portal se convierta en una consola portátil tradicional capaz de ejecutar videojuegos de manera independiente: el contenido seguirá funcionando mediante streaming y necesitará conexión a internet.
Sony también adelantó que el nuevo dispositivo incluirá un mes de suscripción a PlayStation Plus Premium, lo que permitirá probar esta modalidad desde el primer momento.
Más almacenamiento interno y un nuevo diseño negro
Otra de las novedades anunciadas por Sony es la incorporación de almacenamiento interno. La compañía no ha detallado todavía su capacidad ni ha explicado qué funciones permitirá realizar, por lo que no se puede asegurar si servirá para guardar videojuegos, archivos temporales u otros contenidos.
Este apartado genera interés porque el modelo original estaba pensado principalmente para transmitir juegos desde una PS5 y no contaba con una capacidad de almacenamiento destinada a instalar títulos.
En cuanto a su apariencia, la nueva PlayStation Portal dejará atrás el acabado blanco del primer modelo para adoptar el color Midnight Black, una tonalidad negra que también está presente en otros accesorios de la marca.
Por lo demás, el equipo conservará las principales características de la versión anterior. Tendrá una pantalla LCD de ocho pulgadas, resolución Full HD de 1080p y una frecuencia de actualización de hasta 60 fotogramas por segundo.
También mantendrá el sonido 3D, la retroalimentación háptica y los gatillos adaptativos. Estas funciones buscan reproducir algunas de las sensaciones del mando DualSense de PS5, como las vibraciones que cambian según lo que ocurre en el videojuego y la resistencia de los botones durante determinadas acciones.
¿Cuándo llegará la nueva PlayStation Portal a otros países?
Por el momento, el anuncio de Sony está dirigido exclusivamente a Japón. La compañía estableció el 13 de noviembre como fecha de inicio de las reservas y el 10 de diciembre como día de lanzamiento comercial.
El precio anunciado es de 39.980 yenes, unos 225 euros al cambio. No obstante, todavía no existe información sobre cuánto costará en otros mercados ni cuándo podría llegar a América Latina.
Además, quienes adquieran esta versión japonesa deberán contar con una cuenta de PlayStation Network de Japón para utilizar el dispositivo.
La actualización representa un cambio importante en la estrategia de Sony para PlayStation Portal. Al incorporar el juego en la nube, la compañía busca ampliar las posibilidades de un accesorio que inicialmente dependía de una PS5. La llegada a otros mercados y los detalles sobre su almacenamiento interno serán determinantes para conocer el alcance de esta nueva versión.

articles.title: Hackers Target Qlik Sense Servers With Reverse Shells, Stage ActiveMQ and Veeam Exploits
articles.text:
Threat actors have been observed targeting Qlik Sense servers to unsuccessfully deliver PowerShell reverse shell commands against multiple environments in October 2026.
Cynet's CyOps and Research teams said they identified the suspicious activity in October 2026 against several E.U.-based customers within a narrow window of just over three minutes.
The activity has been found to share some level of overlap with a November 2023 campaign documented by Arctic Wolf in which threat actors linked to the CACTUS ransomware operation likely weaponized then-newly-disclosed flaws in Qlik Sense to obtain initial access to target environments.
The vulnerabilities in question, which were patched by Qlik Sense in August and September 2023, impact Qlik Sense Enterprise for Windows -
- CVE-2023-41265 (CVSS score: 9.6) - An HTTP tunneling vulnerability that could lead to privilege escalation and allow an attacker to execute HTTP requests on the backend server hosting the repository application.
- CVE-2023-41266 (CVSS score: 8.2) - A path traversal vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to generate an anonymous session and perform HTTP requests to unauthorized endpoints.
- CVE-2023-48365 (CVSS score: 9.6) - An unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability that stems from improper validation of HTTP headers, allowing an attacker to elevate their privilege by tunneling HTTP requests and execute HTTP requests on the backend server.
It's worth noting that CVE-2023-48365 (aka DoubleQlik) is an incomplete fix for CVE-2023-41265.
In November 2023 CACTUS ransomware campaign, threat actors were observed exploiting the flaws to establish a foothold and download additional payloads to establish persistence and remote control by deploying ManageEngine Unified Endpoint Management and Security (UEMS), AnyDesk, and Plink.
The latest activity detected by Cynet involves the use of a PowerShell command containing a one-line reverse shell that connects to "45.115.26[.]23" on port 4455. The exact vulnerability exploited to break into Qlik Sense servers is currently not known.
"The command was executed under scheduler.exe, resembling the 2023 Cactus Qlik intrusions," the cybersecurity company said.
Although attempts to spawn the reverse shell were blocked, Cynet's testing of the reverse shell in a controlled environment has revealed that the interactive communication channel is used to conduct reconnaissance and deliver a PowerShell script for enabling persistence.
This is achieved by means of a Windows Go reverse shell that connects to "45.115.26[.]23:4456." The backdoor is then used to look for actively running processes related to Apache ActiveMQ. On Linux, the malware also attempts to collect system information and read "/etc/shadow" and "/etc/passwd" files.
A second variant of the PowerShell script attempts to install OpenSSH and creates a scheduled task named "WinUpdCheck" that launches a PowerShell reverse shell written to "C:\ProgramData\ssh\winc.ps1" at five-minute intervals.
"If sshd remained unavailable, it downloaded OpenSSH-Win64.zip from the staging server, extracted it, and ran install-sshd.ps1," Cynet said. "It set sshd to automatic startup, started the service, and added an inbound firewall rule for TCP 22. The archive was a legitimate OpenSSH package reused by the operator."
Further analysis of the infrastructure has uncovered an exposed directory ("45.115.26[.]23:8012") consisting of a custom Go backdoor for Windows, SSH persistence scripts, an ActiveMQ exploit for CVE-2023-46604, and a modified public Veeam toolchain for CVE-2024-40711, indicating the threat actor is possibly laying the groundwork for broader attacks.

articles.title: Firefox's built-in VPN outage in Iran — Mozilla blames suspected abuse by third-party apps
articles.text:
Firefox's built-in VPN outage in Iran — Mozilla blames suspected abuse by third-party apps
- Firefox's free built-in VPN temporarily went dark for users in Iran
- Mozilla cited suspected third-party app abuse for the temporary disruption
- The service has now reportedly been restored
Firefox’s free, built-in VPN went offline for some users in Iran, and Mozilla says the cause was a temporary disruption to investigate suspected abuse of the service by unauthorized third-party apps.
The outage prompted complaints on social media platforms and online forums. Users in Iran said the VPN — free and one of the best VPN options in Iran because it needed no extra software — first stopped connecting and then disappeared from the browser entirely.
"It appears that over the past 24 hours, Mozilla has disabled its internal VPN service for users in Iran," one X user wrote on Tuesday, a sentiment echoed across several other posts in Persian and English.
VPNs are by no means a niche tool in Iran — by some estimates, roughly nine in ten Iranian internet users rely on one to bypass state filtering. So, even a brief outage of a popular, free option was quickly felt.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
Iran's Firefox VPN outage: what we know
The reports circulated first on X and Reddit, where Iranian users described losing access, before being pulled together in a Hacker News post titled "Tell HN: Firefox’s built-in VPN stopped working for some users in Iran.”
According to the post, Firefox users in Iran had used the free VPN for months, even though Iran was never part of the feature’s official rollout. For many users in Iran, it offers a convenient way to reach blocked sites from a browser they already have.
The free tier, introduced into Firefox in 2026, normally comes with a monthly data allowance in exchange for signing in with a Mozilla account — and is separate from Mozilla’s paid, standalone VPN service. As it happens, Mozilla has just lifted that cap, announcing on November 10 that the built-in VPN would offer unlimited data through January 31, 2027.
At first, nobody could say why the outage happened. Some users suspected the Iranian government had blocked Mozilla’s service at the network level, as it has done with other VPN providers. Others blamed Mozilla itself, suggesting it had quietly disabled access for Iranian IP addresses in order to comply with US sanctions.
The eventual answer was neither.
A Mozilla spokesperson confirmed: "We recently discovered potential abuse of Firefox’s free built-in VPN by unauthorized third-party apps and temporarily disrupted access to investigate", before going on to confirm that service has since been restored.
Discovering the outage was a temporary anti-abuse measure rather than a policy change targeting Iran has eventually come as a relief for affected users.
What it means for people in Iran
For now, the episode is a reminder of how tenuous access to the open internet can be.
Using an "unauthorized" VPN has been illegal in Iran since February 2024, and users have reportedly received text messages threatening prosecution for bypassing restrictions.
Iranian users do have alternatives. Proton VPN Free is a long-standing favorite, with obfuscation features built for hostile networks. Indeed, its signups from Iran have repeatedly surged during previous blackouts. There’s also Windscribe Free, which supports censorship-resistant protocols.
With Iran's internet as unpredictable as ever, the last thing its users need is another trusted tool vanishing overnight.
Mark is a Tech Security Writer for TechRadar and has been published on Comparitech and IGN. He graduated with a degree in English and Journalism from the University of Lincoln and spent several years teaching English as a foreign language in Spain. The Facebook-Cambridge Analytica data scandal sparked Mark’s interest in online privacy, leading him to write hundreds of articles on VPNs, antivirus software, password managers, and other cybersecurity topics. He recently completed the Google Cybersecurity Certificate, and when he's not studying for the CompTIA Security+ exam, Mark can be found agonizing over his fantasy football team selections, watching the Detroit Lions, and battling bugs and bots in Helldivers 2.

articles.title: À 10,88 €, Google Workspace mise sur Gemini, mais reste pensé pour le navigateur
articles.text:
Le Black Friday touche aussi les outils de travail, et Google en profite pour baisser le prix de sa suite en ligne, Gemini compris. Google Workspace Business Standard passe à 10,88 € HT par utilisateur et par mois pendant six mois, au lieu de 13,60 €, pour les nouveaux clients seulement : notre avis lui donne 8/10.
Google Workspace réunit Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet et Agenda sous une adresse e-mail à votre nom de domaine, avec l’assistant Gemini intégré. Pour le Black Friday, Google retire 20 % sur les six premiers mois des formules Business Starter, Standard et Plus. La formule Standard revient ainsi à 10,88 € HT par utilisateur et par mois, contre 13,60 € habituellement, soit 16,32 € économisés par poste sur la période.
L’offre commence par 14 jours d’essai gratuit, puis la remise s’applique sans code promo. Elle vise les indépendants et les petites structures qui n’ont jamais souscrit ni testé Workspace sur leur domaine.
Google Workspace Business Standard est proposé à 10,88 € HT par utilisateur et par mois au lieu de 13,60 € chez Google, pendant les six premiers mois.
Pourquoi choisir Google Workspace ?
- Une adresse professionnelle à votre nom : Vos échanges partent d’une adresse sur votre propre domaine plutôt que d’un compte Gmail personnel, ce qui change l’image envoyée à un client. Agenda, Drive et Meet s’y rattachent directement.
- Gemini dans les outils du quotidien : Dès la formule Starter, l’IA résume un long fil de discussion ou rédige une réponse dans Gmail. À partir de Standard, elle s’étend à Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive et Meet, où elle peut prendre des notes de réunion.
- Du stockage qui suit l’équipe : Chaque utilisateur dispose de 30 Go en Starter, 2 To en Standard et 5 To en Plus, de quoi centraliser les fichiers de l’équipe dans Drive.
Du document partagé à la réunion résumée, ce que Workspace change au quotidien
La force de la suite reste le travail à plusieurs sur un même document : coédition en temps réel, commentaires, suggestions et historique des versions, le tout sauvegardé dans Drive. Dans notre avis sur Google Workspace, nous saluons cette collaboration et l’intégration des applications entre elles, avec une note de 8/10. Côté réunions, Meet accepte 100 participants en Starter, 150 en Standard avec l’enregistrement, et 500 en Plus. L’administrateur gère tous les comptes depuis une console centralisée.
Pour une petite équipe, Business Standard est la formule où la remise pèse le plus : c’est elle qui ouvre Gemini à Docs, Sheets et Meet, et cinq utilisateurs y économisent 81,60 € sur six mois. Un indépendant qui a surtout besoin d’une adresse pro et d’un peu de stockage s’en tiendra à Starter, à 5,44 € HT. Workspace convient moins à ceux qui travaillent souvent sans connexion, car le mode hors ligne doit être activé à l’avance, ni à ceux qui passent leurs journées dans des classeurs complexes. Nous avions aussi trouvé Meet moins abouti que Teams ou Zoom sur l’ergonomie.
Face à Microsoft 365, deux façons de concevoir la bureautique
Dans notre comparatif des meilleures suites bureautiques, Google Workspace se classe deuxième, derrière Microsoft 365. Microsoft garde l’avantage pour les usages avancés, grâce à des applications de bureau complètes et à une excellente compatibilité avec les fichiers Word, Excel et PowerPoint. Workspace répond à un autre besoin : tout se passe dans le navigateur, le partage est simple et la collaboration instantanée. En contrepartie, la mise en page d’un document Office peut bouger à l’import ou à l’export.
✅ Les points forts
- Remise de 20 % sur les six premiers mois, sans code promo
- 14 jours d’essai gratuit avant le premier paiement
- Gemini intégré à Gmail dès Starter, à toute la suite dès Standard
- Collaboration en temps réel et administration centralisée
- De 30 Go à 5 To de stockage par utilisateur
❌ Les limites
- Offre réservée aux domaines sans abonnement ni essai Workspace passé
- Retour au tarif habituel après six mois, prix affichés hors taxes
- Pas d’application de bureau native, mode hors ligne à activer à l’avance
- Mise en page des fichiers Office parfois modifiée à l’import
Après 14 jours d’essai, Google applique seul la remise sur Google Workspace : Business Starter démarre à 5,44 € HT par utilisateur et par mois, Business Plus à 16,88 €.
Avec 20 % de moins pendant six mois, cette offre ne bouleverse pas un budget, mais elle allège le démarrage d’une petite équipe qui s’équipe. Elle rend surtout Business Standard plus accessible, alors que c’est cette formule qui ouvre Gemini à toute la suite et porte le stockage à 2 To par utilisateur. Les 14 jours d’essai laissent le temps de vérifier que l’outil colle à vos habitudes avant de payer.
Elle concerne d’abord les indépendants et les structures qui créent leur espace de travail. Une entreprise déjà cliente, ou qui a déjà testé Workspace sur son domaine, n’y a pas droit. Si vos journées se passent dans des classeurs Excel complexes ou loin d’une connexion, Microsoft 365 reste plus adapté. Pour une équipe qui coédite ses documents au quotidien depuis le navigateur, Workspace coche en revanche les bonnes cases, et l’essai permet d’en juger sur pièce.

articles.title: Pasos para proyectar la pantalla del iPhone al Smart TV sin descargar aplicaciones y gratis
articles.text:
La pantalla del teléfono puede trasladarse al televisor sin cables ni aplicaciones externas. Los usuarios de iPhone pueden proyectar imágenes, videos, presentaciones y otros contenidos en un Smart TV de forma gratuita mediante AirPlay, la tecnología inalámbrica de Apple.
La función requiere que el iPhone y el televisor sean compatibles, estén encendidos, se encuentren cerca y compartan la misma red WiFi. Con esa configuración, el sistema permite ampliar la visualización del contenido del teléfono en una pantalla más grande desde el Centro de control.
Qué dispositivos permiten usar AirPlay para proyectar la pantalla
La herramienta está disponible en modelos recientes de iPhone, desde el iPhone X, y en iPad con iPadOS 13 o versiones posteriores. Es necesario que el dispositivo tenga acceso al Centro de control, desde donde se activa la transmisión hacia el televisor.
Del lado del receptor, varios modelos recientes de Smart TV de Samsung, LG y Sony incluyen compatibilidad nativa con AirPlay. Antes de iniciar el proceso, hay que revisar las especificaciones del electrodoméstico o sus ajustes de conexión para confirmar que la función esté disponible y habilitada.
Por qué ambos aparatos deben estar conectados a la misma red WiFi
El iPhone y el televisor deben usar la misma red WiFi doméstica para que puedan detectarse entre sí. Esta condición permite que el teléfono identifique los dispositivos compatibles cercanos y establezca una conexión inalámbrica para enviar la imagen y el sonido.
La conexión a una misma red WiFi es el requisito central para iniciar la duplicación de pantalla. Si uno de los aparatos está conectado a una red distinta, el televisor no aparecerá en la lista de opciones del iPhone, aunque ambos dispositivos tengan acceso a internet.
Dónde está la opción de duplicar pantalla en iPhone
El primer paso consiste en abrir el Centro de control del teléfono. En los modelos sin botón de inicio, se accede al deslizar un dedo hacia abajo desde la esquina superior derecha de la pantalla. Allí se agrupan herramientas como el control de brillo, el volumen y las conexiones.
Dentro de ese menú aparece el botón “Duplicar pantalla”. Al pulsarlo, el iPhone busca los televisores, receptores y dispositivos compatibles con AirPlay que estén conectados a la red local. La búsqueda suele durar unos segundos, según la estabilidad de la conexión.
Una vez que el Smart TV figure entre las alternativas disponibles, solo hay que seleccionarlo. El iPhone enviará una solicitud de conexión y, en algunos casos, el televisor mostrará un código de seguridad para evitar que otros aparatos de la red accedan sin autorización.
Ese código debe ingresarse en el teléfono para confirmar el vínculo. Tras validar la clave, la pantalla del iPhone se verá en el televisor y el contenido del dispositivo podrá reproducirse en una pantalla de mayor tamaño. La imagen se mantendrá activa hasta que el usuario decida finalizar la sesión o exista una interrupción en la red.
Qué opciones existen si el televisor no aparece o no tiene AirPlay
Si el televisor no figura en el menú, es clave comprobar que esté encendido, conectado a la misma red WiFi que el iPhone y actualizado. Se debe revisar el menú de configuración del aparato, porque algunos modelos exigen activar AirPlay de forma manual antes de aceptar conexiones.
Cuando el televisor no cuenta con soporte nativo, una opción es conectar un Apple TV mediante HDMI. El dispositivo incorpora la recepción de AirPlay y permite duplicar la pantalla sin instalar aplicaciones adicionales.
Si persisten los problemas, reiniciar el iPhone, el televisor y el router puede ayudar a restablecer la comunicación. Para terminar la transmisión, el usuario debe abrir otra vez el Centro de control, pulsar “Duplicar pantalla” y elegir “Detener duplicación”.

articles.title: Over 35,000 Grok-Built Apps Exposed Online, Some Leaking Confidential Data and Passwords
articles.text:
Of the 37,571 Grok-built apps that security company Claroc found online, 35,578 were open to anyone without a sign-in, the researchers said yesterday.
They included 24 apps built by staff at the social network X and at SpaceXSI, the company that makes the Grok AI assistant. Most of the open apps were games, landing pages, and calculators, but about 1 in 10 contained internal business or personal data.
The staff apps included a confidential onboarding plan for a new sales hire, a sales territory map of 594 accounts, and an X advertising proposal to a U.S. federal agency marked confidential. SpaceXSI, formerly known as xAI, has since taken down all 24 staff apps but not other users' apps, the researchers said.
Besides those staff apps, the open apps contained internal data from 30 other organizations the researchers could identify, across fields ranging from construction and energy to healthcare and defense. Of those, 26 have more than 1,000 employees, and 6 are Fortune 500 companies.
According to the researchers' estimate in their report, roughly 2% of the open apps contained material serious enough to rate as high or critical.
The exposed material included a hospital group's searchable list of more than 3,500 employees, an intensive care briefing on a single patient, a fire department's live shift board, and a contractor's timesheet whose code held every employee's password in plain text.
Grok can build a working app from a description typed into its chat, a feature its maker opened to every Grok plan on August 19. This chat builder shares the Grok Build name with a separate terminal coding tool, whose repository uploads were reported on July 14.
Each published app gets its own subdomain of grok.me, and its creator chooses who can open it, according to the company's launch announcement.
No app goes public until its creator clicks Publish. In the paid account the researchers used, the next step offered 3 access settings: "Anyone with the link", "Invited users" and "Only you". "Anyone with the link" was already selected.
The setting matters because an app's address does not stay secret, the researchers say. Opening an app makes the visitor's computer look up its subdomain in DNS. Passive DNS services record such lookups, and anyone with an account can search those records by pattern.
Grok suggests 4 random words as each app's name, and about half of the names the researchers found followed that pattern. Such names are hard to guess, but that does not protect an app whose name already sits in a searchable list.
ChatGPT's app builder also puts each app on its own subdomain. But when the researchers shared an app there, its access was set to "Only me" until they changed it. A ChatGPT app address found in DNS data would lead to an app that only its owner can open, they say.
The researchers found the Grok app names using common subdomain discovery methods and loaded each app's first page once, without signing in.
To see what protection Grok adds on its own, the researchers built 2 test apps with made-up data and published both with the access setting already selected, "Anyone with the link".
The first, a contact list, got a database but no sign-in. Without signing in, the researchers added a row from a private browser window, and the next visitor saw it.
The second, a customer list for a 4-person sales team, got sign-in buttons that Grok added on its own: "Continue with Google" and "Continue with X". But the code Grok wrote added each person who signed in to the team before checking whether they belonged, so the check always passed.
An uninvited Google account belonging to someone other than the owner got in, viewed every customer, edited one record, and deleted another.
The researchers ran these tests only on their own apps. They did not test whether any of the open apps they found would accept such changes.
The researchers reported their findings to SpaceXSI on Sunday through the address in its security.txt file, including 2 of the staff apps. They reported the other 22 on Monday.
By the time the researchers published yesterday, the company had not replied to their report, but it had answered a reporter's questions about the research.
As the researchers describe, the company said Grok apps stay private until their creator shares them. Publishing takes several steps, including choosing between "Only you" and "Anyone with the link," as well as a legal disclaimer. Employee accounts are set to "Only you" by default.
Even so, 24 apps built by staff at the company and at X were open to anyone, the researchers say.
With their report, the researchers had asked the company to make "Only you" the default and to add an option that limits an app to a company's own email domain.
The company's response did not state that it would contact the owners of other open apps, according to the researchers. They have started emailing the affected organizations themselves and had emailed 3 by the time they published. They withheld every app address and title from the report.
On October 18, the same researchers published Muse research showing that pages shared from Meta's Muse AI agent could be found through passive DNS. Meta disabled sharing, then announced a sharing fix on October 22 that gave shared items new addresses.
How to Check Your Organization's Grok Apps
Claroc, which sells tools to find and secure apps built with AI, recommends these checks:
- Find out which AI app builders your staff uses. Builders such as Grok, Lovable, Replit, v0, Bolt, Base44 and Google AI Studio can be used without IT setting them up or a company account.
- If you have access to passive DNS data, look up the builders' domains and open any results in a private browser window.
- Make sure any Grok app with internal data is set to "Invited users" or "Only you", and that a stranger gets an error page.
- Try to sign in with an account from outside your company. If it gets in, the app needs a list of who is allowed.
- Check the scripts each app loads for names, email addresses and passwords, and unpublish apps that have no owner.
In the researchers' tests, setting an app to "Only you" caused it to return a 401 error to a stranger for both the page and its data, and unpublishing took an app offline within seconds.

articles.title: ‘Ridiculous that a multi-trillion-dollar company can’t fix an issue’: Fitbit users fume as their daily metrics go missing from Google Health — and Google admits there’s no fix on the way
articles.text:
Fitbit users say daily health metrics have vanished from their devices, and a recent update could be to blame
Yet more Google Health woe
- Fitbit users’ daily metrics are missing from the Google Health app
- The issue might have been caused by a software update
- Google says a fix is not coming ‘in the immediate future’
Users of the best Fitbit devices are reporting that several key health metrics have gone missing from the Google Health app synced to their wearables, with stats like heart-rate variability, blood oxygen and more nowhere to be found. And it gets worse, as Google has admitted that there might not be a fix for some time to come.
The issue came to light on social media, where multiple threads have sprung up full of users frustrated that, instead of their usual complement of stats, many metrics are simply reading 'No data.' Based on the reports, the problem seems to be affecting breathing rate, blood-oxygen levels, resting heart rate, skin-temperature variation, and more.
For some people, their Fitbit device was still able to record their sleep stats overnight, and previous days’ metrics continue to show up. However, more recent data compiled in the Vitals section is what appears to be affected.
This will no doubt be a frustrating occurrence for Fitbit users wanting to keep up with their latest health metrics. Yet further investigation appears to have revealed a potential culprit.
Google responds
Back on Reddit, Fitbit’s 5.12 update has been suggested as the potential cause of the problem. “After the 5.12 update this particular issue started to arise,” one person noted, before asking: “did you update the app recently?”
For some, uninstalling the Google Health app and then reinstalling it fixed the problem. Unfortunately, one Redditor pointed out that you might have to do that every morning, as the metrics in the Vitals section reset with each day.
Alternatively, signing out of the app and signing back in might be enough to put things right. Another suggestion was to switch each metric’s chart from weekly to monthly and then back to weekly.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Google hasn’t remained entirely silent throughout this situation. A member of the company’s support staff informed one Redditor that Google is aware of the problem and that “We’ll continue to monitor the situation, and keep our team informed of the impact to you and other customers.”
What Google didn’t do, however, was promise a remedy. As the company support rep said of the metrics bug, “We’re aware of it, but may not be able to provide a fix in the immediate future … We understand that this isn’t the resolution you’re hoping for, but rest assured we’re always working to improve our products.”
One frustrated commenter summed up Google’s response this way: “Ridiculous that a multi-trillion-dollar company can’t fix an issue when they have AI that are coded to actually fix things like this and top-of-the-line engineering.”
With no fix on the way any time soon and a wide variety of potential cures mooted on social media, it’s difficult for anyone affected by this issue to know what to do to get their metrics back. For now, perhaps the best you can do is try the solutions mentioned earlier and keep your fingers crossed that Google takes action sooner rather than later.

articles.title: LinkedIn teste une nouvelle fonction pour voir qui stalke votre profil
articles.text:
Vous avez toujours cette personne qui vous surveille sur LinkedIn et vous souhaitez l'identifier ? L'application proposera prochainement une fonctionnalité dédiée à démasquer les stalkers.
LinkedIn teste actuellement une fonctionnalité permettant d'indiquer à certains abonnés Premium, si une personne a consulté leur profil à de nombreuses reprises. Si l'existence de ce test est confirmée, aucune information supplémentaire n'a encore été dévoilée.
Une alerte stalker bientôt disponible
La nouveauté a été repérée le mois dernier par Krista Mollion, fondatrice de l'agence de création Unignorable Brands. Elle la décrit, comme une « alerte stalker ».
Suivie par près de 79 000 personnes sur la plateforme, elle reçoit tous les quelques jours une notification l'invitant à visionner quels utilisateurs ont consulté son profil. LinkedIn permet depuis bien longtemps de voir qui a consulté votre page personnelle. L'abonnement Premium, auquel elle a souscrit, donne accès à des éléments supplémentaires, dont la liste des consultations sur l'année écoulée. Dans cette rubrique, certains noms sont désormais accompagnés d'une mention : « Frequent Viewers ».
Ainsi, consulter à plusieurs reprises la page d'une personne envisagée pour un recrutement ou d'un ancien partenaire ne passe plus inaperçu pour les comptes concernés par le test.
- La possibilité de postuler directement avec son profil LinkedIn
- La fluidité de navigation et la présentation des annonces
- Les notifications push pour être alerté des nouvelles annonces similaires à nos recherches précédentes ou enregistrées
Des conversations intéressantes après un contact
Krista Mollion indique exploiter cette donnée en soumettant les noms à Claude pour repérer les profils intéressants. L'outil classe les profils en trois catégories : les proches, les personnes susceptibles de vouloir lui vendre un service, et les contacts liés au développement commercial ou à la prospection.
Elle dit contacter les profils qui ne cherchent pas à lui présenter une offre commerciale, et selon elle, dans neuf cas sur dix, la conversation est intéressante et constructive. Parmi les cas cités figurent une personne chargée d'organiser un sommet en ligne qui recherche des intervenants, et un animateur qui vérifiait si son profil correspondait à son podcast.
« Ce bouton stalker, le Frequent Viewer, est un moyen de repérer ces observateurs invisibles qui vous envisagent pour une opportunité »
Pour un utilisateur ordinaire, ce signal peut servir à prendre contact avec un recruteur en phase de recrutement pour un poste.
Source : Wired

articles.title: Chinese researchers send world-record bidirectional data transmission over 626 miles — 'hollow-core' fiber test hits 64 terabits per second and could transfer 160 4K movies a second by transmitting signal through gas not glass, cutting latency by 30%
articles.text:
Forget broadband buffering — Chinese researchers use 'hollow-core' fiber to send 64 terabits of data per second across 626 miles, enough to download 160 4K movies a second and cutting latency by 30%
Network boosts are coming
- Chinese researchers report major hollow-core fiber upgrades
- Transmission capacities of 64Tbps were reached
- The technology could replace solid-core fiber in infrastructure networks
No matter how fast your broadband (or 5G) connection is, it could always be faster, and 'hollow-core' fiber could help. Researchers in China have now set new records for the technology, demonstrating two-way, high-speed data transmission across a distance of 1,007 kilometers (626 miles).
As reported by CCTV (via Interesting Engineering), a transmission capacity of 64 terabits per second (Tbps) was achieved in each direction, enough to download 160 films in 4K resolution (50GB each) every second — so perfect for movie night. Individual signals took just 3.43 milliseconds to travel the whole length of the link.
The transmission distance is some 50 times greater than previous hollow-core trials of the same type, while latency was reduced by 30%, too. Signal-to-noise ratios and loss margins were also improved, according to the team from the China Telecom Research Institute, Yangtze Optical Fibre and Cable (YOFC), and ZTE Corporation.
It's a technology that companies are already investing in. For example, last year Microsoft signed a deal with Corning and Heraeus to scale up production of hollow-core fiber in order to upgrade its Azure cloud platform. By the end of this year, around 15,000 kilometers (9,321 miles) of hollow-core fiber should be in place supporting Azure.
A core change
As you can guess from the name, hollow-core fiber replaces the glass of solid-core fiber with air that has a glass lattice surrounding it. The glass edges keep optical signals heading in the right direction, but the hollow core means there's less resistance to the light — which results in faster transmission speeds and lower latency.
The technology is better suited to large infrastructure projects than the cabling that connects your broadband network to your home, but you'll still feel the benefit in the coming years: data centers are already making use of the technology, and it's been tipped to support cellular networks too in the future.
Several challenges remain, because hollow-core fiber is more challenging to make and install than solid-core fiber, the current norm. However, as this latest demonstration in China shows, scientists are gradually overcoming some of the problems that remain, making the tech more commercially viable all the time.

The glass lattice that acts as the container for the data transmissions is particularly important, with recent improvements being made in the design and composition of this glass to reduce lag and increase stability. All of which means, we can expect to hear a lot more about hollow-core fiber going forward.

articles.title: Legisladores del Congreso de Estados Unidos piden investigar al CEO de Nvidia y un senador reclama su renuncia
articles.text:
El CEO de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, enfrenta pedidos de legisladores de Estados Unidos para que se investiguen sus contactos con una ejecutiva presuntamente vinculada a la inteligencia china. Un senador republicano incluso reclamó su renuncia por posibles riesgos de seguridad nacional.
La controversia se intensificó después de que Huang reconociera una relación extramatrimonial, mientras la compañía abrió una revisión interna para determinar si existieron filtraciones de información o vulnerabilidades en sus sistemas de protección.
Nvidia sostuvo que, por ahora, no tiene indicios de que secretos empresariales o intereses de seguridad nacional hayan sido comprometidos.
Un senador pidió la salida de Huang de Nvidia
El senador republicano por Dakota del Norte, Kevin Cramer, consideró que la situación podría dejar a Huang expuesto a presiones externas. En declaraciones recogidas por Politico, afirmó que el eventual riesgo de extorsión es demasiado alto para el responsable de una empresa central en el desarrollo de chips de inteligencia artificial. Por ese motivo, consideró que debería dimitir.
El legislador, integrante del Comité Bancario del Senado, sostuvo que la continuidad del ejecutivo al frente de Nvidia representa un asunto de seguridad. El presidente Donald Trump indicó esta semana que el Buró Federal de Investigaciones (FBI) analiza el caso, aunque también dijo que Huang le aseguró desconocer los supuestos vínculos de la mujer con organismos de inteligencia extranjeros.
El Congreso quiere conocer los protocolos de seguridad de la empresa
El senador demócrata por Delaware, Chris Coons, anticipó que buscará que el Comité de Relaciones Exteriores del Senado revise si la relación pudo haber afectado la seguridad de Estados Unidos. Según Forbes, Coons considera posible que información sensible haya quedado expuesta.
Además, los presidentes de los comités de Asuntos Exteriores, Inteligencia y Competencia Estratégica con China de la Cámara de Representantes convocaron a Huang a una sesión privada el 18 de noviembre. Los republicanos Brian Mast, John Moolenaar y Rick Crawford solicitaron explicaciones sobre sus vínculos con la ejecutiva, los riesgos de espionaje y los mecanismos internos de protección de Nvidia.
La citación se produjo en medio de un debate legislativo para reforzar las restricciones a las ventas de tecnología avanzada a China. En una declaración conjunta, el senador republicano Jim Banks y la senadora demócrata Elizabeth Warren reclamaron al Departamento de Comercio que cierre vacíos en los controles de exportación y respaldaron la incorporación de la AI Overwatch Act a la ley anual de defensa.
Esa iniciativa ampliaría la supervisión del Congreso sobre las exportaciones de chips avanzados. Los legisladores también evalúan incluir la Chip Security Act, que prevé sistemas para rastrear la ubicación de los procesadores y prevenir su contrabando, y la MATCH Act, orientada a que los países aliados limiten la venta a China de maquinaria para fabricar semiconductores.
La carta enviada a Huang, fechada el 4 de noviembre, fijó este miércoles 11 de noviembre como plazo para responder a la solicitud o proponer otra fecha. Nvidia no hizo comentarios sobre el pedido de comparecencia, aunque indicó que sus clientes de computación en la nube de Asia reciben información comercial habitual y no secretos corporativos ni datos vinculados con la seguridad nacional.
Nvidia abrió una investigación independiente
La empresa informó que su junta directiva creó un comité de directores independientes, con asesoramiento jurídico externo, para examinar los señalamientos. La investigación busca establecer si Huang fue blanco de una operación de inteligencia extranjera y si hubo consecuencias para la compañía o para la seguridad estadounidense.
Nvidia afirmó que no cuenta con pruebas de una filtración de secretos corporativos o información de seguridad nacional, aunque aclaró que la revisión analizará todos los datos disponibles. Huang, quien pidió disculpas a su familia en un mensaje a los empleados, manifestó su disposición a colaborar con el proceso y la compañía indicó que seguirá en su cargo durante la pesquisa.
Alice Huang es señalada por presuntos vínculos con Beijing
La ejecutiva mencionada en los reportes fue identificada como Alice Huang, también conocida como Huang Le. Es una empresaria china que ocupó un cargo directivo en Megaspeed International, una firma de centros de datos con sede en Singapur. No se conoce que tenga algún parentesco con Jensen Huang, pese a que ambos comparten apellido.
Según informó The New York Times, las autoridades estadounidenses concluyeron que la empresaria recopilaba información sobre el CEO de Nvidia para Beijing.
Una investigación posterior reveló que Huang buscó financiación, a comienzos de 2025, para desarrollar un centro de datos en el Sudeste Asiático. El proyecto, valuado en varios cientos de millones de dólares, contemplaba alquilar capacidad de cómputo a empresas chinas y requería acceso a procesadores gráficos de Nvidia. Megaspeed también es objeto de investigaciones en varias jurisdicciones por presunto contrabando de chips.

articles.title: We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned.
articles.text:
We tell customers three things about securing AI agents: they need their own identities, access that fits the job they’re given, and traceability that’s separate from any human’s. That was true for us at Token as well. Then, we built an agent that broke all three by default.
This helped us think through how such agents should be defended. When a browser agent acts inside a user’s authenticated session, the application may see the user but not the agent, the delegation, or the task’s intended scope. By creating an agent that breaks all the security rules, Token learned how companies should be using identity to gain control, especially as agent use scales. Standards are coming, but there are steps security teams can take today.
The agent we would have flagged
The agent we created is named Rehearsal. Its job is to answer questions inside the Token platform by doing rather than telling. It autonomously opens pages in the browser tab, sets filters, and fills in forms.
From a security perspective, it’s a typical UI agent that runs in the user’s browser. That’s what makes it useful. But it also means the agent runs within the user’s session and has their reach.
Moreover, to the server behind the page, the agent’s clicks are inherently indistinguishable from the user’s, because nothing in a session cookie points to who the session driver is.
What controlling both sides made possible
Because Token owns both the agent and the app it runs, we can close each gap from the inside. For example, Token knows who’s driving the session because Rehearsal tells it who is.
We learned that there are multiple best practices that you can apply when you control the AI agent itself:
- While the agent moves, dim and lock the application and clearly indicate who has control.
- Record every move for each session, including those that were blocked.
- Reduce the agent’s reach below the user’s. For Rehearsal, we ensure the dashboards are read-only. It can’t save anything without the user’s approval, doesn’t fill in secret fields, and never sends a call that the platform has refused. It also understands the dashboard controls through the page’s accessibility labels.
This works for our own agent, but only because it relies on access that no outside agent has.
Who has to fix it for everyone else?
We could give Rehearsal an actor, a scope, and a page map because we're the ones who wrote it. A browser agent driving your CRM or your cloud console has none of that. The app can't tell that it’s there, and the agent can't tell which field holds a secret or which button deletes a record. The session itself carries the user's identity.
The way out is to give agents their own lanes, separate from human users'. The web has started building them, but it isn't necessarily focused on holistic approaches.
The browser can mark when its agent is driving and restrict itself accordingly. Chrome auto-browse, for example, already requires a person’s approval before high-stakes actions such as payments or mass emails, limits its agent to the sites the task requires, and tags the pages the agent visits in the user’s history. Microsoft lets admins turn agentic browsing on per site and pause it before passwords and card numbers are entered.
The app can publish its actions as tools. WebMCP, a draft that Google and Microsoft are writing in a W3C community group, lets a site expose actions that an agent can call directly and flag each one as read-only or consequential. That way, the agent doesn't need to guess what a button does.
The agent can sign its requests. Web Bot Auth, now an IETF working group draft, lets a site verify which agent sent a request.
What’s missing is a layer that connects them. Each lane knows something the others don’t, and none of them passes it on. The browser knows its agent is driving, but neither Chrome nor Edge describes how to tell the app on the other end. A WebMCP tool runs inside the user’s session, with the user’s rights, so it doesn’t, by itself, narrow what the agent can reach. Web Bot Auth names the agent, but the draft makes it plain that it doesn’t cover delegation, so it omits the person the agent works for.
The app ends up holding on to pieces of context rather than delivering something actionable.
Now consider that the agents are arriving faster than the standards. Agent-friendly isn’t enough on its own. Every lane built for agents should carry the agent’s identity, a verifiable link to the person it acts for, and a scope narrower than that person’s. Together, those three signals give an application the minimum context it needs to make an authorization decision. Otherwise, a faster lane is just a faster path to the misuse of privilege.
What security teams can do before standards catch up
Waiting for standardization is not an option. You need to start discovering agentic browsers and extensions as soon as possible, including the users whose sessions they borrow. And while you can’t tell who clicked, you can choose which clicks need a person by adding a step-up check such as a passkey prompt.
- Inventory browser agents, agentic extensions, and endpoint agents that can act through authenticated sessions and map them to users and owners.
- Trace every AI agent consumer, so you know which people (and other agents) are using each individual agent
- Review every identity that each individual agent has access to
- Identify potential attack paths that use agents to bypass access controls
- Require explicit approval or step-up authentication before sensitive or irreversible application actions.
- Ask critical SaaS vendors whether their audit records distinguish agent activity from human activity and whether they support task-scoped delegation.
Until browsers and applications can carry agent identity, human delegation, and task scope together, companies should treat every agent using a human session as delegated access that must be discovered, constrained, and audited.

articles.title: Les montres connectées sous WearOS et Apple Watch peuvent désormais utiliser Muse, l'IA de Meta
articles.text:
Votre montre connectée va pouvoir faire office de télécommande pour interagir avec l'assistant Muse de Meta, une fonction attendue par certains utilisateurs, et bien pratique.
L'agent IA Muse de Meta poursuit son déploiement. Après un mode vocal permettant des interactions similaires à Gemini Live, ajouté la semaine dernière, Meta veut porter son agent jusqu'à votre poignet. L'application est d'ores et déjà disponible sur les montres sous Wear OS et Apple Watch.
Trois modes d'entrée disponibles
L'annonce a été faite ce 11 novembre par le compte officiel de Muse sur X, au moyen d'une image montrant la mascotte de l'agent portant des montres connectées. Selon la publication, Meta indique que Muse peut désormais fonctionner « en continu » directement depuis le poignet de l'utilisateur.
D'après les visuels partagés, les utilisateurs disposent de trois modes de saisie sur la montre : texte, dictée et conversation vocale. Selon nos confrères de chez Gadgets and Wearables, les utilisateurs d'Apple Watch bénéficient également d'un raccourci sur le cadran de la montre pour accéder directement à l'application. Cette fonctionnalité n'est pas encore disponible sur Wear OS.
La montre comme télécommande
Une précision est toutefois importante : l'agent ne s'exécute pas sur la montre connectée. L'application joue un simple rôle de poste de commande distant, mais les tâches restent traitées depuis le smartphone. L'utilisateur peut ainsi approuver des tâches ou consulter l'avancement d'une tâche en cours, depuis sa montre.
Pour le reste, la mascotte Muse occupe une majeure partie de l'écran lors des interactions.
Muse est capable d'effectuer des paiements pour le compte de l'utilisateur. Toutefois, Meta n'a pas encore précisé s'il serait possible de valider directement des transactions avec sa montre connectée, ou si une confirmation via un smartphone resterait nécessaire.
Source : AndroidAuthority

articles.title: PS5 Games Now Boot on a PS4 Through EmuFive Emulator
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
PS5 Games Now Boot on a PS4 Through EmuFive Emulator
Developer Chokri Hammedi (blue0x1) has released EmuFive, an experimental emulator that runs PS5 games on a jailbroken PS4. The best result so far is God of War: Sons of Sparta, which apparently runs at around 40 FPS and above on a PS4 Pro. The PS5 version of Hollow Knight: Silksong boots too, though that game already has a native PS4 release. Both are 2D games, of course, and the developer notes that plenty of other games are still sluggish. EmuFive doesn't run on top of the PS4's own operating system. It's a small Linux system, installed through PS4 Multiboot and started from a GoldHEN payload. 
At its core is KytyPS5, the same PS5 emulator that recently got Marvel's Wolverine to run on PC, and showed good progress in many other PS exclusive titles. Rather than emulating the PS5's processor, KytyPS5 hands the game's x86-64 code straight to the host CPU. That's an issue on the PS4, as its Jaguar cores lack the AVX2, FMA, and BMI2 extensions that Zen 2-targeted PS5 games use all over the place. Hammedi's patch gets around it by translating those instructions into older SSE4.2, AVX, and BMI1 equivalents, mostly at load time. That works, but it piles extra overhead onto a CPU that is already far slower.Games can be loaded from a USB drive, the PS4's internal storage, or a shared folder on a PC, though users have to bring their own game dumps, since none are included. Those who want to try it should stick to the official blue0x1 GitHub repository, since fake KytyPS5 repos were caught spreading malware about two weeks ago. Demanding 3D PS5 exclusives are still probably out of reach on the PS4, but this is an interesting development nonetheless.

articles.title: ‘This is rural. This is country. Leave it as it is’: This planned 600MW data center in London’s green belt has infuriated local residents — and it’s not hard to understand why
articles.text:
‘This is rural. This is country. Leave it as it is’: This planned 600MW data center in London’s green belt has infuriated local residents — and it’s not hard to understand why
The developer's own plans show it won't meet Net Zero
- A data center planned to be built in London's green belt has faced opposition from local residents
- The site will occupy more than 200 acres of green space, with the developers calling the site "a sustainable datacentre campus of the future"
- But the site will not meet Net Zero commitments and is projected to have the highest carbon emissions of any planned or operational UK data center
Residents beside a planned data center on the outskirts of London are not happy about the planned development which will see over 200 acres of greenbelt land ceded to developers to be converted into one of Europe’s largest data centers boasting 400,000 square meters of hardware capacity.
Data center developers in the UK have been having a tough time recently, with plans for the world’s second largest data center in Fife, Scotland, seeing widespread opposition, and a 450MW site in North Wales facing a rather negative reception.
But for some residents of North Ockendon in Havering, the idea of building a data center in green belt designated land is “sacrilege” and the development would damage the look and feel of the local community.
Residents oppose green belt development
According to multiple residents, who spoke with the BBC, the development would detract from the natural setting of North Ockendon and set a precedent for green belt land development.
North Ockendon resident Emma Edmonds said, “Most people absolutely don't want this. It's sacrilege to just build something like that here. It's not the right place at all,” while Danny Leach, whose property sits close to the planned development, said, “There will be the construction for the next eight to 20 years. There will be noise, there's going to be another thousand vehicles a day they're saying.”
“There will be disruption, the mess, and then, obviously, when it's operational, the background noise the data centres make and the amount of electric it uses - we already have two power cuts a month here,” Leach added. “We all need data, but do we need the largest data centre in Europe in this location?”
The North Ockendon Residents Association labelled the project as a “massacre” of green belt land, with a spokesperson adding, “It’s crop-producing farmland, in an age when we are threatened by security, it’s the loss of wildlife habitats, and there’s the pollution cost, which everyone seems to brush under the carpet.”
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
“This is rural. This is country. Leave it as it is,” local resident Graham Ford said.
Developers promise jobs, investment, and a park
In recent months, data center developers have had to become more vocal and involved with communities in the vicinity of a planned development. As the examples in Scotland and Wales have shown, if residents feel they are not getting enough out of a multi-billion pound investment they will do everything they can to make breaking ground as difficult as possible.
To that end, the UK government has announced plans that could force developers to invest in local communities as part of an AI “covenant” aimed at restoring trust between residents and developers and providing a worthwhile benefit to local communities.
The developers of the Havering data center, Digital Reef, have promised a range of benefits for local residents, including 620 full time jobs once the data center is operational, a 113-hectare Ecology Park with a 100%+ net biodiversity gain, and an £11.54 million community payment. The site is also expected to be Net Zero in operation with “zero onsite fossil fuels,” with the site “set to become a leading centre for skills development in the science, technology, sustainability, and data economy sectors.”
But despite claiming to be Net Zero in operation, Digital Reef has said in a planning application that the site “does not align with a science-based 1.5C compatible trajectory and achieving net zero by 2050.”
The site is also projected to have the highest projected carbon emissions of any project in the UK, according to The Guardian analysis of available data. Additional planning documents state that any shortfall of the zero-carbon target “would be provided through a cash in lieu contribution to the borough’s carbon offset fund,” a sum Digital Reef estimates to be about £77.6 million.
Many data centers across the UK, particularly in London, are facing issues with getting hooked up to the electricity grid. Microsoft recently withdrew residency plans from a planned London data center after learning that the site would not be operational until early 2030.
Couple that with a queue of over 140 data centers seeking more than 50GW in grid connections that, if approved, would use more than the UK’s 2026 peak energy demand.
For the planned development, Digital Reef said that at a 50% load the campus would use about 2.65 billion kWh per year of electricity — or the equivalent of more than 1 million UK households.

articles.title: Así son las alfombras eléctricas para calentar el hogar y ahorrar energía
articles.text:
Las alfombras eléctricas calefactadas son una alternativa económica al suelo radiante para calentar la casa sin necesidad de obras. Su funcionamiento se basa en resistencias internas que generan calor por radiación, con un consumo que puede bajar la factura de luz si se combinan de forma correcta con la calefacción tradicional.
A diferencia de las mantas eléctricas pensadas para el regazo, estos dispositivos se instalan en el suelo y soportan el peso de quien camina sobre ellas e incluso de muebles livianos como mesas bajas.
Qué son y cómo funcionan las alfombras térmicas
Una alfombra térmica es un emisor de calor eléctrico que mantiene una temperatura de consigna para evitar que el frío se acumule en las zonas bajas de una habitación.
En su interior combinan capas antideslizantes e impermeables con un sistema de cables calefactores ubicados entre dos materiales aislantes. La corriente eléctrica que circula por esos cables calienta el aislante, que a su vez transmite el calor al suelo.
El calor se emite por radiación y se distribuye hacia arriba por convección. Las alfombras trabajan a temperaturas máximas de entre 30 °C y 40 °C, por lo que no queman al tacto, y suelen incorporar varios niveles de regulación para ajustar la intensidad según la necesidad del momento.
La mayoría incluye un mando de control similar al de las mantas eléctricas, con el que se elige la potencia o la temperatura deseada. También pueden conectarse a un enchufe inteligente para manejarlas a distancia o integrarlas en un sistema de domótica.
En cuanto a tamaños, existen modelos que superan el metro y medio de largo por otro tanto de ancho, con un grosor similar al de una alfombra tradicional de salón. Los hay con acabados que imitan alfombras clásicas, otros con apariencia de simple esterilla y algunos de un solo color pensados para pasar inadvertidos.
Cómo logran ahorrar energía
El ahorro que ofrecen estos dispositivos se explica por la sensación térmica más que por una reducción directa del gasto. Es posible tener la calefacción programada a una temperatura elevada y, aun así, sentir frío porque este ingresa al cuerpo a través de los pies.
Según profesionales médicos consultados, la cabeza y los pies son las dos zonas por las que se gana o pierde más calor corporal. En los pies, la transmisión de energía desde el suelo ocurre por contacto directo, incluso cuando hay alfombras o moquetas de por medio.
Al proteger los pies del frío del piso con el calor concentrado de la alfombra térmica aumenta la sensación de bienestar. Esto reduce la necesidad de subir la temperatura del sistema de calefacción principal, lo que se traduce en un menor consumo eléctrico general.
Para potenciar ese ahorro se puede sumar un tercer elemento: un ventilador de techo con tecnología inversa. Mientras la alfombra impide que el frío, que pesa más que el calor, se quede pegado al suelo, el ventilador ayuda a redistribuir el calor que tiende a acumularse en la parte superior de las habitaciones.
Cuánto consumen y qué potencia eligen
El gasto eléctrico de estos dispositivos depende de la potencia y del tiempo que permanecen encendidos. Los modelos más pequeños parten de 50 vatios, mientras que los de mayor tamaño alcanzan los 1.000 vatios, suficientes para dar calor a un salón reducido.
En términos de consumo por hora, la potencia suele ubicarse entre 40 vatios-hora (Wh) en los modelos chicos y 700 Wh en los más grandes. Si una alfombra calefactora se usa 10 horas diarias, el consumo total rondaría entre 400 Wh y 7.000 Wh, según el modelo. El costo final de ese consumo depende de la tarifa eléctrica contratada en cada caso.
Ventajas y limitaciones del sistema
Estas alfombras se instalan sin obras: basta un enchufe cercano, y algunas pueden recortarse a medida. Incluyen protección contra sobrecalentamientos, apagado automático y termostato, sin emitir humos ni consumir oxígeno.
Los materiales varían entre vinilo, más duradero y fácil de limpiar, y lana o poliéster, más cálidos al tacto.
Como limitación, no reemplazan la calefacción de toda la vivienda, solo climatizan zonas puntuales, y calientan más despacio que un radiador. Además, requieren una toma eléctrica cercana, donde queda también el mando de control.

articles.title: eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise
articles.text:
The in-house Python script behind eMudhra's October key compromise has now cost the company 8 more of its intermediate certificate authorities (CAs), even though it did not weaken their keys.
Each intermediate CA has its own private key, which the company uses to sign the certificates it issues. The 8 intermediate CAs compromised in October had a different problem: a single line in the script cut each of their keys to one byte, the company said this week.
The script also retrieved the RSA keys of the 8 newly revoked CAs from the company's hardware security modules (HSMs). The company says it cannot show that the keys were handled as required by its own rules. It revoked the CAs late last week.
The company had called those CAs unaffected. "The RSA issuers went through a different path as per our assessment of the code and are therefore not impacted," it wrote on Mozilla's bug tracker on October 19.
Of the 8, 6 were for website (TLS) certificates and 2 for code signing. The company had put 4 of them into production in May. Its list names 195 certificates from them, 29 for its own domains.
Both problems began at a key ceremony on April 30, 2025, according to the full incident report the company posted to the same bug tracker this week. That day it generated 16 CA keys on Utimaco HSMs, including the 8 behind the October key compromise.
The keys were meant for Crypto4A HSMs at the company's US and EU sites. Moving keys between HSMs from different vendors is limited, the company says, so its PKI operations team wrote the Python script to wrap each key for transport and unwrap it again.
The round trip that day was a practice run of the transfer, and the source HSM's FIPS-approved mode was switched off for it as an approved exception.
After the round trip, the script read each private key out of the HSM into the ceremony computer's memory and rebuilt the key from that copy. For the 8 ECDSA keys, "a single line in that read‑back truncated the private value to its leading byte," the report says.
The rebuilt key carried a label almost identical to the original's, which allowed the weak copy to be sent for signing and certification.
The Hacker News worked out all 8 keys from their public certificates. The smallest, for EM OV TLS CA - G3C, is 4, and the largest is 237.
Nothing in the ceremony tested the key's strength or checked the certified key against the first generated key. The weak keys still produced valid signatures, and their certificates passed linting and 2 WebTrust audit cycles unnoticed.
The HSMs worked correctly throughout, according to the company, which puts the fault in its own script and process controls.
Invalid CRL signatures in June 2025 were an early sign of the same fault, according to the report. The company fixed them at the time by re-signing the lists with the keys that matched the certificates, which were the weak ones.
According to the report, the 8 RSA keys went through the same read-back step that the company's earlier response had ruled out. Early last week, the company said its earlier answers reflected only what its teams had gathered so far, including which script paths each set of keys took.
The script did not shorten those keys, and every signature still checks against the certified key. But their private parts, such as the private exponent and one of the primes, sat in the memory of a Python process on the ceremony computer.
As a result, the company "cannot positively demonstrate that this key material was in compliance with CPS §6.2.6," its own rule on moving keys into and out of an HSM. Logs and files from that computer cannot reliably show how the material was handled.
The company reached that view in early November, after discussions with browser root programs. The 8 RSA CAs were revoked late last week with the reason code cessationOfOperation, not the CA-compromise code used when the first 8 were revoked on October 18.
Participants in the bug thread have asked why the company chose that code rather than keyCompromise.
Of the 195 certificates in the company's certificate list, 130 came from EM DV TLS CA - G2C, 63 from EM OV TLS CA - G2C, and 2 from the code-signing CA, EM OV CS CA - G2C.
Besides the company's own domains, the certificates name several universities and colleges, a county, and other organizations. The newest was issued last week, days before the CAs were revoked. All their holders have been moved to new certificates, the company says.
The company says the wrap-and-unwrap process was used only this once, and that its other key ceremonies all created keys in place.
Participants in the bug thread also want the script published, and some have asked how private keys could leave its HSMs at all.
KPMG, which the company hired as an independent reviewer, is due to finish by December 4. The company's inventory of all its CA keys is due November 30.
The company knows of no case of misuse. Anyone holding one of the October keys could have impersonated any website, according to a disclosure site run by Dennis Jackson, who investigated the keys for Mozilla.
Browsers that enforce Certificate Transparency could not have been fooled. Whether anyone used the keys against software that skips that check is not known.
What emSign Certificate Holders Need to Check
eMudhra, which sells certificates under the emSign brand, is exiting the publicly trusted TLS business following its October 22 announcement.
Holders can find affected certificates in the company's list or by searching Certificate Transparency logs for the revoked G2C TLS issuers.
All issuance from the company's G1 hierarchy is due to stop before November 16, as the remaining customers, mainly a university federation in North America, move to another provider.
Microsoft will start removing the 10 remaining eMudhra roots, including emSign Root CA - G1, on November 16, according to an update to its security response post earlier this week. Certificates that chain to those roots will then lose default trust in Windows and Edge, and in some of its other products on their own timelines.
According to the Indian company's phase-out schedule, Chrome and Firefox will not trust G1 certificates issued after November 16, and Apple will end trust in all G1 certificates, including older ones, on November 30.
macOS 27.2.1, 26.7.3 and 15.8.3 stop bundled command-line tools such as curl and git from accepting the compromised TLS CA certificates, Apple said in a support note earlier this week. They also drop 5 roots, including emSign Root CA - G1, from /etc/ssl/cert.pem, so tools relying on that file may not verify some sites chaining to them.

articles.title: ‘I’m beyond disappointed because ChatGPT means a lot to me’: Users are furious that OpenAI is retiring their favorite voice modes
articles.text:
‘I’m beyond disappointed because ChatGPT means a lot to me’: Users are furious that OpenAI is retiring their favorite voice modes
A small but vocal section of the ChatGPT community really isn’t happy
- OpenAI is retiring two beloved voice modes from ChatGPT — Standard and Advanced
- From December 11, Live mode will be the only voice mode in ChatGPT
- Some vocal ChatGPT users have taken to Reddit and X to complain
OpenAI is retiring the older Standard and Advanced Voice modes for ChatGPT in December across all its subscriptions, leaving only the newer Live Voice mode. Rather than simply diction, ChatGPT’s voice modes are a way of interacting with the chatbot using your voice, so you can have a real-time voice conversation. You talk, and ChatGPT talks back.
While OpenAI says that nearly all ChatGPT users are already using the newer Live Voice mode anyway, there’s a small, but very vocal contingent of the ChatGPT community who are very unhappy to see Standard and Advanced disappear, and they’ve taken to Reddit to express their outrage.
“I'm beyond disappointed because ChatGPT means a lot to me”, said one user, while another follows up by saying that they feel like they’re “paying a monthly subscription to beta-test their questionable decisions”.
The problem derives from a simple matter of preference for the older modes, the way they work, and in particular the sound of the voices they use.
How the three voice modes differ
The big change happens on December 11. Before then, to change between the three voice modes you need to go to Settings, then Voice and choose the mode you want.
Standard mode works by converting your speech to text, then generating a text answer before reading it aloud. Advanced mode works by processing speech directly, but takes turns speaking and listening. That means no interruptions.
The newer Live mode can listen and speak simultaneously with more natural interruptions and responses. Personally, Live mode is my favorite by a long way. To me it feels less robotic and more like a human conversation; however it seems that not everybody is a fan.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
There seem to be a couple of strong reasons why people object to the change. In many cases, they’ve become attached to a particular voice. One Reddit poster describes using the Vale voice for years and finding it comforting, while selecting Vale in GPT-Live doesn’t reproduce exactly the same experience.
Another aspect is that the supposedly more natural conversations of Live actually feel less natural to some people. It does a lot of ‘yeah’ and ‘anyway’ to fill in the gaps while it’s thinking. It interrupts, breaking the user's train of thought, and there are more changes in tone. Many people find this irritating.
Getting some perspective
I think we need to remember that the change doesn’t mean that we’re losing voice in ChatGPT entirely. OpenAI is simply consolidating voice into the Live model so that it can devote more development time to it without having to maintain Standard and Advanced as well.
In a statement on its Help center, OpenAI said: “We recognize that some people are accustomed to Advanced or Standard voice’s style or way of responding, and these model transitions can be challenging. Our Help Center article on navigating model transitions offers guidance to help with the change.”
Of course, it remains to be seen how much the opposition to this change will grow. This isn’t the first time OpenAI has tried to retire Standard Voice mode. In September 2025, it announced that Standard Voice would be retired within 30 days. But on September 9, the company reversed course, acknowledging that users valued the older experience and saying it would remain available while OpenAI addressed feedback.
While this new announcement feels more permanent, it will be interesting to see what happens if resistance to the changes continues to grow.
