articles.title: Für Solaranlagen oder Teleskopspiegel: Roboter baut autonom Strukturen im All
articles.text:
Für Solaranlagen oder Teleskopspiegel: Roboter baut autonom Strukturen im All
Wer derzeit große Strukturen wie Sonnensegel oder Habitate in den Orbit oder darüber hinaus bringen will, muss diese entweder am Boden zusammenfalten oder in Einzelteile verpacken und später per Hand zusammensetzen. Künftig könnte es eine dritte Option geben: Strukturen von Robotern bauen lassen.
Roboter: Autonom Struktur im All gebaut
Ein von der Caltech entwickelter und von der Darpa finanzierter Roboter hat jetzt erstmals genau eine solche Konstruktion erfolgreich demonstriert. Eine Premiere, wie Sergio Pellegrino, Professor für Luft- und Raumfahrt am Caltech und leitender Wissenschaftler am Jet Propulsion Laboratory der Nasa in einer Mitteilung erklärt.
Das Astra genannte Robotersystem ist Ende März 2026 ins All gestartet. Ziel war es, eine Reflektorantenne mit einem Durchmesser von 1,4 Metern aus Faserverbundrohren und Verbindungselementen aus Aluminium zu errichten. Das Ganze sollte der Roboter dann mit einer reflektierenden Folie überziehen.
Demonstration zeigt Machbarkeit
Laut Darpa ähnelt die Konstruktionsweise einer Hightechversion von Kinderspielzeug-Sets wie K-Nex oder Tinkertoy. Die Automatisierung des Zusammenbaus sei allerdings alles andere als ein Kinderspiel. So stieß das Team zeitlich an seine Grenzen und konnte nur den ersten Abschnitt der Antenne bauen.
Da die Astra-Mission im Dezember 2026 endet, ist nicht davon auszugehen, dass die Antenne noch finalisiert wird. Die Demonstration im Rahmen des Nom4d-Projekts soll aber die Machbarkeit des Montagekonzepts gezeigt haben. Die Caltech-Forscher:innen wollen den Entwurf jetzt vereinfachen und verfeinern.
Ziel: Riesige Spiegel für Weltraumteleskope
Zudem könne man nach dem erfolgreichen Test über die neuen Forschungsrichtungen nachdenken, die diese Demonstration eröffnet habe, so Pellegrino. Künftig könnten damit etwa riesige Spiegel für leistungsfähigere Weltraumteleskope oder die Basis für Solaranlagen im Orbit gebaut werden.
Andrew Detor, Nom4d-Manager der Darpa, geht es eigenen Angaben zufolge vor allem darum, „den effizienten, skalierbaren Bau sehr großer Strukturen im Weltraum“ zu ermöglichen. Mit „sehr groß“ seien Größenordnungen von Hunderten Metern oder Kilometern gemeint. Alles, was aktuell auch nur in diese Richtung gehe, sei heutzutage noch nicht realisierbar.

articles.title: Olaf Sakkers is betting he can beat the emerging-manager squeeze | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Entering into the world of venture capital has never been easy, especially as a first-time fund manager. But it’s especially daunting right now.
According to PitchBook data, firms raising their fourth fund “or later” captured a whopping 88.2% of U.S. VC fundraising dollars through the first three quarters of this year, while first-time funds captured a measly 4.5%. Just 81 first-time funds closed in the first nine months of 2026. That puts the year on track to be the worst for first-time managers in at least a decade, according to PitchBook’s estimate.
Olaf Sakkers has spent the past five years proving that difficult doesn’t mean impossible. He founded his firm RedBlue Capital in 2021 and closed its first fund with roughly $5 million in capital commitments in 2023. He has now held a first close on a second fund that he says will total at least $50 million.
Raised in South Africa, he studied anthropology at Princeton, focusing on global health and health policy, and wrote his thesis on HIV in his home country. He moved to Israel after graduating and was drafted into the Israel Defense Forces, where he says he had a desk job liaising with the U.S. military, and where he became interested in autonomous vehicles.
An introduction led to Michael Granoff, founder of the venture firm Maniv Mobility and an early backer of electric-vehicle startup Better Place. Granoff, who had money to invest, hired him on the spot, Sakkers says. Neither had been a venture investor at that point, so they built a fund “almost by accident,” learning as they went. Sakkers says he ran the investment process day to day, backing Israeli founders who were bringing cybersecurity skills into the automotive world, and later expanding to the U.S. and other markets.
By 2021, Sakkers says, he was an equal partner in Maniv’s economics, but he wanted something different — more formal and scalable — so struck out on his own. Today, RedBlue backs what he calls the “real economy,” including robotics, logistics, manufacturing and energy.
Getting to this point has been a test of endurance as much as salesmanship, seemingly. Sakkers says that institutional limited partners, outfits like endowments and pension funds, have been the toughest to win over because his checks are small (and theirs are comparatively huge) but also because their risk model is built to “avoid getting a zero,” which is why they tend to gravitate toward established brands.
Says Sakkers, it’s akin to founders who come to be seen as “inevitable,” after they’ve previously founded another company. Meanwhile first-time founders often battle against the “gravity of perception,” meaning a more dominant brand can bend how people perceive a newer one.
His answer has been to let the results speak, but it takes time. “It’s a long-term game of building trust, demonstrating performance over time,” Sakkers says.
The first fund was a proof of concept, backed by LPs he had known for a while, including family offices. The second draws on family offices and institutions.
RedBlue writes small checks, $50,000 to $100,000, mostly joining deals led by other investors rather than leading them. That lets it do more deals and be “the last investor that they take” on by promising practical help, including introductions to lead investors like Andreessen Horowitz and Thrive Capital, and to customers. Founders expect little from VCs, in Sakker’s view, so RedBlue tries to overdeliver on the support part.
By his account, the results are strong. Of 28 investments, he says that 15 have been marked up, and he cites a net internal rate of return of “significantly above 50%.” There has been just one exit — an acqui-hire — so most gains from the tiny fund remain on paper and unrealized.
Public records support part of Sakker’s story. HappyRobot, which RedBlue backed early, raised a $150 million Series C at a $1.2 billion valuation in August. Westmag, which makes motors for drones and robots and which Sakkers backed at pre-seed alongside Nat Friedman, emerged in June with an $11 million seed led by Andreessen Horowitz. Flai, an AI startup for car dealerships, followed its 2025 seed with a $27 million Series A. And Humble Robotics, a driverless-truck startup in whose $24 million seed round RedBlue participated, announced a $51 million Series A led by Obvious Ventures earlier this month.
Sakkers argues that discipline is his edge. RedBlue publishes thesis essays, such as one on robotics, and runs on a custom database that he built with Claude Code to log relationships, meeting notes and introductions.
That lets him and his lone full-time principal, based in New York, work asynchronously. AI agents, he says, are “useless if they just have to guess,” so everything gets written down. He contrasts that with Benchmark’s more artisanal model, which he says suits a firm with a record he lacks. Long exit timelines for physical-world companies don’t worry him, either: even a $50 million to $100 million fund, he says, can sell stakes on the secondary market.
The data isn’t uniformly grim. Smaller venture capital funds between $1 million and $10 million consistently outperform larger funds of $100 million or more at the top end of net TVPI (total value to paid-in capital, which compares a fund’s total value to the money invested in it) across recent vintages tracked by the software outfit Carta.
In the meantime, Sakkers is out there knocking on doors, making introductions between disparate parties, and calling up reporters like this one to tell his story. It’s not easy to make a mark in a world where the spoils accrue to the few, but he says he never seriously considered a safer job. “Life is short, and regrets last forever,” he says.

articles.title: Blockbuster IPL trade: Hardik Pandya moves to Punjab for Rs 18 Cr, Arshdeep heads to MI
articles.text:
Blockbuster IPL trade: Hardik Pandya moves to Punjab for Rs 18 Cr, Arshdeep heads to MI
Hardik Pandya's trade brings the curtain down on his second stint with MI, a franchise with which he won four IPL titles.
Flamboyant all-rounder Hardik Pandya moved to Punjab Kings from Mumbai Indians at an increased fee of Rs 18 crore, while PBKS traded pacer Arshdeep Singh for him, completing the biggest and most high-profile exchange of players in the history of IPL.
Pandya's existing fee was Rs 16.35 crore. Arshdeep, on the other hand, moved to Mumbai Indians (MI) at an unchanged price tag of Rs 18 crore, read a statement from the IPL.
Before this, Chennai Super Kings (CSK) had acquired Sanju Samson this year for Rs 18 crore from Rajasthan Royals, who in turn got Ravindra Jadeja for Rs 14 crore and Sam Curran for Rs 2.4 crore from CSK.
Transfer fee is a bipartite agreement between two franchises and it is independent of retention fee (the salary paid to a player by the franchise).
It was mutually decided by MI and PBKS that Pandya's trade fee will go up by Rs 1.65 crore and, as per existing rules, he would get 50% of the hike. The rest would go to Mumbai Indians.
Pandya's trade brings the curtain down on his second stint with MI, a franchise with which he won four IPL titles.
Having first joined MI in 2015, the 33-year-old had starring roles with both bat and ball during the team's title-winning campaigns in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020. After seven seasons with Mumbai, Pandya moved to Gujarat Titans (GT) at a fee of Rs 15 crore in 2022 and led the franchise to the title in its debut season. GT also reached the final in 2023.
Pandya returned to MI in 2024, taking over captaincy from stalwart Rohit Sharma but the franchise's performance nose-dived, and it was speculated that the injury-ravaged maverick was unhappy with how things panned out.
He struggled to win over fans after taking over leadership and was incessantly booed in the first season after his return. The second season was slightly better but by the end of the third season (2026), things went downhill.
Stories of dressing room dissension surfaced and it was clear that all wasn't okay among the senior group of players, including now former T20 skipper Suryakumar Yadav, and pace legend Jasprit Bumrah who were bypassed for captaincy.
Rohit's sudden removal also remained a thorny issue and it is now being widely speculated that he will return to captain the franchise for what could well be his last season. He is expected to have Tilak Verma as his deputy and long-term successor.
"Hardik has shared some very special moments with Mumbai Indians. We have seen him grow as a cricketer, make his mark on the world stage and then return to lead the team," MI owner Akash Ambani said in a statement.
"I have great respect for him, both as a cricketer and as a person, and wish him nothing but the very best for everything that lies ahead," he added.
The Mumbai team managed to win just four of its 14 matches in the season gone by, and Pandya skipped the closing stages of the league due to fitness concerns.
However, he remains a force to reckon with as a player. Across 162 IPL matches, he has scored 2,955 runs at a strike rate of 146.28 and claimed 82 wickets, underlining his value as a proven match-winner.
"Some laughs, endless memories and a whole lot of madness! Thank you, Arsh for the memories," Punjab Kings said in a statement acknowledging his contribution to the team.
Arshdeep, meanwhile, moves to MI after eight seasons with PBKS, where he made his IPL debut in 2019 and established himself as one of the competition's leading left-arm fast bowlers.
With 111 wickets in 96 IPL matches, he is PBKS' all-time leading wicket-taker. He claimed 21 wickets in the 2025 season and followed that with 14 wickets in this year's IPL. The 27-year-old is also India's leading wicket-taker in the T20 format with 151 scalps in 104 matches.

articles.title: Anthropic lance Claude Meetings, l’IA qui transforme les réunions en plans d’action et tâches
articles.text:
Au milieu d’une visioconférence sur Google Meet, vous demandez à Claude de dessiner le planning du projet dont vous discutez avec vos collègues, et l’assistant d’Anthropic le construit sous vos yeux avant la fin de l’appel.
Anthropic a présenté Claude Meetings. Avec cette fonction, son IA entre dans vos réunions vidéo en tant que participant visible. Claude suit la conversation et commence à travailler sur les tâches évoquées en même temps que vous parlez. Le service ouvre en bêta pour les abonnements Team et Enterprise, et uniquement sur Google Meet, car Microsoft Teams et Zoom ne sont pas compatibles au lancement. Claude débarque ainsi dans l’outil de visioconférence de Google, où Gemini prend vos notes en français pendant vos appels.
Claude rédige vos plans d’action pendant l’appel
Impossible de faire entrer l’assistant en douce. « Claude se signale en tant que participant et publie un avis dans le chat de la réunion », précise Anthropic. Et si vous recevez des invités extérieurs à votre entreprise, Claude ne rejoint l’appel qu’avec l’accord d’un administrateur.
Une fois dans la réunion, Claude prend des notes et répond dans le chat aux questions des participants. Il va aussi chercher des chiffres dans les applications connectées à votre compte, rédige des plans et établit des échéances. Quand la discussion porte sur l’organisation d’un projet, vous pouvez lui confier un tableau blanc partagé, Claude Whiteboards, disponible en bêta pour tous les abonnements payants. Claude le remplit au fil de la conversation, et il suffit de lui demander à voix haute de regrouper les idées par thème ou de signaler les étapes oubliées.
Après l’appel, vous retrouvez sur claude.ai les notes et les documents produits par l’assistant. Chez Anthropic, Claude assiste à presque toutes les réunions internes depuis environ deux mois, selon Nicholas Lin, responsable produit chargé du travail de bureau.
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace
Anthropic concurrence Copilot et Gemini jusque dans Google Meet
Les assistants de réunion ne manquent pas. Dans Teams, Microsoft réserve aux abonnés de Microsoft 365 Copilot son agent Facilitator. Il prend les notes de toute l’équipe et répond dans le chat aux questions restées en suspens. Chez Google, Gemini vous envoie le compte rendu de vos réunions Meet et prévient chaque participant dès qu’il commence à écrire. Anthropic promet d’aller plus loin, en faisant passer votre équipe de la discussion à l’exécution sans attendre que la réunion se termine.
Pour garder vos documents dans Claude, Anthropic a sorti en même temps Claude Sheets, en bêta pour tous les abonnements payants. Avec ce tableur, Claude met en place vos budgets et vos tableaux de suivi, que votre équipe peut ensuite modifier à plusieurs et exporter vers Excel. Nicholas Lin reconnaît une version assez basique, peu adaptée aux modèles financiers complexes. Anthropic a enfin ouvert à tous Claude Data, l’ancien Claude Dashboards, qui récupère les données de vos logiciels de gestion de la relation client pour les transformer en tableaux de bord.
Anthropic ne prétend pas pour autant chasser Excel ou Google Sheets de votre entreprise. « Je pense que les produits de Microsoft et de Google gardent leur utilité, selon les moments et les besoins », souligne Nicholas Lin.

articles.title: Estafa suplanta la cuenta de WhatsApp de amigos y familiares para pedir dinero: claves para no caer
articles.text:
Una estafa que suplanta cuentas legítimas de WhatsApp permite a los ciberdelincuentes pedir dinero a amigos y familiares desde conversaciones reales, una maniobra que aprovecha la confianza construida con un contacto conocido y dificulta detectar el engaño antes de realizar una transferencia o un pago urgente.
La víctima puede recibir el pedido dentro del historial habitual de mensajes, desde el mismo número con el que se comunica desde hace tiempo. El dueño de la cuenta, mientras tanto, puede no advertir que alguien utiliza su identidad para escribir en su nombre.
La Policía Nacional de España alertó que esta modalidad se diferencia de los fraudes que llegan desde números desconocidos o perfiles falsos. El mensaje aparece en un chat auténtico y puede conservar la foto, el nombre y los antecedentes de conversación del contacto suplantado.
Cómo los ciberdelincuentes ejecutan la estafa en WhatsApp
Para ejecutar el fraude, los atacantes necesitan acceder sin autorización a una cuenta o a los mecanismos que permiten utilizarla.
Entre las posibilidades investigadas figuran vulnerabilidades de seguridad que, en determinadas circunstancias, comprometen una cuenta sin que su titular entregue voluntariamente contraseñas ni códigos de verificación.
Asimismo, se han descrito incidentes con sesiones no autorizadas capaces de enviar mensajes en nombre del usuario legítimo. Esa actividad puede pasar inadvertida para el propietario de la cuenta durante un tiempo.
El riesgo aumenta cuando la solicitud apela a la urgencia, exige una transferencia inmediata o plantea una situación imprevista. Aunque los estafadores pueden imitar la forma de escribir de familiares o amigos, expresiones inusuales, errores ortográficos o palabras escritas de manera distinta pueden revelar la suplantación.
La pauta principal es confirmar cualquier pedido de dinero mediante una llamada telefónica u otra vía alternativa de contacto, incluso si el mensaje procede de una persona conocida. Una conversación habitual no garantiza que quien escribe sea realmente el titular de la cuenta.
De qué forma mantener la cuenta de WhatsApp libre de riesgos
Mantener WhatsApp y el sistema operativo del teléfono actualizados permite disponer de las correcciones de seguridad disponibles. La Policía Nacional aconseja activar la verificación en dos pasos, una protección adicional frente a determinados intentos de apropiación de cuentas.
La revisión periódica de los dispositivos vinculados permite cerrar sesiones desconocidas, aunque su ausencia no descarta necesariamente una intrusión. Tampoco deben compartirse códigos de verificación ni contraseñas recibidos por SMS o mediante otras aplicaciones.
Los mensajes sospechosos incluyen enlaces para activar supuestas funciones nuevas, descargar una aplicación o solicitar información personal. Entre los datos que pueden pedir figuran números de tarjetas de crédito, cuentas bancarias, fechas de nacimiento y contraseñas.
Otras señales incluyen pedidos para reenviar mensajes, reclamos de pago para seguir usando WhatsApp y referencias a loterías, juegos, empleos, inversiones o préstamos. En algunos casos, el estafador inicia una conversación para ganarse la confianza de la persona antes de solicitar información o dinero.
Ante la sospecha de una estafa, deben conservarse las conversaciones y los justificantes bancarios. Los hechos deben comunicarse de inmediato a la entidad bancaria y denunciarse ante las autoridades competentes.
Qué hacer en caso de recibir un mensaje sospechosos
Si un mensaje parece sospechoso o suena muy bueno para ser cierto, no hay que abrirlo, compartirlo ni reenviarlo, sobre todo si no hay certeza de que algo sea cierto o no conoces a la persona que escribió el mensaje.
Antes de abrir un enlace o un archivo, hay que revisarlo con atención. A simple vista, es posible que los enlaces y archivos parezcan legítimos, pero podrían ser maliciosos.
Si no hay certeza sobre la identidad de un contacto desconocido, hay que hacerle preguntas personales para confirmar su identidad. Se podría confirmar su identidad con una llamada o una videollamada.

articles.text:
Wednesday, November 11th 2026
Corsair Launches a Delightful Pink Colorway of its Best-selling 3500X and FRAME 4000D Cases
Corsair is proud to announce that two of its best-selling cases are launching in a new blush pink colorway with upgraded cooling and aesthetics. The wraparound-glass 3500X RS-R ARGB and modular FRAME 4000D RS II ARGB mid-tower cases combine this distinctive, pastel look with enhanced cooling capabilities. Both cases deliver standout visuals and superb cooling performance right out of the box, making them ideal for builds that perform as well as they look.
The FRAME 4000D is one of Corsair's best-selling cases thanks to its fully modular design, exceptional cooling capacity, and builder-friendly features. The new pink edition builds on this foundation with several upgrades over the standard FRAME 4000D RS ARGB. For starters, the pre-installed fans have been upgraded to new RS II ARGB fans for both intake and exhaust, delivering effective low-noise cooling with vibrant RGB lighting.These second-generation fans provide high airflow with exceptionally low noise at everyday operating speeds thanks to their Magnetic Dome bearing, which deliver low-noise operation and excellent longevity. The front-mounted fans feature the all-new RS360 II ARGB Unified Frame, delivering consistent lighting, reduced vibration, and simplified cabling. 
An additional RS120 II ARGB exhaust fan brings the total to four pre-installed fans, providing comprehensive system cooling. All four fans connect directly to the motherboard for easy setup and convenient control through motherboard software.The pink FRAME 4000D also features a full-coverage tempered-glass side panel that showcases your hardware, clean cable management, and RGB lighting. A compact PSU shroud completes the look, providing mounting locations for two 120 mm fans to deliver direct GPU cooling. An additional 120 mm fan can be installed in the bottom front of the chassis, bringing the total to 13x 120 mm fan mounts, one more than the standard FRAME 4000D. 
Beyond its cooling upgrades and striking new look, the FRAME 4000D PINK retains the modular design and builder-friendly features that have made the original a favorite among PC enthusiasts. These include dual InfiniRail Fan Mounting Systems in the front and top, support for two 360 mm radiators, compatibility with reverse-connector motherboards, and a 3D Y-pattern front grille for excellent airflow. 
It also features the FRAME Modular Case System, allowing users to swap components to refresh their build's appearance, enhance functionality, or both. Available modular options include front and side panels, motherboard trays, front I/O panels, and PSU shrouds. The result is a versatile case designed for high-performance builds with extensive customization options.The 3500X features wraparound tempered-glass panels that provide an expansive view of your hardware. The new pink edition comes equipped with four pre-installed fans, compared to three in the standard black and white versions. These include three white RS120-R reverse-rotor ARGB side-intake fans and an additional white RS120 ARGB rear-exhaust fan, delivering effective cooling and vibrant lighting ready to build. The three side-intake fans draw cool air into the chassis, while the rear fan exhausts warm air to maintain consistent airflow and help keep component temperatures low. 
The Corsair 3500X RS-R ARGB Mid-Tower Glass PC Case combines powerful cooling, bold aesthetics, and a clean, modern design with wraparound tempered-glass panels. Three pre-installed RS120-R reverse-rotor ARGB intake fans and one RS120 ARGB exhaust fan deliver vibrant lighting and powerful airflow, with lighting controlled through a standard +5V ARGB motherboard header. 
Its spacious interior accommodates large graphics cards, CPU coolers, and radiators up to 360 mm for custom or all-in-one liquid cooling. The 3500X also supports reverse-connector motherboards and includes a GPU anti-sag stabilization arm, while double-shot grommets help keep cable routing clean and organized.

articles.title: Trump admin loses fight to spy on random journalists’ LinkedIn DMs
articles.text:
The Trump administration’s fight to stop suspected leaks of top-secret military information on LinkedIn can’t sweep in “a vast number of confidential sources” of random journalists “who have no conceivable relationship” to the Department of Justice’s investigation, an appeals court ruled Tuesday.
The order came after the DOJ asked LinkedIn to turn over 18 months of communications from targeted journalists who collectively published more than 1,000 articles on many different topics over that time period. The request was not limited to journalists involved in a controversial report from a news outlet that Trump said exposed confidential military information in a foreign country. (The outlet is not being named to protect national security secrets.) Instead, the DOJ cast a wide net, requesting extensive LinkedIn data on journalists who had any possible link to the journalists around the time the report was drafted.
The majority of journalists have LinkedIn accounts and publish their contact information to encourage sources to connect on the platform, LinkedIn argued. So allowing that government overreach went beyond harming targeted journalists and threatened to undermine a critical platform where journalists frequently connect with confidential sources, judges ruled. Even more concerning, the Trump administration secured a secrecy order barring LinkedIn from telling anyone about the sweeping request for a year. That left journalists unaware for far too long that their First Amendment rights had been compromised, judges ruled.
Judge: Security and free speech can coexist
Penning the unanimous opinion from a three-judge panel, Ronald Reagan-nominated judge J. Harvie Wilkinson III rejected LinkedIn’s request to quash the order entirely and ordered the US district court to substantially narrow the order to avoid posing a grave threat to press freedoms.

articles.title: Airalo lança eSIM único para usar em diferentes viagens • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Airalo lança eSIM único para usar em diferentes viagens
Novo modelo dispensa a instalação de um chip virtual a cada destino e será disponibilizado para todos os clientes.
A Airalo vai permitir que clientes usem o mesmo eSIM em diferentes viagens internacionais. O novo modelo dispensa a instalação de um chip virtual a cada destino, permitindo que o usuário mantenha o perfil no celular e contrate pacotes de dados conforme a viagem.
Segundo a empresa especializada na venda de eSIMs, a mudança é viabilizada por uma infraestrutura de rede central própria. A novidade começou a ser liberada gradualmente na segunda-feira (09/11) e deve levar até 12 meses para alcançar os mais de 30 milhões de clientes da plataforma.
Com o novo modelo, o viajante mantém o mesmo eSIM instalado no celular e contrata pacotes de dados conforme o destino. Atualmente, quem usa esse tipo de serviço geralmente precisa instalar um novo perfil quando viaja para outro país. A proposta da Airalo é permitir a reutilização do chip virtual em diferentes viagens.
A empresa também permitirá comprar ou recarregar pacotes mesmo depois que o anterior expirar, sem exigir uma conexão Wi-Fi ou outro eSIM ativo. Segundo a Airalo, será possível ainda testar a conexão antes da viagem.
A plataforma prevê pacotes com duração de 1 a 30 dias para a maioria dos destinos, além de planos globais com validade de até 365 dias. A disponibilidade e as condições variam conforme o destino e o pacote escolhido.
A migração ocorrerá por etapas. Até receberem a atualização, os clientes continuarão usando o serviço normalmente.
O eSIM de viagem é uma das opções para acessar a internet fora do Brasil, mas não a única. Vivo, Claro e TIM, por exemplo, oferecem roaming internacional, serviço que permite usar a linha brasileira em redes de operadoras parceiras no exterior. Dependendo do plano, o roaming pode já estar incluído na mensalidade ou exigir a contratação de um pacote adicional.
Outra opção, também popular, é comprar um chip físico ou eSIM de uma operadora local no país de destino. O serviço da Airalo, no entanto, é uma alternativa para quem prefere acertar a internet separadamente, já que o cliente contrata um pacote de dados separado, válido para determinado país ou região.

articles.title: Montech King 95 3D Pro case review: The King has returned
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The King 95 3D is a solid, premium-class mid-tower with three tempered-glass panels for panoramic views inside. The seven included Link fans on the Pro version deliver enough airflow and RGB bling, but can get noisy at full speed. For $119 or $199 for the Pro, it’s an excellent update from the original King 95.
Reasons to buy
- + 3-pane window panel views
- + Pro version includes seven fans
- + Integrated GPU support
- + Adjustable angle on bottom fans
- + Cool RGB lighting strip on the outside
Reasons to avoid
- - RGB lighting from the fans is polarizing
- - Lacks vertical GPU mounting option
- - No E-ATX support
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
PC case, cooling, and PSU maker Montech is celebrating its 10th anniversary this year and has released a new flagship ATX chassis, the King 95 3D and 3D Pro. Like the previous King 95, the 3D version keeps the signature 15-degree curved-glass panoramic front panel and adds a top glass panel, giving you a third window and a unique aesthetic for viewing your build. An integrated, contoured ARGB strip follows the chassis's smooth lines, making it look every bit the king of the castle.
Inside, the large mid-tower chassis supports multiple radiators (though only one 360mm), large graphics cards (plus integrated adjustable GPU support), CPU air coolers, and spots for 2.5- and 3.5-inch drives. However, it doesn't support E-ATX motherboards. The King 95 3D supports rear-connect motherboards and has ample room for cable routing and management. The front aluminum panel IO runs vertically, as with previous King cases, and includes a fast USB 3.2 Gen2x2 (20 Gbps) Type-C port. Overall, it has everything you want in a premium chassis. The uncommon three-panel view into your PC is a great way to show off your rig.
The King 95 3D is available for an inexpensive (at least for curved glass) $119.90 if you want to select your own fans. The 3D Pro includes seven pre-installed LINK Fan INF 120 fans for builders who want a more coordinated look out of the box, plus it includes the Lumi hub (a dedicated fan controller), for $199.90. We have the 3D Pro version in our lab and ran the case through thermal and noise testing in its out-of-the-box configuration to show how it performs compared to others. Will it make our best PC cases list? It has a chance. But before we get into the details, here are the case's specifications from Montech.
Montech King 95 3D Product Specifications
| Type | Mid-Tower | 
| Dimensions (H x L x W) | 21 x 21 x 18.8 x 11.8-inches (534 x 480 x 300mm) | 
| Motherboard Support | Mini-ITX, Micro ATX, ATX | 
| Back-connect Motherboard Support | Yes | 
| Color | Black or White | 
| Storage Support | (1) 3.5-inch (2) 2.5-inch | 
| PCIe Expansion Slots | 7 | 
| Fan Support | Top - 3x120 Front - N/A Bottom - 3x120mm Side: - 2x120mm Rear - 2x120mm | 
| Pre-installed fans | (5) Link Fan INF 120 (Reverse blades, side/bottom) (2) Link Fan INF 120 (rear) | 
| Radiator Support | Front - N/A Top - 120/240/360mm Side - 120/240mm Rear - 120mm | 
| CPU Cooler Clearance | 172mm | 
| GPU Clearance | 450mm (max, depends on config) | 
| Vertical GPU Support | No | 
| PSU Length | 220mm | 
| Dust Filters | Side and Bottom | 
| Other features | Great internal views, 7x pre-installed fans (Pro version), integrated GPU support, adjustable angle bottom fans | 
| MSRP | King 95 3D - $119.90 (w/o fans) King 95 3D Pro - $199.90 (w/7 pre-installed fans) | 
| Warranty | 1 Year | 
Features of the King 95 3D
▶️ External Features
From the outside, the King 95 3D Pro looks the part of its royal name. That signature curve and three panes of glass offer a panoramic view inside your case like few others, letting you show off your PC from even more angles. It also features a frosted, continuous LED strip running along the tiered top, right side, and bottom, adding some tasteful bling to the chassis. If you get the Pro version with the seven fans, it’s an RGB light show inside which could be polarizing. I do wish there were an option for preinstalled non-RGB fans, since the seven included ones and the infinity mirror styling may not be for everyone. Still, the curved front corner and clean lines really cement the King 95 3D as one of the better-looking panoramic cases on the market.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Up front, the removable curved glass corner with a smoked tint sets it apart from most others. On the right, the front IO panel runs vertically, with the power button on top and the LED on/off button below. It has three USB ports: one 3.2 Gen2x2 (20 Gbps) Type-C and two USB 3.2 Gen1 (5 Gbps) Type-A ports. Finally, it has a 3.5mm audio jack. That continuous 118-LED strip is visible from the front, running along the top, down the right edge, and along the bottom edge. I’m not a fan of a lot of RGB, but this implementation is tasteful. You can control this lighting through the motherboard software or Montech's Lumi software, which lets you fully customize the fans and RGB strip.
The main window panel also uses a smoke-colored tint, with Montech branding in the upper-right corner, and it's secured to the frame by two captive thumbscrews on the back. To remove it, loosen the thumbscrews, slide the panel back, pull from the top, then lift it out of the slots. Easy. I have to say, the biggest problem with all this glass is keeping it pristine and fingerprint-free.
The other (metal) side panel, behind the motherboard, slots into the frame and is secured the same way. It has filtered venting along the top and side for the fans/radiator locations, plus another area for airflow near the power supply and drive mounting locations. In the middle is a gold placard with Montech King 95 3D 10th anniversary badging. Note: The dust filters on this panel aren't removable, so you’ll need to remove the whole panel to clean things up.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
At the top, we get a better look at the third windowed panel, letting observers peer into the case from a different angle rather than straight on or from the front. We can also see the tiered top and part of the long RGB strip. Taking this panel off isn’t as simple as the rest. Yes, it’s also secured by two captive thumbscrews on the back, but to remove it, you’ll need to open the main window panel to expose a retaining screw, remove it, then loosen the back thumbscrews and slide it to the rear. After you remove the top glass, you can remove the upper and side retaining screws to take it out. When building, I didn’t find this necessary, but it’s good to know you can take it apart if needed.
Looking at the case from behind, one of the first things I noticed was the vertical PSU mounting location on the left. This space supports up to 220mm power supplies, which is all but the largest on the market. On the right, we see space for two 120mm fans, the motherboard I/O, and seven horizontal expansion slots. Unfortunately, Montech says the King 95 3D does not support vertical GPUs.
Underneath the case, there isn’t a lot going on. We get a better look at the four short rubber-bottom ‘feet’ and the removable dust filter. Montech put on its thinking cap and designed the dust filter to slide out from the front, so chances are you won’t have to move your heavy case to clean it.
▶️ Internal Features
Inside, the case uses a dual-chamber design, with the power supply and all wires hidden behind the motherboard tray. At the bottom, we see three Link Fan INF 120s (reverse blade) along with the mirror finish. The magnetically linked, daisy-chainable fans run up to 2,300 RPM (2,200 RPM on the reverse blade), pushing between 65-67 CFM with a maximum rating of 32dBA (29 dBA on the standard blade). A single Link Fan INF 120 costs $19.90, while a 3-pack (with Lumi Hub) is $64.90. If you do the math for seven fans and the Lumi Hub, it’s cheaper to buy them with the case rather than separately.
When powered on, the mirrored sides become an infinity panel, and with all seven matching, it creates a consistent view across the build. The bottom fan bracket is adjustable, with three positions (8 degrees). We left it down during testing, but with it up, you can focus more air towards the GPU and show off whatever fans you put in the space.
The motherboard tray has plenty of cutouts to access the back of the motherboard for easy installation/removal of air coolers or AIO/custom water-cooling blocks. The case also supports rear-connect ecosystems, including Asus BTF, Gigabyte Stealth, and MSI Project Zero boards. Grommets surround the motherboard tray and are in ideal locations, but like most, they pull out easily when you try to route cables, especially those with larger connectors. I wish all case vendors would secure these better, since they're a pain to reinstall, especially when the case is full of cables.
Up top, we can see the huge gap above the motherboard tray for more fans and radiators. The case cooled just fine with the seven included fans and our air cooler, though GPU temps ran a bit warmer in our noise-normalized testing. That top gap is begging to be filled with fans, even if only for aesthetics. If you plan to use an AIO cooler, this isn’t a problem, since the radiator/fans will fill the space.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
From the front, you can see the two Link INF 120mm fans and, at the bottom, the tool-less, adjustable GPU support strut. The back has space to mount two 120mm fans or one 120mm radiator. You can also see the seven horizontal expansion slots held in by thumbnail screws.
Inside, the top of the case above the motherboard space fits up to three 120mm fans or a 360mm radiator. The space is offset back from the motherboard tray, which is a boon for cable management. Normally, there’s barely any room to route the EPS cables, but here there's plenty. Just note that if your build uses air cooling, you will need to fill that area with fans to make it look good. Otherwise, it’s just a blank open space above the motherboard.
On the rear side of the chassis, we get a good look at the space behind the motherboard tray and the fan baffles. There’s plenty of room to route cables, and Montech has multiple pre-installed Velcro straps for cable routing. Even with the power supply installed, there’s plenty of room underneath it to stash excess cables.
At the bottom, we see a simple ARGB hub that consolidates the three different ARGB cables from the fans into one header to control all of them. Montech also includes a magnetic Lumi fan/RGB hub (which supports up to 13 Link Fans total) with both the Pro and non-Pro variants. Oddly, it comes loose/uninstalled on the Pro, but installed on the non-Pro. The box in the lower-right holds one 3.5-inch HDD and a single 2.5-inch drive. The second 2.5-inch drive mounts in the other location at the bottom left, next to the side fans.
We do like the look of the King 95 3D Pro case in black, and I bet it looks great in white with an all-white build too. The curved glass and 3-panel panoramic interior views are great for anyone who’d like to show off their now-ridiculously expensive parts. The included Link Fan INF 120 fans work well and run relatively quietly. If there’s an aesthetic drawback, it's that I’m not a huge fan of all the RGB and infinity mirrors on the pre-installed fans. It’s a lot, and it makes me yearn for an option with preinstalled fans and no RGB. Of course, you can turn them off in the software, or buy the non-Pro and choose whichever fans fit your build.

articles.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth | TechCrunch
articles.text:
CoreWeave is rewriting how it pays for the AI boom, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings, reported on Tuesday. CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices.
The new strategies could help CoreWeave finance its growth more efficiently while squeezing more cash from existing infrastructure. But these bets only hold if today’s demand and pricing power continue.
CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% from the year prior, but it also posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense.
“We will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during Tuesday’s earnings call.
Instead, CoreWeave’s plan is to rely on loans backed by specific customer contracts, drawing on funds as needed to finance most of infrastructure it still has to build to deliver on its significant backlog of $132.5 billion.
CoreWeave also said it expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months, including more than $3 billion tied to signing new customer contracts for capacity it has already built, which requires no additional spending on hardware.
Rivals Nebius and IREN have also relied on hefty Microsoft prepayments to pay for computing capacity, signaling that the industry is moving toward asking Big Tech to pay up for their buildouts.
Upfront payments could alleviate CoreWeave’s immediate borrowing needs, but they also commit the company to providing services at a price that might be less attractive down the road if compute demand continues to surge.
CoreWeave is also looking to capitalize on that growing demand by signing more shorter-term contracts that can command much higher prices.
The company raised prices across its offerings by about 25% in July and by another 10% later in the quarter. Prices are still climbing this quarter, in a way that “more than offset[s] cost increases,” said Intrator.
“We are also allocating more capacity to short-term opportunities, where the pricing justifies it, selling capacity at more than $40 million per megawatt annually, while pricing for new infrastructure on four and five-year contracts is moving to $20 million to $25 million per megawatt,” the chief executive said.
CoreWeave’s financing strategy now revolves around those opportunities. In August, the company closed a $2.6 billion loan, its first designed specifically for shorter-term customer contracts. Known as DDTL 5.5, it lets CoreWeave borrow in installments as it needs the money.
While short-term deals let CoreWeave charge higher prices and change them more frequently, it’s a tradeoff. Lenders give more weight to longer-term contracts, even if they’re priced lower, because they value predictable cash flow and consistency to repay the loan above all.
Even though Wall Street reacted positively to CoreWeave’s earnings, bond investors are much less sanguine. Last month, yields on some of the company’s bonds hit above 15%, highlighting that investors are concerned about the debt needed to fund data center buildouts before those investments see a return.
In short, CoreWeave is finding new ways to expand without relying on unsecured debt. The strategy it has chosen could boost profits, but it also carries greater risk around contract renewals and pricing — and it just goes to show how dependent the AI infrastructure boom is on sustained, and as yet unproven, demand.
TechCrunch has reached out to CoreWeave for more information about its loan facility.

articles.title: Ring: Diese Drohne soll in Privathaushalten bald Patrouille fliegen
articles.text:
Sicherheitsroboter für dein Zuhause: Ring bringt Drohne und Rover auf den Markt
Bisher war Ring vor allem für seine Video-Türklingeln bekannt. Jetzt macht das zu Amazon gehörende Unternehmen den nächsten Schritt und gründet eine eigene Robotik-Sparte. Erklärtes Ziel von Ring Robotics sei es, die Sicherheit in Büros und Eigenheimen zu erhöhen. Die Produkte könnten allerdings erneut für Zündstoff sorgen, denn das Unternehmen stand schon mehrfach wegen Datenschutzbedenken in der Kritik.
Diese Ring-Drohne fliegt im Haus Patrouille
Das erste Gerät von Ring Robotics ist eine Sicherheitsdrohne für den privaten Gebrauch, die sogenannte Ring Drone Cam. Sie soll das eigene Zuhause überwachen, wenn gerade niemand da ist. Die „fliegende Innenraum-Überwachungskamera“ ist dafür konzipiert, von Raum zu Raum zu fliegen, das Geschehen im Haus zu überwachen und die Bewohner:innen im Falle eines Problems zu alarmieren. Wenn sie nicht im Einsatz ist, verharrt sie inaktiv auf einer Ladestation.
Laut Herstellerangaben ist sie mit anderen Ring-Geräten kompatibel. Löst beispielsweise eine Ring-Klingel an der Hintertür aus, soll die Drohne dorthin fliegen und die Situation überwachen. Sie nimmt Videos in 2K-Auflösung auf. LED-Leuchten ermöglichen es ihr, auch nachts Wache zu halten. Nutzer:innen steuern die Drohne über die Alexa Home Map. Hier lässt sich auch einstellen, dass sie zu bestimmten Zeiten im Haus Patrouille fliegt. Das Gerät kommt am 27. Januar auf den Markt und soll 270 US-Dollar kosten. Es ist nicht der erste Versuch von Ring, eine Drohne ins Eigenheim zu bringen. Die sogenannte Always-Home-Cam wurde 2020 vorgestellt, kam aber nie auf den breiten Markt.
Ring Rover soll Einbrecher:innen verschrecken
Das zweite Produkt ist der Ring Rover. Er ist für den Einsatz in Büros oder Geschäften gedacht und überträgt Videos in 4K, die sich die Nutzer:innen in der mobilen Ring-App ansehen können. Zudem lässt sich ein Auslöser einstellen, der automatisch eine Aufzeichnung startet, sobald der Roboter eine Person erkennt. Dank der Periskopkamera soll er auch über Gegenstände hinwegblicken können.
Der Ring Rover ist mit einer Zwei-Wege-Audiofunktion ausgestattet. Das bedeutet, dass Nutzer:innen nicht nur hören können, was vor Ort vor sich geht – sie können über das Gerät auch mit Mitarbeiter:innen oder Einbrecher:innen sprechen. Wie bei der Drohne lässt sich auch hier einstellen, wann der Roboter die Räume abfahren soll. Er ist ab dem 16. Dezember für 1.000 Dollar erhältlich.
Datenschutz bleibt für Ring ein heikles Thema
Laut Unternehmensangaben laufen beide Geräte mit AI Pilot, dem firmeneigenen KI-System. Dadurch soll es Drohne und Rover unter anderem möglich sein, durch eigenständiges Erkunden einen detaillierten Grundriss des Hauses oder Büros zu erstellen. Trotz ihrer Nützlichkeit ist die Wahrscheinlichkeit hoch, dass Drohne und Rover bestehende Kritik wieder aufflammen zu lassen. Bedenken hinsichtlich des Datenschutzes verfolgen Ring schon seit Langem.
In Deutschland ist der Einsatz besonders schwierig, da für Überwachungskameras strenge rechtliche Vorgaben gelten. Sie dürfen ausschließlich das eigene Grundstück erfassen – öffentliche Bereiche und Nachbargrundstücke sind tabu. Auch eine permanente Bewegungsüberwachung ist in Deutschland unzulässig, wie der Bundesgerichtshof in einem Urteil bestätige. Als besonders problematisch gelten Geräte, die sich per App dauerhaft aktivieren lassen oder jede Bewegung automatisch aufzeichnen.

articles.title: IBM presenta un procesador cuántico que puede expandirse mucho más allá de un solo chip
articles.text:
IBM ha presentado Quantum Nighthawk r3, su nuevo procesador cuántico diseñado para ejecutar cálculos más complejos y acercar esta tecnología a usos prácticos. El nuevo chip es capaz de ejecutar hasta 10.000 operaciones cuánticas sobre 520 qubits programables. IBM busca ponerse al día y competir con otras empresas como Microsoft, Google y Amazon en la carrera por desarrollar ordenadores cuánticos funcionales.
De acuerdo con una publicación en su web, el IBM Nighthawk r3 es la apuesta más ambiciosa de la compañía hasta la fecha. Además de la potencia de cálculo, el chip cuenta con 2.034 qubits físicos y una arquitectura que permite conectar varios procesadores entre sí. Según IBM, esto último le permitirá realizar cálculos más complejos sin sacrificar el rendimiento ni la precisión.
A diferencia de los procesadores tradicionales que encontramos en el ordenador o el móvil, un chip cuántico trabaja con qubits. Estos aprovechan las propiedades de la física cuántica para representar más información al mismo tiempo y resolver problemas que serían imposibles para un superordenador actual. Este proceso no solo involucra el número de qubits, sino también la velocidad con la que se tienen que realizar los cálculos una y otra vez hasta determinar cuál es la solución correcta.
IBM menciona que su arquitectura Nighthawk es capaz de ejecutar algoritmos millones o miles de millones de veces, gracias a sus sistemas de reinicio rápido de qubits y conectividad que reducen el tiempo entre operaciones. El Nighthawk r3 puede ejecutar hasta 10.000 operaciones cuánticas dentro de un mismo circuito, las cuales pueden aprovecharse en tareas como optimización de redes eléctricas, simulaciones de materiales magnéticos y experimentos de química cuántica.
La clave de Nighthawk: conectar varios chips en un solo sistema
Además del nuevo procesador, IBM confirmó que tiene planes de unir dos chips Nighthawk r3 mediante enlaces cuánticos especializados. Esto crearía un sistema con más de 1.000 qubits y evitaría algunos de los problemas comunes que enfrentan las empresas para producir estos procesadores. En lugar de fabricar un chip gigantesco, la arquitectura optaría por un sistema modular que podría escalarse con más procesadores conectados entre sí.
Comparado con lo que están desarrollando el resto de tecnológicas en la computación cuántica, IBM ha tomado otro camino. Nighthawk apuesta por aumentar el número de qubits y la velocidad de ejecución, mientras que compañías como Microsoft, Google y Amazon se enfocan en la corrección de errores. El Majorana 1 de Microsoft usa qubits topológicos diseñados para ser más estables, mientras que el Ocelot de Amazon se enfoca en los "cat qubits" para mejorar la corrección de errores en los cálculos.
La compañía confirmó que actualizará su plataforma para que los chips cuánticos trabajen junto con las supercomputadoras de alto rendimiento. Según IBM, esto ayudaría a ejecutar aplicaciones complejas y corregir errores. El Nighthawk r3 mantendrá la conectividad de red cuadrada y operaciones de su predecesor, añadiendo 10 interconexiones entre chips diseñadas para conectar procesadores en sistemas más grandes.
La plataforma IBM Quantum, que combina la computación cuántica y los superordenadores, estará disponible para investigadores y desarrolladores.

articles.title: FinMin asks ministries to make EVs the default and preferred choice for staff car purchases
articles.text:
FinMin asks ministries to make EVs the default and preferred choice for staff car purchases
To promote electric mobility, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, and account for prevailing market prices and vehicle lifecycle costs, the Finance Ministry is revising the net dealer price ceiling for procuring EVs and internal combustion engine vehicles.
The Finance Ministry has asked ministries and departments to make electric vehicles (EVs) their "default and preferred choice" for staff cars, and set a price cap of Rs 20 lakh for procurement of such vehicles.
The Finance Ministry said that, to promote electric mobility, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, and account for prevailing market prices and vehicle lifecycle costs, it is revising the net dealer price (NDP) ceiling for procuring EVs and internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles.
Accordingly, the NDP ceiling for EVs has been set at Rs 20 lakh, double the Rs 10 lakh limit set for ICE vehicles (petrol/diesel/hybrid).
The 2022 instructions prescribing the guidelines regarding procurement and hiring of cars by ministries/departments had fixed the NDP ceiling at Rs 6 lakh.
In an office memorandum dated November 10, the Expenditure Department said going forward, ministries/departments shall ordinarily procure EVs at the time of condemnation/replacement of their existing ICE staff cars.
"EVs shall be the default and preferred choice for procurement," it said.
In cases where a ministry/department considers that procurement or deployment of EVs is not practical and proposes to procure an ICE vehicle, a duly justified proposal would have to be sent to the Department of Expenditure for relaxation on a case-by-case basis.
"Such a proposal may be referred with the approval of the Secretary of the Administrative Ministry/Department and concurrence of the Financial Adviser," it added.
The Finance Ministry also said that all ministries and departments will continue to adhere to the 2022 instructions mandating the hiring of EVs.
In cases where hiring of ICE vehicles is considered necessary, the proposal has to be referred to the Department of Expenditure for relaxation on a case-to-case basis.
The Finance Ministry's instructions comes in the backdrop of Government's efforts to accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles as part of its broader push towards clean mobility, energy security and reduction of carbon emissions.
The policy approach combines financial incentives, promotion of domestic EV manufacturing, development of charging infrastructure and measures to encourage greater consumer and institutional adoption.

articles.title: Vous ne rêvez pas : la Nintendo Switch 2 en version européenne peut passer à 334,46€ sur AliExpress pour le 11.11
articles.text:
La Nintendo Switch 2 voit son prix chuter sur AliExpress dans le cadre du 11.11. Mais pour espérer obtenir la console en version européenne à 334,46 €, il faut cumuler deux remises et être parmi les premiers à valider votre commande.
La Nintendo Switch 2 se trouve régulièrement en promotion, mais en ce jour de 11.11, c’est chez AliExpress qu’elle est la plus abordable. En effet, il est possible d’y obtenir la console hybride de Nintendo pour seulement 334,46 €. Ce tarif s’obtient en utilisant le code promo 11FR60, qui permet de bénéficier d’une remise immédiate de 60 €, mais aussi en réglant la commande via PayPal, pour obtenir 33 € de réduction supplémentaire. L’offre concerne la console en version européenne, et attention : AliExpress ne propose que 256 unités à ce prix.
La Nintendo Switch 2 peut revenir à 334,46 € sur AliExpress en cumulant le code 11FR60 et la remise PayPal.
Pourquoi choisir la Nintendo Switch 2 ?
- Pour son format hybride : elle permet de poursuivre une partie sur son écran intégré ou sur le téléviseur.
- Pour son écran plus grand : elle embarque une dalle Full HD de 7,9 pouces, contre 6,2 pouces pour la première Nintendo Switch.
- Pour la continuité du catalogue : elle accueille les jeux Switch 2 et reste compatible avec la grande majorité des jeux de la première Switch.
Une console pour ne pas choisir entre le salon et la mobilité
L’un des points forts de la Nintendo Switch 2 était déjà présent sur la première Switch. Il s’agit de son fonctionnement hybride, qui permet de jouer sur le téléviseur quand la console est sur son dock, ou en mode portable, sur batterie. Son écran LCD de 7,9 pouces renforce l’immersion en déplacement, et ses 256 Go de stockage permettent d’installer de nombreux jeux. Vous pouvez aussi étendre cette capacité avec une carte microSD Express.
Dans notre test de la Nintendo Switch 2, nous avons apprécié les progrès en matière de performances, d’affichage et de finitions par rapport à la précédente console de Nintendo. L’autonomie reste toutefois une concession, puisqu'elle se situe entre 2 et 6,5 heures selon les jeux.
Une expérience satisfaisante, mais on aurait aimé de l’OLED
Si les performances de la Nintendo Switch 2 permettent de profiter de meilleurs graphismes et de jeux plus fluides que sur la première Switch, on regrette tout de même que Nintendo n’ait pas intégré d’écran OLED à cette nouvelle mouture. Côté contraste, la dalle LCD marque un recul par rapport à la Switch OLED. Dommage.
✅ Les points forts
- Utilisation en mode portable, sur table et sur téléviseur.
- Écran Full HD de 7,9 pouces.
- Joy-Con 2 magnétiques et détachables.
❌ Les limites
- Autonomie limitée sur les jeux exigeants.
- Pas d’écran OLED.
Pour obtenir la Nintendo Switch 2 à 334,46 € sur AliExpress, vérifiez que le code 11FR60 et la remise PayPal sont bien appliqués avant de commander.
Si vous ne possédez pas encore de Switch 2 et que vous avez envie de vous lancer dans le remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, cette offre peut vous permettre de sauter le pas à un prix raisonnable. Elle a aussi de l’intérêt si vous souhaitez retrouver une grande partie de votre catalogue Switch sur la nouvelle console.
Mais si vous estimez que vous n’avez pas encore fait le tour du catalogue de votre Switch, ou si vous avez une Switch OLED et que repasser au LCD ne vous fait pas rêver, vous pouvez patienter encore un peu.

articles.title: Hoy en Lidl (rebajado a 37,99 euros): este taladro atornillador Parkside ideal para los manitas de casa
articles.text:
Tener a mano una herramienta polivalente para montar muebles, colgar estantes o realizar pequeñas reparaciones sin depender de enchufes ni cables es básico en cualquier hogar. En el catálogo de bricolaje de Lidl, la gama Parkside se ha consolidado como la referencia indiscutible por su relación calidad-precio y este taladro atornillador recargable de 12 V (PBSA 12 F5) destaca como una compra práctica y ahora está disponible por 37,99 euros.
Taladro atornillador de impacto recargable 20 V »PSBSA 20-Li C3« con batería – con cargador
Si no llegas a tiempo para conseguir este chollo de Lidl, en Amazon tienes también una alternativa a un precio similar. Se trata de este taladro atornillador Betenst (rebajado hoy a 29,95 euros) y que viene con dos baterías y varias brocas y puntas.
BETENST Taladro Atornillador 21V, Taladro Inalámbrico con 2 Batería 2,0Ah
Diseño compacto de 12 V, portabrocas extraíble y kit completo con batería
La clave de esta herramienta Parkside es su equilibrio entre ligereza y fuerza, pensado para trabajar cómodamente en espacios reducidos o por encima de la cabeza sin que sufras fatiga en los brazos.
Incorpora un engranaje de dos velocidades con un par de apriete máximo de 28 Nm, regulable en 19 niveles de par más una posición específica para taladrado. Esto permite desde apretar tornillos en maderas delicadas sin pasarlos de rosca hasta perforar con precisión en madera o metal ligero.
Incorpora también un portabrocas automático de sujeción rápida que se puede desmontar sin herramientas mediante un sistema de liberación rápida. Al quitarlo, la punta del taladro deja al descubierto un portapuntas magnético integrado que acorta el cuerpo de la herramienta y permite atornillar en rincones donde un taladro convencional no cabe.
Viene equipado con una batería de iones de litio de 12 V (2,0 Ah) con tecnología de equilibrado de celdas y un cargador de 2,4 A que completa la carga en apenas 60 minutos con apagado automático. articles.title: Les droits TV de la Ligue 1 pourraient finir sur une grosse plateforme américaine
articles.text:
Ligue 1 : la diffusion des prochains championnats pourrait atterrir chez Disney ou Skydance
Et si les prochains championnats de France de football étaient diffusés sur Disney+ ou encore les plateformes de Skydance ? Cette éventualité est aujourd'hui assez envisageable.
Commeprévu en octobre dernier, ce 3 novembre 2026 un nouvel appel d'offres a été lancé par la Ligue de football professionnel (LFP). Son objectif : trouver un diffuseur pour les cinq saisons allant de 2027 à 2032 de la Ligue 1.
D'après Bloomberg, deux poids lourds de l'audiovisuel américain considereraient leur participation à cet appel d'offre conçu pour relever un secteur en perte de revenus depuis des années : Disney et Skydance.
Disney et Skydance toujours plus accros au sport
Si aucune annonce, candidature ou enchère n'est officielle pour le moment, ces deux possibles candidats ont du sens.
Pour Disney, propriétaire de Disney+ et d'ESPN, le sport n'est pas une passion véritablement récente. Rien que pour le football, la firme diffuse déjà la Liga espagnole en partenariat avec DAZN, mais aussi la Ligue des champions féminine de l’UEFA jusqu’en 2030.
Pour Skydance (Paramount+), qui possède désormais les branches de Warner Bros. Discovery comme Eurosport ou HBO Max, là aussi le sport est déjà bien représenté (tennis, cyclisme, JO...), et y ajouter du football aurait du sens.
L'entité qui remportera l'appel d'offres, et qui devra pour cela proposer plus que ce que Ligue 1+ génère, aura plusieurs choix : acquérir l'ensemble des droits audiovisuels du championnat, se contenter d'obtenir un accord de distribution exclusive de la plateforme Ligue 1+, ou bien sous-licencier une partie des matchs à d'autres diffuseurs. Ces derniers pourraient par exemple être beIN Sports ou Canal+ s'ils n'emportent pas les enchères eux-mêmes.

articles.title: Infidelidad de Jensen Huang: expertos en gobierno corporativo advierten riesgos para Nvidia
articles.text:
Dos profesores de gobierno corporativo afirmaron que no conocen un caso comparable al de Jensen Huang, el CEO de Nvidia que admitió una relación extramatrimonial con Alice Huang, ejecutiva que los servicios de inteligencia de Estados Unidos creen que espiaba para China. La acción de Nvidia cayó cerca de 9,5% en dos días.
Según TechCrunch, que entrevistó a Ann Lipton, de la Universidad de Colorado, y a Todd Henderson, de la Universidad de Chicago, hubo antes casos de infidelidad y de acoso sexual de directivos, pero ninguno que además implicara un posible riesgo para la seguridad nacional. Ambos dijeron que observan el caso sin tomar partido por Huang ni en su contra.
La acción de Nvidia bajó el 4% el lunes y más del 5% el martes, aunque la empresa no difundió novedades relevantes. El martes, el directorio informó que contrató al bufete Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz y al exfiscal federal Joon H. Kim para investigar si se comprometieron secretos de la compañía o la seguridad nacional, según CNBC.
Qué debe averiguar la investigación
Lipton identificó tres preguntas: si Huang violó la ley, si incumplió las políticas internas de Nvidia y si engañó al directorio, incluido cuándo estuvo al tanto de las sospechas. Calificó la investigación como el elemento más habitual de todo el episodio y advirtió que será tan exhaustiva como quieran los directores que la lleven a cabo.
Henderson planteó dos escenarios. En uno, Huang contrató a una empresa de comunicación de crisis porque la infidelidad era embarazosa, sin saber quién era la mujer. En el otro, sabía que era una sospechosa de espionaje. “Creo que es muy diferente”, dijo. Wired informó que Huang contrató a esa firma un año antes, según recordó TechCrunch.
Para Henderson, no avisar al directorio de ese vínculo “parece una falta que justifica el despido”. También señaló que los bufetes que realizan investigaciones internas “saben quién les paga”, aunque aclaró que no sugería que eso ocurra en este caso.
El directorio dijo el domingo 8 de noviembre que no tiene motivos para creer que se hayan comprometido secretos de Nvidia ni la seguridad nacional. Henderson dijo que el dato clave es qué obtuvo, si algo, Alice Huang: información sobre fábricas o diseños de chips interesaría al Departamento de Justicia, y datos corporativos comunes probablemente no.
Demandas de accionistas y el peso del directorio
Lipton anticipó demandas de accionistas de dos tipos. La de fraude bursátil, que “solo trata de mentir”, ya existe: una demanda colectiva propuesta acusa a Nvidia y a Huang de engañar a los inversores al describir como normales los tratos con Megaspeed, la empresa en la que Alice Huang era ejecutiva. “Se puede tener tantas aventuras con espías chinas como se quiera, pero no se puede mentir al respecto”, dijo Lipton.
El segundo tipo, por mala gestión bajo la ley de Delaware, donde está constituida Nvidia, es mucho más difícil. Los accionistas deben probar que el directorio no puede manejar el problema, normalmente porque sus miembros están implicados o dependen del CEO. Lipton recordó que un tribunal rechazó esa vía en un caso contra McDonald’s.
The New York Times señaló que el directorio de 10 miembros tiene antecedentes de lealtad hacia Huang. Lipton consideró, aun así, que la investigación con abogados externos dificulta una demanda de ese tipo.
Nvidia funciona con una estructura plana, con más de 60 subordinados directos de Huang, y no parece tener un plan de sucesión, algo que Lipton calificó como “un peligro para cualquier empresa”. Sus hijos Spencer y Madison, y su yerno Nico Caprez, trabajan en la compañía. Lipton lo describió como falta de higiene corporativa, y Henderson dijo que la idea de que un hijo lo suceda “parece una locura”.
Los profesores señalaron un punto a favor: Nvidia no tiene acciones con voto privilegiado. Huang posee cerca de 3,6%, según informes citados por TechCrunch, por lo que no controla la votación y, según Lipton, es más fácil de reemplazar. El presidente Donald Trump dijo el martes que el FBI también investiga el caso, según UPI.

articles.title: Reddit "Reviews" will use AI to turn subreddit posts into product recommendations
articles.text:
Connecting the dots: Reddit is traditionally described as the "front page of the internet," a place where almost every netizen goes to look for user recommendations and genuine product experiences. Over the next few weeks, the popular social network will start turning its user-focused communities into a full AI-powered review outlet.
Reddit has announced a significant way in how the company plans to do business on the web. The newly introduced Reddit Reviews service will turn one of the internet's most popular "places" into a review and recommendation hub. Just like everything else related to user-generated data these days, RR makes extensive use of generative AI models to repackage individual opinions and user experiences into a commercial, purchase-oriented platform.
In Reddit's own words, RR leverages the wealth of user opinions already available in some of the site's most popular communities. When a user searches for a product on Reddit, GenAI will provide contextualized summaries and comparisons highlighting the most interesting features of that product.
Reddit Reviews will organize relevant "conversations" taken from the service's communities, turning user interactions into an "easy-to-digest" format.
Each review will include both positive and negative traits of a product, plus additional info related to its specific category. For an espresso machine, RR might provide information about how much counter space the device takes up, how beginner-friendly it is, and more.
Additional RR features include an option to navigate the full category a product belongs to, so users can explore different choices related to their original search. After testing the feature for months, Reddit is now ready to bring the Reviews service to the site's wider community, with a few caveats: RR will initially be available to US visitors.
At launch Reddit Reviews will base its recommendations on around 10,000 products across four categories: Electronics, Health & Beauty, Home & Garden, and Fashion & Apparel. As far as I can tell, the AI-powered reviews can be viewed only in the "new" Reddit site – no option appears to exist to access RR from the "old," still very popular design. Reddit plans to expand Reviews to more product types and visitors outside the US throughout 2027.
The new Reviews section marks another change in the traditional Reddit experience. Reddit CEO Steve Huffman recently announced that the platform will evolve into a "primarily logged-in experience," in part because AI bots are freely extracting data from the site without bringing the company any financial benefit. Reddit has insisted in an Australian court that it isn't a social network, while Reddit Reviews touts the platform's inherent social interactions, where people freely discuss almost every topic you can think of.

articles.title: Nintendo unleashes DMCA takedown wave against open-source Switch modchip firmware, 144 tools disabled — Picofly, SX Core, and HWFLY among casualties following criminal trial victory
articles.text:
Nintendo unleashes DMCA takedown wave against open-source Switch modchip firmware, 144 tools disabled — Picofly, SX Core, and HWFLY among casualties following criminal trial victory
Even open-source isn't safe from Nintendo's legal team
Nintendo has set its famously litigious sights on the open-source firmware that powers hardware modchips on Nintendo Switch. Earlier this week, GitHub posted a DCMA request from Nintendo of America confirming that an entire network of 144 total repositories, including the parent repository, was taken down. Mod chip firmware for hardware including SX Core, SX Lite, Picofly, and HWFLY was targeted.
Early original Nintendo Switch consoles shipped with an unpatchable hardware exploit found in the device's recovery mode, which has since been patched in later units such as the Switch Lite and Switch OLED (the modchip hack doesn't work on Switch 2). As such, running custom software on patched Switches requires hardware modification, soldering a microchip like a Picofly, HWFLY, or SX Core to your Switch's motherboard. These chips require firmware, specifically code that can perform the voltage glitching required during boot to hack the Switch.
Rather than playing whack-a-mole with vendors of off-the-shelf microcontrollers, Nintendo has instead issued a DCMA takedown notice to the entire family of GitHub repos hosting this firmware. "The reported repositories offer, link to, or otherwise provide access to mod chip firmware including but not limited to SX Core, SX Lite, Picofly, or HWFLY," the DCMA request from Nintendo reads. "The firmware allows Nintendo Switch modchips to illegally circumvent Nintendo’s TPMs in order to run illegal copies of Nintendo Switch games. Specifically, during operation, the mod chip firmware at the reported repositories circumvents the technological protection measures put in place on the Nintendo Switch console by bypassing the boot sequence.
Nintendo went on to state that because these repositories are designed "primarily" to unlawfully circumvent technological measures controlling access to work protected under the DCMA, distributing mod chip firmware "constitutes unlawful trafficking in technology that is 'primarily designed or produced for the purpose of circumventing a technological measure that effectively controls access' to copyrighted works." In support of this argument, Nintendo cited criminal proceedings brought by the US Department of Justice against Team-Xecuter, a maker and seller of SX Pro, SX Core, and SX Lite modchips.
While these modchips can be (and are) used for game piracy, they unlock a host of features including running homebrew and custom applications, emulation, alternative operating systems, and more. They also enable game modding, custom themes, and even Switch overclocking. Naturally, Nintendo has chosen to focus on their utility in accessing pirated games and bypassing DRM.
Because much of this hardware and firmware is already out in the wild, the move won't have any impact on existing Switch owners who have a modchip installed. However, this will prevent firmware updates to existing modchips, as well as firmware flashing and reflashing. Naturally, it will also prevent future potential hardware modders from hacking their Switch in the same way.
Nintendo is famous for its fervent prosecution of copyright law, but developments in AI are turning this into a drastically more complicated battle. Nintendo's Zelda remake was dumped online on the same day it launched on Switch 2, while earlier this year one developer used AI to bring the original Nintendo 64 version to iOS. In July, Mario Kart Wii was recompiled for PC in 4K with over 200 tracks.

articles.title: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.
articles.text:
The last few years have seen significant debate over the widespread use of AI-powered tools in game development and the responsible disclosure of that usage to players. That debate has exploded into a full-blown controversy in the indie game development space this week, as Big Walk developer House House has publicly and belatedly disclosed minimal AI use in its popular co-operative puzzle exploration game.
This particular controversy has been brewing behind the scenes for months, as judges and jury members for the prestigious Independent Games Festival Awards discussed the issue in private discussion groups. But the debate started to break into public view on Monday when 19 members of the 50-plus-member jury released a signed statement outlining a stance “declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity.”
Noting “a significant increase in the number of submitted games developer with generative AI tools,” the group of jurors called out AI’s ecological, economic, psychological, and labor harms in rejecting tools whose use, they said, is still “not a foregone conclusion in our industry.”
The jurors also urged the IGF as a whole to “adopt a strong anti-AI policy for future years that disallows games containing any AI-generated work.”
The big walkback
Although the jurors’ statement didn’t name any specific games, by Tuesday morning, one critical darling in particular was increasingly being noted as a central part of the debate. In a statement provided to Aftermath (and added to the game’s FAQ page shortly thereafter), developer House House admitted publicly that “LLMs were used sparingly” near the end of Big Walk‘s development “to help work through some difficult technical challenges and bugs.”
That limited AI use—which House House says represents “well under 0.1% of Big Walk‘s code—stemmed in part from a thorny Unity engine bug that was slowing the game down with “infinite length” shadows during some game situations. After consulting with a Unity engineer who determined a fix “wasn’t possible,” House House said it consulted an LLM chatbot, which suggested a possible fix that the developers “had to modify… extensively” into the 10 lines of code that ended up in the final game (At least one social media user says the bug was indeed fixable with significant human effort, though).

articles.title: With $720M round, Britain's Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Fractile, a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy,” its government stated.
Alongside the likes of Axelera, Etched, and OLIX, this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips. Such chips are one of several avenues being explored to reduce the cost of inference — aka using increasingly demanding AI models in production.
However, Fractile seeks to go beyond hardware with a full-stack approach that also includes a machine learning compiler to maximize the speed at which LLMs will get executed on its chips.
As a result, the company frames itself as a frontier AI company, and its latest round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Redpoint was priced accordingly. According to the British government, the valuation was “over £5 billion” — quite possibly $7 billion, a figure reported both by the Financial Times and a Reuters source.
Still, Fractile’s main differentiator will arguably be its hardware design. After a pivot, its approach now revolves on DRAM, the most common type of RAM, but stacked on top of each chip in such a way that it is hoping will bypass the usual tradeoff between memory and capacity.
This tradeoff has become more problematic with the rise of agentic AI, as companies seek to perform longer chains of tasks with large models without compromising on speed. As compute struggles to keep up, hopes are high for AI chips, despite their limited availability to date.
In a LinkedIn post, Fractile CEO Walter Goodwin wrote that “there is still a lot of work ahead” for the company, and that the new funding will enable the startup to “ship [its] first chips and systems next year.”
