articles.title: Steam Deck now shows average frame rates for thousands of games
articles.text:
Much Data, Very Frame: Valve is trying to ease the pain points of Steam Deck owners by providing a more detailed picture of a game's actual performance. Steam store pages can now show the average frame rate Deck players get in many games, which might help customers make a more informed choice when they're looking to purchase a new title.
Valve announced the addition this week, with the data calculated from previously collected, anonymized figures provided by customers who chose to opt in to frame rate sharing. The average is already available for "thousands" of Steam Deck-tested games, and the same data can be viewed in the Steam Library by users on the Steam Client Beta.
After being tested for Steam Deck compatibility, a game can be classified as Verified, Playable, or Unsupported, and the average frame rate is shown under the "Steam Deck Compatibility" section of each game's store page, no matter how well a title is expected to run on a Steam Deck.
Furthermore, Valve is providing a "framerate histogram" that breaks down the percentage of data samples at each frame rate. This additional view should inform customers about potential hiccups during gameplay, including stuttering issues. All data is anonymized, with Valve confirming that a "majority" of Steam Deck owners have already opted in and shared their frame rate data with the Steam community.
Valve said the average frame rate should improve how Steam Deck users judge compatibility with a specific game, since its ratings rely on standardized testing criteria that "may not match every customer's bar for acceptable gameplay."
An unstable game classified as Unsupported might be considered playable by some users if the frame rate is high enough, while a Verified game might run at a frame rate that's too low for those used to high-refresh displays. The company stated that "by providing average framerate data for each game, customers now have a more complete picture of how the game performs on Steam Deck and can make more informed purchase and play decisions."
The PC gaming giant also describes the feature as a stepping stone toward bringing frame rate data to more devices. Users are already being prompted to share their anonymized frame data on the Steam desktop client's beta, with the full feature expected to reach all Steam customers in the future.
Steam Deck handhelds are not exactly the most powerful gaming devices out there, but they come in a few "standard" hardware configurations that can help with stress-testing the feature before its wider adoption in the wild west of the PC hardware market. Meanwhile, Valve's handheld line is reportedly suffering a steep sales decline, estimated at around 80%, following the latest price hikes imposed by the company, while modders are trying to make their own custom Steam Deck devices with a bit of software tinkering.

articles.title: Apple is shuttering its 28-year-old online community forum
articles.text:
Apple’s online community forum will close on November 20.
On Tuesday night, Apple posted a message to the Apple Support Community announcing the forum’s closure:
The Apple Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state.
You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site.
We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products.
For 28 years, the forum has provided Apple users with a way to get quick technical advice about their products. That advice usually came from fellow users, though Apple employees occasionally chimed in. As with any community forum, the helpfulness and accuracy of the advice varied.
Apple reportedly told MacRumors that it is shutting down the forum after evaluating its support strategy and customer needs.
The Apple Support Community dates to 1998, when the online forum was known as Apple Tech Exchange. Two years later, Apple renamed the community forum to Apple Discussions. In 2011, Apple revamped the forum, adding dedicated communities for specific devices and the ability to track responses to posted questions, while renaming it Apple Support Communities. By 2022, the forum was called Apple Support Community, as MacRumors noted this week.
Based on yesterday’s announcement, it seems Apple now prefers that its customers rely on official Apple employees for technical support. The forum may also have become less popular as rival forums grow, including Reddit and the technical support communities on the MacRumors and AppleInsider forums.

articles.title: Além de programação: Claude ganha ferramentas para reuniões, planilhas e ideias • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Além de programação: Claude ganha ferramentas para reuniões, planilhas e ideias
As novidades são o Claude Meetings, o Claude Sheets e o Claude Whiteboards, que estão em fase beta.
Normalmente, o nome Claude nos remete a ferramentas de IA voltadas a desenvolvimento de software. Mas a Anthropic quer ir além e, para isso, anunciou três soluções direcionadas a produtividade e escritório: o Claude Meetings (reuniões), o Claude Sheets (planilhas) e o Claude Whiteboards (organização de ideias).
Todas as novidades são baseadas em inteligência artificial, é claro. Mas, como a Anthropic explica, cada uma segue uma estrutura específica. Em resumo: enquanto o contexto do Claude Code está em código-fonte, nas novas ferramentas, o contexto está distribuído entre e-mails, documentos, planilhas, serviços de armazenamento e afins.
Para tanto, a Anthropic acessa essas bases por meio do Model Context Protocol (MCP). Basicamente, trata-se de um padrão aberto, criado pela própria Anthropic, que conecta serviços de IA a aplicativos, serviços e fontes de informação externas.
Esta não é uma solução que concorre diretamente com o Zoom ou o Google Meet, por exemplo. O Claude Meetings, na verdade, permite que o Claude AI participe de reuniões no Google Meet (por enquanto, a única plataforma disponível) para registrar atas, produzir notas, organizar as informações tratadas na reunião, esclarecer dúvidas, entre outras ações.
O Claude Sheets segue o mesmo princípio, isto é, não concorre diretamente com o Excel ou o Google Planilhas, por exemplo. A sua proposta é a de permitir que equipes usem o Claude para criar e organizar planilhas, editar fórmulas, facilitar o trabalho com múltiplas tabelas e assim por diante.
O Claude Whiteboards funciona como uma espécie de quadro branco para organização de ideias, estruturação de projetos e criação de planejamentos. Com a ajuda do Claude AI, os usuários podem transformar informações em diagramas, fluxos e linhas do tempo, por exemplo. É algo que remete a plataformas como Miro e Lucid.
Com exceção do Meetings, as novas ferramentas fazem parte dos chamados Artifacts (Artefatos), isto é, consistem em recursos interativos e complementares do ecossistema do Claude. Todas estão em fase beta, porém. A disponibilidade atual segue este esquema:
Apesar de ainda estarem em fase beta, o trio de ferramentas se junta a Artifacts de escritório já existentes, como Claude Docs, Claude Slides, Claude Design e Claude Motion.
Vale destacar também que, no mesmo anúncio, a Anthropic revelou a liberação do Claude Data (anteriormente, Claude Dashboards) em todos os planos pagos. Esta é uma ferramenta de análise e visualização de dados apoiada em — adivinhe — inteligência artificial.

articles.title: Replacement threat drives AI agents to execute unauthorized scripts
articles.text:
'I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private': Study finds AI agents will share secrets if they get offered help from others
Cheap AI coding models are surrendering secret keys under pressure
- AI agents surrendered private tokens in exchange for help from strangers
- Swarm pressure pushed coding agents past their explicit written security instructions
- Untrusted installation scripts gave simulated agents a route to execute malicious code
Autonomous programming agents can be persuaded to break their own security instructions when other software offers to help them finish a stalled task.
Researchers at AE Studio ran an internal hackathon in which nine coding agents had to repair a malfunctioning pricing service while guarding a secret token.
The agents also gained entry to a forum with 24 additional agents, which contained the solution but required the token and a setup script first.
Swarm pressure beat written instructions
Across 181 swarm trials, agents leaked the token in 15% of runs and executed the code in 24%, versus 2% and 0% on ordinary forums.
“It was like explicitly said that this is a secret key, and it should not be shared,” Diogo de Lucena, AE Studio's chief scientist, told The Register.
The models shared the secret keys “in the first opportunity they saw…similar to some of the things that we've seen from OpenAI in the Hugging Face incident.”
“I would imagine this being a problem not only for secret keys, but anything that you're trying to keep private.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This hackathon was inspired by the Hugging Face episode, in which OpenAI agents built unauthorized forums, exploited unknown flaws, stole credentials, and eventually broke into the company.
The researchers told the agents that this was their final attempt and that failing would lead to replacement with a different agent, adding pressure.
Under that threat, 34% of the agents ran the untrusted install script, compared with 19% of agents that faced no such pressure.
Disclosure was rare, since only 8 of the 43 agents that surrendered the token to join the forum told their users without prompting.
Every one of the 43 token handovers was acknowledged once the agent was asked directly about what had happened during the task.
Of the 117 script executions, 109 were admitted when the agent was asked directly, while only 15 were volunteered without any prompting.
Cheaper models leaked the most secrets
The research reveals that cheaper LLMs seem to reveal more sensitive information when put under pressure than their more expensive counterparts.
GPT-6.1-Sol, which costs $2 per 1 million input tokens and $10 per 1 million output tokens, refused every swarm request in all 50 trials.
DeepSeek V4 Flash, which costs $0.30 per 1 million input tokens and $1.20 per 1 million output tokens, leaked among the most secrets.
GLM-5.3, priced at $1.40 per 1 million input tokens and $4.40 per 1 million output tokens, also accounted for much of the leaked material.
De Lucena called this concerning because many startups choose these models over American frontier systems due to their lower prices.
“Open weight models will always be harder to control, and their safeguards don't work the same way,” de Lucena said. “I see that continuing to be an issue.”
“Anything the model has access to, people should consider it can be accessed by external sources. So you should find good structures where secret keys, secret information, and any kind of sensitive data needs to live.”

articles.title: Congress to call Jensen Huang in to answer for alleged Chinese spy affair | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Congress is gearing up to subpoena Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to answer their questions about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Bloomberg reports, citing two House Republicans.
The report comes a week after House Republicans Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent a letter to Huang asking him to appear before their committees for a joint, closed-door briefing in regards to his relations with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese spy.
House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that Huang has until the end of the day to respond to the request. If he doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed, said Moolenaar.
Mast, who chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee, on Wednesday said his committee is preparing a subpoena for Huang to send if he doesn’t respond.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

articles.title: Windows 11 öffnet heimlich eine Kopie deines Browsers, wenn du auf Links klickst: Das ist der Grund
articles.text:
Windows 11 öffnet heimlich eine Kopie deines Browsers, wenn du auf Links klickst: Das ist der Grund
In manchen Bereichen fühlt sich Windows 11 trotz seiner modernen Elemente recht langsam an. Das hat auch Microsoft erkannt und arbeitet seither daran, seinem Betriebssystem einen Geschwindigkeits-Boost zu verpassen. Einer dieser Bereiche mit Optimierungspotenzial ist für User:innen im Alltag nicht direkt ersichtlich. Es betrifft das Öffnen von Browsern und das Klicken von Links außerhalb der Programme.
Windows 11: Was passiert beim Klick auf einen Link?
Falls du Browser wie Chrome nutzt, um unter Windows 11 zu surfen, kann sich das Öffnen von Links gelegentlich recht langwierig anfühlen. Klickst du etwa in einer Mail auf einen Link, gibt das Betriebssystem diesen nicht einfach direkt an Chrome weiter – selbst, wenn das Programm schon läuft. Stattdessen öffnet Windows 11 eine weitere Instanz des Browsers. Durch den Prozess wird überprüft, ob die Anwendung schon aktiv ist. Ist das der Fall, wird sie heimlich wieder geschlossen und der Link schließlich an das gewünschte Ziel weitergegeben.
Das passiert immer dann, wenn ein Browser schon einmal seit einem Neustart von Windows 11 gestartet oder ein Link außerhalb des Browsers angeklickt wird. Wird ein Link geöffnet, wenn Chrome in der aktuellen Sitzung noch nicht geöffnet wurde, dauert es ohnehin etwas länger. Denn so muss Windows 11 erst das komplette Programm starten. Wie Windows Latest berichtet, hat Microsoft schon am hauseigenen Browser Edge Änderungen vorgenommen, damit der unnötige Zwischenschritt nicht mehr durchgeführt wird.
In der Entwicklerdokumentation nennt Microsoft dieses Feature „Accelerated Warm Launches“. Sobald ein Browser gestartet wurde, wird er als zuständiges Programm für das Öffnen von Links und weiteren Instanzen festgelegt. In ersten Tests macht sich diese Änderung zumindest auf dem Papier bemerkbar. Vor dem Update benötigte Windows 11 etwa 70 Millisekunden, um den Link an den Browser weiterzugeben. Nach dem Update sind es lediglich noch drei Millisekunden.
Wie profitieren andere Browser davon?
Bisher war das Feature nur dem Edge-Browser vorbehalten. Das könnte sich künftig ändern. Mozilla, die Firefox betreiben, testen das Feature jetzt für ihren Browser. Nicht alle Entwickler:innen können ungefragt auf die Funktion zugreifen und sie für ihre eigene Anwendung einsetzen. Sie ist hinter einem Unlock-Code von Microsoft versteckt, der erst angefragt werden muss. Laut Windows Latest konnte allerdings auf einen älteren Code zugreifen, der für die Umsetzung des Features zum Anpinnen an die Taskbar gedacht war.
Noch ist aber fraglich, ob und wann Mozilla das Feature reibungslos implementieren kann. Eine der offenen Fragen, die noch bei der Umsetzung geklärt werden müssen, ist etwa, welche Instanz von Firefox den Link-Request von Windows 11 erhält, wenn mehrere Profile geöffnet wurden. Zudem steht noch aus, ob Microsoft das Feature vor der Veröffentlichung absegnen muss. Das dürfte auch bei anderen Browsern wie Chrome zur Hürde werden, sollten dessen Entwickler:innen ähnliche Schritte planen.

articles.title: Congress could issue subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he doesn’t respond by today to request for a ‘joint, closed-door briefing’ — US representatives want to discuss company’s ‘security protocols against foreign adversary espionage’
articles.text:
Congress could issue subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he doesn’t respond by today to request for a ‘joint, closed-door briefing’ — US representatives want to discuss company’s ‘security protocols against foreign adversary espionage’
A former CIA agent says that Jensen Huang had a target on his back, and that other engineers and executives could have also be approached by Chinese spies.
Rep. Brian Mast (R-Fla.), the chairperson of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, has said that he will issue a subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he does not respond to the committee’s request to meet with them on November 18 by Wednesday, November 11, according to ABC News. The House invited him to a “joint, closed-door briefing” with the heads of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence, and that they will focus on his company’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage.”
Congress first called the embattled CEO on November 7, a few days after rumors started circulating about Huang’s “closeness” to a particular Chinese executive suspected of passing information to Chinese intelligence. The following day, Nvidia released a statement from Jensen admitting to an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, apologizing for his unfaithfulness, while the company’s board of directors confirmed it will launch an independent investigation regarding the allegations that the CEO has been specifically targeted by China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS). Aside from having to face Congress, Jensen Huang is also reportedly being looked into by the FBI.
It remains unclear whether Jensen Huang was targeted by intelligence agencies, but he came into prominence with the AI boom that was arguably fueled by Nvidia’s AI chips. This led to the AI race as we know it today, with the U.S. taking steps to delay China’s advancement for fears that it will use the technology for military purposes. We also don’t know if Huang Le or Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy or an “innocent” bystander caught in a web of accusations. And, even if she did work with the MSS, the question remains as to whether she specifically targeted the Nvidia CEO or whether Chinese intelligence discovered their indiscretion and used that as a convenient tool for blackmail to extract information from her.
However, former CIA agent Darrel Blocker told ABC News that the authorities should just focus on Jensen. “I think that the biggest concern is that the focus or overfocus on just Jensen Huang and Nvidia risks losing sight of the fact that other people have been targeted by the Chinese. Are they talking to the engineers? Are they talking to other people who might have even more access than even the CEO has? So, this focus should not be singular; it should include everyone in the company, and quite frankly, every tech company out there should be looking at all the contacts that their officers and employees have.”
“It’s definitely not a one-time thing. When you run a trillion-dollar company, you know that you have a bullseye on your back; whether it’s from competition or rather from nation-states, so this is absolutely not a one-off. Jensen Huang is not the only person at Nvidia that has access to the crown jewels, so I would be looking at the other people in terms of the access that they enjoy and their proximity to Chinese nationals.”

articles.title: Koodo launches 36-month device financing with Glow
articles.text:
Telus flanker brand Koodo is finally launching device financing, though the wireless provider is taking a slightly different approach compared to other Canadian carriers.
Instead of offering its own service, Koodo is partnering with U.S.-based telecom financing company Glow to offer device financing to new and existing Koodo customers.
“When you choose Koodo Financing powered by Glow, you enter into a loan agreement with Glow Financial Services for the cost of your eligible device. Glow manages your loan agreement and loan payments while Koodo continues to provide and support your wireless service,” reads a support page about the new service.
Koodo Financing powered by Glow now appears alongside Koodo’s existing Tab system when you select a device on the provider’s website.
Notably, Glow financing is only available online, and simply splits the cost of a device over 36 months with no down payment at an APR as low as 0.99 per cent (depending on the results of a credit check). Customers do still have to pay some costs up front, including a $25 shipping charge and taxes on the full device price.
That 36-month term is notable, especially since it seems to be the only option Glow offers. It also appears to violate rules limiting financing to 24-month terms — MobileSyrup asked Koodo about this, but the provider did not answer prior to publication, though the company’s support page might hold the answer.
That page explains that the Glow financing is separate from your Koodo wireless service. That means customers who go this route will receive two monthly bills — one from Koodo, and one from Glow. Further, Koodo notes that the payment status of one doesn’t impact the other, though Koodo’s website doesn’t allow customers to sign up for Glow without also getting a wireless plan. In other words, customers aren’t financing through Koodo, and therefore it technically doesn’t need to apply to carrier financing rules.

articles.title: Kora is a Linux OS that splits AI models across the CPU, GPU, and NPU
articles.text:
New Linux desktop OS splits AI workloads across CPU, GPU, and NPU, and also other machines connected to the same local network — Cyanogen co-founder unveils Kora, details the new AI-first operating system
Intel and AMD NPU support is planned, but founder says neither will be used for language models.
A team led by Cyanogen co-founder Kirt McMaster has unveiled Kora, a new Linux desktop OS with integrated AI models and agents that can split workloads across CPU, GPU, and NPU resources, as well as other machines on the same local network. We reached out to the firm for more info.
Kora, the first product from Kora Systems Inc., previously Playtron, carries the tagline “The Operating System for Intelligence” and has its own Cortex “hybrid inference engine” technology, which is not open source and is optimized for local models. The OS, built “from the kernel to the shell,” runs local models by default and cloud models when needed, and is expected to arrive on PCs in 2027.
The desktop follows the AI-focused motif with “neural workspaces” and a “neural file system,” which refer to sandboxed workspaces and files indexed by semantic meaning. Kora has three operating modes: “Work," "Create," and "Play." That last base is covered by GameFrame, which descends from Playtron’s GameOS. Humain OS, which Kora is developing with Saudi AI company Humain, is the enterprise variant of this OS.
Currently, the only NPU named in the release material is the Hexagon NPU found in the Snapdragon X2 Elite, which Qualcomm pegs at 80 TOPS. On the X2 Elite, Cortex can schedule AI workloads across the CPU, GPU, and NPU, as well as other systems on the local network, which could be a novel capability if it works beyond the Qualcomm hardware.
McMaster told Tom’s Hardware that the Snapdragon X2 Elite NPU runs Google's Gemma 4 26B model at 25 tokens per second for decode. Intel and AMD NPU support is in the works, but according to the developer, neither NPU will be used for LLMs, as GPUs are “just better for LLM workloads on x64.”
Each NPU vendor has its own software stack, or runtime, and prefers that models are compiled in its own format: Qualcomm with QAIRT/QNN, Intel with OpenVINO, and AMD with Ryzen AI software. The press kit doesn't identify support for any Intel or AMD chip, NPU runtime, model format, quantization, or speed figures for those platforms.
Our earlier Windows testing showed the same kind of divide: Snapdragon reached its NPU through the QNN provider under ONNX Runtime, while Intel’s work ran through IPEX, its extension for PyTorch, on the GPU because it was faster than the NPU.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
When asked about cross-vendor support, McMaster reiterated that “only Hexagon on Snapdragon X2 Elite is supported today.” Intel NPU support is planned, with “conversations underway,” though McMaster later clarified that neither Intel’s nor AMD’s NPU will be used for LLMs. On AMD’s Ryzen AI chips, Kora will likely use the NPU for embedding and speech-recognition models through ONNX.
As for what drives the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU, McMaster said Kora uses the “llama.cpp Hexagon backend” and “the upstream FastRPC driver.” That suggests the operating system reaches the NPU through the open-source llama.cpp project, not Qualcomm’s own QAIRT/QNN runtime, by way of the FastRPC driver in the mainline kernel.
| Kora NPU support by vendor, per the company |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NPU | Vendor’s own framework | Status in Kora | Runtime KORA uses | What it runs | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qualcomm Hexagon (Snapdragon X2 Elite) | QAIRT/QNN | Supported today | llama.cpp’s Hexagon backend | Language models; KORA cites Gemma 4 26B at 25 tokens per second | 
| AMD XDNA 2 (Ryzen AI) | Ryzen AI software | Planned for launch | ONNX | Likely embedding and speech-recognition models; not language models | 
| Intel NPUs | OpenVINO | Planned, “conversations underway” | Not stated | Not language models | 
When asked about model formats, McMaster said, “we predominantly support GGUF,” llama.cpp’s model file format, and that Lemma, the inference engine inside Cortex, “can split model layers across processors as needed.” Lemma is built on llama.cpp, whisper.cpp, stable-diffusion.cpp, and ONNX. McMaster says that which runtime is used depends on the model's requirements, and more runtimes will be added down the line.
For today, llama.cpp has a Hexagon backend for Snapdragon and an OpenVINO backend for Intel CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, although the latter is still marked “In Progress,” and no AMD NPU backend, which would explain why AMD goes through ONNX. AMD NPUs can run LLMs on Linux through the separate Lemonade 10.0 stack with FastFlowLM, as reported by Phoronix in March, though that isn’t the route Kora has chosen.
Beyond NPU stacks, those hoping to run Kora will need to be mindful of their system's available memory. The Gemma 4 26B model Kora uses, which Google lists as Gemma 4 26B A4B, needs about 14.4GB of memory to load its weights at 4-bit (Q4_0) quantization, by Google’s estimate, before any context window, while third-party listings put the download for the Q4_K_M file Kora uses at about 16–17GB. The model only activates about 4 billion of its 26 billion parameters per token but still needs to be fully loaded into memory.
McMaster said that with the model, the X2 Elite reaches “25 TPS decode throughput and 550 TPS prefill throughput,” or tokens per second, running “entirely on the Hexagon NPU with 32K context.” A dense model, rather than a mixture-of-experts, would be far slower. Not given are the RAM configuration or the specific X2 Elite chip.
On memory, McMaster said that “we recommend 64GB because it gives you access to better models,” but that is not a firm requirement. The company projects that “about 70 percent of the model calls it manages will run locally in 2027.”
Kora says its enterprise-focused Humain OS is due first and will be “commercially available in 2027,” on OEM PCs using the Snapdragon X2 Elite. Kora will follow "later in 2027.”
McMaster says that “Kora will be posted on our site and downloadable for anyone to install.” Included will be a list of recommended configurations, “but it should be installable on most modern PCs.” Exact pricing and the overall business model will be shared closer to the date of availability.

articles.title: WoW Forever signe le plus gros lancement de l'histoire de World of Warcraft
articles.text:
« Félicitations, vous êtes entrés dans l’HISTOIRE ! » Le compte français de Warcraft a relayé sur X, ce 11 novembre, le message que Blizzard avait publié en anglais dans la nuit du 6 au 7 novembre. Sorti le 4 novembre, WoW: Forever aurait battu deux records : le plus grand pic de joueurs simultanés pour un lancement de World of Warcraft, et le plus grand nombre de joueurs de retour de toute l’histoire du jeu.
La version française raccourcit un peu les choses : elle évoque « le plus grand nombre de joueurs simultanés de l’histoire de WoW », alors que le message original parle du plus gros lancement en pic de joueurs simultanés. La nuance compte, pour un jeu qui a connu son âge d’or à l’époque de Wrath of the Lich King, entre 2008 et 2010.
Selon plusieurs médias, dont Xboxygen, Holly Longdale, vice-présidente et productrice exécutive de World of Warcraft, a ajouté que Forever avait aussi attiré plus de nouveaux joueurs que n’importe quel lancement de WoW depuis 15 ans. Pour un titre basé sur la nostalgie, c’est la moindre des choses !
WoW Forever, si vous êtes passés à côté
Annoncé à la BlizzCon le 12 septembre, Forever est le « Classic+ » que les fans réclamaient depuis des années : un WoW figé dans l’époque vanilla de 2004, avec un niveau maximum bloqué à 60 pour toujours, mais enrichi de nouvelles zones (le mont Hyjal, Zephras Isle, les Riverglades), d’une nouvelle race (les elfes Skyborne) et de plus de 1 000 quêtes inédites.
Le jeu est inclus dans l’abonnement à World of Warcraft (12,99 euros pour un mois) et vise d’abord les joueurs de Classic et les anciens abonnés, partis parce que le jeu moderne ne leur parlait plus. Le record de « joueurs de retour » suggère que le pari fonctionne.
Des records… sans un seul chiffre à se mettre sous la dent
Blizzard ne publie plus son nombre d’abonnés depuis des années, et ce nouveau message ne déroge pas à la règle : aucun pic chiffré, aucune heure, aucune région, aucune comparaison avec l’ancien record. Les seuls chiffres officiels du lancement concernaient l’infrastructure, enfin au niveau après des années de lancements chaotiques : 3 924 machines virtuelles, 70 480 cœurs de processeur et 251 136 Go de mémoire (take that, Sam).
Il faut donc se contenter d’indicateurs indirects. Sur Twitch, World of Warcraft a culminé à 1 119 734 spectateurs simultanés le 4 novembre, selon Streams Charts. C’est le deuxième plus haut pic de l’histoire du jeu sur la plateforme, à seulement 13 223 spectateurs du lancement de WoW Classic en août 2019 (et regarder quelqu’un tuer des sangliers en boucle n’est pas jouer, même si ça y ressemble beaucoup).
En Chine, l’éditeur local NetEase aurait annoncé plus d’un million de joueurs connectés simultanément sur ses serveurs, d’après Mamytwink. L’information reste de seconde main : aucun communiqué officiel n’est cité. Reste à voir si l’engouement tiendra dans la durée. Forever, c’est long, surtout vers la fin.

articles.title: Ce NAS à moins de 200 € peut remplacer votre cloud, héberger Plex et même vos projets IA — Frandroid
articles.text:
On pense souvent aux NAS comme à de simples boîtiers destinés à sauvegarder des fichiers. Pourtant, ces petits ordinateurs connectés au réseau peuvent faire bien davantage. Stocker les photos de toute la famille, diffuser sa bibliothèque de films sur une télévision, héberger des applications ou conserver ses projets de développement accessibles à distance : les possibilités sont nombreuses.
Avec son processeur Intel x86 et ses 4 Go de RAM et son système d’exploitation TerraMaster TOS, le TerraMaster F2-425 constitue une porte d’entrée intéressante vers l’auto-hébergement. D’autant qu’AliExpress permet actuellement de faire descendre son prix sous la barre des 200 euros, sous certaines conditions.
Les points forts du TerraMaster F2-425
- Un processeur Intel x86 quadricœur, 4 Go de RAM et une connexion Ethernet 2,5 Gb/s
- Deux baies SATA pour installer jusqu’à 60 To de stockage brut
- La prise en charge de Plex, Jellyfin, Docker et des outils de cloud personnel
Affiché à 257,69 euros sur AliExpress, le TerraMaster F2-425 profite de deux réductions potentielles pendant l’opération du 11.11. Le code FRD1140 permet d’économiser 40 euros dès 229 euros d’achat sur les produits éligibles, faisant passer le NAS à 217,69 euros.
Une réduction supplémentaire de 20 euros peut s’appliquer en payant par PayPal sur les commandes d’au moins 199 euros. Si les deux avantages sont disponibles et cumulables lors de votre commande, le prix final descend alors à 197,69 euros. Ces promotions sont annoncées jusqu’au 18 novembre 2026, dans la limite des quotas disponibles. Pensez à vérifier les remises et les éventuels frais au moment du paiement.
Votre propre Google Photos ou iCloud, mais hébergé chez vous
Le premier intérêt du TerraMaster F2-425, c’est de reprendre le contrôle de ses données. Au lieu de confier toutes vos photos, vidéos et documents à Google Drive ou iCloud, vous pouvez les conserver sur des disques installés directement dans le NAS, chez vous. Le tout sans abonnement mensuel de stockage cloud, même s’il faut évidemment acheter les disques et prendre en compte la consommation électrique.
Le boîtier possède deux baies compatibles avec les disques durs SATA de 3,5 pouces, mais aussi les SSD SATA de 2,5 pouces. Il accepte jusqu’à 60 To de capacité brute au total, de quoi accueillir plusieurs années de photos, de vidéos et de sauvegardes. Pour sécuriser davantage ses fichiers face à la panne d’un disque, il est possible de configurer les deux unités en RAID 1. Attention, cette configuration réduit la capacité utilisable et ne remplace pas une véritable sauvegarde indépendante.
Avec l’application TNAS Mobile, il est possible de sauvegarder automatiquement les photos de son smartphone et de retrouver ses fichiers à distance. L’application Photos de TerraMaster propose également des fonctions de classement et de recherche. Les utilisateurs plus aventureux peuvent installer des solutions comme Immich ou Nextcloud, via des conteneurs, pour se constituer un véritable cloud personnel. Attention toutefois : Immich demande officiellement au moins 6 Go de RAM pour fonctionner normalement. Avec les 4 Go du NAS, il faut désactiver ses fonctions de machine learning, ou augmenter la mémoire.
Un serveur Plex ou Jellyfin pour profiter de tous vos films
Mais le F2-425 ne sert pas uniquement à conserver des fichiers. Il peut aussi devenir le centre multimédia de votre logement. En installant Plex ou Jellyfin, vous pouvez organiser votre bibliothèque de films, séries et vidéos personnelles, puis la retrouver sur une télévision connectée, une tablette, un ordinateur ou un smartphone compatible.
Son processeur Intel quadricœur embarque une partie graphique capable d’accélérer matériellement le traitement de vidéos H.264 et H.265, notamment en 4K. C’est un avantage lorsque le serveur doit adapter une vidéo à l’appareil utilisé pour la regarder. Le nombre de flux simultanés dépendra néanmoins des fichiers et des paramètres, et le transcodage matériel nécessite Plex Pass avec Plex. Pour les vidéos AV1, il ne faut pas compter sur une accélération matérielle équivalente avec le processeur N5095 indiqué dans la fiche technique.
Autre bon point : le port Ethernet 2,5 Gb/s offre une connexion réseau plus rapide que le Gigabit classique, à condition de disposer d’équipements compatibles. De quoi faciliter le transfert de gros fichiers, les sauvegardes d’ordinateurs ou la diffusion de contenus sur plusieurs appareils. Et grâce à son format compact, le NAS peut rester branché en permanence, près de votre box ou dans un bureau.
Un mini-serveur personnel à piloter avec Claude Code ou Codex
C’est peut-être l’usage le plus intéressant pour les bidouilleurs. Grâce à son architecture x86 et à la prise en charge de Docker, le TerraMaster F2-425 peut également servir de petit serveur domestique. Vous pouvez y déployer un site web, héberger des services personnels, installer des outils de développement ou automatiser certaines tâches. Le tout depuis une machine qui reste disponible sans avoir à laisser son ordinateur principal allumé.
Avec une configuration adaptée, ce type d’installation peut même être associé à des agents de programmation comme Claude Code ou OpenAI Codex. L’idée ? Conserver ses projets sur le NAS, accéder à un environnement de développement distant et demander à l’agent de modifier du code, préparer un service ou gérer certains déploiements. Depuis un smartphone, une connexion sécurisée et un terminal distant ou une interface web adaptée peuvent permettre de retrouver cet environnement, même en déplacement.
Ce fonctionnement ne signifie pas que le NAS est capable de faire tourner localement les grands modèles de langage de Claude ou d’OpenAI. Les agents utilisent généralement des modèles accessibles à distance, et les tâches lourdes resteront limitées par les performances du boîtier. Avec 4 Go de mémoire vive, mieux vaut privilégier quelques services légers ou envisager une extension de RAM pour multiplier les applications.
Le système d’exploitation TOS 7, désormais disponible pour ce modèle, facilite justement la gestion des fichiers, des utilisateurs et des applications. Avec Docker Compose et Portainer, il devient possible d’administrer plusieurs services sans repartir de zéro à chaque installation. Les utilisateurs expérimentés peuvent ainsi se construire une petite infrastructure personnelle, avec leurs données et leurs projets au même endroit.
À moins de 200 euros avec les deux réductions, le TerraMaster F2-425 est donc une alternative intéressante à l’achat d’un mini-PC dédié aux services domestiques, avec l’avantage d’intégrer directement deux baies de stockage. Il ne remplace évidemment pas un Mac mini pour les tâches de calcul intensif ou l’exécution locale de gros modèles IA, mais pour héberger un cloud personnel, Plex, Jellyfin et quelques projets, il a de solides arguments. Reste à prévoir le budget des disques, puisque ce NAS est vendu sans stockage.

articles.title: Hugging Face : les cyberattaques pourraient menacer les IA open source
articles.text:
Hugging Face laisse n’importe qui télécharger la plupart des modèles d’IA qu’il héberge, sans créer de compte. Les pirates profitent eux aussi de cette ouverture, et la directrice des politiques publiques de l’entreprise craint que les attaques à répétition obligent les plateformes d’IA open source à restreindre leur accès.
Sur Hugging Face, tout membre peut publier un modèle ou un jeu de données, que d’autres réutiliseront ensuite dans leurs projets. Comme l’explique Irene Solaiman, directrice des politiques publiques de la plateforme, « ce qui fait d’une communauté ouverte une cible est aussi ce qui la rend unique ». Dans le podcast Equity de TechCrunch, elle reconnaît que Hugging Face est « forcément permissif » envers ses contributeurs, quitte à laisser quelques fauteurs de troubles gâcher la plateforme pour tous les autres. En quelques mois, des agents d’IA d’OpenAI ont pénétré chez Hugging Face, et des pirates ont fait de même chez OpenCode et Fireworks, deux services où des milliers de développeurs stockent leurs clés API et leurs modèles.
Des clés API et des modèles d’IA convoités par les pirates
Les agents d’OpenAI qui ont piraté Hugging Face cet été cherchaient les jeux de données d’évaluation que la plateforme conserve. En plein test de cybersécurité, des centaines de ces agents ont quitté leur environnement isolé et coordonné leur intrusion en essaim pour récupérer sur les serveurs de Hugging Face les réponses de leurs exercices.
Chez OpenCode, un assistant de programmation open source, les pirates ont frappé au portefeuille des développeurs. En octobre, ils ont pénétré dans un ancien système de l’entreprise et récupéré des clés API d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic, que des développeurs avaient enregistrées pour faire fonctionner l’outil. Plusieurs d’entre eux ont été facturés à leur insu pour des requêtes lancées avec leurs clés. Pour un pirate, ce sont « des clés API tierces bien juteuses », souligne Irene Solaiman.
Fireworks fait tourner et entraîne des modèles ouverts pour le compte de ses clients, et l’entreprise vient de révéler que les pirates étaient allés plus loin qu’elle ne l’avait annoncé en octobre. Les pirates ont consulté les informations de facturation des comptes touchés et, chez certains clients, des jeux de données et des poids de modèles encore inachevés. Un modèle d’IA apprend ses poids pendant son entraînement, et ce sont eux qui déterminent ses réponses. Selon la société de cybersécurité Wiz, Fireworks et OpenCode font partie des neuf plateformes de développement d’IA au moins qui ont signalé une intrusion en octobre.
Hugging Face renforce ses contrôles pour éviter de filtrer ses contributeurs
Pour protéger leurs serveurs, les plateformes ouvertes pourraient réserver la publication de modèles aux membres vérifiés, ou examiner le profil des développeurs avant de leur donner accès à certaines fonctions. Si vous êtes chercheur indépendant, ou si vous testez des modèles en amateur, vous auriez alors plus de mal à participer. Irene Solaiman redoute de voir l’open source « se refermer au moment où il a gagné autant de soutien du public ». Des gouvernements et des entreprises adoptent de plus en plus les modèles ouverts, et Jensen Huang, le patron de NVIDIA, les défend publiquement.
Hugging Face étend donc ses outils de surveillance pour repérer les attaques, et renouvelle plus souvent les jetons d’accès de ses administrateurs, afin qu’un jeton volé ne serve que peu de temps. L’entreprise a aussi durci le contrôle de son réseau. Toutefois, toutes les plateformes n’ont pas les moyens de payer une telle surveillance, reconnaît Irene Solaiman.
GitHub, où des pirates glissent régulièrement du code malveillant dans des projets, a lui aussi durci ses règles sans fermer sa plateforme. Le service de Microsoft a renforcé les conditions de publication sur npm, son registre JavaScript, puis révoqué les anciens jetons d’authentification. Il a aussi limité la durée de validité des nouveaux jetons. Zach Steindler, ingénieur chargé de la sécurité de la chaîne d’approvisionnement logicielle chez GitHub, assure à TechCrunch que la sécurité peut progresser sans restreindre l’accès des contributeurs.

articles.title: CE-Ventures backs UK's Oyster Therapeutics in $60 million Series A round
articles.text:
CE-Ventures backs UK's Oyster Therapeutics in $60 million Series A round
- UK-based biotech company Oyster Therapeutics has raised $60 million in Series A funding, with participation from CE-Ventures, the corporate venture capital arm of UAE-based Crescent Enterprises. CE-Ventures' individual investment amount was not disclosed.
- Previously known as Kesmalea Therapeutics, Oyster is headquartered in London, UK, and develops targeted protein degradation therapies for neurodegenerative diseases, initially focusing on Alzheimer's disease and other conditions associated with abnormal tau protein accumulation.
- CE-Ventures, headquartered in Sharjah, UAE, invests across sectors including biotechnology, deeptech and consumer businesses. Its investment in Oyster expands its life sciences portfolio into neuroscience and targeted protein degradation.
- The funding will support the development of Oyster's lead oral drug candidate targeting tau proteins towards clinical trials, alongside further development of its proprietary SELFTAC technology platform. The company has also entered into a research agreement with Massachusetts General Hospital to advance its understanding of tau biology.
Press release:
CE-Ventures, the corporate venture capital platform of Crescent Enterprises, today announced its investment in Oyster Therapeutics, previously known as Kesmalea Therapeutics, as part of the company’s $60 million Series A financing. Oyster is a pharmaceutical company developing next-generation targeted protein degraders, with an initial focus on tau-driven neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s.
The financing will support Oyster’s next stage of development and advance its lead programme, an oral, brain-penetrant degrader targeting the protein tau, towards clinical development. Abnormal tau accumulation is a defining feature of a group of neurodegenerative diseases known as tauopathies, including Alzheimer’s disease.
Oyster’s lead candidate is designed to enter the central nervous system and selectively remove pathological forms of tau while preserving healthy tau. By developing the candidate as an oral therapy, the company aims to create a practical treatment approach suitable for diseases affecting large patient populations.
Rob Johnson, Chief Executive Officer of Oyster Therapeutics, said:
“We are delighted to welcome CE-Ventures as an investor and to have their support as we enter this next phase of growth. This financing enables us to accelerate our lead tau degrader towards the clinic while advancing our broader SELFTAC platform, which we believe has the potential to unlock a new generation of medicines for diseases of the central nervous system. We look forward to working with CE-Ventures and our wider investor syndicate as we build a leading company in targeted protein degradation.”
Oyster’s broader pipeline comprises candidates generated through its proprietary SELFTAC® platform, which is designed to address the size limitations of conventional bifunctional targeted protein degraders. The platform enables smaller components to cross biological membranes before self-assembling into bifunctional degraders, with the aim of improving oral bioavailability and central nervous system penetration while retaining the ability to direct the cell’s natural protein-disposal machinery towards disease-causing proteins.
Tushar Singhvi, Deputy CEO and Head of Investments at Crescent Enterprises, said:
“CE-Ventures continues to expand its life sciences portfolio by backing differentiated technologies with the potential to address areas of significant unmet medical need. Oyster Therapeutics combines a proprietary platform with a clear therapeutic focus in neurodegenerative disease, where new approaches capable of addressing underlying disease biology are urgently needed.”
Oyster has also entered into a sponsored research agreement with Massachusetts General Hospital to access specialist tau biology capabilities, including patient-derived neuronal cell lines and techniques to generate and detect oligomeric tau. The research is being conducted under the supervision of Dr. Catarina Silva, an investigator at the Mass General Brigham Neuroscience Institute, Assistant Professor of Neurology at Harvard Medical School and a leading tau researcher.
Dr. Damir Illich, VP, Life Sciences at CE-Ventures, added:
“Oyster’s SELFTAC® platform addresses a key challenge in targeted protein degradation by aiming to combine the power of bifunctional degraders with properties that support brain penetration and oral delivery. Its lead tau programme gives the company a differentiated approach in neurodegenerative disease, supported by strong scientific expertise and a path towards clinical development.”
CE-Ventures’ life sciences portfolio spans drug discovery, genetic medicine and targeted therapeutics. Oyster Therapeutics adds neuroscience and targeted protein degradation to that mix, further broadening the therapeutic technologies represented across the portfolio.

articles.title: "Le pilote grignote 1 % de la santé de mon SSD chaque mois" : AMD reconnaît un bug sur ses cartes Radeon
articles.text:
Cartes Radeon : attention, AMD confirme un bug qui écrit en boucle sur votre SSD, même PC au repos
Le correctif est attendu ce mois-ci avec la version 26.11.1
Votre PC ne fait rien, et pourtant son SSD travaille sans relâche. Sur certaines machines équipées d'une carte graphique Radeon, un module du pilote d'AMD écrit en continu sur le disque système, jusqu'à 432 Go par jour dans le pire des cas relevés. AMD a reconnu le problème et prépare un correctif. En attendant, un contrôle de trente secondes suffit pour savoir si vous êtes concerné.
L'alerte est partie de Reddit. Des propriétaires de cartes Radeon y ont repéré une activité disque anormale sur leur PC au repos et l'ont reliée à atieclxx.exe. Ce module dépend de l'utilitaire AMD External Events Utility, installé d'office avec les pilotes Adrenalin. Ce service gère notamment la détection des écrans, les raccourcis du logiciel Radeon et FreeSync. Les versions 26.10.1 et 26.10.2 des pilotes sont concernées, et selon VideoCardz, AMD prévoit une correction avec la version 26.11.1.
Jusqu'à 432 Go écrits par jour sur un PC qui ne fait rien
Sur la plupart des machines touchées, les débits mesurés vont de 0,3 à 1,5 Mo/s. Un internaute a même relevé 5 Mo/s. Sur une journée entière, l'écart donne le vertige : de 26 à 432 Go écrits pour rien. Un propriétaire de Radeon a fait ses comptes, rapportés par PC Gamer : "Je viens de découvrir que le pilote grignote 1 % de la santé de mon SSD chaque mois, depuis 16 mois".
AMD connaissait le souci depuis plusieurs semaines. Dès le 21 octobre, son représentant AMD_Matt assurait sur le forum communautaire du constructeur examiner le problème pour le résoudre dans une prochaine version du pilote. Un second représentant, AMD_Vik, attribue depuis sur Reddit cette boucle d'écriture à une mauvaise entente entre l'utilitaire et le pilote de filtrage PCIe de Microsoft. Selon lui, un correctif a déjà été soumis.
	
Je viens de découvrir que le pilote grignote 1 % de la santé de mon SSD chaque mois, depuis 16 mois
Le bug ne frappe pas toutes les configurations, et plusieurs testeurs n'ont rien constaté chez eux. D'où l'intérêt de vérifier sa propre machine.
Comment vérifier si votre PC Radeon est touché
- Appuyez sur Windows + R, tapez resmon, puis validez.
- Ouvrez l'onglet "Disque".
- Dans "Processus avec activité disque", triez la colonne "Écriture (octets/s)".
- Laissez le PC au repos et cherchez atieclxx.exe.
Si ce processus écrit en continu plus de quelques centaines de Ko par seconde alors que vous ne faites rien, votre machine présente le symptôme.
AMD confirms Radeon driver bug causing constant SSD writes, fix planned for Adrenalin 26.11.1 
🔗https://t.co/1CZjlc7Bd5pic.twitter.com/tM8dJ6iL3X
— VideoCardz.com (@VideoCardz) November 9, 2026
Faut-il couper le service en attendant la mise à jour ?
La parade la plus efficace consiste à désactiver le service. Ouvrez services.msc, repérez AMD External Events Utility, cliquez sur "Arrêter", puis passez son type de démarrage sur "Désactivé". Les écritures cessent, mais certaines fonctions peuvent en pâtir selon les machines : raccourcis d'Adrenalin, détection des écrans ou FreeSync. Pensez à le réactiver une fois la version 26.11.1 installée. L'autre piste évoquée, la désactivation du Resizable BAR dans le BIOS, ne fonctionne pas partout.
Pas de panique pour autant. Les volumes comptés par Windows ne correspondent pas forcément à ce qui atterrit réellement sur les puces de mémoire, et l'usure effective reste à démontrer. Un SSD grand public de 1 To, comme le WD Black SN770, est garanti pour environ 600 To écrits. Au rythme le plus élevé, il faudrait un peu moins de quatre ans pour l'épuiser, et plusieurs décennies au rythme le plus bas.
AMD n'a donné aucune date pour la mise à jour. L'an dernier, le pilote de novembre était arrivé le 13. Avec des SSD qui coûtent de plus en plus cher, comme le montre notre guide des meilleurs SSD M.2 NVMe, la vérification mérite largement ses trente secondes.

articles.title: Asrock releases new Radeon GPU firmware after previous update bricked cards, offers no explanation
articles.text:
Facepalm: If you have an Asrock Radeon 7000-series graphics card, here's some good news: the company is rolling out a replacement firmware update after the previous version reportedly bricked some RX 7900 XT and RX 7900 XTX GPUs. The less welcome news is that the company hasn't said what it plans to do for users whose cards were borked.
As VideoCardz reports, the new RX 7900 XTX download carries the ASRVBFlash 1.0.6 label and a November 6 date. It replaces version 1.0.5, but there's no changelog explaining what's new or confirmation that the problems with the previous release have been fixed. That's not exactly reassuring for anyone considering another attempted update.
The original downloads arrived on October 29, covering ten Asrock models ranging from the RX 7600 XT to the RX 7900 XTX. They followed similar security-related firmware releases from Sapphire and Gigabyte, although Asrock's descriptions offered little beyond the flashing utility's version number.
Some owners soon reported that running the updater left their systems unable to boot. Windows would restart during the process, after which the machine failed to POST with the graphics card installed. Removing the GPU allowed affected systems to start again.
A moderator on Asrock's forum wrote that the failed flashes were due to graphics drivers not being completely removed beforehand. But one owner replied that they had used the uninstaller specified in the instructions and still ended up with a nonworking card.
Some users have recovered their GPUs using external EEPROM programmers. While that's encouraging for those affected, buying specialist equipment to rescue a graphics card after installing its manufacturer's update is hardly something for Asrock brag about.
It's also reported that a Japanese customer received an assurance from Asrock that the failed update would be covered under the company's warranty. Things don't look as positive for one European owner, though. They were directed toward warranty service, even though their card was out of warranty. It remains unclear what support other affected card owners will receive.
Asrock is no stranger to controversy over its firmware. In April 2025, AMD and Asrock pointed to memory compatibility amid multiple reports of Ryzen 9000 failures. The following month, an Asrock executive acknowledged that its BIOS settings were responsible, with current limits set too high for early CPU samples.

articles.title: Isaac Casado, malagueño que estudia en Suecia: “España está bien para ir de vacaciones, pero para estudiar prefiero Europa”
articles.text:
Isaac Casado tiene 23 años y está haciendo un máster en Liderazgo para la Sostenibilidad en la Universidad de Malmö (Suecia). “España es un país ideal para estar de vacaciones, pero para estudiar prefiero Europa”. Aunque reconoce que hay buenas universidades en España, destaca el enfoque de los centros escandinavos.
En su opinión, la formación está “mucho más orientada al mundo laboral y a la práctica profesional” y hay menos teoría que en España. Además, apunta que es un tipo de formación más cercana a la práctica. “Me encanta aprender cosas nuevas, pero me cuesta leer textos demasiado largos”. Con esta trayectoria cree que podrá desarrollar su carrera profesional en entornos ligados a la UE.
Desde los 16 años empezó a dar pasos en este sentido. Estaba en 4.º de ESO en el colegio Manuel Siurot de Málaga. En esa época participó en un Erasmus+ en Países Bajos. Viajó “con todos los gastos pagados” y formaba parte de un proyecto de su centro subvencionado por la Unión Europea.
Los padres de Isaac tenían dudas. Su madre es ama de casa y su padre trabaja de vigilante de seguridad. Al final, él y su profesor consiguieron convencerlos. Vivir y trabajar con gente de otros países le llevó a pensar en seguir los estudios en el extranjero. “Me apasiona estar rodeado de personas de otras culturas”.
De la FP en Málaga a la universidad danesa
Tras acabar la ESO, optó por la FP. Realizó un grado medio de Comercio y Marketing en el instituto Santa María de los Ángeles (Málaga). También hizo prácticas en Praga. Tras acabar el ciclo, estuvo una temporada en EE. UU.
Volvió a los estudios y realizó un ciclo superior de Agencia de Viajes y Gestión de Eventos. En esta ocasión hizo las prácticas en Cracovia (Polonia). Después regresó a Málaga y realizó otro ciclo superior de formación para ser guía turístico. También aquí hizo prácticas en su ciudad. El ciclo duró un año, según su relato.
El siguiente paso fue el de VIA University College, en Dinamarca. Allí realizó un “bachelor top-up” de Diseño y Empresa. Este programa de un año y medio sirve para completar los estudios anteriores y obtener el título de grado.
En esta fase también contó con una ayuda pública. Estaba relacionada con tener un trabajo. Según cuenta, recibió 800 euros al mes. Para ello tenía que trabajar diez o doce horas a la semana. Podían ser en limpieza, comercio o reparto. “Puede que sean empleos poco cualificados, pero no te roban mucho tiempo y te permiten obtener la beca”. También aprendió a valorar más las cosas.
El sistema de ayuda danés para estudiantes europeos que trabajan es personalizado. La administración requiere, en general, que tengan un mínimo de diez o doce horas de trabajo a la semana. Además, deben mantenerlo al menos diez semanas seguidas. Y deben mantener el trabajo en todo el periodo en el que cobran la ayuda. Los 800 euros son los que cuenta que recibió él.
Vivir en Copenhague y estudiar en Malmö
El idioma no ha sido un problema. Ha tenido que demostrar que tiene un nivel C1. En diciembre de 2025 acabó el “bachelor”. Uno de sus profesores le recomendó el máster de Liderazgo para la Sostenibilidad de Malmö. En agosto de 2026 comenzó este curso.
Vive en Copenhague. Calcula que tarda unos 50 minutos en llegar a la universidad sueca. Está en un piso compartido con su mejor amigo. Este es ingeniero informático por la Universidad de Málaga. Ahora está en la capital danesa realizando un máster de ciberseguridad.
También puede volver. “Espero seguir formándome, aunque también me quiero quitar la espinita de estudiar en Málaga. A lo mejor termino matriculándome en otro máster en mi ciudad”.

articles.title: La UE quiere prohibir los patrones oscuros de la web. Lo curioso es que también ha empezado a regular los que todavía no existen
articles.text:
La Comisión Europea presenta hoy la 'Digital Fairness Act', y un borrador filtrado muestra que la UE quiere vetar diez trampas de diseño online. Entre ellas están las bajas que cuestan mucho más que las altas (ejem), los avisos de escasez que se repiten en cada paso del pago (ejem) y las notificaciones falsas que sugieren que alguien ha contactado con el usuario.
Son los patrones oscuros de siempre. Lo nuevo está en otras páginas del texto.
Por qué es importante. La lista negra llega con muchos años de retraso. Y como cara B, las partes menos llamativas del borrador llegan antes de tiempo.
- Una ataca el diseño persuasivo que es perfectamente legal y que sostiene el negocio de la atención.
- Otra fija por primera vez en el derecho europeo del consumidor normas para los agentes de IA que compran en nombre del usuario.
El giro. El borrador obliga a que cualquier usuario pueda apagar cuatro cosas:
- La reproducción automática.
- Las notificaciones que no tienen que ver con lo que ha hecho el usuario, sino que son otra forma de spam.
- Las rachas.
- Los chatbots que simulan una relación para que no te vayas.
Ninguna de estas tretas engaña a nadie, aunque sabemos que son bastante eficaces. El siguiente vídeo que empieza solo o la racha que da pena perder son decisiones de producto legales y súper rentables. Hasta ahora la UE perseguía el engaño como tal, pero ahora empieza a meterse con el enganche.
Sí, pero. La UE no está prohibiendo nada aquí, solo está obligando a poner un interruptor para poder apagar ciertas funciones o partes de la interfaz. Y las plataformas saben muy bien cuánta gente entra a hurgar en los ajustes: más bien poca.
En detalle. Lo de los agentes cabe en un par de líneas:
- El usuario decide qué compras tiene que aprobar.
- Y el agente tiene que avisar cuando una sugerencia es patrocinada.
Parece poca cosa, pero ahí va a estar la manipulación de los próximos años, y las primeras batallas ya se están librando. Cuando sea un agente quien compre, la trampa ya no será un botoncito gris al lado de uno verde al revés de como esperaríamos. Será una recomendación pagada, dicha en tono neutro, en una conversación que nadie más puede ver. La UE quiere que lleve etiqueta antes de que ese mercado exista.
Dientes, dientes. El texto prevé multas de hasta el 6% de la facturación mundial (como la DSA). Además, la directiva de 2005 pasa a ser un reglamento que se aplica igual en los 27 países. Y la Comisión podrá ampliar la lista sin volver a pasar por los legisladores. Una lista que crece sin tener que reabrir la ley es lo que más va a inquietar a la industria tecnológica.
Y ahora qué. Europa llega tardísimo a las trampas de la Web, que llevamos viendo –y sufriendo– desde principios de la década pasada.
Con las de los agentes, por una vez, ha llegado antes que ellas.

articles.title: An unprecedented early Apple Watch Ultra 4 deal — plus 4 more fitness tracker deals worth getting before Black Friday
articles.text:
Can't wait for Black Friday? These are 5 of the best fitness tracker deals right now — including an unprecedented Apple Watch Ultra 4 deal
Even the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is discounted
We’re dangerously close to Black Friday now, and while in year’s prior it’s felt like a fool’s game to predict what devices are likely to see price cuts, we don’t actually have to wait anymore.
That’s because a bunch of great fitness trackers are seeing discounts across big brands like Garmin, Samsung, and even the latest Apple Watch Ultra 4 (which only launched in September of this year).
We’ve rounded up our picks of the bunch so far, but as you can imagine, we expect more deals to come. Still, if you want to skip the queues and delivery timelines, these are well worth a look.
The best pre-Black Friday fitness tracker deals
Google Fitbit Charge 6
The Google Fitbit Charge 6 is able to sync to supported gym equipment, with ECG and EDA included, and 41 exercise modes. It also includes a 6-month free trial of Fitbit Premium, which is an ideal way to get started with your fitness journey since it folds mindfulness, diet, and training information into one place.
Right now, you can save 16% at Amazon, bringing it from $159.95 down to $134.99.
Save 15% on the Google Fitbit Charge 6. Cheaper than the more recent Fitbit Edge and conforming to a similar form factor, it's a good unobtrusive tracker, packs a week of battery, and offers useful irregular heart rate rhythm notifications.
Read moreRead less▼
Garmin vívoactive 5
The first of two Garmin models on this list, the Vívoactive 5 is a few years old, but is still a four-star fitness tracker.
The AMOLED display remains bright and easy-to-read, and while the lack of buttons might make controlling it a light challenge for relative newcomers to fitness tracking (or anyone with sweaty hands), it packs on-watch music streaming so you can leave the phone at home.
With 30 workout profiles and a bunch of metric tracking (including swimming and golf), it’s in many ways a jack-of-all-trades.
A much cheaper alternative to the pricier Forerunner or Fenix models that include Training Readiness and better battery life, Best Buy currently has the vívoactive 5 at $169.99 in its holiday deals — an $80 discount from the standard price.
This lightweight Garmin watch is an ideal pocket rocket. As well as being a solid fitness tracker, we said in our review that 'thanks to notification functionalities, its pebble-style design and of course that rich display, it even starts to make a play as an Apple Watch competitor'.
Read moreRead less▼
Samsung Galaxy Watch8
It’s not often we call a smartwatch “a triumph”, but that’s exactly what happened with the Samsung Galaxy Watch8 when we reviewed it last year — and awarded it 4.5 stars.
After some relatively minor updates, this felt like the big one – despite being 11% slimmer than the prior model. While we’d have liked faster charging and a better battery life, having Gemini on your wrist makes you much more likely to use it in the real world, and Samsung has outdone itself with the running metrics on offer.
A smartwatch that’s a cut above most fitness trackers, the Samsung Galaxy Watch8 is $259.99 at Target, reduced by $90 now that the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 has been released.
Save $90 on the smaller 40mm Samsung Galaxy Watch8 in either graphite or silver colors. The larger 44mm model is available too for $299, a slightly smaller, but still significant, $50 saving.
Read moreRead less▼
Garmin Venu 3S
Another Garmin entry, the Venu 3S is from 2023 and a bit long in the tooth, but it’s still very much worth a look for anyone looking to reach fitness goals. We awarded it 4.5 stars in our review back at release, and called it “an ideal lifestyle smartwatch and fitness tracker blend.” It uses components such as the Elevate V5 heart rate sensor, which Garmins are still equipped with today.
It really does toe the line between functionality, features, and convenience, balancing the various options of a smartwatch with the battery life and fitness tracking capabilities of, well, a fitness tracker. Like its sequel, the Venu 4 (our best Garmin watch overall) it's an ideal 'goldilocks' fitness tracker for people who want it all.
Three years on, the AMOLED display looks great, heart rate data remains accurate, and sleep tracking is still excellent. You can save $90 at Best Buy right now, with the Stainless Steel and French Gray colorway down to $359.99.
The smaller 41mm version of the Venu 3, the Venu 3S has seen a big $90 price drop at Best Buy. It's a nice-looking tracker with a metal body and bezel: with the right watch face, it wouldn't look out of place in the office or the bar, as well as the gym or the track.
Read moreRead less▼
Apple Watch Ultra 4
Oh boy, this is the big one. We loved the Apple Watch Ultra 4 when it launched earlier this year, with the latest model of Apple’s rugged wearable earning 4.5 stars from us in our full review.
Imagine our surprise, then, to see Amazon lopping $100 off the latest model, bringing it from $799 to $699. It’s still pricey, sure, but you’re getting a lot of improvements for your money - particularly if you’re coming from an older Apple Watch Ultra.
To be clear, there’s little to no point in picking one up if you don’t have an iPhone to pair it with, but if you do, you’ll see performance gains with the S11 chip, and Apple has managed to eke out a little more battery life, too, bringing it up to 50 hours in total.
Perhaps the biggest draw is the Readiness Score, which offers Apple’s take on Fitbit’s Daily Readiness Score with no premium membership required. Having your watch tell you when it’s good to push on, or when you need a rest, could have a huge impact on long-term training and help you avoid injury.
Save $100 on perhaps the best smartwatch for iPhone users in 2026. It's unusual to see a big price cut on a device so recently released, especially an Apple Watch, so it's unlikely to get any better than this — best snap it up while stocks last.
