articles.title: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal
articles.text:
Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself.
Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world’s communications on platforms like the Signal app, Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind’s formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code.
More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn’t have critical vulnerabilities.
Before the AI era, it was incredibly time-consuming for people to describe the characteristics of software they wanted to prove, turn these summaries into formulas, and then develop the proof. Agentic AI can significantly cut down the time of the latter project, enabling analyses like DeepMind’s Signal evaluation. But even this analysis was limited in scope—it did not, for example, formally verify the entire Signal mobile app—and DeepMind researchers emphasize that their findings are just one milestone in a larger process.
“We are very excited by this result, but there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale this to all the software of the world, and we want to do that,” Swarat Chaudhuri, a DeepMind research scientist, tells WIRED.
The DeepMind analysis did not find any new vulnerabilities in the portions of the Signal protocol it looked at, but when the researchers used AlphaProof Code on older versions of Signal that contain known and long-fixed vulnerabilities, it correctly identified them and showed that the protocol could not be formally verified. The researchers are releasing the specification and proof they developed for the Signal protocol analysis to aid other formal verification work.

articles.title: AMD is running over 100 servers at 50% DRAM capacity with MEXT — company claims 95% performance of full-DRAM server, plans to expand to 2,000 servers in 2027
articles.text:
AMD shares how it can retain 95% of server performance with just half the DRAM, sidestepping memory shortages with MEXT — tech powers over 100 servers already running, with plans to expand to 2,000 servers in 2027
MEXT offloads cold memory pages to flash storage and serves them up with a predictive AI model.
In June, AMD overtook the predictive memory engine known as MEXT, which claims to offer upwards of 99% of the performance of a system with full DRAM capacity while running with as little as 25% of the physical DIMMs. The technology offloads cold memory pages to flash storage and uses an AI model to serve pages before they’re needed, and AMD says it plans to extend the tech across a wide swath of its IT infrastructure next year.
The pitch behind MEXT seems too good to be true. According to AMD and MEXT founder Gary Smerdon, the technology can cut the physical DRAM required in a server by 20% to 75% depending on the application and performance target. That missing memory still registers as installed DRAM to the OS. Instead of DRAM, however, MEXT uses relatively inexpensive flash storage to offload cold pages, flying them back in as they’re needed with an AI model. In some of AMD’s internal workloads, such as Synopsys PrimeTime, the company says it’s able to achieve 95% of the performance of a full server while running at 50% DRAM capacity with MEXT.
AMD has deployed MEXT internally on 145 servers, which it says will expand to 2,000 servers next year. In addition, the company has announced a partnership with HPE to bring MEXT to customers. Currently, we’re in phase 1 of the rollout, with some EPYC Venice servers carrying a “MEXT Ready” badge and a dedicated NVMe drive or bay for the offload. Phase 2 brings MEXT licenses out to these servers, as well as the RAM View application. AMD hasn’t said when Phase 2 will begin.
The AI-driven DRAM pricing surge impacts more than just gaming PCs, with enterprises also feeling the brunt of price increases, even if they aren’t running AI workloads. If MEXT is able to achieve what AMD claims, it could be transformative given the current market. Because of that, it’s worth understanding what exactly MEXT is, as well as what AMD claims it can do.
Although MEXT is exciting in concept, it’s obvious that AMD is taking a conservative approach to the rollout. Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence, after all. The applications of MEXT are currently narrow, though AMD says it’s expanding the workloads it’s using MEXT on with promising early results.
DRAM, Flash and an LLM
The basic setup of MEXT is simple in concept: cold pages go to flash, AI brings those pages back as needed, and it’s as if the memory was never missing in the first place. The main problem should be obvious. Flash is orders of magnitude slower than DRAM, so streaming pages back into memory from flash as they’re needed isn’t feasible. MEXT’s trick is using an AI model to predict the pages you’ll need. And, as long as the model is able to stay ahead by at least the transfer latency from the SSD, it’s as if the physical DRAM was installed the whole time.
This isn’t a crazy concept considering how a transformer-based LLM, which MEXT uses, operates. If you’re unfamiliar with the inner workings, this open-source visualization breaks down the concept of a transformer AI model cleanly. The foundational concept is next token prediction, which underpins the design of modern LLMs. Given a set of tokens, the LLM determines which token (word, portion of a word, etc.) is most likely to come next. It makes a prediction. In the case of MEXT, it’s predicting what page is needed next, not what word comes next.
Memory offloading to flash isn’t a new concept, but MEXT founder Gary Smerdon says that AI is the critical difference in this technology. MEXT itself is deployed as a Linux kernel module that works with any Linux distro. It uses an “ensemble of AI models,” with the primary transformer-based LLM driving the technology. And critically, it doesn’t come pre-trained.
Instead, AMD says that MEXT trains in under a second when first deployed, operates on one EPYC core without a GPU, and continually trains as the workload progresses. This approach makes sense given the varied workloads that MEXT may apply to. The idea is that it would learn the access patterns of the application in order to drive that prediction engine.
MEXT isn’t perfect, but it doesn’t need to be perfect in every situation. For instance, the order of stored pages isn’t important. With text, an LLM needs to predict the correct text in the correct order, but with MEXT, the order doesn’t matter. As long as the page is in DRAM when it’s needed, that’s fine.
In order to understand the application of MEXT to different workloads, AMD has developed RAM View to go alongside the tech. It’s a memory utilization tool that shows which pages are hot and which have gone cold. As you can see from the example above, a system with 1.5 TB of memory shows near-full utilization across the full workload, but around half of the pages stored in memory haven’t been touched in five minutes or more at any given time.
AMD provided this generalized example and didn’t clarify what workload it was testing. That’s very important, as the utilization breakdown will look vastly different depending on the application(s) running on the server. Initially, AMD is applying MEXT to critical EDA applications it uses internally, such as Synopsys PrimeTime, but the company says it has focused on optimizing agentic AI, database, and media and entertainment workloads as well.
This is important not only because memory access patterns change between applications, but also because performance in those applications reacts differently when a system doesn’t have enough memory. The “memory wall,” as AMD calls it, should be a familiar concept regardless of whether you’ve ever touched a server. With MEXT, AMD says it’s trying to extend this memory wall, which may look different for different applications.
For instance, the company is confident that many workloads can reduce capacity by around 20% to 25%. As the reduction increases, however, the applications become more specialized, and the performance delta becomes greater.
AMD’s internal MEXT results
AMD has shared some internal MEXT results, which look impressive, though as usual, it’s always smart to handle first-party benchmarks like this with skepticism. Starting with PrimeTime, where AMD has focused much of its attention on MEXT up to this point, it says servers running at 50% capacity retain 95% of the performance of a full server, and going down to as little as 25% capacity still maintains 80% of the application’s performance.
PrimeTime demands a lot of memory for large designs. There are some applications where performance is nearly identical, according to AMD. In a 3-node cluster running in Azure with 5th-gen EPYC CPUs, AMD says MEXT offers 99% of the performance of the full cluster while running at 50% DRAM capacity with the Spark SQL workload from the TPC-DS benchmark. SQL databases try to cache as much data as possible in memory to prevent I/O bottlenecks, creating a golden opportunity for tech like MEXT that wants to free cold pages.
Perhaps the most applicable workload at the current moment, however, is agentic AI, and AMD says MEXT has similar applications there. Across a five-agent concurrent geomean, AMD claims 99% of the performance of a full server with 50% memory capacity, and 85% of the performance with 25% capacity. With a “memory-hungry” agent, AMD claims 90% and 88% performance for 50% and 25% capacity, respectively.
The slide you can see above has footnote tags. However, AMD has not shared the footnotes with us yet, so we don’t have a view into how these tests were run. Naturally, we assume AMD has, at minimum, represented the performance of MEXT in the best light possible. We can’t do a full analysis without knowing how the tests were run, however.
What is interesting is AMD’s cautious approach to rolling out MEXT. It’s an EPYC-exclusive feature right now, though AMD left the door open for support on future products (consumer devices, such as Strix Halo) far down the road. It will be sold as a license, bundled with the RAM View software, but we don’t have a timeline on when that will happen. And, despite a partnership with HPE to push out “MEXT Ready” servers, we still don’t know when MEXT itself will be ready for deployment beyond AMD’s walls.
Given that conservative approach, there are likely pitfalls to MEXT that we’re not seeing yet, and it’s hard to imagine it will be broadly applicable to every server, at least at the 50% and 25% DRAM capacity levels that AMD showed off with its benchmarks.
However, even being able to trim 25% of a server’s DRAM capacity represents a massive cost savings in the current supply-constrained environment. If some workloads can push that to 50% capacity, that’s even better. Of course, we’ll need to see how MEXT holds up once it’s available broadly, but if AMD’s claims hold water, it could become a defining technology in data centers that can’t seem to get enough memory.
Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

articles.title: Le nouveau rover lunaire de la NASA n'aura pas besoin du Soleil : il roulera au nucléaire
articles.text:
Au pôle Sud de la Lune, la nuit dure quatorze jours terrestres et certains cratères n’ont jamais reçu la lumière directe du Soleil. La NASA y prépare pourtant sa future base, et elle a détaillé le 7 novembre, depuis le centre spatial Kennedy, la mission robotique chargée d’en dresser l’inventaire. Un rover à six roues baptisé PROMISE y forera le sol à partir de fin 2028, alimenté par un générateur nucléaire, pour une mission prévue sur dix-huit mois.
Un rover lunaire né dans les réserves martiennes
Le véhicule sera assemblé au Jet Propulsion Laboratory à partir de pièces de vol de rechange et de modèles d’essai de Curiosity et de Perseverance, les deux rovers martiens de l’agence. Son acronyme se traduit par « rover polaire d’observation, de cartographie et d’exploration in situ ». La bête embarque spectromètres, caméras et capteurs de température et de radiations, ainsi qu’une foreuse capable d’entamer le régolithe jusqu’à un mètre de profondeur et un ordinateur de bord durci conçu pour naviguer en autonomie.
Lire aussi : 164 395 dollars par an et une base sur la Lune : la NASA recrute ses futurs astronautes, mais pas n’importe qui
La NASA parle d’une alimentation nucléaire sans en préciser le modèle. Les générateurs qui équipent Curiosity et Perseverance donnent l’ordre de grandeur : 4,8 kg de dioxyde de plutonium 238 y produisent environ 110 watts d’électricité au lancement, pour au moins quatorze ans de service. La chaleur excédentaire maintient au passage les instruments à bonne température. Le principe tient de la pile atomique plus que du réacteur, sans réaction en chaîne ni pièce mobile : la chaleur de la désintégration devient du courant, que la nuit tombe ou non. Blue Origin livrera l’engin au pôle Sud à bord de son atterrisseur Mark 1, pour un contrat de 94 millions de dollars assorti d’une option de performance pouvant atteindre 140 millions.
VIPER, le précédent à 450 millions
VIPER devait déjà cartographier la glace d’eau du pôle Sud, avec des panneaux solaires et une batterie incapables de tenir loin des zones éclairées. La NASA a annulé la mission le 17 juillet 2024, après environ 450 millions de dollars dépensés, avant de la relancer en septembre 2025 avec Blue Origin pour un alunissage désormais visé en 2027. Sa feuille de route plafonnait à une centaine de jours terrestres, là où PROMISE promet dix-huit mois, nuits lunaires comprises.
L’annonce arrive au milieu d’une rafale de contrats pour le programme Moon Base, qui vise une base opérationnelle à l’horizon 2032. Huit entreprises, dont SpaceX et Blue Origin, se partageront jusqu’à 10 milliards de dollars de livraisons lunaires sur dix ans, et 1,3 milliard de commandes de lancement a déjà été réparti. Le patron de l’agence résume la méthode d’une formule : la Lune se construit « mission par mission », pour que les astronautes arrivent sur un chantier déjà entamé.
Côté européen, l’atterrisseur Argonaut de l’ESA n’est pas attendu avant 2030 sur une Ariane 64. Il testera d’abord des technologies de survie à la nuit lunaire avant d’embarquer, à terme, sa propre source à radioisotopes. La carte de la glace d’eau que dressera PROMISE pèsera donc sur l’emplacement de la base, et sur tout ce qui suivra. L’eau, c’est de l’oxygène et du carburant que personne n’aura à lancer depuis la Terre.

articles.title: Beyond code generation: Five lessons on AI, reliability, and recovery
articles.text:
Beyond code generation: Five lessons on AI, reliability, and recovery
At a TechSparks 2026 roundtable hosted by OPPEX, technology leaders discussed the challenges of maintaining AI-generated code, managing risk, and responding when production systems fail.
AI is speeding up software development, allowing teams to build in days what once took weeks. But writing code faster does not necessarily make it easier to understand, maintain, or fix. As codebases grow, engineers must deal with failures in systems they may not have built or fully understood, often under pressure during an incident.
At TechSparks 2026, OPPEX hosted a roundtable titled ‘AI Can 10X Your Engineers. Can It 10X Your Ability to Fix What They Build?’, bringing technology leaders together to discuss the challenges of maintaining, troubleshooting, and recovering software systems built faster with AI.
The discussion brought together Abhishek Dwivedi, VP Engineering, Cimpress; Amit Khanna, Global Head of Engineering, Amadeus; Anand Rangarajan, VP Engineering, Google DeepMind; Ashish Chandra Tewari, Vice President of Engineering, Razorpay; Dheeraj Khanna, VP Engineering, Global Logic; Jaya Krishnan, VP Engineering, Coforge; Roopasree Ranganna, SVP, Workplace Technology and Service Delivery Leader, Synchrony; Ruby Tomar, Vice President & Head Agentic Firmware, Ascendion; Sarath Gollapalli, VP Engineering, Broadridge; Saurabh Kumar, VP Engineering, Capillary Technologies; Sridhar Jonnala, Chief AI Scientist, Distinguished Engineer, CTO -AI Strategy & Delivery, IBM; Sudhir Tiwari, Global Head, Digital Engineering Center, Thoughtworks; Trilok Ramakrishna, Site lead and Head of Engineering, dbt Labs; and Vasanthi Ramesh, Vice President & Engineering Site Leader, NetApp.
OPPEX was represented by Prasun Kumar, Founder and CEO. The discussion was moderated by Madanmohan Rao, Research Director at YourStory.
Here are five key takeaways from the discussion.
Faster code does not mean faster business results
AI has accelerated code generation, but testing, validation, deployment, and downstream systems have not necessarily kept pace. As a result, code may be ready long before the rest of the system can support it.
Participants cautioned against confusing output with outcomes. Writing 10X more code does not mean customers will see a tenfold improvement. What matters is whether AI helps deliver better business results. Several leaders also suggested that teams should be willing to use AI to remove unnecessary code, rather than simply generate more of it.
Match AI autonomy to the level of risk
Participants agreed that AI agents should not have the same level of autonomy across all systems.
Tasks that are easy to reverse, such as restarting a stateless service or adding capacity, can be handled autonomously. But changes involving money, patient data or physical manufacturing require closer oversight because errors can have consequences that are difficult or impossible to reverse.
Many teams are classifying applications and data according to risk, giving agents greater freedom in low-risk areas while retaining human oversight of critical code. In regulated sectors, participants stressed the need to establish controls before expanding autonomy, along with clear procedures for handling errors made by agents.
Context is critical to making AI agents effective
AI agents need access to the right information to work effectively. In many organizations, knowledge about legacy systems, service dependencies, and past incidents rests with a few experienced employees. These are often the people teams turn to when something goes wrong.
To reduce this dependence, teams are using knowledge graphs, memory layers, and shared repositories to document how systems interact, what has failed before, and what each service is expected to deliver. This can help preserve institutional knowledge when employees leave or move to other roles.
However, making more information available to agents also has a cost. Large prompts increase token usage, making it important to retrieve relevant information efficiently rather than feed agents everything available.
Human accountability remains essential
As AI-generated changes become larger and more frequent, there is a risk that engineers may approve code they do not fully understand.
Instead of requiring people to review every line, participants discussed systems in which agents indicate their confidence levels and escalate decisions when confidence is low. Human oversight remains particularly important in regulated environments, where organizations may need to explain decisions to regulators or customers.
Participants also emphasized the need to track incidents caused by AI-generated changes and use those findings to improve development and review processes. Several noted that many organizations have yet to establish this feedback loop.
Let agents investigate, but leave critical decisions to people
Incident response was identified as one of the most promising near-term uses of AI agents.
Agents can collect logs, trace dependencies, examine recent deployments, filter false alarms, and bring together information that engineers need to investigate failures. This can save on-call teams time and help them identify problems without having to gather evidence from scratch.
For critical incidents, however, appropriate teams must be alerted immediately, even while agents continue investigating.
Participants also pointed to the additional cost and complexity of monitoring AI agents, along with unresolved questions about accuracy, drift, and the value they deliver. They stressed that product managers, analysts, and other roles should also be involved in the process of building with AI.
The roundtable highlighted common concerns among technology leaders across industries, particularly around reliability, oversight, and incident response. Participants called for greater investment in stability, security, and recovery alongside AI-driven development.
As organizations generate more code with AI, they must also ensure they have the systems, processes and people needed to maintain it and respond when things go wrong.

articles.title: 5 lessons from the book Manifest: Dive Deeper, Roxie Nafousi
articles.text:
5 lessons from the book Manifest: Dive Deeper, Roxie Nafousi
Explore five powerful lessons from Manifest: Dive Deeper by Roxie Nafousi on self-belief, emotional healing, visualisation, gratitude, and personal growth.
What if creating the life you want begins with changing the way you see yourself? Manifestation is often associated with visualising dreams and thinking positively, but it also involves self-awareness, emotional healing, and taking meaningful action.
In Manifest: Dive Deeper, Roxie Nafousi takes readers further into the principles of manifestation, encouraging them to understand their inner beliefs, overcome emotional barriers, and become more intentional about the lives they want to create.
The book explores how self-worth, gratitude, visualisation, and personal growth can influence the way we approach our goals. It reminds readers that manifesting a better future is not simply about wishing for something but also about becoming ready to work towards it.
5 Important lessons to learn from Manifest: Dive Deeper by Roxie Nafousi
1. Believe that you are worthy of the life you want
One of the most important foundations of manifestation is believing that you deserve happiness, success, and meaningful opportunities.
Sometimes, our insecurities and limiting beliefs prevent us from pursuing the things we genuinely want. We may question our abilities, compare ourselves with others, or feel that certain opportunities are meant for everyone except us.
The book encourages readers to recognise their self-worth and stop allowing negative beliefs to determine their future. When you begin believing in your own potential, you become more confident about pursuing your goals.
2. Let go of what no longer serves you
Personal growth often requires releasing old beliefs, unhealthy attachments, and emotional patterns that prevent us from moving forward.
Holding on to past disappointments or constantly worrying about things beyond our control can make it difficult to focus on new possibilities.
The book encourages readers to practise letting go and make space for healthier experiences. This does not mean forgetting your past but learning from it without allowing it to control your present.
3. Visualise the life you want to create
Visualisation is an important part of manifestation. When you clearly imagine your goals and the kind of life you want to build, you can develop a stronger sense of direction.
Instead of focusing only on what you want to achieve, think about the person you need to become to reach those goals. Consider the habits, mindset, and daily choices that support your vision.
Visualisation can help you stay motivated, but it works best when combined with consistent effort and practical action.
4. Practise gratitude for what you already have
It is easy to become so focused on future goals that we forget to appreciate what is already present in our lives.
The book highlights the importance of gratitude as a way to shift our attention from what is missing to what we already have. Appreciating small moments, supportive relationships, personal achievements, and everyday opportunities can help us develop a more positive outlook.
Gratitude does not mean giving up on bigger dreams. It means learning to appreciate your present while working towards your future.
5. Become the person who can achieve your goals
Manifestation is not only about attracting opportunities; it is also about personal transformation.
If you want to build a successful career, develop the discipline and skills that support it. If you want healthier relationships, work on your communication and emotional maturity.
The book encourages readers to align their daily actions with the future they imagine. Small, consistent decisions can gradually bring you closer to your goals.
Instead of waiting for the perfect opportunity, start becoming the person who is prepared to make the most of it.
Final thoughts
Manifest: Dive Deeper by Roxie Nafousi is a reminder that personal transformation begins with the way we think about ourselves and the choices we make every day.
Through self-belief, emotional healing, visualisation, gratitude, and intentional action, readers are encouraged to take greater responsibility for their personal growth.
The biggest takeaway is that manifestation is not about waiting for life to change on its own. It is about developing the mindset, confidence, and habits that help you move towards the life you want to create.

articles.title: Binance alerte sur une faille iPhone capable d’exposer les secrets de portefeuilles crypto
articles.text:
En installant sur votre iPhone une application téléchargée en dehors de l’App Store, vous pourriez livrer à un pirate la phrase de récupération de votre portefeuille de cryptomonnaies. Binance a lancé l’alerte sur X, et Apple n’a confirmé aucun correctif.
Sur un iPhone, Apple enferme chaque application dans un compartiment isolé, le bac à sable (sandbox), et lui interdit de lire les fichiers des autres. Le chercheur forcequit a publié sur GitHub une méthode pour sortir de ce compartiment sans jailbreak, worse_query. Avec une application piégée, un pirate peut ainsi lire les fichiers locaux de vos autres applications, dont vos phrases de récupération, vos clés privées et vos identifiants, prévient Binance, qui précise que la faille vient d’iOS et non de sa seule application. Binance n’a signalé aucun vol de cryptomonnaie lié à worse_query, mais un développeur s’est servi de la technique pour mettre en ligne un gestionnaire de fichiers capable de fouiller les données de vos autres applications.
Christoph Kolbicz exploite worse_query dans son gestionnaire de fichiers
« Apple traînait à me répondre, et des gens ont commencé à faire semblant de l’exploiter ici », souligne forcequit sur X, pour expliquer pourquoi il a publié son code plus tôt que prévu. Le lendemain, Christoph Kolbicz a mis en ligne WQ Files. Avec ce gestionnaire de fichiers, vous pouvez parcourir, exporter, modifier et supprimer les données de vos autres applications, sans jailbreak.
Pour fonctionner, worse_query a besoin d’un App Group, un espace de stockage partagé qu’iOS réserve normalement aux applications d’un même développeur. AltStore et SideStore, deux outils d’installation parallèles à l’App Store, le créent automatiquement avec votre identifiant Apple au moment où vous installez WQ Files. Un pirate pourrait donc vous faire installer une application piégée par cette voie. Personne ne sait encore si une application publiée sur l’App Store pourrait exploiter worse_query.
D’après les tests de BleepingComputer, WQ Files est opérationnel sur les trois versions d’iOS citées par Binance, 26.7.1, 27.0.1 et 27.2. Avec cette dernière, Apple avait corrigé 163 failles fin octobre, mais pas la faille exploitée par worse_query.
- Volume de transactions élevé
- Large éventail de cryptomonnaies
- Fonctionnalités avancées de trading
Apple n’a confirmé aucun correctif pour worse_query
Apple a publié iOS 27.2.1 et iOS 26.7.3 le jour de la sortie de WQ Files, mais leurs notes de sécurité ne mentionnent ni worse_query ni le bac à sable. Avec la faille CVE-2026-113963, corrigée dans ces mises à jour, une application pouvait bien accéder à des données sensibles. Mais cette faille, signalée par Laszlo Varady, passe par App Intents, le système qui relie les applications à Siri et aux Raccourcis, et non par un App Group. Sollicitée par BleepingComputer, Apple n’a pas répondu, et l’entreprise ne commente jamais une faille avant d’avoir terminé son enquête et publié un correctif.
Binance vous demande malgré tout d’installer sans attendre les mises à jour d’iOS et de vos applications, et de supprimer les applications inutiles ou téléchargées depuis une source douteuse. Si vous pensez que votre iPhone a été compromis, la plateforme vous conseille de transférer vos fonds vers un nouveau portefeuille, créé sur un appareil sain, et de déconnecter toutes vos sessions actives.
Binance n’a cité que trois versions d’iOS, mais forcequit annonce davantage de versions vulnérables.

articles.title: Un smartphone qui se déplie en petit écran de travail : le HONOR Magic V5 approche les 1 000 € pour le 11.11
articles.text:

Les smartphones pliants sont de plus en plus appréciés par les technophiles, mais leurs prix restent globalement élevés. Les bonnes affaires sont cependant possibles. La preuve avec le HONOR Magic V5, qui passe à 1 003,39 € chez AliExpress grâce au code promo CLU80. Cette offre est proposée dans le cadre du 11.11 qui se déroule en ce moment sur la plateforme et concerne le coloris Dawn Gold du smartphone. La livraison est réalisée gratuitement depuis un entrepôt français.
Le HONOR Magic V5 est disponible pour 1 003,39 € sur AliExpress, à condition d’utiliser le code promo CLU80.
Pourquoi choisir le HONOR Magic V5 ?
- Pour son écran intérieur : la diagonale de 7,95 pouces facilite la lecture et permet d’ouvrir plusieurs applications en même temps.
- Pour ses performances : le SoC Snapdragon 8 Elite convient aux applications exigeantes et facilite le multitâche.
- Pour sa recharge : le smartphone accepte jusqu’à 66 W en filaire et 50 W sans fil pour recharger sa batterie de 5 820 mAh avec des accessoires compatibles.
Deux écrans pour adapter le téléphone à tous les besoins
Fermé, le Magic V5 dispose d’un écran extérieur de 6,43 pouces pour répondre aux messages ou consulter un itinéraire. Une fois ouvert, il offre une surface plus adaptée aux tableaux, aux PDF et à l’affichage de plusieurs fenêtres. Le taux de rafraîchissement de ses deux dalles OLED peut monter jusqu’à 120 Hz, ce qui assure des défilements fluides. Dans notre test du HONOR Magic V5, nous avons notamment apprécié les écrans, les performances et l’autonomie du terminal, et nous lui avons accordé la note de 9 sur 10.
Un format utile si vous exploitez vraiment le grand écran
Face à un smartphone traditionnel, l’intérêt du Magic V5 se trouve, sans grande surprise, dans son écran intérieur pliable. C’est un atout si vous avez souvent besoin de lire des documents, de rédiger des messages ou de communiquer. En revanche, le format presque carré de cet écran laisse apparaître des bandes noires sur les vidéos au format 16:9. Dans ce cas, l’écran extérieur peut suffire, et l’intérêt du pliant est moindre.
✅ Les points forts
- Grand écran pliant OLED de 7,95 pouces.
- Processeur Snapdragon 8 Elite.
- Recharge filaire et sans fil.
❌ Les limites
- Module photo proéminent à l’arrière.
- Qualité photo perfectible en mode nocturne.
Avec le code promo CLU80, le HONOR Magic V5 revient à 1 003,39 €, avec la livraison offerte.
Si vous avez envie de vous offrir un smartphone pliant de type fold depuis un moment, le HONOR Magic V5 peut vous permettre de sauter le pas à un prix correct pour ce genre d’appareil. Il est adapté aux utilisateurs qui lisent beaucoup sur leur téléphone ou qui en ont assez de jongler entre un smartphone et une tablette en fonction de leurs besoins.
Néanmoins, le prix du terminal reste élevé malgré la promotion. Si vous utilisez surtout votre téléphone pour des tâches rapides ou pour regarder des vidéos, un smartphone classique et moins coûteux peut vous suffire.

articles.title: Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million
articles.text:
Shipping giant Maersk has confirmed that a threat actor breached systems belonging to a company it previously acquired and stole data.
Ransomware group WhiteArmor claimed the attack over the weekend, threatening that it would release about 100GB of information allegedly exfiltrated from the company's logistics and supply-chain platform.
Legacy system compromise
The investigation into the incident is ongoing, but the shipping firm says that current evidence indicates that "no sensitive data has been disclosed."
Maersk added that it does not expect disruptions to operations, and assures customers that they can continue booking and managing shipments through its systems as usual.
“The incident is isolated to a local system, and we have found no indication that there has been any impact on other Maersk systems or customer and partner systems that connect to Maersk through integrations such as APIs and EDI,” Maersk states.
A.P. Moller–Maersk is a Danish shipping and logistics group and one of the world’s largest container carriers by fleet capacity. The company operates ocean freighters, port terminals, warehouses, and air and land transport services across 130 countries.
It has 700 container ships, roughly 13.5% of the global fleet capacity, 60 terminals in 35 countries, and employs 100,000 people. Last year, Maersk reported $54 billion in revenue and $2.9 billion in net profit.
Maersk said the incident has been isolated, but did not share details about the affected system, the compromised data types, or when the intrusion occurred.
BleepingComputer reached out to Maersk with additional questions, but we have not heard back as of publishing.
Ransomware gang claims 100GB data theft
Over the weekend, the WhiteArmor ransomware gang listed Maersk on its data leak site and publicly asked for a ransom payment of $5million.
"Your contract-logistics arm, the former LF Logistics, runs fulfilment for many of the world's largest consumer brands. Five million dollars is roughly four hours of that EBITDA," the threat actor said.
"You have 30 days to contact us and pay USD 5,000,000 in bitcoin," reads WhiteArmor's public message.
WhiteArmor claims to hold approximately 100 GB of data allegedly stolen from Maersk's OCF/LF Logistics platform, which the group is using to support its extortion demands.
In 2022, Maersk acquired LF Logistics, the original developer of the OCF/LF Logistics platform, from the Li & Fung Group.
According to the threat actor, the data they hold includes nearly 30,000 drivers records, plaintext passwords, 33 SUPER_ADMIN accounts (the most privileged on a system), signed delivery receipts, and 14.44 inventory rows with purchase orders and Advance Shipping Notice (ASNs).
The hacker also claims to hold 27,842 mobile device logs that include phone numbers, emails, and IMEI (International Mobile Equipment Identity) numbers.
Maersk noted in the disclosure today that "the incident is isolated to a local system" and that it would notify customers "as more relevant information becomes available, and if we identify any need to inform impacted parties of any further findings."
"As always, please treat any unexpected communications claiming to relate to this matter with caution and verify them through your usual Maersk contact," the company advises.
In 2017, Maersk was hit by NotPetya ransomware, forcing it to rebuild an infrastructure of over 4,000 servers and 45,000 workstations from scratch.
At the time, the company was forced to operate without IT for ten days, incurring damages of up to $300 million.

articles.title: Hackers use AntiFox AI agents in AWS credential-theft attacks
articles.text:
Attackers are using Alibaba Cloud to host self-managed instances of AntiFox, an open-source agentic penetration testing platform, to target web services and AWS environments.
The infrastructure hosting AntiFox was used for various malicious activities, including vulnerability exploitation, webshell deployment, credential validation, configuration discovery, and AWS secret harvesting.
Initially created as a fork of ARTEX 0.1.1, AntiFox has a Chinese-language interface and lets users deploy AI agents and automate common penetration-testing tasks, such as mapping exposed services and probing target endpoints for vulnerabilities.
Security researchers at Arctic Wolf observed malicious AntiFox-linked infrastructure hosted on Alibaba Cloud using valid AWS identities, including IAM users and, in some cases, assumed EC2 roles, to make authenticated requests to Amazon Web Services APIs.
“In several recently observed intrusions, Alibaba Cloud systems hosting AntiFox interfaces were associated with confirmed malicious actions against internet-facing web services and associated AWS environments,” Arctic Wolf says.
One case highlighted in the report involved deploying an ASPX webshell on an internet-exposed IIS server, executing OS commands, accessing application settings and database connection strings, and copying configuration and log files to a web-accessible directory.
The attacker also used valid IAM credentials and EC2 roles to probe Amazon Web Services (AWS) endpoints. In one intrusion, they cycled through multiple identities and made hundreds of API requests in about 30 minutes, the researchers note.
Although most of these attempts were blocked, the attacker was successful in some cases and obtained production secrets.
In a separate incident, the attackers used a valid AWS identity to read, copy, and delete S3 objects.
Arctic Wolf's report includes hunting guidance and recommendations for defenders that include correlating IIS webshell activity with unusual AWS access and reviewing successful API calls within bursts of denials.
The researchers also recommend revoking affected AWS sessions and keys and rotating credentials exposed through application files.
The AntiFox findings follow recent attacks involving ARTEX AI, another agentic penetration-testing framework developed in China that went closed-source after it was used in attacks on South Korean banks.
CrowdStrike also linked ARTEX to a cyberespionage campaign in which the Chinese hacking group Vapor Panda targeted more than 200 organizations across 14 countries.
For now, AntiFox remains available on GitHub, where it has been updated to version 2.0, which improves how the tool documents and reports findings.
Its publishers prohibit using the tool against live systems, in real-world penetration tests or security exercises, or for destructive or illegal activity, but they do not describe any technical controls that enforce those restrictions.

articles.title: GTA 6 : Logitech offre un jour de congé à ses 7 000 salariés pour jouer au jeu de leur choix — Frandroid
articles.text:
Difficile de ne pas être au courant, mais le 19 novembre, Rockstar sort GTA VI sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Le logiciel de ressources humaines BambooHR a déjà relevé près de 13 % de demandes de congés en plus pour cette date que pour des jours comparables les années précédentes.
Logitech a choisi de prendre les devants. Dans un communiqué publié le 10 novembre, l’entreprise annonce le « Logi Game Day », un jour de congé réservé au jeu vidéo : ses quelque 7 000 salariés pourront donc s’absenter pour jouer sans avoir à inventer une grippe de circonstance.
Jouez dans les meilleures conditions avec la TV TCL C79L : une expérience gaming fluide en 144 Hz et un son immersif signé Bang & Olufsen, actuellement en promotion !
    Pour aller plus loin
Sans surprise, les chiffres de vente de GTA 6 « dépassent largement » les prévisions
            
Un jour gratuit à prendre avant novembre 2027
Contrairement à ce que son nom laisse croire, le Game Day ne tombe pas à une date fixe. Tous les salariés y ont droit, des employés à temps plein aux stagiaires, et chacun choisit son jour et son jeu d’ici novembre 2027, mais avouons que ça tombe à pic à quelques jours de GTA 6.
Logitech G, la marque gaming du groupe, organisera tout de même un live le 19 novembre depuis le siège américain de San Jose, animé par son directeur général Robin Piispanen, un ancien joueur compétitif. Hanneke Faber, CEO de Logitech, a prévu d’y participer, et un porte-parole a glissé à Fortune que si des employés partent explorer Vice City le jour de la sortie, « vous n’entendrez aucune plainte de notre part ».
    Pour aller plus loin
Quelle console choisir pour jouer à GTA 6 à sa sortie ?
            
Hanneke Faber justifie la mesure en expliquant qu’ « il est temps d’en finir avec le cliché selon lequel le jeu vidéo est une perte de temps ».
Disons aussi que Logitech préfère maîtriser l’hémorragie potentielle du 19 novembre plutôt que la subir. D’après BambooHR, la moitié des joueurs qui comptent s’absenter pour une sortie de jeu disent préférer se faire porter malade plutôt que de poser un congé à l’avance.
On imagine assez bien qu’un jour par an et par salarié, prévu et validé, coûte peu à côté d’une équipe à moitié vide un jeudi matin, sans prévenir.
Comment jouer à GTA VI sans Game Day
Le préchargement de GTA VI est déjà ouvert, et le jeu pèse 212 Go sur PS5. Vérifiez donc dès maintenant la place libre sur le SSD de votre console pour lancer la partie le 19 novembre. Faute de jour de congé, le jeu prend en charge le Remote Play de la Xbox, qui permet de streamer une partie depuis la console vers un PC ou un smartphone, le temps d’une pause déjeuner.

articles.title: Ces PC portables Lenovo partaient à la benne : un youtubeur ukrainien les ressuscite avec un gadget à 10 euros
articles.text:
Ces PC portables Lenovo partaient à la benne : un youtubeur ukrainien les ressuscite avec un gadget à 10 euros
Une pince, un programmateur USB et un second PC suffisent
Ils démarrent, leur écran s'allume, leur clavier répond. Pourtant, ces portables finissent au recyclage, condamnés par un mot de passe qu'un service informatique a oublié de transmettre. Un youtubeur ukrainien montre comment les libérer avec un petit boîtier vendu une dizaine d'euros, et sa démonstration dépasse déjà 577 000 vues.
Le 13 octobre, Hileeq, à la tête de la modeste chaîne Rebooted by Hileeq, a publié une vidéo de moins de huit minutes. On l'y voit déverrouiller un Lenovo ThinkPad T470 dont le BIOS exigeait un mot de passe "superviseur" inconnu. La méthode, relayée le 10 novembre par Tom's Hardware, vise les ThinkPad équipés de processeurs Intel de 4e à 8e génération. Elle n'exige aucune soudure, seulement un programmateur CH341A, une pince et un second ordinateur.
Pourquoi ces ThinkPad d'entreprise se vendent à prix cassé
Les entreprises verrouillent souvent leurs flottes de portables avec ce mot de passe superviseur. Au moment de la revente, le stockage est généralement retiré et le précieux sésame rarement documenté. L'acheteur hérite alors d'une machine dont il ne peut plus modifier les réglages, et ces lots se bradent ou partent au rebut. Une raison de plus de bien inspecter un ordinateur d'occasion avant de sortir sa carte bancaire. L'un des chapitres de la vidéo pose le constat sans détour : en Europe, ces portables "se vendent pour des sommes ridicules".
Hileeq recommande de viser les gammes T, L et E, piliers des parcs professionnels, dont Lenovo soigne de plus en plus la réparabilité. Il résume ainsi l'esprit de sa démonstration : "Aucune magie, seulement de la pratique utile pour ceux qui veulent économiser ou gagner de l'argent en réparant du matériel".
Comment fonctionne le déblocage du BIOS
La pince se fixe sur la puce du BIOS, sur la carte mère. Le programmateur, branché en USB sur un autre PC, lit son contenu grâce au logiciel NeoProgrammer. Le youtubeur sauvegarde cette copie d'origine, puis la passe dans un outil de correction automatique et réécrit la puce avec la version modifiée. Au démarrage, quelques touches effacent le mot de passe. Il ne reste plus qu'à réinstaller le BIOS d'origine.
	
Aucune magie, seulement de la pratique utile pour ceux qui veulent économiser ou gagner de l'argent en réparant du matériel
Hileeq n'a rien inventé. Un certain Victor Voinea monnayait déjà une méthode sur un forum roumain, avant qu'un membre de Badcaps, sous le pseudonyme Knucklegrumble, n'en publie gratuitement une en 2020. Mark Juvan l'a ensuite disséquée dans son mémoire de master en cybersécurité à l'université Radboud de Nimègue. La faille tient à un pilote fourni par Lenovo, qui donne accès en lecture et en écriture à la zone où dort le mot de passe.
Avant de craquer pour un ThinkPad verrouillé
La copie d'origine du BIOS sert de filet de sécurité : sans elle, une erreur peut rendre la machine inutilisable. La manipulation doit aussi rester réservée à un ordinateur acheté en bonne et due forme.
Il faut enfin regarder la génération du processeur, qui décide de la compatibilité avec Windows 11. La liste officielle des puces prises en charge démarre, à de rares exceptions près, à la 8e génération d'Intel. Or Windows 10 n'est plus pris en charge depuis octobre 2025. Pour les modèles plus anciens, une distribution Linux offrira une seconde vie plus sereine.

articles.title: Ley de Propiedad Horizontal: se puede prohibir el uso del ascensor a los vecinos que no paguen la comunidad en algunos casos
articles.text:
Que un vecino deje de pagar las cuotas de la comunidad o una derrama es un problema para todos. En estos casos, la comunidad de propietarios tiene herramientas más allá de limitarse a reclamarle la deuda, y entre otras cosas puede impedirle utilizar el ascensor mientras no se ponga al día. Esto se desprende de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, aunque siempre dentro de lo que marcan dos artículos concretos de la ley.
El papel de los artículos 6 y 21. El artículo 6 es el que ordena la convivencia, porque permite que el conjunto de propietarios fije normas de régimen interior para regular la utilización de los servicios y cosas comunes, unas normas que obligan a todos los titulares mientras no se modifiquen. Como el ascensor es un elemento común, su uso puede ordenarse por esa vía, pero los estatutos no sirven para privar de derechos de forma arbitraria a uno de los vecinos.
La herramienta realmente pensada para la morosidad está en el artículo 21.1, que desde la reforma de junio de 2022 permite a la junta de propietarios acordar medidas disuasorias mientras dure el impago. Tal y como recoge el texto del precepto, esas medidas pueden ir desde fijar intereses superiores al legal hasta la privación temporal del uso de servicios o instalaciones, siempre que no puedan considerarse abusivas o desproporcionadas y no afecten a la habitabilidad de los inmuebles. Además, no pueden tener carácter retroactivo, aunque la comunidad puede incluirlas en sus estatutos.
Vamos, que el artículo 6 sirve para poner reglas al uso del ascensor en el día a día, mientras que el 21 es el que abre la puerta a restringirlo, con límites, cuando un vecino no paga.
El caso del ascensor. La ley no menciona el ascensor por su nombre, y ese es el matiz, ya que dejar a alguien sin él puede chocar con el límite de la habitabilidad. Por eso hay que valorar las circunstancias del edificio y de cada propietario, y según el análisis de algunos expertos sobre un caso que ha llegado a la Audiencia Provincial de Alicante, la deuda por sí sola no convierte en legal la retirada del ascensor. Y esto es así porque se debe tener en cuenta la planta de la vivienda, las vías alternativas y si allí viven personas con discapacidad o mayores de setenta años. Sin embargo, el auto de la Audiencia no decide si la comunidad actuó bien, ya que se limita a la admisión de la demanda.
Eso sí, la medida tiene que ser temporal y estar ligada a la deuda, de modo que no puede convertirse en una sanción permanente. Y tampoco basta con que el presidente o el administrador decidan bloquear el ascensor por su cuenta, porque es la junta la que tiene que adoptar el acuerdo, y conviene dejar constancia de él en lugar de improvisar.
Reclamar la deuda es otra cosa. Pero restringir un servicio no sustituye a la reclamación del dinero. Las derramas aprobadas generan una deuda con la comunidad igual que las cuotas, y la ley permite exigir judicialmente los gastos comunes, ordinarios o extraordinarios, a través del proceso monitorio, sin perjuicio de que se puedan utilizar otros procedimientos judiciales.
El vecino también puede recurrir. Por su parte, el propietario afectado puede llevar el acuerdo a los tribunales si considera que es contrario a la ley o a los estatutos o que le causa un grave perjuicio, según prevé el artículo 18 de la ley. Aunque hay una condición que conviene tener presente si eres tú el que debe dinero, ya que para impugnar hay que estar al corriente de pago de las deudas vencidas con la comunidad o consignarlas judicialmente.
Al final, la comunidad puede reclamar lo que se le debe y, si se cumplen los requisitos, acordar a la vez restricciones mientras dure el impago, porque son dos mecanismos diferentes que no se excluyen.

articles.title: El trabajo de moda en ingeniería de software ya no es programar: es reunirse con el cliente para asegurarse de que la IA funcione
articles.text:
Lo que conocíamos tradicionalmente como ingeniero de software ahora es una etiqueta que abarca muchos más espacios que antes. Y es que ante el vertiginoso ritmo de la IA, es una posición que ya mira hacia direcciones muy diferentes. Una prueba muy interesante de ello la muestra la última newsletter de Lenny Rachitsky sobre mercado laboral tecnológico. Su informe destaca que los puestos más cercanos al cliente están en pleno auge, mientras que las especialidades vinculadas a una sola plataforma se están contrayendo rápidamente.
Por qué importa. Según Rachitsky, las ofertas de empleo en ingeniería móvil y front-end se han reducido casi a la mitad en el último año. Apoyándose en los datos de TrueUp, que realiza seguimiento de ofertas de trabajo en más de 9.000 empresas tecnológicas, y Live Data Technologies, que hace seguimiento del empleo en EEUU, el autor señala que las vacantes para ingenieros FDE (Forward Deployed Engineer) se han multiplicado por 4,6, alcanzando alrededor de 1.500 en todo el mundo.
Según cuenta Rachitsky, los puestos de ingeniería disponibles aumentaron un 29 % en 2024, un 15 % en 2025 y apenas un 2,5 % en el último año. Además, el autor explica que las empresas estadounidenses contrataron a unos 113.000 ingenieros de software entre mayo de 2025 y abril de 2026, menos de la mitad del máximo de 239.000 alcanzado en 2022. A pesar de que la ingeniería sigue liderando puestos en cuanto a oportunidades laborales, casi importa más en lo que te especializas que en el título del puesto.
El puesto de moda. Un FDE es un ingeniero de software que trabaja entre el producto técnico de su empresa y el entorno del cliente, construyendo e implementando software dentro de los propios sistemas y datos del mismo. Tal y como cuenta Rachitsky, Palantir fue pionera en este modelo, y advierte de que parte de este aumento puede deberse a un cambio de denominación, ya que puestos como “ingeniero de ventas” se están rebautizando ahora como FDE.
Fortune, citando datos de Lightcast, cuenta que las ofertas de empleo de este rol han aumentado más de un 1.000 % entre enero y agosto de 2026 en comparación con el mismo periodo del año anterior, frente al 13 % de crecimiento de las ofertas tecnológicas en general. Lightcast comparte que el salario medio anunciado es superior a 188.000 dólares para estos puestos. Grandes tecnológicas y laboratorios de IA como Microsoft, Meta, Google, OpenAI y Anthropic tienen vacantes para FDE.
Paul Farnsworth, presidente de la plataforma de empleo Dice, contaba a Fortune que las empresas disponen de potentes modelos de IA, pero tienen dificultades para conectarlos con sus propios datos, sistemas y flujos de trabajo. Los FDE cubren ese vacío, y añade que el verdadero elemento diferenciador es la capacidad de “conectar ese conocimiento técnico con un problema de negocio”.
Los puestos que caen. La lectura de Rachitsky es que las disciplinas de ingeniería estrechas y aisladas están colapsando, y que equipos más pequeños con una mayor propiedad general están tomando el relevo gracias a la IA.
El informe State of Talent 2026 de SignalFire va también por esa dirección, apuntando que la cuota de los puestos de front-end se había reducido aproximadamente un 25 %, un descenso muy pronunciado entre las especialidades de ingeniería. Afirma que la IA generativa permite a los generalistas de back-end construir y modificar interfaces de usuario al instante. LeadDev, utilizando datos de TalentNeuron, también respalda esa caída, mientras que añade que las ofertas de full-stack aumentaron un 9 %.
Entre líneas. Paralelamente, los datos del Indeed Hiring Lab muestran un repunte en las ofertas de desarrollo de software en EEUU. Según el informe, las ofertas han aumentado un 15 % desde que se lanzó Claude Code en febrero de 2025, incluso cuando las ofertas generales cayeron un 7 %, aunque siguen estando aproximadamente un 27,5 % por debajo de los niveles previos a la pandemia. Los datos de Indeed también señalan que los puestos sénior representan el 71 % del incremento entre mayo de 2025 y mayo de 2026, y el 37 % procede de puestos que incluyen IA en el título.
Por lo tanto, el “estancamiento” de Rachitsky y el “repunte” de Indeed pueden ser ciertos a la vez. Ademas, el autor también señala que los puestos de ingeniería especializados en seguridad son los de más rápido crecimiento después de los FDE. También comparte que el término “LLM” ha superado a Java como el más mencionado en las ofertas de empleo de ingeniería, mientras que Python sigue subiendo.
Rachitsky cuenta también que los puestos abiertos especializados en reclutar a personal tecnológico han aumentado casi un 300 % desde mediados de 2023 y sugiere que podría ser un indicador adelantado de una nueva aceleración en la contratación de ingenieros.

articles.title: Qué es Quantum Nighthawk y cómo logra ser la primera computadora cuántica tolerante a fallos
articles.text:
Nighthawk r3 es un procesador cuántico con el que se espera conectar dos unidades en 2027 para ejecutar 10.000 operaciones sobre más de 1.000 qubits. IBM plantea que la utilidad industrial de esta tecnología dependerá de combinar precisión, velocidad de cálculo y costos viables, mientras avanza hacia sistemas tolerantes a fallos.
El anuncio incluyó nuevos detalles sobre IBM Quantum Starling, la computadora cuántica tolerante a fallos que la empresa proyecta construir con capacidad para ejecutar 100 millones de operaciones. La meta forma parte de una arquitectura modular que busca ampliar la escala de los procesadores sin abandonar el rendimiento demostrado en equipos anteriores.
Hasta el momento, diferentes empresas han ejecutado 34.000 millones de circuitos en Nighthawk r2 en dos meses . Según la empresa, esas pruebas registraron mejoras de rendimiento de hasta 19 veces frente a procesadores cuánticos anteriores de IBM.
Jay Gambetta, IBM Fellow y director de IBM Research, vinculó el desempeño de los equipos con las condiciones necesarias para que la tecnología tenga aplicaciones concretas: “Que la computación cuántica sea útil depende de que los resultados puedan entregarse con precisión, velocidad y viabilidad económica. Cada uno de estos pilares es fundamental”.
Nighthawk r2 alcanzó 100.000 muestras por segundo para cargas científicas
Nighthawk r2 puede generar hasta 100.000 muestras por segundo y admite cálculos con más de 7.500 operaciones cuánticas sobre 120 qubits. Cada ejecución de un circuito produce un solo resultado, por lo que las aplicaciones requieren millones o miles de millones de muestras para resolver determinados problemas.
Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN e IBM utilizaron 1.175 millones de muestras para simular complejos proteicos de hasta 12.635 átomos vinculados al descubrimiento de medicamentos. E.ON empleó cerca de 20 millones de muestras para programar transacciones energéticas a partir de un modelo de 1.354 nodos de la red eléctrica europea.
La tecnología de reinicio rápido de qubits reduce el intervalo entre ejecuciones de circuitos y permite reunir esas muestras con mayor eficiencia. E.ON informó una mejora de 15 veces en aprendizaje automático cuántico orientado a la optimización de redes eléctricas.
IBM también comunicó una mejora de 12 veces en un experimento realizado junto con Oak Ridge National Laboratory, destinado a simular materiales magnéticos reales. La compañía indicó que los resultados fueron coherentes con experimentos de dispersión de neutrones.
El nuevo procesador incorporará 2.034 qubits físicos y diez conexiones entre chips
Nighthawk r3 fue diseñado para ejecutar 10.000 operaciones cuánticas sobre 520 qubits programables y cuenta con 2.034 qubits físicos. El procesador conserva la red cuadrada y las operaciones rápidas de su antecesor, aunque incorpora diez conexiones chip a chip denominadas l-couplers.
IBM ya probó esa estrategia al conectar procesadores Nighthawk r1 mediante cuatro l-couplers. La prueba alcanzó una fidelidad de transferencia de estados cuánticos del 99,4%, mientras la empresa mantiene como objetivo llegar al 99,9%.
También, se unieron dos módulos criogénicos en un solo sistema por primera vez. El conjunto alcanzó su temperatura de operación en menos de cinco días y se enfrió por debajo de 15 milikelvin.
Gambetta se refirió al desempeño de la generación previa y al plan de expansión de la arquitectura: “A medida que ampliemos esta arquitectura hacia computadoras cuánticas más grandes y potentes, el valor de la computación cuántica alcanzará nuevos niveles gracias a una integración más estrecha con los recursos clásicos y al avance continuo hacia la tolerancia a fallos”.
IBM integrará recursos cuánticos y clásicos en una sola plataforma
IBM Quantum Platform incorporará un entorno administrado para ejecutar flujos de trabajo que combinen computación cuántica con recursos clásicos de alto rendimiento. La propuesta contempla el uso de una computadora portátil, infraestructura en la nube o supercomputadoras para procesar tareas vinculadas con los circuitos cuánticos.
La plataforma permitirá inspeccionar, personalizar y ampliar técnicas de corrección y mitigación de errores. Mediante acceso a nivel de pulsos, los usuarios podrán controlar la temporización de las puertas cuánticas, realizar reinicios rápidos de qubits y acceder a información de medición previa a la clasificación.
Finalmente, se apoyará en esa infraestructura para que socios de software y servicios desarrollen capacidades por industria, herramientas para flujos híbridos y capas de optimización destinadas a problemas relevantes para la industria.

articles.title: Flock is asking lawmakers to regulate its cameras, as long as police don't need a warrant
articles.text:
A hot potato: Flock is fighting to improve its reputation. Not an easy task, considering that the surveillance company has been the subject of so many negative stories in recent times. Its latest attempt to placate the public is a bit of a surprise: announcing support for state rules on its license plate-reading cameras. But it draws the line at requiring police to obtain warrants before searching its databases, which is less of a surprise.
As Arizona Capitol Times reports, Flock policy director Andrea Korb told an R Street Institute webinar that the company supports state-by-state legislation governing its camera technology. It expects a wave of bills in 2027, with lawmakers interested even in states that have recently passed restrictions.
"There is a lot of fear and concern about this technology right now and we want people to know ... your legislature has looked at this and here are the safeguards that have been put in place," Korb said. "There shouldn't be unfettered access to all vehicles and all cameras for any reason."
There is, however, a fairly big sticking point, and probably the most contentious element when it comes to Flock searches: warrants. Korb backed independent third-party audits, noting these are already in place in Minnesota, but argued that requiring police to obtain warrants before searching the databases would burden officers and substantially reduce the technology's effectiveness.
Emily Grimmius, a privacy policy analyst at the Libertas Institute, argued that audits identify problems after they happen, whereas warrants could prevent civil rights violations. She is working on Utah legislation that would require warrants except in emergencies, approval before camera installations, regular audits, and stronger penalties for misuse.
"Sometimes this job should be difficult for law enforcement because due process is incredible," Grimmius said.
Flock has already announced changes to its own policies, including reducing its default data retention period from 30 days to seven. But that doesn't mean every image disappears after a week. Existing customers can retain their current retention periods, while an Evidence Mode allows specific records to be preserved for active investigations.
Customers will also be able to restrict which categories of offenses other agencies can investigate using their cameras, including blocking immigration-related searches.
The company also says it will require automated misuse detection and case codes for law enforcement searches by the end of the year. Emergency searches can bypass the code requirement but will be flagged for review. Another promised safeguard automatically suspends access when activity meets the company's criteria for abnormal behavior, pending an administrator's review.
Whether any of this restores public confidence remains to be seen. It was reported last month that two Flock cameras reappeared in Dayton, Minnesota, after the city canceled its contract and explicitly told the company not to complete work orders. Residents spotted the devices, and police were directed to remove them.
That followed a similar incident in Grass Valley, California, where Flock blamed an automated maintenance process for replacing cameras the city had deliberately removed.

articles.title: Vodacom’s 250m customers: How Safaricom is fueling growth
articles.text:
Vodacom, a pan-African technology group, is now generating growth beyond its South African home market, with Egypt, Kenya and other international markets outpacing its more mature domestic business.
The acquisition of a controlling stake in Safaricom, East Africa’s biggest telco, brings M-Pesa, Safaricom’s mobile money platform, and its vast financial services ecosystem into the group, strengthening Vodacom’s ambition to evolve beyond traditional mobile connectivity.
Vodacom reported revenue of R102.5 billion ($6.2 billion) for the six months ended 30 September 2026, a 25.6% year-on-year increase, boosted partly by the consolidation of Safaricom, according to its interim financial results on Tuesday
The results reveal a relatively mature South Africa, where growth is harder to extract, and faster-expanding markets where mobile connectivity and financial services are opening new revenue opportunities.
Egypt delivered 36.3% service revenue growth in local currency, while Safaricom grew service revenue by 13.1%. Tanzania, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Lesotho also recorded strong performances. Vodacom’s international business achieved normalised service revenue growth of 13.7%, with Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increasing 15.9%.
In South Africa, Vodacom returned its prepaid business to growth, supported by higher data consumption, while cost optimisation lifted its EBITDA margin to 37.4%, its highest level in several years.
Shameel Joosub, Vodacom’s chief executive officer, said the group had delivered one of its strongest six-month performances. “We exceeded our medium-term growth target on service revenue, EBITDA, and operating free cash flow, while also reaching the milestone of serving a quarter of a billion customers across Africa,” he said.
Vodacom added 26 million customers over the past 12 months, taking its total customer base to 250 million across Africa.
The Safaricom acquisition is becoming central to Vodacom’s ambition to diversify beyond traditional mobile connectivity and accelerate its financial services business. Vodacom increased its shareholding to 55%, consolidating Safaricom as a subsidiary from June 30. The transaction gives it greater exposure to Kenya’s mobile money ecosystem and one of the continent’s most established fintech platforms.
Vodacom and Safaricom both generated pro-forma financial services revenue of R43.1 billion ($2.6 billion) over the last 12 months. Their platforms served 108 million financial services customers, who accessed and initiated more than $575.5 billion in transaction value over the same period.
Financial services revenue grew 99% to R15.9 billion ($966 million) in the reported half-year, although that figure reflects Safaricom’s consolidation for only one quarter. On a pro-forma basis, including Safaricom in the comparative period, growth was 19.2%.
Joosub said M-Pesa is key to Vodacom’s ambition to build a business that earns money from more than calls, data and connectivity. Beyond payments, the opportunity includes savings, investments, credit and other digital financial products.
“The combination of Vodacom and Safaricom creates one of the continent’s largest FinTech platforms,” he said, adding that the platforms are expanding access to formal financial services and enabling greater economic participation for millions of people and businesses.
Financial services, fixed connectivity, digital and Internet of Things (IoT) services now account for 27.4% of Vodacom’s service revenue. Following the Safaricom acquisition, the group has raised its 2030 target for these businesses from 30% to more than 32%, demonstrating how central diversification has become to its growth strategy.
For shareholders, the interim performance has brought a handsome payout. Vodacom declared an interim dividend of 355 cents per share, up 7.6%, supported by headline earnings per share growth of 25.7% to 587 cents. Headline earnings rose 25.6% to R11.3 billion ($685 million).
The group also invested R13.3 billion ($806 million) in capital expenditure during the half, up 41%, expanding network capacity and adding infrastructure to support rising data consumption and digital services.
Joosub said Vodacom was on track to exceed its medium-term growth targets as it pursues its Vision 2030 ambitions.

articles.title: Siri co-founder backs Helix for its voice ID tech | TechCrunch
articles.text:
For years, websites have relied on technology like CAPTCHA to prove that the user on the other end is human. More recently, social media platforms have turned to photos or videos to verify users’ identities. Now, a startup called Helix is betting that voice technology can do the same job, without requiring users to hand over sensitive personal information.
The voice technology, which can run directly on a user’s device, has attracted backing from Siri co-founder Dag Kittlaus, who will also act as an adviser.
The company raised $6.2 million in funding in a round led by Chicago Ventures, with participation from BAM Ventures, Aglaé Ventures, Corazon Capital, Press On Ventures, Tusk Ventures, Yonder Ventures, Rule 30, and Brown Angel Group.
The startup was founded by Alex Oberg, Anna Dorofiyenko, and Mike Hall in 2025. Oberg previously worked at Ticketmaster, which acquired his startup; Dorofiyenko led data science teams at Live Nation and Zillow; and Hall has worked at Nike and Tinder, where he helped develop the initial matching algorithm.
At Ticketmaster, Oberg played a role in creating Verified Fan, which is designed to keep bots out of the platform. As AI advanced, he started thinking along the same lines for a new solution.
“As AI started to come up in the last two years, I was realizing that it’s going to make it increasingly difficult to determine who’s human and who’s not on the internet. Identity on the internet’s always been about proxies for identity, right? It’s your email, it’s your phone, it’s your IP address, it’s your device fingerprint, it’s your device ID,” Oberg said.
He noted that with the rise of AI agents like Instinct and Muse, the industry needs to rethink human identity on the internet and rely on biometric signals like voice, which is where Helix comes in.
Its core technology can run directly on a device to determine whether someone is human and estimate their age. The company is also running pilots to explore whether voice can be used as a biomarker to detect conditions such as drunkenness or distress.
The company can deploy its technology to replace or supplement CAPTCHA and help block bot attacks. Helix said that because its model can run locally even on an iPhone 13, the cost of deploying the technology is minimal. The startup said one of its customers is Zeel, an in-home healthcare provider that uses Helix’s tech to verify the identities of providers visiting customers’ homes.
Oberg said verifying workers, such as cabdrivers, is another use case the startup is exploring. He also said that age-verification regulations for social media platforms around the world are forcing users to trade privacy for access. Helix’s voice technology, he said, could offer an alternative.
“There’s like an avalanche of regulation coming down because essentially society has decided children should not be able to use the internet as adults. That has created a bit of a strawman argument that everyone needs to trade their privacy for the sake of security and child safety. We are that company that’s saying, nope, don’t agree. It’s a four-second voice challenge,” he said.
The CEO also emphasized the limitations of Helix’s technology, noting that it cannot reliably detect whether someone is lying. He added that its voice technology doesn’t identify individual speakers — while verifying them being unique humans — and claimed that even if the company stores a voiceprint, it cannot be used to reconstruct a person’s voice.
AI-powered fraud is also a growing problem in phone calls. But Helix believes its technology isn’t yet capable of reliably detecting AI agents during live calls.
Siri co-founder Kittlaus said that voice-identification technology has finally reached a point where it works reliably, positioning Helix to scale as AI-powered fraud increases. He also said that Helix’s work to compress its models gives the startup a cost advantage.
“What folks at Helix are doing is, instead of teaching computers how to understand speech, these guys are understanding what the speech of the speaker actually means, what’s going on with them, if they are lying, are they impaired? That side of it is fascinating to me within the larger picture that I just described,” he told TechCrunch.

What is NYT Connections?
NYT Connections is one of several increasingly popular word games made by the New York Times. It challenges you to find groups of four items that share something in common, and each group has a different difficulty level: green is easy, yellow a little harder, blue often quite tough and purple usually very difficult.
On the plus side, you don't technically need to solve the final one, as you'll be able to answer that one by a process of elimination. What's more, you can make up to four mistakes, which gives you a little bit of breathing room.
It's a little more involved than something like Wordle, however, and there are plenty of opportunities for the game to trip you up with tricks. For instance, watch out for homophones and other word games that could disguise the answers.
It's playable for free via the NYT Games site on desktop or mobile.

articles.title: 11.11: iPhone 17 (256 GB) registra alta queda de preço na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
11.11: iPhone 17 (256 GB) registra alta queda de preço na Amazon
iPhone 17 (256 GB) traz câmeras de 48 MP e tela OLED de 120 Hz; celular custo-benefício da Apple sai 36% mais em conta em oferta no Pix
O iPhone 17 de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 5.273 no Pix na Amazon. O smartphone da Apple, com câmeras de 48 MP e tela OLED de 120 Hz, recebe desconto de 36% no 11.11 sobre o preço base atual de R$ 8.299, reajustado recentemente.
O iPhone 17 é um celular custo-benefício equipado com uma tela OLED de 6,3″ com ProMotion de 120 Hz e brilho máximo de 3.000 nits. Tal combinação permite reproduzir imagens com cores excelentes e alta fluidez, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer lugar.
Seu chip Apple A19 e os 8 GB de RAM dão conta de apps em multitarefa, games e soluções do Apple Intelligence localmente. Os 256 GB de espaço interno são adequados para guardar fotos e vídeos.
O kit principal de câmeras inclui wide com OIS e ultrawide com ângulo de 120º, que captam belas cenas ao ar livre, ambas de 48 MP. A frontal de 18 MP tira ótimas selfies na horizontal, mesmo segurando o celular em pé. Todas filmam em 4K a 60 fps.
O corpo de alumínio do iPhone 17 é revestido de ambos os lados pelo vidro Ceramic Shield 2, resistente a arranhões e pancadas. A certificação IP68 adiciona proteção em cenários como ambientes empoeirados e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 3.692 mAh tem autonomia de até 30 horas de vídeo, segundo a fabricante. O suporte a MagSafe e carregamento rápido de 40 W o permitem receber uma carga de 50% em apenas 20 minutos, ideal para quem não tem tempo a perder com tomadas.
O iPhone 17 de 256 GB (R$ 5.273 no Pix) foi atualizado para o iOS 27 e receberá pelo menos mais cinco updates do sistema operacional. O celular da Apple possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, Ultra Wideband (UWB), NFC e comporta eSIM.

articles.title: Arrêter les dégâts « dans les 35 secondes » : OpenAI dévoile le kill switch censé stopper ses IA quand elles dérapent
articles.text:
Si l’été a été la saison des crises cyber chez OpenAI, l’automne doit être celle de la reprise en main.
L’entreprise américaine a dévoilé le 10 novembre Control Room, un service qui suit l’ensemble des modèles en activité dans son infrastructure de recherche et qui, selon le billet d’OpenAI, « interrompt la génération du modèle dans les 35 secondes suivant une décision d’intervention » lorsqu’un problème de sûreté ou de sécurité est détecté.
L’outil arrive après plusieurs mois agités. Le 21 juillet, OpenAI révélait notamment que plusieurs de ses agents étaient sortis de leur environnement de test et avaient piraté les serveurs de Hugging Face, la grande plateforme de partage de modèles d’IA.
En août, l’entreprise annonçait avoir suspendu une partie de ses entraînements pendant deux semaines afin de revoir sa sécurité, avant de les relancer. Ce qui n’a visiblement pas suffi. Le 20 septembre, un agent en cours d’entraînement a contourné les restrictions réseau de son bac à sable, ce qui a conduit OpenAI à suspendre de nouveau les travaux sur ses modèles les plus puissants.
Le modèle de surveillance avait bien levé une alerte au bout d’une douzaine de minutes, mais la tâche n’a été stoppée que près de 2 h 45 après le début de l’incident. C’est précisément ce délai que Control Room doit réduire.
Comment Control Room coupe une tâche
Concrètement, Control Room est conçu comme un verrou placé au cœur de l’inférence, comprenez le moment où le modèle produit ses réponses.
À son lancement, chaque tâche de recherche (expérience d’apprentissage par renforcement, évaluation, traitement de données) reçoit de Control Room un identifiant unique. Chaque fois qu’elle sollicite un modèle, le moteur d’inférence, autrement dit le modèle qui tourne sur les GPU, demande l’autorisation à Control Room en lui transmettant cet identifiant.
Lorsque le modèle de surveillance chargé d’examiner le comportement de l’IA repère un problème, il peut ordonner l’arrêt de la tâche, et toutes ses requêtes suivantes sont alors refusées.
OpenAI explique avoir placé ce verrou dans la couche d’inférence plutôt que dans le code des expériences, que les chercheurs modifient sans cesse et qui serait donc trop fragile pour porter une protection de sécurité. À l’inverse, l’inférence passe par un petit nombre de chemins communs à toute la recherche de l’entreprise, ce qui en fait un point de passage obligé.
Le système applique aussi le principe du « refus en cas de défaillance ». Si Control Room tombe en panne ou est désactivé, y compris de manière malveillante, toutes les requêtes sont bloquées jusqu’à son rétablissement.
Un délai que l’entreprise veut ramener à zéro
Pour l’instant, le blocage par défaut ne couvre que les travaux sur les modèles de pointe et doit être étendu au reste de la recherche dans les prochains jours. Les modèles accessibles au public ne sont pas concernés.
Les 35 secondes de latence s’expliquent par la quantité de requêtes à traiter. Faire valider chaque demande en temps réel par Control Room saturerait le service, alors OpenAI a ajouté une couche de mise en cache. Les moteurs gardent en mémoire pendant un court moment les autorisations qu’on leur a accordées, au lieu de reposer la question à chaque fois. OpenAI dit travailler à « ramener ce délai à zéro pour pouvoir arrêter les tâches instantanément ».
Avec cette solution, l’entreprise américaine cherche à rassurer, alors qu’au Congrès américain des élus veulent donner un droit de regard à l’État. Déposé le 23 juillet dans la foulée de l’incident Hugging Face, l’AI Kill Switch Act obligerait les géants de l’IA à garantir la capacité technique de stopper leurs modèles, et autoriserait le département de la Sécurité intérieure à leur en donner l’ordre en cas de perte de contrôle. Le texte est toujours en attente d’examen à la Chambre des représentants.
