articles.title: Ecovacs casse les prix : le GOAT A1600 perd 800 €
articles.text:
Aspirer, laver les sols, tondre la pelouse… Ecovacs n’attend pas le Black Friday pour faire baisser le prix de ses robots. Deux aspirateurs robots laveurs et un robot tondeuse profitent de remises pouvant atteindre 800 €, valables jusqu’au Cyber Monday du 30 novembre.
Vous le savez sans doute, le ménage et l’entretien du jardin partagent un terrible point commun : ils reviennent toujours. À peine les sols nettoyés, les poussières, miettes et autres poils d’animaux refont leur apparition. Et lorsque la pelouse commence à prendre quelques centimètres de trop, il faut également trouver le courage de ressortir la tondeuse. Pour répondre à ces problématiques, à l’occasion du Black Friday, la marque met l’accent sur deux aspirateurs robots laveurs particulièrement autonomes, ainsi qu’un robot tondeuse destiné à prendre en charge l'entretien du jardin.
Et l’autre bonne nouvelle pour celles et ceux qui envisagent de s’équiper, c’est que ces trois appareils profitent de promotions jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026, avec des réductions pouvant atteindre 800 euros.
DEEBOT T90S PRO OMNI : un aspirateur robot qui soigne aussi le lavage des sols
Un robot aspirateur qui se contente de ramasser les poussières, c’est déjà très pratique. Mais s’il peut également laver les sols, nettoyer sa propre serpillière et gérer une bonne partie de son entretien, alors l’expérience prend une autre dimension. C'est justement ce que propose le DEEBOT T90S PRO OMNI.
Son système OZMO ROLLER 3.0 repose sur un rouleau de microfibres de 27 cm, alimenté en eau propre grâce à 32 jets sous pression. Celui-ci tourne jusqu’à 260 tours par minute et exerce une pression de 4 000 Pa pour s’attaquer aux traces et autres saletés incrustées. Un système de rinçage continu évacue les eaux sales au fil du nettoyage, afin de limiter les risques de redéposer les saletés sur le sol.
Ecovacs promet une réduction de 67 % des traces d’eau résiduelles.
Côté aspiration, la technologie BLAST annonce jusqu’à 40 000 Pa et un débit d’air de 16 L/s. La brosse principale ZeroTangle 4.0 limite quant à elle l’enchevêtrement des cheveux et des poils, un point intéressant pour les propriétaires d'animaux.
La technologie AIVI 3D 4.0 améliore quant à elle la détection des obstacles et permet au robot de longer les murs et les meubles avec davantage de précision. Il peut ainsi nettoyer au plus près des bordures, tout en limitant les contacts et en optimisant la couverture des surfaces.
Le T90S PRO OMNI soigne également les finitions avec TruEdge 3.0, une technologie qui permet au rouleau de s’étendre de 1,5 cm pour longer les plinthes et atteindre ces zones habituellement délaissées. Il peut franchir des seuils jusqu’à 2,5 cm et deux obstacles consécutifs jusqu'à 4,9 cm. Sur les tapis, le rouleau se soulève automatiquement de 15 mm pour éviter de mouiller les fibres. Pratique !
Enfin, sa station OMNI automatise une bonne partie de son entretien. Elle se charge de laver le rouleau et le réservoir d’eaux usées avec de l’eau chauffée jusqu’à 75 °C, avant de procéder au séchage à l’air chaud à plus de 60 °C. Le robot bénéficie également de la recharge rapide PowerBoost, qui lui permet de récupérer 10 % de batterie en seulement trois minutes.
À partir du 9 novembre et jusqu’au 30 novembre, le DEEBOT T90S PRO OMNI passe de 799 à 549 euros, soit 300 euros de remise.
DEEBOT T90 MAX PRO Care Kit : 40 000 Pa pour ne rien laisser traîner
Le DEEBOT T90 MAX PRO Care Kit reprend les grandes lignes de cette approche, avec en prime un argument supplémentaire du côté de l’aspiration. Ici, Ecovacs annonce jusqu’à 40 000 Pa grâce à sa technologie BLAST, avec un débit d’air de 16,45 L/s. De quoi s’attaquer aussi bien aux poussières quotidiennes qu’aux miettes et aux poils d’animaux présents sur les sols durs et les tapis.
Le robot embarque lui aussi le système OZMO ROLLER 3.0, avec un rouleau de 27 cm, une pression de 4 000 Pa et une rotation à 260 tours par minute. Celui-ci est rincé en continu grâce à 32 jets d’eau, tandis que la technologie TruEdge 3.0 améliore le nettoyage le long des murs et des plinthes.
La station OMNI constitue un autre élément intéressant. Elle lave le rouleau à 100 °C, puis le sèche à 45 °C. Elle assure également le vidage automatique de la poussière dans un sac de 2,5 litres. Le robot relève par ailleurs son rouleau de 15 mm lorsqu’il détecte un tapis, afin d’éviter de mouiller les fibres.
Pour compléter l’ensemble, pas de technologie AIVI 3D 4.0 ici, mais une navigation dToF LiDAR associée à TrueDetect 3D, ainsi qu’un système ZeroTangle 4.0 destiné à limiter les cheveux coincés dans la brosse. Son profil de 95 mm lui permet également de passer sous certains meubles bas.
Enfin, l’appellation “Care Kit” n’est pas anodine, puisque cette version est livrée avec des accessoires supplémentaires, notamment deux brosses latérales, une brosse cylindrique et trois cartouches filtrantes.
À partir du 9 novembre et jusqu’au 30 novembre, le DEEBOT T90 MAX PRO Blanc Care Kit sera proposé à 399 euros au lieu de 599 euros, soit 200 euros d’économie.
GOAT A1600 LiDAR PRO Care Kit : la tondeuse qui s’occupe aussi des bordures
Changement de décor, puisqu’avec le GOAT A1600 LiDAR PRO Care Kit, Ecovacs s’attaque cette fois à l’entretien de la pelouse, avec un robot tondeuse conçu pour fonctionner sans câble périphérique.
Son système de navigation Dual-LiDAR HoloScope 360 associe un LiDAR rotatif à 360°, un capteur 3D-ToF et une caméra dotée d’intelligence artificielle. De quoi permettre à l’ensemble de cartographier automatiquement le jardin et de planifier les déplacements du robot, avec une précision annoncée de 2 cm.
Mais sa particularité la plus intéressante se trouve peut-être au niveau des bordures. Le GOAT A1600 LiDAR PRO intègre en effet un coupe-bordures TruEdge, destiné à automatiser également cette finition, souvent laissée à la charge d’un appareil supplémentaire (comme un rotofil par exemple). Ecovacs annonce ainsi une coupe au plus près des bordures via son trimmer intégré.
Sous son capot, le robot dispose de deux disques de coupe, sa capacité de tonte peut atteindre 400 m² par heure, tandis que la hauteur de coupe se règle électriquement entre 3 et 9 cm. Il est également en mesure de gérer des pentes jusqu’à 50 % (27°) et de franchir des barrières de 4 cm. La détection des obstacles repose sur la technologie AIVI 3D, capable d’identifier plus de 200 types d’objets, y compris les petits animaux.
Là aussi, le pack “Care Kit” permet de bénéficier d’un ensemble d’accessoires d’entretien supplémentaires, avec pas moins de 48 lames de rechange, et pour le trimmer, 4 rouleaux de fil de coupe et 2 capots. De quoi voir venir les beaux jours avec une certaine sérénité.
Le GOAT A1600 LiDAR PRO Care Kit voit lui aussi son prix chuter à partir du 9 novembre : il passe de 1 599 à 799 euros, soit 800 euros d’économie, et l’offre reste valable jusqu’au 30 novembre, le jour du Cyber Monday. L’occasion d’équiper le jardin à moitié prix bien avant que la pelouse ne reprenne de la vigueur au printemps.

articles.title: AWS had its agents build a free and open emulator for AWS. They now maintain it, too.
articles.text:
AWS had its agents build a free and open emulator for AWS. They now maintain it, too.
AWS on Wednesday launched an emulator for AWS called AWS Emulator.
That, by itself, is interesting and may raise some questions about the future of LocalStack. But what’s maybe most interesting is that the emulator was entirely built by a team of agents and will also be maintained by them going forward.
Since AWS wasn’t sure it could actually copyright the work of these agents — and didn’t want to assert copyright where none may exist — the emulator is available under the Creative Commons Zero license, which puts the code into the public domain.
Tom ‘Spot’ Callaway, a principal open source software strategist at AWS, told The New Stack that there have obviously been other emulators in the past — and AWS itself has built some, too.
“The challenge is that they get out of date very quickly,” he explains. “They don’t always reflect reality on the ground, and because of that, they’re often not trusted. And we didn’t even trust them internally.”
With the rise of agentic coding tools, the team also saw a need for a better emulator that could help agents test code against AWS services without having to hand over AWS credentials to the agents.
Meanwhile, the team was also looking at a test case for building a full project with agents, and the emulator proved to be a good testing ground, in large part because it provided a bounded problem with clear goals and the ability to test the results.
Since AWS already publishes a full set of API models as Smithy models and generates all its SDKs from those files, “there’s no reason that we can’t also generate mock emulation around that same logic,” Callaway says.
A weekend Kiro experiment
The project goes back to an experiment by Matt Goldberg, a senior principal engineer on the AWS Developer Tools team. Callaway says the team was “heavily inspired by the Anthropic work where they instantiated a compiler,” referring to the C compiler that Anthropic researchers had a team of agents build earlier this year.
Goldberg writes in a blog post that he first asked Kiro, AWS’s agentic coding tool, to build an emulator for Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS). It came back with a first version 15 minutes later. He then had Kiro build out the rest of AWS over a weekend. That version unsurprisingly had gaps, he notes, but his team started testing its own software against it the following Monday.
“I got to admit, the first time I heard about this, I was like, ‘Are we sure this is a good idea?’” Callaway says.
The more the team iterated on it, he adds, the more comfortable he became that this was a good problem for agents to take on.
In its current version, AWS Emulator supports 438 public AWS API models covering more than 200 services. As AWS updates them and releases new services, the agents will quickly update the emulator, too.
Callaway expects the gap between a new AWS service launching and the emulator supporting it to be “days, not weeks, not months,” though he notes the team hasn’t yet seen how that plays out with the project in public.
The emulator itself is written in Rust and runs locally on Linux, macOS, and Windows, without a network connection or an AWS account.
“There’s no AI inside of AWS Emulator,” Callaway says. “It does not do an LLM callout at all.”
Three teams of agents
AWS says it divides the work among three teams of agents. The first develops test scenarios from the public Smithy models and runs them against real AWS services to establish how the emulator should behave.
These scenarios can involve several services working together, rather than just individual API calls. As Callaway explains, “if the docs don’t tell the truth, then the cloud becomes the source of truth.”
The second team runs those scenarios against the emulator and investigates where its behavior differs from AWS. It groups failures that appear to have a common cause and files issues in the code repository.
Finally, the third team picks up those issues and changes the code to address them. Before those changes can merge, they have to pass build and test checks, as well as reviews by other agents for security problems, coding standards, and regressions in the emulator’s behavior.
The human engineers, meanwhile, focus on improving the system that directs the agents.
“We don’t edit it. We don’t modify it,” Callaway says of the emulator’s code. “If we find that the code has issues, we try and trace those issues back to the agent and fix the agent so that it doesn’t make bad code.”
So when there is a problem in the code those agents generated, the team will change how the agents work, rather than patch the code by hand.
Goldberg writes that an earlier version of the agents at one point decided to write their own Python interpreter so the emulator could support Lambda functions. The team has since instructed them to reuse existing libraries.
“I think we’ve learned a lot about sandboxing,” Callaway says, “haven’t we all in the last few months?”
The first iterations of the system “did not have as aggressive a sandbox as they needed to,” he says, and there was some early concern about the agents looking at the source code of AWS’s internal services to figure out how to implement something like Aurora. The team also spent a lot of time reassuring Amazon executives that the framework building the emulator wasn’t going to “go rogue.”
No pull requests accepted
That hands-off approach goes for outside contributors, too.
“We’re not going to take pull requests on the project at all,” Callaway says. “The agents will be doing that. We will take issues from customers.”
He describes the agents as “their own little pull request army.” If they keep getting a particular API wrong, “that’s a bug in the agent,” he says, and he expects customers to mostly contribute scenarios the emulator doesn’t handle well yet.
AWS is also publishing the benchmark it uses to test the emulator “so that you can not trust us,” Callaway says. “You can run that benchmark.” Others could also use it to benchmark their own work, he notes.
What the emulator can’t do
Users shouldn’t expect the emulator to do the things the actual services do, though.
“I run this SQL query, and I don’t get the right results,” Callaway says. “Well, guess what? There’s no database.” The emulator, he says, “really was built for the purposes of testing coverage.”
AWS says it will share more about the project at its re:Invent conference, which starts Nov. 30. The New Stack will be there — and we’re even throwing a party.

articles.title: Tata Motors partners with Finzo EV Solutions to make electric commercial vehicles more accessible
articles.text:
Tata Motors partners with Finzo EV Solutions to make electric commercial vehicles more accessible
Under the MoU, Tata Motors customers will get access to quick loan disbursements, flexible repayment plans and a 25% assured buyback guarantee.
Tata Motors has partnered with battery lifecycle firm Finzo EV Solutions (Turno) for providing tailor-made financing schemes for its electric Small Commercial Vehicle and Pickup (e-SCVPU) customers.
Under the memorandum of understanding (MoU), Tata Motors customers will get access to quick loan disbursements, flexible repayment plans and a 25% assured buyback guarantee, the company said.
"Our partnership with Turno strengthens our EV ecosystem by offering end-to-end ownership support to customers. By removing financing hurdles and safeguarding long-term resale value, we are empowering customers across the country to switch to zero-emission mobility with greater confidence," said Pinaki Haldar, Vice President & Business Head for SCVPU at Tata Motors Ltd.
As electric commercial mobility gains momentum, customers need greater clarity and assurance around the value of their vehicle over its lifecycle, said Varun Nair, Director, Turno.
"Our partnership with Tata Motors brings together customised financing and assured buyback support to address these needs and make the transition to electric mobility easier.
"By leveraging our expertise in battery intelligence and EV lifecycle management, along with our assured buyback programme, we are building greater certainty around the ownership and resale journey of electric commercial vehicles," Nair added.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes Exchange sign-ins broken by Windows Server updates
articles.text:
Microsoft has fixed Outlook sign-in and mail delivery issues on Exchange Server systems after installing the October 2026 Windows Server security updates.
Microsoft acknowledged this known issue in mid-October, confirming that users had trouble accessing email or signing in to Outlook after installing the latest updates on systems running Windows Server 2019 and later.
As explained at the time, the sign-in and mail flow issues are caused by a new default limit on the amount of memory Endpoint Mapper uses when handling Endpoint Lookup calls, introduced by the October 2026 updates.
"After installing the October 2026 Windows security update [..], some on-premises Exchange servers might experience issues accessing or sending email. Users might be unable to sign in to Outlook on the web (OWA), or email messages sent from Outlook might remain in the Outbox and not be delivered. Additionally, Exchange might experience issues accessing mailboxes during mailbox replication," Microsoft said at the time.
"Not all Exchange servers will be impacted by installation of those updates equally; the severity and speed of impact varies based on Exchange server load. Some servers might never see a problem," it added in a separate blog describing the issues.
However, Microsoft said that this Outlook on the web (OWA) known issue isn't linked to the October 2026 Exchange server security updates and urged customers not to uninstall them.
Fixed by November Patch Tuesday updates
In a new update to the Windows release health dashboard, Microsoft said the November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates (KB5131080 and KB5131090) address this known issue and advised affected users to install them on all affected systems.
Microsoft also shared a temporary workaround that should resolve these issues for those who can't immediately deploy this month's cumulative updates, which requires modifying a registry key on affected Exchange Server systems.
To do that, IT administrators have to run the following command from an elevated Command Prompt on the Exchange Server to increase the maximum number of Endpoint Lookup calls and the amount of memory that Endpoint Mapper can use, and then restart the device:
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Rpc" /v EpmapSavedContextCap /t REG_DWORD /d 65536 /f
After the system reboots, the admins should monitor the Exchange environment and raise the Endpoint Mapper memory limit if it recurs.

articles.title: Les radars militaires peuvent désactiver une partie de votre réseau Wi-Fi et vous ne pouvez rien faire
articles.text:
Vous êtes chez vous, et le canal 5 GHz de votre réseau Wi-Fi se coupe d’un seul coup : tous vos appareils basculent alors sur le 2,4 GHz, parfois avec peine. Aucune explication, vous vous dites que c’est un bug ; peut-être que vous redémarrez votre box. En réalité, c’est peut-être à cause d’un radar militaire si ce canal s’est coupé.
Le canal 5 GHz de votre réseau Wi-Fi se coupe tout seul ? C’est peut-être normal
Effectivement, votre box Internet ou votre routeur Wi-Fi peut parfois abandonner brutalement le canal 5 GHz et tout faire basculer sur le 2,4 GHz. Si vous avez un écran dessus, ou un journal, il y aura peut-être un message affiché, indiquant simplement « radar ». Il ne s’agit généralement pas d’un bug, mais d’un mécanisme réglementaire, baptisé Dynamic Frequency Selection (DFS).
Il oblige le Wi-Fi à céder la place aux radars, y compris les radars militaires. En France, les bandes 5 GHz ne sont pas entièrement libres : une partie est partagée avec des services prioritaires, notamment des radars. C’est l’ANFR, l’Agence Nationale des Fréquences Radio, qui gère les bandes de fréquences dans le pays. Concernant les bandes 5 GHz, parmi les radars prioritaires il y a ceux dédiés à la météorologie, l’aéronautique, l’armée, ou pour les communications satellites. Donc lorsqu’un routeur Wi-Fi détecte un signal radar sur le canal qu’il utilise, il doit arrêter d’émettre sur ce canal et en choisir un autre, le plus souvent le 2,4 GHz, qu’on trouve sur tous les routeurs.
Si le retour du canal 5 GHz prend du temps, c’est normal : avant de l’utiliser à nouveau, votre routeur doit « l’écouter » pour vérifier que plus aucun radar n’est présent. En Europe, la norme ETSI relative au 5 GHz impose qu’un équipement doit quitter le canal dans les 10 secondes et ne pas le réutiliser durant au moins 30 minutes.
Les radars de l’armée et de Météo France ont la priorité sur votre box Internet
Sur son site, l’ANFR donne un exemple, celui de Météo France : l’organisme dispose « de plus radars hydrométéorologiques en bande C utilisant des fréquences 5 GHz réparties sur le territoire français » pour étudier les précipitations. Mais ils peuvent être gênés par des fréquences 5 GHz utilisées de manière non conforme et fausser les prévisions de Météo France. Même chose pour des radars militaires, on peut l’imaginer.
C’est pourquoi les équipements Wi-Fi pour les particuliers doivent avoir un comportement réglementé. Un équipement doit notamment « scanner en continu la bande de fréquence dans laquelle il fonctionne pour vérifier qu’il n’y a pas un radar météo ou une autre application autorisée utilisant la même fréquence », précise l’ANFR. C’est là qu’entre en jeu la sélection de fréquences dynamique, ou DFS. L’agence nationale dit d’ailleurs constater des perturbations très régulières des radars météo. Si la prochaine fois il pleut alors que ce n’était pas prévu, ce n’est peut-être pas la faute d’Évelyne Dhéliat ou de votre application météo, mais peut-être celle de votre box Internet.
S’il est avéré que c’est votre box Internet ou votre routeur Wi-Fi qui a brouillé des radars météo par exemple, vous encourrez d’ailleurs des sanctions pénales. L’article L39-1 du Code des postes et des communications électroniques sanctionne le fait de perturber les émissions d’un service autorisé en utilisant une fréquence, un équipement ou une installation radioélectrique dans des conditions non conformes. Les contrevenants s’exposent à six mois d’emprisonnement et 30 000 euros d’amende. Mais pas d’inquiétude à avoir : si vous n’avez pas désactivé le DFS de votre équipement Wi-Fi, vous n’avez rien à craindre. À noter qu’il est interdit de désactiver ou modifier le DFS de ses appareils Wi-Fi et en théorie, ce n’est pas possible de le faire. S’il est possible sur certains routeurs de privilégier des canaux non-DFS, il ne faut pas utiliser cette fonction pour contourner les obligations réglementaires.

articles.title: Inside the economics of OPay and Moniepoint’s business
articles.text:
A Bolt driver in Nigeria will likely ask you to pay via OPay at the end of a trip, while a local store is more likely to have a Moniepoint terminal at its checkout. Both fintechs, which hold microfinance banking licences, have become synonymous with scale in Nigeria’s payments market, carving out niches in consumer payments and merchant processing.
In 2025, Nigeria processed more than ₦1.2 quadrillion ($880.51 billion) worth of electronic transactions. Moniepoint and OPay accounted for a significant share of this activity, processing a combined $644.85 billion.
Moniepoint said it processed 14 billion transactions worth ₦412 trillion ($286.85 billion at ₦1,436.31/$ as of December 31, 2025) in 2025. OPay processed 62.3 billion transactions worth $358 billion. OPay processed 4.45 times as many transactions as Moniepoint, but Moniepoint’s average transaction value was $20.49, approximately 3.56 times OPay’s $5.75.
Moniepoint said it serves more than 20 million businesses and individuals, while OPay reported 50.1 million monthly active users.
These numbers offer a window into the operating economics of both companies: who moves more money, who makes more money from moving it, and who keeps more of what they make?
It is important to note that Moniepoint operates largely in Nigeria, with a recent expansion into Kenya. OPay operates in Indonesia, Egypt, and Pakistan, but derives most of its scale from Nigeria. It generated 88.1% of its revenue from the country in 2025.
What the average numbers show
Moniepoint’s average transaction value of $20.49 is approximately 3.56 times OPay’s $5.75.
This difference could reflect Moniepoint’s greater concentration of merchant payments, business transactions, or other relatively large payments. OPay’s lower average could reflect more frequent, lower-value consumer transactions.
These are hypotheses rather than confirmed explanations. The companies’ transaction disclosures do not provide enough detail to establish exactly what drives the difference.
There are other indicators of how frequently their customers use their platforms. OPay says its digital wallets were used an average of 209 times per user per month. Moniepoint said its cards were used 1.7 million times daily.
However, the total value passing through a payment platform is not the same as the revenue it earns. Their revenue depends on fees, commissions, lending, merchant services, and other income sources.
OPay disclosed $536.25 million in revenue in 2025. Moniepoint does not publicly disclose revenue figures.
One way to illustrate Moniepoint’s revenue potential is to examine OPay’s revenue relative to the value it processed. Its $536.25 million in revenue represented about 0.15% of its $358 billion in transaction value.
If Moniepoint generated revenue at the same rate, its $286.85 billion in transaction value would translate to approximately $430.28 million in revenue.
This is an illustrative scenario, not an estimate of Moniepoint’s actual revenue. The two companies have different transaction mixes, fee structures, and revenue sources.
Loans are becoming another revenue engine
Both OPay and Moniepoint increased their lending activity in 2025, using the financial activity passing through their platforms to extend credit.
OPay originated $938.3 million in new loans in Nigeria, up 284.71% in one year.
Moniepoint, meanwhile, said it disbursed more than ₦1 trillion ($696.23 million) in loans to small businesses in 2025. In 2023, it disbursed $71 million in working capital loans.
Moniepoint uses its merchant relationships to extend business credit. Its terminals give it visibility into how much a business processes, how frequently it receives payments, and how its transaction activity changes over time.
This provides an alternative source of information for assessing a business that may not have conventional financial statements or sufficient collateral.
The company’s lending portfolio targets merchants, including provision stores, supermarkets, restaurants, and wholesale distributors. It says businesses that received its loans recorded an average 36% increase in transaction value after accessing credit.
OPay’s lending operation has a broader consumer-facing distribution advantage. Its wallet gives it access to millions of users who already transact frequently on the platform. In 2025, its quarterly unique borrowers in Nigeria reached 4.6 million, more than twice the 2.1 million recorded a year earlier.
While OPay has built much of its credit product around consumers, it is also looking to expand merchant lending, which it recently introduced. The company says merchant loans typically feature higher limits, lower rates, and longer tenors aligned with business cash flow cycles.
Both companies are effectively turning payment histories into credit intelligence, but they are applying that information to different customer segments.
For OPay, lending is already a significant contributor to revenue. In 2025, it generated $260.3 million in loan financing revenue, up from $71.5 million in 2024. This represented growth of approximately 264.1% and accounted for 48.5% of its total revenue.
But lending also carries risks. OPay’s provision for expected credit losses increased from $24.8 million in 2024 to $121.3 million in 2025, nearly five times the previous year’s figure.
The provision was approximately 46.6% of its loan-financing revenue. This is not the same as realised loan losses, but it shows the growing credit risk exposure accompanying the expansion of its lending business.
Moniepoint’s lending economics are not public, making it difficult to establish how much revenue its credit business generates or how much it spends managing defaults. The company claims that its non-performing loans (NPLs), loans for which principal or interest payments are overdue by 90 days or more, are small.
According to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), NPLs rose to 7% in 2025.
Profits
Processing billions of transactions and generating hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue is one thing. Turning that activity into profit is another.
For payment companies, scale comes with considerable costs: technology infrastructure, transaction processing, customer acquisition, regulatory compliance, fraud management, staff costs, and, increasingly, the cost of extending credit.
OPay generated $536.25 million in revenue in 2025 and ultimately made $110.79 million in income before taxes. That translates to a net profit margin of approximately 20.66%. In other words, it retained about 21 cents in profit per dollar of revenue.
Moniepoint does not disclose its revenue or profit figures. However, applying OPay’s revenue-to-transaction-value ratio and net profit margin to Moniepoint’s transaction value produces an estimated profit of $88.89 million. This is an indicative estimate, not a reported financial result, and assumes both companies have comparable revenue yields and cost structures.
The numbers show how OPay has built a high-frequency payments business and is increasingly extracting revenue from lending. Nearly half of its 2025 revenue came from loan financing, although rising complaints about high interest rates to cover credit-loss provisions indicate that this growth carries additional risk.
Moniepoint, on the other hand, has built a merchant-focused payments network that gives it access to business transaction data and opportunities to extend working capital. Its higher average transaction value and growing lending portfolio point to a different monetisation strategy: building deeper financial relationships with merchants rather than relying primarily on the frequency of everyday consumer payments.
The ₦1,000 Journey
Explore the hidden infrastructure, relationships, and data behind an everyday digital payment.
OPay: Consumer & Merchant
Moniepoint: Merchant & Consumer
Both companies have built considerable scale in Nigeria. But sustaining that position will increasingly depend on how they navigate a changing regulatory environment.
In June 2026, the CBN introduced new market-structure requirements that could constrain financial institutions seeking to dominate both consumer payments and merchant acquiring.
In a circular, the regulator stated that any licensed financial institution controlling more than 25% of the consumer-issuing market would be restricted to a maximum of 15% market share in merchant-acquiring activities.
For OPay and Moniepoint, this introduces another variable into an already competitive market. Their ability to grow will depend not only on how many transactions they process or how much revenue they generate, but also on how they position themselves across the layers of Nigeria’s payments infrastructure.

articles.title: El remake de "Zelda: Ocarina of Time" vendió 5,2 millones de copias en cuatro días
articles.text:
Nintendo vendió más de 5,2 millones de copias de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time para la consola Switch 2 en los primeros cuatro días tras su lanzamiento, el 5 de noviembre. Es la mayor cifra de ventas en un estreno de un juego publicado por la marca para esa consola, según informó la compañía.
De ese total, 810.000 unidades se vendieron en Japón, precisó la empresa en su comunicado. El juego es una recreación completa del título original de 1998 para la consola Nintendo 64, con gráficos renovados y mejoras de jugabilidad que preservan la experiencia original, indica la compañía.
El juego salió a la venta en todo el mundo a USD 59.99. Bloomberg informó que acumula 96 puntos sobre 100 en Metacritic, un sitio que reúne las notas de la prensa y de los jugadores, tanto en la valoración de los críticos como en la de los usuarios.
Solo Mario Kart World vendió más unidades en la Switch 2, según Bloomberg, que recordó que ese título formó parte del paquete de lanzamiento de la consola. El remake de Zelda ya superó las ventas acumuladas de Donkey Kong Bananza, otro título popular de 2025.
Una consola que esperaba un éxito
Bloomberg describió el primer año de la Switch 2 como irregular, con precios de equipos más altos por el encarecimiento de la memoria. El medio comparó el efecto potencial con el de la primera Switch, que en 2017 salió con The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild y atrajo a jugadores ajenos a Nintendo.
Nintendo confirmó oficialmente que vendió más de 26 millones de consolas Switch 2 en total, según informó la compañía en su comunicado.
Antes del comunicado ya había indicadores. El sitio Nintendo Everything recordó que el juego tuvo el segundo mayor estreno de la serie Zelda en el Reino Unido y el mayor lanzamiento en formato físico de 2026 en ese país.
El lugar del remake dentro de la serie
Según el cálculo de TheGamer, con 5,2 millones el remake ya es el octavo título más vendido de la serie. Superó a Phantom Hourglass, con 4,76 millones, y a A Link to the Past, con 4,61 millones, y quedó por detrás de la versión de Ocarina para la Nintendo 3DS, con 6,44 millones.
El medio también calculó que le faltan unos 1,31 millones de copias para superar al primer The Legend of Zelda, de 1986, y que el Ocarina original de 1998 vendió 7,6 millones. La saga cumple 40 años en 2026. Los títulos más vendidos de la serie, siempre según TheGamer, son Breath of the Wild, con casi 35 millones de copias, y Tears of the Kingdom, con 21,73 millones.
El remake también tiene una prueba pendiente en Estados Unidos. Nintendo Everything indicó que habrá que esperar a la publicación del informe de ventas de noviembre de la consultora Circana, prevista para el 17 de diciembre, para conocer su desempeño en ese mercado.

articles.title: Rockstar confirma el tamaño del mapa de GTA 6: la superficie total, con Vice City y alrededores, es casi tan grande como los mapas de GTA IV, GTA V y RDR 2 juntos
articles.text:
Podemos decir que el territorio terrestre de Leonida (donde están Vice City y sus alrededores) es casi igual de grande que los mapas jugables de GTA IV, GTA V y Red Dead Redemption 2 juntos. Esto es lo que nos cuentan desde Rockstar sobre el próximo mundo abierto de GTA 6.
Por otro lado, también podemos compararlo con GTA V. El nuevo mapa es algo así como el doble de grande. Esto incluye a Vice City y su entorno. Y eso es algo que ya habían comentado sobre el mapa de GTA 6.
Tenemos que destacar que este será el escenario de la nueva historia protagonizada por Jason Duval y Lucía Caminos. Ambos son compañeros de delito y podemos decidir qué tan íntima será la relación entre ellos. Además de esto, ya sabíamos de estos dos personajes y de los paisajes gracias a la página web y el segundo tráiler de GTA VI.
Más interiores en un mapa más grande
Por otro lado, Aaron Garbut (corresponsable del estudio y jefe de desarrollo) nos cuenta que han aumentado en un orden de magnitud el número de interiores respecto a otras entregas de Grand Theft Auto.
Garbut asegura que todos los callejones están tan bien trabajados y son tan interesantes como el resto. Nos dice que muchas personas han pensado en cada sitio del mapa.
Garbut afirma que sigue encontrando lugares en los que nunca había estado, aunque lleva años jugando al título en desarrollo (en versiones cada vez más densas).
En una de las sesiones de juego de la mañana de aquel encuentro, ha entrado en una casa que no conocía. En una de las habitaciones había unas fotos familiares de un perro. Cuando ha entrado en la otra habitación, ha podido ver cómo este había dejado todo hecho un desastre mientras estaba solo. “Estaba todo destrozado. En una esquina había cacas, que estaban algo esparcidas por el suelo”, ha relatado.
También ha influido en el desarrollo de GTA 6 Red Dead Redemption 2. El juego de Jason y Lucía llegará el 19 de noviembre de 2026 en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S (web oficial de Rockstar).

articles.title: GTA 6 : adieu les 60 images par seconde, la PS5 Pro garde un effet pour elle seule, et même la vieille Xbox One est de la fête
articles.text:
GTA 6 sur PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series et Xbox One : tout le monde ne sera pas logé à la même enseigne, voici les différences
Pendant des mois, Rockstar a laissé les joueurs spéculer. À neuf jours de la sortie, le studio abat enfin ses cartes, console par console. La fluidité sera la même pour tout le monde, la PS5 Pro décroche un privilège graphique que personne d'autre n'aura, et les possesseurs d'une vieille Xbox One, que l'on croyait exclus, sont finalement de la partie. Avec quelques conditions.
Rockstar Games a profité de l'ouverture du préchargement, le 10 novembre, pour détailler les performances de Grand Theft Auto VI. Le studio explique que son jeu a été "entièrement développé à partir de zéro pour offrir la meilleure expérience possible sur la génération actuelle de consoles, avec une cible de 30 images par seconde". Aucun mode à 60 images par seconde n'est annoncé, quelle que soit la machine.
Le téléchargement réclame jusqu'à 212 Go, y compris pour la version physique de GTA 6 sans disque, qui ne contient qu'un code. Mieux vaut anticiper les préparatifs à prévoir avant le lancement de GTA 6.
Sony et Microsoft ont aussitôt relayé l'annonce, accompagnée d'une nouvelle vidéo. Chacun revendique au passage un record de précommandes sur sa boutique.
GTA 6 sur PS5 et PS5 Pro : même cadence, ombres exclusives
La console haut de gamme de Sony obtient deux atouts. Rockstar écrit noir sur blanc que "la PlayStation 5 Pro offre des visuels à couper le souffle, avec une netteté améliorée grâce à la PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) et des ombres en ray tracing disponibles uniquement sur PlayStation 5 Pro".
Le PSSR affine l'image par intelligence artificielle, une technologie que nous avions passée au crible dans notre test de la PS5 Pro. Le ray tracing simule le trajet réel de la lumière : les ombres gagnent en précision et se diffusent avec naturel. Le studio ne dit rien, en revanche, de la définition d'affichage ni des autres effets lumineux.
	
Des ombres en ray tracing disponibles uniquement sur PlayStation 5 Pro
La pilule passera mal chez une partie des acheteurs. Facturée 899,99 € en France depuis avril, la PS5 Pro faisait espérer une fluidité doublée.
Son processeur, à peine plus véloce que celui de la PS5, rendait ce rêve fragile : selon les analyses de Digital Foundry, foule, circulation et physique sollicitent d'abord le CPU dans un monde ouvert de cette ampleur. Les différences de performances entre PS5 et PS5 Pro se joueront donc sur la beauté de l'image.
Les fichiers du préchargement laissaient déjà entrevoir ce traitement de faveur. Des dataminers y avaient repéré deux jeux de données de ray tracing, l'un au format de la PS5, l'autre à celui de la Pro.
Ils avaient aussi trouvé un bloc lié à l'histoire, vide sur la première et lourd de 223,5 Mo sur la seconde : les premiers indices d'un traitement graphique réservé à la PS5 Pro.
writing a thread about the chunks of the download, but before that the most interesting bit is that PS5 Pro *may* have some exclusive assets.
bvh4 and bvh8 refer to some data that differs for raytracing on Base/Pro, and the Story set for Base is empty (64KB) but Pro's is 223.5MB pic.twitter.com/KB6FQfdT43
— Lucas7yoshi_RS - nerd (of Rockstar's Games) (@Lucas7yoshi_RS) November 9, 2026
Toutes les PS5 profitent par ailleurs des vibrations haptiques de la manette DualSense, de l'audio 3D Tempest et de chargements raccourcis. Que vous jouiez sur le modèle d'origine ou sur sa version affinée, détaillés dans notre test de la PS5 avec lecteur de disque et notre test de la PS5 Slim avec lecteur de disque, l'expérience sera la même, puisque les deux partagent la même puissance.
De quoi permettre à Rockstar de répéter que son jeu "se joue mieux sur PlayStation 5". Sony savoure : sur son blog officiel, le constructeur annonce que GTA VI est devenu le jeu le plus précommandé de l'histoire du PlayStation Store.
La bande-annonce de lancement, dévoilée le 15 octobre, a d'ailleurs été entièrement capturée sur PS5.
GTA 6 sur Xbox : la Xbox One invitée grâce au cloud
Côté Microsoft, qui revendique de son côté le titre le plus précommandé de l'histoire du Microsoft Store, la Xbox Series X fait tourner le jeu en natif dans les meilleures conditions. Notre test complet de la Xbox Series X détaille la puissance de cette machine.
La Xbox Series S offre l'accès natif le moins cher, et notre test de la Xbox Series S en pèse les forces et les limites.
La surprise vient de la Xbox One. Incapable de faire tourner GTA 6, elle pourra le diffuser en streaming via Xbox Cloud Gaming, dès le 19 novembre à 7 h, heure française.
L'image calculée à distance reprend les réglages graphiques de la Xbox Series S, et Rockstar prévient que la qualité de la connexion pourra peser sur les performances.
Le streaming reste payant. Il faut d'abord acheter le jeu, puis disposer d'heures de cloud. Depuis novembre, le Game Pass en inclut un quota mensuel : 15 heures avec l'offre Ultimate, 10 avec Premium et 5 avec Essential.
Microsoft vend aussi, depuis le 11 novembre et dans certains pays, des forfaits d'heures sans abonnement. Pour un jeu de cette ampleur, le compteur risque de tourner vite.
Le jeu fonctionnera enfin en lecture à distance sur PlayStation comme sur Xbox, depuis sa propre console. Ceux qui hésitent encore sur leur machine trouveront tous les verdicts dans notre comparatif des consoles de jeu.
Près de trois ans après le tout premier trailer, dévoilé en décembre 2023, le verdict tombera le jeudi 19 novembre.

articles.title: How LinkedIn, Netflix & DoorDash Run Agents, Evals & Inference in Production: QCon AI New York 2026
articles.text:
QCon AI New York 2026 has published its full schedule for December 15–16. Engineers from LinkedIn, Netflix, DoorDash, Figma, and other organizations will examine the architecture and operational decisions behind production AI systems, including agent authorization, evaluation pipelines, model serving, and AI-assisted software delivery. With the conference a few weeks away, there is still time to join other practitioners before the full ticket price takes effect on December 9.
The program addresses questions facing teams moving beyond initial AI deployments: where to enforce agent permissions, how to connect offline evaluations to production behavior, and how to support growing inference workloads. It also examines how coding agents affect code review, engineering practices, and organizational adoption.
The following presentations explore these challenges through systems the speakers build and operate.
Keynotes
Nancy Wang, CTO at 1Password, who founded and scaled AWS Data Protection and previously worked at Rubrik and Google, opens day one with When Software Becomes a User: Identity and Authorization for Agents in Production. She argues that identity systems assume a human behind every credential, with a stable role, a bounded session, and someone accountable afterward. Agents have none of these.
Tara Sainath, Distinguished Research Scientist at Google DeepMind, lead of the Gemini Audio area and modeling lead for Project Astra, opens day two with Audio Processing with Large Language Models. She covers how LLMs have changed audio processing, and the research and product impact of audio LLMs at Google.
Agents in production
Pratik Agarwal, Distributed Systems Engineer on Figma's sandbox and caching platforms, explains how Figma provisions and secures production agents. Figma found that the trust boundary for agents extends beyond the sandbox. Warm pools cut provisioning latency by 90%, and availability rose from 99% to 99.95%.
Ronak Nathani, Principal Staff Software Engineer in Compute Infrastructure at LinkedIn and host of the Software Misadventures podcast, presents LinkedIn's Kubernetes ops agent, which works across 500,000+ nodes and 5M+ pods. Its guardrails sit on the server, including rate limits, delete protection, and peer approval for production changes.
Evals that decide whether a change ships
Fabio Flores, Software Engineer at DoorDash who leads foundation development for its agentic ordering system, explains the eval loop behind it. Every change is checked before launch by an LLM judge calibrated against human reviewers. The same rubrics score simulated and real sessions, so offline gains carry into production.
Emrick Donadei, Software Engineer on the Google DeepMind infrastructure team who works on evaluation and safety for agentic harnesses, covers agent evals the whole organization can write and keep running. The talk starts from a common problem: an eval that passes once, then fails on the next run.
Inference cost and model serving
Fan Yang, Staff Software Engineer building Netflix's AI serving platform, and Rajat Shah, Staff Software Engineer who leads the technical architecture for ML model serving, explain how Netflix serves ML and GenAI from one platform. It handles about 1 million inference requests per second across 300+ models, after five years of consolidation. They cover what multi-tenancy costs to operate.
Salina Wu, Software Engineer building Pinterest's generative AI serving platform, and Cristian Lopez, Software Engineer on GenAI Serving at Pinterest, present Pinterest's vision-language model serving stack on NVIDIA Dynamo. It is built for multimodal workloads with heavy prefill computation and large KV cache pressure.
AI-assisted software engineering
Min Chen, Principal Staff Engineer at LinkedIn with more than 25 years of software development experience, presents LinkedIn's AI code review system. It reviews tens of thousands of pull requests a week across about 10,000 repositories. More than 60% of sampled suggestions are accepted, and a validation pipeline filters findings before developers see them.
Joey Wang, engineering lead at Harvey who created Spectre, Harvey's internal collaborative cloud agent platform, explains how Harvey shipped its agents internally first on Spectre. Spectre passed 7,000 merged pull requests across every repository before the agents reached lawyers.
Engineering leadership and adoption
Liz Fong-Jones, Technical Fellow at Honeycomb and site reliability engineer with more than two decades of experience, and Rebecca Murphey, Principal for AI Ops at Honeycomb and author of Build: Elements of an Effective Software Organization, reflect on Honeycomb's 2x initiative. Peak weekday PR merges to Honeycomb's main monorepo rose from about 30 to about 74 between early 2025 and April 2026, and have held steady since.
Brian Yang, Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI who builds AI-native advertising and monetization systems, covers making AI adoption work across an engineering team. He looks at what happens after every engineer has coding agents, when one person finds a way of working that teammates struggle to reproduce.
Also on the program
Other sessions come from engineers at Anthropic, Microsoft, BlackRock, Databricks, Datadog, Tessl, LangChain, Baseten, and Google Cloud’s DORA team. Topics include agentic standards, sandbox density, SRE agents, AgentOps for financial services, inference with vLLM, voice agents, software factories, and enterprise AI adoption. Explore the full schedule.
Group registration for teams of three or more closes on November 27, 2026, with savings of $50 to $125 per ticket. Individual tickets are $1,790 until December 8, the last price before the full rate applies. Tickets can be transferred to a colleague free of charge until December 11, 2026.
Engineers who need approval can use the Convince Your Manager page, which provides an email template built around the sessions relevant to their work.

articles.title: Introducing usage-based pricing for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Introducing usage-based pricing for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming
Usage-based metering for bidirectional streaming solves a software billing problem for real-time speech AI. Customers deploying streaming models on Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming pay for the endpoint infrastructure that hosts the model. Separately, model providers listing on AWS Marketplace need a way to charge for what customers consume during a live stream. Today, we’re announcing usage-based metering for Amazon SageMaker bidirectional (bidi) streaming inference, so model providers can report actual usage for the AWS Marketplace software charge. Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint infrastructure charges still apply.
Deepgram, the real-time speech AI company, is the launch partner for this capability, bringing usage-based Speech-to-Text (STT) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) billing to AWS Marketplace. This post builds on a series of innovations between Deepgram and AWS. First, we introduced bidirectional streaming for real-time inference on Amazon SageMaker AI, which supports long-lived bidirectional streams between clients and model servers. Then, Deepgram enhanced Amazon SageMaker AI support with AWS Identity and Access Management (AWS IAM) temporary delegation, simplifying secure authentication for enterprise deployments, and expanded observability with enhanced metrics. Now, with usage-based metering, we further strengthen the foundation for production real-time AI, aligning billing with how customers consume streaming and real-time AI workloads.
Why streaming broke the existing billing model
With AWS Marketplace software metering for SageMaker AI real-time request-response inference, model providers can report a unit count in an HTTP response header. AWS Marketplace uses that quantity for the software charge. This works for request-response APIs where the billable quantity is known when the response is sent.
Bidirectional streaming is different. A client streams audio and receives transcriptions through the SageMaker AI API using an HTTP/2 event stream. SageMaker AI connects to the model server over WebSockets. A session can last 30 seconds or 30 minutes. Usage accumulates as the session runs, and the final total isn’t known until it ends. A response header alone can’t report periodic usage during that live session.
Hourly software pricing can charge customers while a model is available, including quiet periods. With usage-based metering, providers can align the AWS Marketplace software charge with reported usage. SageMaker AI endpoint infrastructure charges remain separate and continue to apply while the endpoint is provisioned.
How companion metadata streaming works
The solution introduces a second WebSocket connection alongside the existing inference stream. When a bidirectional streaming session starts, SageMaker AI establishes two connections to the model server:
- Data connection: carries inference request and response data, the existing bidirectional stream.
- Metadata connection: a companion WebSocket dedicated to metering data.
Model servers opt in by returning one header on the WebSocket upgrade response:
X-Amzn-SageMaker-Metadata-Stream-Supported: true
SageMaker AI then opens a companion WebSocket to the model server at /invocations-bidirectional-stream-metadata. Both connections carry the same X-Amzn-SageMaker-Request-Id header, which the model server uses to correlate metering records with the active inference session.
The model server sends metering data as JSON text frames on the metadata connection. Send records at a frequency that matches the billing model: incrementally as usage accrues (recommended), either as each unit is consumed or as periodic batches of units consumed since the previous record. Send any final record as soon as the session ends. Each frame contains exactly one metering record, rather than an array of records. The metadata stream has a rate quota of one message per second per connection, with a maximum message size of 512 bytes.
We recommend sending metering records incrementally as usage accrues. This reduces the amount of usage left unreported if a session ends unexpectedly. Transport delivery alone does not establish that usage has been billed. Validate reported units against AWS Marketplace reports and buyer charges.
Metering messages use the inference.count dimension, and ConsumedUnits supplies the quantity for that dimension. If the product charges per second of audio, a record reporting 12 minutes of metered audio carries 720 seconds as ConsumedUnits: 720. The dimension name doesn’t mean one unit per request. The provider defines which audio counts as metered usage, and the AWS Marketplace offer maps the unit to its price. The listing shows one price per unit, labeled per request, with up to three decimal places. The ClientToken field supports idempotency. If a duplicate token arrives on the same connection, SageMaker AI drops the duplicate message silently.
The metadata connection runs over TCP, which provides ordered, reliable delivery at the transport layer. If it fails to establish or drops mid-session, inference continues by default because X-Amzn-SageMaker-Metadata-Stream-Required defaults to false. Set this header to true when the provider must stop inference if the metadata stream becomes unavailable. This choice trades inference availability for metering continuity. It doesn’t guarantee that malformed or dropped records are billed.
What this means for customers
If you deploy real-time AI models for transcription, contact centers, voice agents, or captioning, the new metering model changes how the AWS Marketplace software charge is calculated. SageMaker AI endpoint infrastructure charges still apply.
Transparent, per-unit billing through AWS Marketplace means usage flows directly into your AWS bill. You get consolidated AWS billing, negotiated rates through private offers, and no separate billing relationship with the model provider to manage.
Pay for audio processed according to the product’s unit definition. If the product charges per second of audio, 12 minutes of metered audio equals 720 billable seconds and ConsumedUnits: 720. An open connection lasting 12 minutes doesn’t, by itself, define the billable audio quantity. The provider’s counting rules determine the metered usage, whereas endpoint infrastructure charges remain separate.
Model providers can offer negotiated per-unit rates or fixed-price contracts through AWS Marketplace private offers.
We recommend discussing directly with your AWS account representative or partner representative.
What this means for model providers
If you’re a model provider listing on AWS Marketplace, you can configure your model server to report usage during streaming inference sessions through companion metadata streaming.
The SageMaker Marketplace Onboarding Agent Skill accelerates onboarding with an opt-in inference metering path. Its starter templates advertise metadata-stream support and build validated, incremental ConsumedUnits frames for the companion WebSocket. Review and production-harden the code before submission.
Align billing with your pricing model by defining what one unit represents and reporting units as the session progresses. AWS Marketplace charges one per-unit price for real-time inference.
The following three-step walkthrough describes how to integrate your model server to report metering data during bidirectional streaming inference sessions.
Step 1: Opt in using data WebSocket response headers
When SageMaker AI opens the data WebSocket connection to your model server, include these headers in your WebSocket upgrade (101) response:
|  | Header | Required | Values | Description | 
| 1 | X-Amzn-SageMaker-Metadata-Stream-Supported | Yes (to opt in) | TRUE | Signals that your model server supports the companion metadata stream. If absent or not true, no metadata connection is attempted. Without the metadata stream, the session is not metered for the model provider’s software charge. | 
| 2 | X-Amzn-SageMaker-Metadata-Stream-Required | No | true / false | This header only takes effect when X-Amzn-SageMaker-Metadata-Stream-Supported is true. If true, inference stops when the metadata connection fails. If false or absent, inference continues in data-only mode. Default: false. Choose true when metering continuity takes priority over inference availability. This setting doesn’t guarantee billing for malformed or dropped records. | 
| 3 | X-Amzn-SageMaker-Metadata-Invocation-Path | No | Custom path string | Overrides the default metadata WebSocket path. Default: /invocations-bidirectional-stream-metadata. | 
Step 2: Accept the metadata WebSocket connection
After your model server returns X-Amzn-SageMaker-Metadata-Stream-Supported: true, SageMaker AI opens a second WebSocket connection to your model server at the default path /invocations-bidirectional-stream-metadata (or the custom path you specified by using X-Amzn-SageMaker-Metadata-Invocation-Path).
SageMaker AI includes the header X-Amzn-SageMaker-Request-Id on both the data and metadata WebSocket handshakes. Your model server must do the following:
- Accept the WebSocket upgrade on the metadata path.
- Use X-Amzn-SageMaker-Request-Id to correlate the metadata connection with the corresponding data connection for the same inference session.
Step 3: Send metering messages
Send metering data as a JSON object in a WebSocket text frame on the metadata connection. Each frame must contain exactly one metering record. In this example, the product charges per second of audio, and the record reports 12 minutes of metered audio as 720 units:
Message fields:
|  | Field | Required | Type | Constraints | Description | 
| 1 | Metering | Yes | Object | — | Container for the metering record. | 
| 2 | Metering.Dimension | Yes | String | Must be inference.count | The billing dimension. Must be inference.count. | 
| 3 | Metering.ConsumedUnits | Yes | Number | 0 or greater | The units consumed since your previous record. Each record is billed separately. A value of 0 is accepted but not billed. | 
| 4 | Metering.ClientToken | No | String | Max 64 characters | A unique token (for example, a UUID) for idempotency. If the same ClientToken is sent multiple times on the same connection, only the first occurrence is recorded. | 
Send metering records incrementally as usage accrues to reduce unreported usage if a session ends unexpectedly. Reconcile the reported quantities with AWS Marketplace reports and buyer charges to verify billing, including interrupted-session tests.
Constraints and limits
|  | Limit | Value | Notes | 
| 1 | Maximum message size | 512 bytes | Total size of the JSON text frame | 
| 2 | Maximum send rate | 1 message per second per connection | Exceeding this rate might result in dropped messages | 
| 3 | Maximum Dimension length | 128 characters | — | 
| 4 | Maximum ClientToken length | 64 characters | — | 
| 5 | Messages per frame | Exactly 1 | Don’t batch multiple metering records in a single frame | 
| 6 | Frame type | Text frames only | Binary frames are not supported for metering | 
Error handling and failure modes
The Required header controls what happens when the metadata connection becomes unavailable. Set it to true to stop inference, or use the default false to let inference continue in data-only mode. This is a choice between metering continuity and inference availability. Malformed messages can still be dropped with either setting.
|  | Scenario | Required = true | Required = false (default) | 
| 1 | Metadata WebSocket fails to connect | Data stream is terminated | Data stream continues normally (data-only mode) | 
| 2 | Metadata WebSocket drops mid-session | Data stream is terminated | Data stream continues normally. Metering stops | 
| 3 | Malformed metering message | Message is dropped. Metadata connection stays open | Message is dropped. Metadata connection stays open | 
| 4 | Data connection breaks mid-stream | Metadata stream is closed | Metadata stream is closed | 
List your model on AWS Marketplace
- Register your AWS account as an AWS Marketplace seller. For paid products, complete the tax and banking information.
- Create a SageMaker AI model package from your container in a supported publishing Region, and an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role that AWS Marketplace can assume to read it.
- In AWS Partner Central, choose Build, Machine learning, then Create machine learning product, and add the model package as the first version.
- Choose per-inference pricing. You set one per-unit price for real-time inference across all instance types, shown per request with up to three decimal places. You also set an hourly price for each batch transform instance type. Choose the pricing model when you create the listing because you can’t switch a released listing between hourly and per-inference pricing.
- After validation, request Public visibility. For enterprise buyers, extend private offers with a negotiated per-unit rate or a fixed-price contract.
Validate billing before release
Validate the integration with a Limited listing and an allowlisted test buyer. Use an appropriate offer, including a private offer where needed, so the test exercises the intended unit and price mapping.
- Run a known-quantity test. For a product priced per second of audio, send 12 minutes of metered audio and check that the reported records total 720 units.
- Reconcile the model-server records with the seller’s usage reports and the buyer’s charges. Allow time for reports to populate and verify the usage type <region code>-SMMP:inference.count.m.i.c (for example, USE1-SMMP:inference.count.m.i.c in us-east-1). Confirm the offer’s unit and price mapping rather than assuming a fixed reporting delay.
- Test normal completion, interrupted sessions, metadata-stream loss, and malformed messages. Compare reported and billed quantities for each case with the SageMaker AI and AWS Marketplace teams before release.
- Delete test endpoints when testing is complete to avoid ongoing infrastructure charges.
Getting started with Deepgram on AWS Marketplace
To deploy Deepgram with usage-based metering on SageMaker AI, follow these steps.
- Subscribe to the Deepgram Voice AI streaming model you need on AWS Marketplace, such as Deepgram Nova-3 Monolingual Speech-to-Text (STT) Streaming.
- Deploy a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint using the Deepgram model package from your AWS Marketplace subscription.
- Connect to the endpoint using the SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming API and stream audio through its HTTP/2 event stream.
Deepgram’s model server calculates metering automatically, and Amazon SageMaker AI and AWS Marketplace process it. You don’t need to configure anything on the client side.
Clean up
When you finish testing, delete the SageMaker AI real-time endpoint and model resource to stop infrastructure charges. If you no longer need the product, remove the AWS Marketplace subscription.
Conclusion
With usage-based metering for bidirectional streaming, model providers can align AWS Marketplace software pricing with reported usage during a live session. Customers pay the software charge for the metered units defined by the product and offer. Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint infrastructure charges remain separate and still apply. Learn more about Amazon SageMaker AI.
To get started:
- For customers, subscribe to a Deepgram Voice AI streaming model on AWS Marketplace, such as Deepgram Nova-3 Monolingual Speech-to-Text (STT) Streaming
- For model providers, follow the integration walkthrough in this post to add usage-based metering to your own model server.
Acknowledgements
Special thanks to Kareem Syed-Mohammed (Principal Product Manager), Susmitha Marupaka (Product Marketing Manager), Zhengfei Ji (Software Development Engineer for Amazon SageMaker AI), and EJ Ferrell for reviewing this post and leading the development of this capability.

articles.title: AMD launches Zen 6 Epyc 9006 series with up to 256 cores, 512 threads, and TSMC N2
articles.text:
Highly anticipated: AMD has fully pulled back the curtain on its first Zen 6 CPU lineup. Debuting with Epyc server chips, the new architecture offers up to 256 cores and 512 threads at the top end, and AMD has promised substantial upgrades in AI, GPU hosting, and per-watt performance.
AMD's first Zen 6 Epyc processors, labeled the 9006 series and codenamed Venice, are now shipping to server clients, with SP7 systems arriving first and SP8 following in the first half of 2027. The company recently published the full technical specs for every SP7 and SP8 CPU in the lineup, mainly promoting their usefulness for AI workloads.
As expected, AMD's new flagship Epyc 9996 raises the maximum core count to 256, with 512 threads, clocked at up to 4.1GHz. With 1GB of L3 cache, it sits at a 2.55GHz base clock and defaults to 600W, though it can be configured down to 400W.
AMD's rack-density comparisons also reference a 400W, 256-core 9956, but that chip isn't on the published list. According to AMD's internal benchmarks, the 9996 at least doubles the Intel Xeon 6980P's performance in some tasks and more than triples it in others.
Early independent testing backs up the scale of the gains: Tom's Hardware measured a dual 9996 server at up to 93% faster than a dual Epyc 9965 in SPEC CPU 2026's intrate test. AMD lists the top-end chip at $14,904, but the lineup also scales all the way down to the eight-core, 16-thread Epyc 9016, at just $700.
Shifting to TSMC's N2 process node grants Epyc Venice up to a 2.6x improvement in performance per watt. AMD also claims 1.87x as many AI agents per CPU dollar compared to recent Intel Xeon processors.
With a 5.3GHz maximum boost clock on its high-frequency host-node parts, Venice also supposedly delivers up to 1.8x the LLM inference output of the previous Epyc generation. PCIe 6.0 doubles CPU-to-GPU I/O bandwidth, with up to 128 lanes in dual-socket SP7 systems and on SP8.

Since AMD recently declared itself a data center-first company, it remains unclear exactly when Zen 6's architectural advantages will filter down to consumer-grade products. articles.title: Citrix, Ivanti Patch Critical and High-Severity Vulnerabilities
articles.text:
Citrix and Ivanti on Tuesday announced patches for 19 vulnerabilities in their products, including multiple critical- and high-severity flaws.
Ivanti fixed 13 vulnerabilities across five products, including two critical-severity defects in Cloud Services Application (CSA) and Endpoint Manager (EPM).
Tracked as CVE-2026-121683 (CVSS score of 9.4), the CSA flaw is described as a missing authentication issue that could allow remote, unauthenticated attackers to “add and delete arbitrary trusted EPM Core certificate entries”.
CSA version 5.0.8.1 patches the bug. Deployments running with a Dual NIC configuration cannot be exploited externally, Ivanti notes.
The critical EPM issue, tracked as CVE-2026-121653 (CVSS score of 9.8), is an SQL injection bug that could lead to remote code execution (RCE) without authentication.
It was resolved in EPM version 2024 SU8, which also addresses a medium-severity cleartext transmission of sensitive information exploitable via MitM attacks.
Ivanti released patches for four vulnerabilities in Sentry, including a high-severity remote code execution (RCE) flaw. Tracked as CVE-2026-105425, the bug was also fixed in Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM), along with five medium-severity issues.
On Tuesday, the company also addressed a medium-severity defect in User Workspace Manager (UWM). Ivanti says it has no evidence of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild.
Citrix rolled out fixes for six security defects in XenServer, including CVE-2026-102705, a high-severity bug that could allow attackers to infer the Pool Secret and compromise the host.
The remaining five issues could lead to privilege escalation or could allow administrators with any role to terminate the running tasks of other roles.
Additionally, Citrix released XenServer updates that mitigate several AMD CPU vulnerabilities that could allow guest VMs to compromise the host or infer the active memory content of another VM.
