articles.title: Por que os games viraram a nova mina de ouro do cinema e do streaming
articles.text:
Durante décadas, a relação entre videogames e cinema foi marcada por adaptações que nem sempre agradavam aos fãs. Filmes eram transformados em jogos para aproveitar campanhas de lançamento, enquanto personagens dos games chegavam às telonas em produções que frequentemente tinham dificuldade em reproduzir o que os tornava especiais.
Esse cenário mudou. Super Mario Bros. O Filme, The Last of Us, Arcane, Fallout e Um Filme Minecraft demonstram que os videogames se tornaram uma das principais fontes de propriedade intelectual (IPs) para o cinema e o streaming. Mais do que adaptações, estamos falando de universos capazes de conquistar públicos em diferentes formatos.
O sucesso comercial ajuda a explicar esse interesse. Super Mario Bros. O Filme ultrapassou US$ 1,3 bilhão em bilheteria mundial, enquanto Um Filme Minecraft arrecadou aproximadamente US$ 960 milhões. São números que colocam essas produções entre os grandes sucessos recentes de Hollywood.
Mas há uma questão mais interessante por trás desses resultados: por que algumas propriedades intelectuais conseguem atravessar diferentes mídias, enquanto outras fracassam?
O jogo mudou
Uma das principais razões para essa transformação é de ordem geracional. Quem cresceu jogando videogame hoje também consome cinema e streaming, trabalha na indústria audiovisual e, em muitos casos, participa das decisões sobre quais projetos recebem investimentos.
Os videogames deixaram de ser vistos como um entretenimento exclusivamente infantil e passaram a ocupar um espaço central na cultura popular.
Para os estúdios de cinema e as plataformas de streaming, isso representa uma oportunidade comercial. Uma franquia de games bem-sucedida já possui personagens conhecidos, universos estabelecidos e, principalmente, uma comunidade de fãs.
Isso não significa sucesso garantido, mas reduz parte da incerteza envolvida na apresentação de uma história completamente desconhecida ao público.
Outro fator importante é a evolução das tecnologias de produção. Ferramentas digitais, animação e efeitos visuais tornaram mais viável a representação de mundos que antes seriam extremamente caros ou difíceis de reproduzir.
Entretanto, há uma diferença fundamental entre adaptar um jogo e simplesmente usar sua marca para vender ingressos.
Uma relação de mão dupla
Quando uma propriedade intelectual de games chega ao audiovisual, ela leva consigo uma comunidade, uma identidade visual e um universo que o público já conhece.
Por outro lado, o cinema e o streaming oferecem algo extremamente valioso para os jogos: a possibilidade de alcançar pessoas que nunca seguraram um controle.
Alguém pode conhecer The Last of Us pela série da HBO antes de descobrir os jogos da Naughty Dog. Da mesma forma, uma criança pode assistir ao filme do Mario sem nunca ter jogado nenhum título da Nintendo.
Esse movimento cria um ciclo de valorização da propriedade intelectual. O jogo fortalece a produção audiovisual, enquanto o audiovisual amplia o reconhecimento da marca e pode despertar interesse pelos jogos.
É o conceito de transmídia, no qual uma propriedade intelectual se desenvolve em diferentes mídias, aproveitando as características de cada uma delas.
Mas há um desafio que costuma passar despercebido; cada mídia tem sua própria linguagem.
A experiência dos dois lados
Ao longo da minha carreira na indústria de games, tive a oportunidade de trabalhar nos dois sentidos dessa relação.
Um dos projetos foi Swan Princess Hidden Tales, baseado na franquia cinematográfica A Princesa Encantada. Nesse caso, o desafio era transformar uma propriedade intelectual originalmente criada para o cinema em uma experiência interativa.
Não bastava reproduzir personagens e cenários. Era necessário compreender o público da franquia, respeitar sua identidade e encontrar mecânicas que fizessem sentido naquele universo.
Afinal, uma boa história cinematográfica não se transforma automaticamente em um bom jogo. O jogador precisa ter algo interessante para fazer.
Anos depois, vivi o caminho inverso com Starlit Toons, uma série de animação baseada no universo dos jogos Starlit.
Nos games, os personagens já possuíam identidade visual, personalidade e funções ligadas às mecânicas de jogo. Mas uma série de animação exige algo diferente: narrativa, conflitos, relações entre personagens e desenvolvimento de histórias.
Um personagem pode funcionar perfeitamente em um jogo simplesmente por ter uma habilidade divertida. Na televisão, isso não é suficiente. Ele precisa sustentar uma história e despertar o interesse de quem assiste.
Essas duas experiências reforçaram uma percepção importante: adaptar uma propriedade intelectual não significa reproduzir o produto original, mas preservar sua essência enquanto se constrói uma experiência adequada à nova mídia.
O que torna uma IP valiosa?
Na indústria, existe um conceito interessante chamado deck appeal, relacionado à capacidade de uma propriedade intelectual despertar interesse quando apresentada a possíveis parceiros, investidores ou produtores.
Embora não exista uma fórmula universal, alguns elementos ajudam a identificar o potencial de uma marca para funcionar em diferentes formatos.
O primeiro é possuir personagens ou símbolos reconhecíveis. Mario pode ser identificado por sua silhueta. Pikachu é reconhecido mesmo por pessoas que nunca jogaram Pokémon.
O segundo é apresentar um mundo com regras próprias. O universo de Minecraft, por exemplo, possui uma lógica visual e funcional facilmente identificável.
O terceiro é ter uma ação central, aquilo que podemos chamar de verbo da propriedade intelectual. Em Mario, saltamos. Em Pokémon, capturamos e treinamos criaturas. Em Minecraft, construímos e exploramos.
O quarto elemento é a identidade emocional. Uma propriedade intelectual precisa transmitir algo reconhecível, seja humor, aventura, competição, nostalgia ou suspense.
Por último, existe a capacidade de expansão. Aquele universo permite novas histórias, personagens, produtos ou experiências sem perder sua identidade?
Esses elementos não garantem uma adaptação bem-sucedida, mas ajudam a compreender por que algumas marcas conseguem sobreviver muito além do produto que lhes deu origem.
Até cubos podem virar protagonistas
Um dos exemplos mais interessantes dessa discussão é Minecraft.
Seu universo é composto essencialmente por blocos. Não há uma narrativa linear obrigatória, e o protagonista não possui uma personalidade tão definida quanto a de personagens tradicionais do cinema.
Ainda assim, Minecraft se tornou uma das marcas mais reconhecidas da indústria do entretenimento.
O segredo está na combinação de uma identidade visual inconfundível, um mundo com regras próprias e uma ação central extremamente poderosa: construir.
LEGO segue uma lógica semelhante. O produto original é um brinquedo de montar, mas sua capacidade de representar praticamente qualquer universo permitiu a criação de jogos, filmes e séries.
Transformers e Cars demonstram outro caminho: objetos que ganham personalidade, emoções e conflitos, tornando-se personagens capazes de sustentar narrativas.
Já Tetris representa um caso particular. O jogo é praticamente uma mecânica pura, sem personagens nem um universo narrativo tradicional. O filme lançado pela Apple TV em 2023 encontrou seu caminho ao contar a história dos bastidores da comercialização do jogo, e não ao tentar transformar blocos que caem em personagens de aventura.
Isso demonstra que uma propriedade intelectual não precisa necessariamente nascer com uma grande história para chegar ao audiovisual. Mas para chegar ao audiovisual, necessariamente precisamos de um personagem para contar uma história.
Nem toda adaptação funciona
Apesar do entusiasmo da indústria, a adaptação de propriedade intelectual continua sendo um negócio arriscado.
Um dos erros mais comuns é acreditar que o reconhecimento da marca será suficiente para garantir o sucesso. Utilizar personagens famosos sem compreender o que os tornou populares pode resultar em produções que não agradam nem aos fãs originais nem ao novo público.
Outro problema é ignorar a comunidade. Os fãs têm expectativas em relação a personagens, mundos e comportamentos. Isso não significa que uma adaptação precise reproduzir fielmente cada detalhe, mas as mudanças precisam fazer sentido dentro da proposta.
Também existem desafios comerciais. Direitos de licenciamento, exclusividade, plataformas e cronogramas precisam estar bem estruturados. Uma estratégia mal planejada pode impedir que uma propriedade intelectual aproveite oportunidades importantes de expansão.
Para os desenvolvedores independentes, especialmente no Brasil, essa discussão merece atenção.
Nem todo estúdio precisa transformar seu jogo em uma série de televisão. Entretanto, pensar na identidade, nos personagens e no universo de uma propriedade intelectual desde o início pode ampliar suas possibilidades comerciais no futuro.
Um jogo pode ser o primeiro produto de uma marca muito maior.
O futuro não está apenas nos jogos
Durante muito tempo, desenvolvedores criavam jogos pensando principalmente em suas mecânicas, plataformas e modelos de negócio.
Esses elementos continuam fundamentais. Mas a crescente aproximação entre games, cinema e streaming adiciona uma nova perspectiva, o valor de um jogo pode ultrapassar o próprio jogo.
Isso não significa que todo projeto precise nascer como uma franquia transmídia. Muitos dos melhores videogames funcionam justamente porque exploram características que nenhuma outra mídia consegue reproduzir.
O importante é compreender que uma propriedade intelectual forte pode abrir portas em diferentes mercados, desde que haja uma estratégia coerente de expansão.
Talvez a pergunta mais importante para quem desenvolve um jogo hoje não seja apenas se ele tem potencial para vender milhares ou milhões de cópias, mas sim se retirarmos a jogabilidade, ainda existe um universo, um personagem ou uma ideia que as pessoas gostariam de acompanhar?
A resposta pode determinar se estamos criando apenas um jogo ou construindo a próxima grande propriedade intelectual do entretenimento.

articles.title: Ocarina of Time is even better if you use a smartphone app
articles.text:
I never liked hunting for Golden Skulltulas in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. The game has 100 of them tucked all over Hyrule, and even over my many hours with the N64 classic growing up, I can’t remember ever actually finding all of them, or even wanting to. Jumping into the Ocarina of Time remake, I expected to ignore the Golden Skulltulas once again. But while poking around Nintendo’s Zelda Notes companion app, I discovered that its maps are a huge help to tracking down all of the elusive golden spiders — and pretty much every other collectible in the game — and now I find myself constantly opening up the app to make sure I haven’t missed a secret.
Ocarina of Time is even better if you use a smartphone app
Finding Ocarina of Time’s hidden collectibles is a lot easier with the help of Zelda Notes.
Inside Zelda Notes, which is available in the free Nintendo Switch app (you don’t need a Switch Online subscription to use it), you can peruse a big map of Hyrule and tap on individual areas for a closer look. The app offers just enough direction to nudge me toward an elusive pickup; when zoomed in, the app drops icons on the map showing you the locations of different collectibles, and if you tap on an icon, the app will show a popup noting any items or special requirements you need to fulfill to be able to obtain it. There are also a bunch of filters you can apply, like swapping between the maps for child and adult Link and toggling categories of icons on and off.
For Skulltula hunting, the map has already saved my sanity many times. While exploring, I’ll often come across the telltale Golden Skulltula sound but have no idea how to get to the tricky spider, even with the help of additional chimes from the new Echo Gem Skulltula tracking item. But with a peek at the Zelda Notes app, I can pinpoint the exact location of where the Skulltula is supposed to be and if I need to use a certain item or change the time of day to be able to get to it.
I recently delved into the Shadow Temple, for example, and I couldn’t figure out how to get up to a Skulltula that I saw while coming down an elevator. But when I checked the icon on the Zelda Notes map, it said that I needed the Scarecrow Song to create a hookshot point, which I hadn’t gotten yet. As soon as I finished the dungeon, getting the Scarecrow Song was my first priority.
Zelda Notes has been useful for tracking down Pieces of Heart, too, which give Link more health once you collect enough. While running up and down Zora’s River, I kept seeing two Pieces of Heart on faraway ledges that I couldn’t figure out how to get to. (My memories of my extensive time with Ocarina of Time as a kid also failed me.) But tapping one of the icons on the Zelda Notes map revealed that I needed a Cucco to get to it — and suddenly, I understood why there was one of the chirping white birds near the entrance of the zone.
Yes, it can be annoying to have to open my phone and dig through an app to track down all of the Skulltulas and other objects of curiosity scattered around Hyrule. I play video games to try and get away from my phone, not look at it more. And sure, I could just look up an online guide, but that often means wading through walkthroughs of varying quality, trusting an AI summary, or scrubbing through a YouTube video. But with Zelda Notes, I’m usually in and out relatively quickly, putting down my phone after seeing a clue or an icon that pushes me in the direction of the next golden spider. I’ve already found more than 70 Golden Skulltulas, and to my surprise, I now want to hunt for the full 100.

articles.text:

                                                                UCIe Connectivity for 2.5D and 3D Multi-Die Designs                                                    
Low Power-High Performance
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
The differences and engineering considerations behind choosing and implementing UCIe connectivity for advanced multi-die designs.
								November 11th, 2026 - 
								By: Synopsys
								
							
UCIe provides a common standard for die-to-die connectivity, but connecting dies in a 2.5D package is fundamentally different from connecting them in a 3D design.
In 2.5D designs, UCIe links traverse package channels where insertion loss, crosstalk, and increasing data rates influence PHY and package design. In 3D designs, shorter vertical connections and fine-pitch bonding allow bandwidth to scale through connection density, reducing the need for high-speed serialization, equalization, and channel training.
This white paper examines those differences and the engineering considerations behind choosing and implementing UCIe connectivity for advanced multi-die designs.
What you’ll learn:
- How UCIe connectivity differs across 2.5D and 3D designs
- How F2B and F2F topologies affect interface design
- How 3D integration changes implementation, test, and reliability requirements
- How to align UCIe IP, package topology, and implementation strategy

articles.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
articles.text:
The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world’s most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.
Operating since September 2022, the Russia-based ransomware group Qilin is the currently the most industrious ransomware-as-a-service gang, according to a report (PDF) this month by the cybersecurity firm NCC Group (KrebsOnSecurity profiled the administrator of the second most active ransomware group — The Gentlemen — in June).
Qilin attracts affiliates to hack into companies and deploy ransomware by offering them at least 80 percent of any extortion amount paid by victims. Its members practice the “double extortion” model, stealing sensitive data before encrypting systems and threatening to publish the files online. Unlike most ransomware partnerships based out of Russia, Qilin is happy to team with English-speaking affiliates, and its leader has shared on Telegram that they’ve worked with ransomware groups like Scattered Spider and RansomHub.
The head of Qilin goes by the handle “Haise,” but they weren’t always known by this nickname. It is not uncommon for cybercriminals to change their handle periodically as an operational security (opsec) measure. Doing so is generally a smart move, because it helps to sever one’s ties to older identities that may not have been as careful on basic opsec, such as separating their real life identity from their cybercrime activities. But even those cautious criminals will sometimes have to reference their past monikers when applying for membership at a new forum. And forums eventually get hacked or seized. That is precisely what happened with Haise.
The cyber intelligence platform Intel 471 records that in June 2022, Haise applied for membership to RAMP, a closely-guarded Russian cybercrime forum that was created as a haven for ransomware affiliate programs. Intel 471 has indexed direct messages from RAMP (the forum was seized by the FBI in January 2026), and those missives show the RAMP administrator approved Haise’s application, referring to this user as Haise and by their Telegram username: Alexbigboss44.
Searching Intel 471 for Alexbigboss44 reveals this was the Telegram account name shared by the user Rjun on the Russian cybercrime forums Exploit and XSS two years earlier in 2020. The cyber intelligence platform Flashpoint finds Alexbigboss44 is a prolific participant in cybercriminal forums and Telegram channels, primarily focused on the illicit trade of traffic, logs, and corporate access [full disclosure: Flashpoint is an advertiser on this blog].
Flashpoint says this user was engaged in high-volume acquisition of Facebook logs and Google Ads accounts to facilitate fraudulent advertising and gambling schemes, and that they functioned as a broker and operator — managing a network of traffickers and purchasing compromised data to fuel their operations.
The link between the Qilin administrator Haise and the much older Rjun and Alexbigboss44 accounts was shared privately earlier this month by IntelHawk, which describes itself as an AI-based platform capable of de-anonymizing threat actors based on historical usernames, stylometry and other signals.
IntelHawk founder and chief technology officer Leo Bogod said an analysis of these identities shows a progression from novice arbitrageur and credit card fraudster in 2018–2019 to a more experienced participant and organizer of complex cybercrime-related activities in 2020–2023, with increasing attention to malware, botnets, and payment infrastructure.
Where does this connection between these threat actor identities lead? Intel 471 finds that by the time Alexbigboss44 was applying for membership to RAMP, Rjun was already a longtime member of several other Russian crime forums, including Darkmarket, Verified, and Zloy. Intel 471 says Rjun signed up at all of these sites with the email address mail-30a@mail.ru.
The identity threat protection firm Spycloud found the email address mail-30a@mail.ru at one time used the password “Rjun132” [Spycloud is also an advertiser on this blog]. A search for that email at the breach tracking service Constella Intelligence shows that it appeared in records maintained by gosuslugi.ru, the official digital platform for state and municipal services in the Russian Federation.
Gosuslugi was breached in late 2025, reportedly exposing more than 20 million records with full names, birth dates, and mobile numbers. According to the leaked Gosuslugi records (via Constella), the address mail-30a@mail.ru belongs to 36-year-old Aleksey Mikhailovich Yakovtsev from St. Petersburg, Russia.
Flashpoint finds Haise has long used a Telegram account with the user ID 118329521, recording more than 5,000 messages from this user since 2018. Records from Russia’s education watchdog Rosobrnadzor reveal that Mr. Yakovtsev went to grade school in Murmansk and that he holds a master’s degree in computing and information systems.
A search on this Telegram ID in Constella shows it is linked to the Russian phone number +79602347275. Pivoting on that phone number in Constella reveals it is connected to the email addresses aleksey1990yakov@mail.ru and rjun123321@mail.ru. IntelHawk finds that +79602347275 belongs to Yakovtsev’s biological sister, and that Aleksey often used his sister’s email address when registering at different websites.
That phone number appears on several airline flight records at Russian travel agencies that have experienced a data breach in recent years, and those records show Aleksey Yakovtsev, born August 18, 1990, flew between St. Petersburg and Murmansk at least three times between 2013 and 2014.
More recent flight records show that while Mr. Yakovtsev has not traveled by plane outside of Russia, he does fly frequently between Saint Petersburg and Sochi. Often called the “Russian Riviera,” Sochi is Russia’s largest resort city, situated along the coast of the Black Sea and about 1,200 miles south of Saint Petersburg by plane.
Attempts to reach Mr. Yakovtsev via email and phone were unsuccessful.
Further reading: Gang Exposed, an anonymous Twitter/X account that has a history of successfully deanonymizing suspected ransomware actors, reached similar conclusions about Haise’s real-life identity, crediting IntelHawk’s platform for helping to connect the dots.
Mr Krebs,
My computer exposure was in 1990; an Apple 2+. Since first becoming aware of you, I have followed your insights (that doesn’t cover all, of course).
Please accept my deep appreciation for your efforts, and for the safety of all right-minded person on this earth.
If you ever feel it safe to come to the surface, please me know, in any fashion.
John Royal

articles.title: Mercedes lance une IA embarquée qui fonctionne même sans réseau : ce qui change pour les conducteurs
articles.text:
Lancé en 2018 sur la Classe A, le MBUX de Mercedes est connu plutôt performant avec son interface réactive et son assistant vocal assez fin. Une bonne base que la marque allemande souhaite aujourd’hui améliorer avec un nouveau modèle d’intelligence artificielle développé en collaboration avec la start-up américaine Liquid AI. L’idée est de s’affranchir des derniers obstacles auxquels se heurtent encore ces systèmes.
Le principal problème étant le fonctionnement dans une zone souffrant d’une faible couverture réseau : généralement, l’assistant se bloque automatiquement en se limitant aux fonctions essentielles sans pouvoir poursuivre une discussion avec l’utilisateur. C’est frustrant, raison pour laquelle le système porté par Liquid AI pourra se passer de la connexion réseau du cloud pour continuer à travailler en bonne intelligence.
Confidentialité et réactivité : les deux grands atouts du système
Côté confidentialité, l’ensemble marque aussi des points car le traitement des données se faisant intégralement dans le véhicule limite les allers-retours vers un centre de données. Les informations sensibles pouvant éventuellement être échangées sont ainsi protégées au maximum. Aussi, ne pas dépendre du réseau permettra une latence réduite, ce qui améliorera encore l’expérience utilisateur.
Ola Källenius, le PDG de Mercedes, a justement rappelé qu’ « avec de nombreux lancements de produits à venir et l’IA qui change notre façon de travailler, nous nous concentrons sur la construction d’une marque plus rapide, plus efficace et encore plus compétitive ». Si le rythme s’accélèrera irrémédiablement, le constructeur ne perd pas de vue les attentes premières de ses clients sur la commande vocale.
Quotidien ou questions complexes : comment fonctionne le nouvel assistant ?
Les indications les plus fréquentes portent ainsi sur la navigation, la radio, la ventilation et les appels. Peaufiner la compréhension de ces instructions demeure donc primordial. Cela dit, les questions plus complexes demeurent bien au centre du système basé sur Liquid AI. Et dans le cas où les interrogations dépassent les capacités du modèle américain, un basculement vers les modèles basés sur le cloud sera effectué pour y apporter une réponse.
Jason Hoff, PDG de la branche nord-américaine de Mercedes, confirme qu’ « un système basé sur l’IA qui permette une interaction conversationnelle plus libre est, selon nous, une priorité absolue pour nos clients ». Le responsable affirme en parallèle que la marque allemande investit massivement dans le développement de systèmes de conduite autonome améliorés avec d’autres partenaires.
Quels modèles Mercedes reçoivent la mise à jour et quand ?
L’assistant vocal basé sur Liquid AI est d’ores et déjà en cours de déploiement en Amérique du Nord. Les Classe E et CLE sont en effet les premières à en profiter. Elles seront rapidement suivies des Classe S, GLC et GLE. L’arrivée de ce nouvel équipement ne réclamera aucun abonnement supplémentaire. Il est probable que les modèles européens soient par la suite concernés.

articles.title: Private scandals that derailed tech execs’ careers; Neha Nagar’s new book on helping people invest
articles.text:
Private scandals that derailed tech execs’ careers; Neha Nagar’s new book on helping people invest
Executive exits can result from violations of company policies, even when no criminal wrongdoing has been established. Brian Krzanich resigned from Intel over a consensual subordinate relationship, while Phaneesh Murthy was dismissed by iGate for failing to disclose a relationship.
Dear Reader,
Anthropic has launched the roadshow for its blockbuster IPO, seeking a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. The Claude maker aims to raise as much as $64.4 billion through the share sale, in what could become one of the largest public offerings in history. The proposed valuation comes amid growing investor scrutiny of the enormous costs of building AI infrastructure.
The controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has raised questions about succession planning at the AI chip giant. Valued at around $4 trillion, Nvidia faces a difficult question: Who could eventually succeed the executive who built it into an AI powerhouse?
OpenAI has unveiled Control Room, which is a rapid-response kill switch designed to pull the plug on rogue AI workloads and safety threats in under 35 seconds. Control Room will be a central system to track model workloads across the research infrastructure of OpenAI.
Closer home, the board of IIFL Finance has greenlit a massive Rs 6,414 crore ($686 million) primary capital raise, headlined by private equity heavyweight Blackstone. In what marks one of the largest PE infusions into a listed Indian NBFC, Blackstone is committing Rs 5,000 crore ($535 million) via compulsorily convertible preference shares. The instruments will convert at Rs 602 per share within 18 months, handing the firm a roughly 16% stake on a fully diluted basis.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Private scandals that derailed tech execs’ careers
- Neha Nagar’s new book on helping people invest
Here’s your trivia for today: Which arcade gaming pioneer founded by Nolan Bushnell took its name from a Japanese board game term equivalent to "check" in chess? (Scroll down for answer)
Technology
Private scandals that derailed tech execs’ careers
Several prominent tech leaders have seen their careers interrupted or upended by personal conduct and relationship controversies rather than operational failures. The scandal surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang mirrors past high-profile executive cases across global tech and Indian startups.
While the nature of the allegations ranges from undisclosed consensual relationships to sexual harassment claims, these incidents consistently trigger governance reviews, leadership transitions, and broader scrutiny of corporate culture.
Key takeaways:
- Executive exits can result from violations of company policies, even when no criminal wrongdoing has been established. Brian Krzanich resigned from Intel over a consensual subordinate relationship, while Phaneesh Murthy was dismissed by iGate for failing to disclose a relationship.
- Severe misconduct fallout can prompt broad organisational issues, as seen in the protests at Google in 2018 following reports of a $90 million payout to Android creator Andy Rubin amid credible misconduct findings.
- Legal outcomes vary significantly across cases; TVF founder Arunabh Kumar stepped down amid allegations in 2017 but was fully acquitted by a court in 2022 due to lack of evidence.
Inspiration
Neha Nagar’s new book on helping people invest
Earning money is not the same as managing it. In her book, Simple Money Serious Wealth: How to Turn Ordinary Income into Extraordinary Net Worth, Neha Nagar provides an investment structure for readers.
While a social media platform helps disseminate information, it has its structural limitations. A book, on the other hand, gives the author the space to explain an entire concept elaborately.
Key takeaways:
- Her debut book Simple Money Serious Wealth was published on October 24. It sold over 3,000 copies in the first 24 hours, according to a post on the author's Instagram account.
- The creator-turned-author believes India is still far away from reaching financial literacy. There are many reasons for this, she says.
- Fear stops many people from exploring investment strategies, Neha says, as many Indians still associate the stock market with gambling.
News & updates
- Startup awards: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade has opened applications for the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards, offering a prize of Rs 25 lakh in each category to recognise innovative, scalable and impactful startups across the country.
- Fundraising: Arka Fincap Limited, a Kirloskar Group-promoted non-banking financial company has raised an initial investment of Rs 525 crore from The Rise Funds, the global impact investing arm of TPG.
- Jobs moving to India: Australian airline Qantas will outsource 850 local corporate jobs to consulting giant Accenture with most roles moving to India. The move comes amid the company’s AI push.
Which arcade gaming pioneer founded by Nolan Bushnell took its name from a Japanese board game term equivalent to "check" in chess?
Answer: Atari

articles.title: CoreWeave tests AI integrations on its cloud before you migrate
articles.text:
CoreWeave tests AI integrations on its cloud before you migrate
Moving an AI workload to another cloud means bringing more than a model and its data. Your serving layer, observability dashboards, security controls, and storage systems have to work together on the new infrastructure. For platform teams, proving those connections under real traffic can become the slowest and riskiest part of the move.
As a stack grows across vendors and clouds, each project adds more integration questions. A compatible specification is a starting point. It doesn’t guarantee a tool will behave as expected in production, or that the runbooks and security workflows built around it will carry over.
Make production validation visible
An integration needs to work on the infrastructure where you plan to run it, under production traffic. The tools should also be ones your team already uses or has asked for.
“A compatible specification is a starting point. It doesn’t guarantee a tool will behave as expected in production, or that the runbooks and security workflows built around it will carry over.”
We built the CoreWeave Partner Network to make that validation visible. It brings relationships with CrowdStrike, VAST Data, Reflection, IBM, and other technology vendors into a curated network of integrations tested under real-world production conditions on CoreWeave Cloud.
The network covers four parts of the AI stack, from training and inference to data movement, security, and the next iteration:
- Infrastructure: compute, storage, networking, servers, and interconnects, with partners including VAST Data, Dell, AMD, IBM, BackBlaze, and Pulumi.
- Data services: storing, processing, moving, and accessing AI data throughout its lifecycle, with ClickHouse, Encord, LanceDB, and Datology.
- Independent software vendors (ISVs): orchestration, observability, and model development, including Grafana, Datadog, Union, SkyPilot, IBM, Pinecone, Redis, LlamaIndex, and Clockwork. A dedicated security segment includes CrowdStrike, Zscaler, and Cranium.
- Models, agents, and inference: foundational software and services for building, training, serving, and scaling applications, with Reflection, RadixArk, Inferact, OpenRouter, and Red Hat.
Together, these integrations support running and observing models, curating data, improving behavior, and evaluating the next release. Every partner must meet the same requirement: an integration that works on CoreWeave infrastructure under production conditions. Partners enter the network because customers run them or ask for them.
Read the workload evidence
IBM trained its Granite models on CoreWeave around one of the first deployments of Nvidia GB200 NVL72 clusters. Cohere built North, its agentic AI platform, on one of the industry’s first production GB200 NVL72 clusters and reported training three times faster than on Nvidia Hopper.
Mistral AI trains its models entirely on CoreWeave and cites training 2.5 times faster on Nvidia GB200 NVL72 systems. Decart uses Nvidia HGX B200 at production scale through its CoreWeave collaboration, on a platform that includes Weights & Biases.
The underlying relationships predate the network announcement. CoreWeave and Weights & Biases have run production integrations with Encord, Pinecone, and other partners since the early wave of open-source large language models (LLMs) and frontier-model training.
Jon Jones, CoreWeave’s Chief Revenue Officer, describes the change as making existing partner work visible before customers build. The network also provides a repeatable way to pursue deeper integrations, joint go-to-market work, and shared innovation.
The partners emphasize different parts of that system. VAST Data co-founder and chief technology officer Alon Horev describes combining CoreWeave’s AI cloud with the VAST AI Operating System across large-scale training, fine-tuning, production inference, and continuous agentic workloads. CrowdStrike CEO and founder George Kurtz emphasizes security built into the infrastructure running AI. Adam Lawrence, general manager of IBM Americas, points to IBM and Red Hat technologies as a way to expand choice and reduce integration work when deploying and scaling AI.
Carry over the operations you already use
Your team has already built runbooks around its observability tools. Grafana and Datadog integrations let you carry that work over. CrowdStrike, Zscaler, and Cranium provide security integrations, bringing existing threat visibility and response tooling.
Inference integrations serve a similar purpose: keeping the models available as teams expand onto CoreWeave, without rebuilding the serving layer. The goal is to add capacity while retaining the parts of the stack that already work.
“A marketplace listing still leaves your team to validate the integration. An LLM can suggest what’s popular without telling you what works on your infrastructure.”
A marketplace listing still leaves your team to validate the integration. An LLM can suggest what’s popular without telling you what works on your infrastructure. We select partners based on customer demand and test their integrations across all four segments.
Include the tools your agents call
The integration problem also reaches inside agent execution. Most closed models include web search, while most open-weight models do not. Teams choosing open weights for cost, control, or customization have often had to connect a search provider separately.
CoreWeave is extending its partner approach to these tools, beginning with Exa, Parallel Web Systems, and You.com. The announced search layer provides access through one integration instead of a separate contract for each provider.
Teams can enable it through a single setting on a standard inference request or access it from inside a CoreWeave Sandbox, without setting up a separate software development kit (SDK) or account. The arrangement is nonexclusive, so using the integration does not restrict future provider choices.
We announced the search partnerships at Fully Connected, with the remaining integration work planned for the following weeks. As those integrations become available, they will meet the same production-validation standard as the rest of the network.
Start with the connections your workload needs
Before adding another cloud, check the serving, data, observability, and security connections your workload depends on. Ask which integrations have been tested under production conditions and what your team will still need to validate.
“Before adding another cloud, check the serving, data, observability, and security connections your workload depends on.”
The CoreWeave Partner Network lists validated partners. CoreWeave account teams can discuss a specific integration and workload, and partner sessions from Fully Connected 2026 offer another way to see the integrations in use. Teams interested in new collaborations can explore the partner program.

articles.title: OpenAI lance la fiche « Google My Business » de ChatGPT, avec un agent IA en prime
articles.text:
Si vous avez déjà géré la fiche Google d’un restaurant, d’un commerce ou d’une boutique, le principe va vous sembler familier. OpenAI a annoncé le 10 novembre 2026 le lancement en bêta de Businesses in ChatGPT, une nouvelle manière pour les marques d’exister dans les réponses du chatbot. L’entreprise met en avant un argument massue : ChatGPT serait utilisé par 1,2 milliard de personnes chaque semaine. Autant dire que ça fait un paquet d’opportunités et beaucoup de ratés potentiels si vos infos ne sont pas à jour.
Tout passe par un nouvel outil, le Business Hub. Une entreprise peut y revendiquer sa présence dans ChatGPT puis, une fois vérifiée, mettre à jour ses informations clés et ajouter des flux de produits avec prix et disponibilités. L’idée est simple à comprendre : que ChatGPT cesse de recommander une référence en rupture de stock ou un tarif d’il y a deux ans.
Le Business Hub est ouvert à toute entreprise éligible située dans un pays où ChatGPT est disponible, d’après l’annonce d’OpenAI. Les marchands Shopify ont droit à une procédure simplifiée : ils peuvent connecter leur boutique directement, et leurs produits éligibles sont déjà intégrés à ChatGPT via le catalogue de Shopify. Nous avons testé en France : cela fonctionne parfaitement, Businesses in ChatGPT est même traduit dans notre langue.
L’outil fournit aussi des statistiques : nombre de mentions dans les réponses, clics vers le site, et « sujets de découverte », c’est-à-dire les thèmes de conversation dans lesquels le site est cité. OpenAI promet que ces données restent agrégées : les entreprises ne voient jamais les conversations des utilisateurs, et les chiffres ne s’affichent qu’au-delà d’un certain volume d’échanges.
Un agent IA pour chaque marque
La nouveauté la plus ambitieuse s’appelle Business Agent. Après avoir revendiqué leur fiche, les entreprises éligibles peuvent créer, tester et publier un agent qui répond aux questions des clients à partir des informations qu’elles fournissent. Lorsqu’une marque apparaît dans une réponse, on peut cliquer sur son profil et, si un agent existe, lancer une discussion avec lui pour comparer deux produits ou vérifier qu’une offre correspond à ses besoins.
Le modèle économique est assumé : les entreprises pourront sponsoriser leur agent et s’en servir comme destination pour les ChatGPT Ads. Une suite logique, quelques mois après la fin officielle du ChatGPT gratuit et sans publicité, et dans la continuité des fonctions d’achat intégrées, comme le paiement via PayPal annoncé l’an dernier.
Pour l’instant, les Business Agents sont réservés aux sites de e-commerce et de services en ligne éligibles, aux États-Unis. OpenAI indique vouloir étendre le dispositif à d’autres marchés et catégories d’entreprises, sans calendrier.
Pour les marques françaises, revendiquer sa fiche dès maintenant ne coûte rien et permet au moins de voir comment ChatGPT parle de vous. On vous recommande même de le faire au plus vite : passer à côté de cette opportunité pourrait être aussi problématique qu’avoir snobé Google My Business dans les années 2010. Côté utilisateurs, il faudra surveiller de près la frontière entre réponse « indépendante » et agent sponsorisé : sur le papier, elle est nette, mais dans un chatbot, tout ressemble un peu à une conversation.

articles.title: La Fiscalía ordena investigar la difusión de contenido sexual de menores en TikTok
articles.text:
La Fiscalía ordena investigar la difusión de contenido sexual de menores en TikTok
La fiscal general Peramato ha designado a la fiscal de Criminalidad Informática para indagar los delitos relacionados con posibles delitos relacionados con el abuso sexual infantil en la plataforma
La fiscal general del Estado, Teresa Peramato, ha decidido este miércoles que se inicie una investigación por la difusión de contenido sexual de menores en la plataforma TikTok, destapada por una investigación periodística de Maldita.es. Peramato ha encargado a la fiscal de Sala Coordinadora contra la Criminalidad Informática, Elvira Tejada, que indague en posibles delitos relacionados con el abuso infantil y la corrupción de menores en la red social, según ha informado la propia Fiscalía.
Maldita.es publicó este lunes una profusa investigación que revelaba que los periodistas habían encontrado en la red 1.183 vídeos de abuso infantil explícito con 48 millones de visualizaciones, además de 26.000 perfiles potenciales de pederastas que comentan y comparten ese material. La organización dijo que había pedido a TikTok, a la que llamaban el “hogar del pederasta”, que retirara el contenido y había interpuesto una denuncia ante la Fiscalía para que se iniciaran acciones contra la plataforma.
La denuncia presentada hace constar que en la red social son públicas las interacciones para difundir y vender material de abuso infantil. Y no solo eso, sino que TikTok recomienda y promociona contenido de esa naturaleza a quienes lo buscan e, incluso, gana dinero con este tipo de actividad.
Un portavoz de la red social aseguró en un comunicado que “tan pronto” Maldita.es publicó las informaciones que fundamentan la denuncia, TikTok tomó “medidas para identificar y eliminar el contenido”. Además, insiste en que la compañía ha presentado informes al Centro Nacional de Niños Desaparecidos y Explotados (NCMEC, por sus siglas en inglés) “cuando ha correspondido” y que el contenido sexualmente explícito con menores está categóricamente prohibido" en la plataforma.
Peramato ha decidido que el Ministerio Público debe adentrarse en el asunto y ha firmado un decreto este miércoles para encargar el tema a Tejada. Según ha informado la propia Fiscalía, esta misma mañana los responsables de Maldita.es han comparecido ante la fiscal Tejada para ratificar su denuncia y presentar el material probatorio oportuno “que será objeto de inmediato análisis y valoración”.
“Creemos que es un paso en la dirección que siempre hemos buscado: que las plataformas se hagan responsables de la seguridad de sus usuarios”, ha dicho Clara Jiménez, cofundadora de Maldita.es, tras conocerse la decisión de la Fiscalía. “Si la única manera es que la justicia investigue, por eso hemos declarado hoy ante la fiscalía y hemos entregado 1 Terabyte de evidencia del fracaso sistémico de TikTok.”
La publicación periodística ha traído, además, una ola de reacciones dentro y fuera del Gobierno. El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha publicado un mensaje en la red social X en el que ha calificado la decisión de la fiscal como una “gran noticia”. “La Fiscalía acaba de abrir diligencias por la difusión de material de abuso sexual infantil en TikTok. Ya lo advertimos hace tiempo: se acabó la impunidad en las redes sociales. Ninguna plataforma está por encima de la ley. Mucho menos de los derechos de nuestros hijos e hijas”, ha escrito.
La ministra de Juventud e Infancia, Sira Rego, que se reunió este martes con los representantes de Maldita.es, aseguró que iba a hacer todo lo que estuviera en su mano para bloquear de manera cautelar la red social. “Vamos a ir con todo. Estamos activando todas las medidas que tenemos a nuestro alcance. Si de nosotros dependiera, estaría cerrado desde ayer”, insistió en unas declaraciones.
Rego solicitó también este martes por escrito a la Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) que cerrara la plataforma, aludiendo al artículo 66.1 del Reglamento General de Protección de Datos de la Unión Europea, que contempla que “en circunstancias excepcionales, si una autoridad de control cree que es urgente intervenir para proteger los derechos y libertades de interesados, se podrán adoptar inmediatamente medidas provisionales destinadas a producir efectos jurídicos en su propio territorio”.
La Agencia Española de Protección de Datos ha anunciado, por su parte, que va a pedir a TikTok información concreta sobre las actuaciones que está realizando para retirar de su red los contenidos de abuso sexual infantil localizados antes de ordenar el bloqueo que impida el acceso a esos contenidos. El organismo ha aclarado también en una nota de prensa que no tiene competencias para decretar el cierre de la plataforma, por lo que solo podrá bloquear los enlaces específicos denunciados, según un comunicado emitido este miércoles.
En su comunicado, el portavoz de TikTok ha asegurado, en este sentido, que trabaja “estrechamente” con la AEPD y todas las autoridades competentes en una “respuesta colectiva” para asegurarse de eliminar el contenido nocivo que garantice la seguridad infantil. “Dado que los actores malintencionados adaptan continuamente sus tácticas, trabajamos incansablemente para mejorar nuestras medidas de protección”, ha añadido.

articles.title: Cette IA de Google utilise votre smartphone Android à votre place, et ce n’est que le début
articles.text:
Vous voulez tester une nouvelle appli sur un smartphone Android ? Ouvrez un menu, appuyez sur un bouton, remplissez un formulaire, vérifiez le résultat…. ARTEMIS automatise ces scénarios à partir de simples instructions en langage naturel. Une fois configuré, il suffit de lui indiquer ce qu’il faut tester pour qu’il puisse utiliser le téléphone et vérifier lui-même le comportement de l’application.
Ce projet open source développé par Google est plus qu'un simple outil de test automatisé. Il sert d’intermédiaire entre un agent d’IA et un appareil Android, afin que celui-ci puisse observer l’interface, effectuer des actions et vérifier leur résultat. Un émulateur peut certes faire le job, mais ARTEMIS permet de travailler avec un appareil physique connecté en USB.
- Instructions en langage naturel
- CLI pour tests et benchmarks
- Intégration MCP et SDK Python
Décrivez le test, ARTEMIS s’occupe du reste
Plutôt que d’écrire manuellement une série d’actions, il suffit de décrire en langage naturel ce que l’on veut vérifier. ARTEMIS peut alors ouvrir les applications, naviguer dans leurs interfaces, saisir du texte, appuyer où il faut et, selon le mode choisi, vérifier si l’objectif a bien été atteint.
Le système combine l’arborescence d’accessibilité, l’OCR et l’analyse visuelle pour retrouver des éléments dans des interfaces classiques, mais également dans des écrans plus complexes faits avec Canvas, Compose ou Flutter. Si une action échoue, le système peut chercher une autre manière de poursuivre le scénario.
Deux modes d’exécution sont proposés. Flash privilégie la rapidité avec une boucle d’observation et d’action qui prend généralement quelques secondes par étape. Pro ajoute une phase de planification, des vérifications intermédiaires et un contrôle final, ce qui le destine davantage aux scénarios longs ou aux tests de stabilité.
ARTEMIS : pour les développeurs, pas seulement pour les testeurs
ARTEMIS peut être utilisé depuis une interface web, le terminal ou un SDK Python. Mais son intégration MCP est probablement sa fonctionnalité la plus intéressante. Un assistant comme Codex, Claude Code ou Antigravity peut ainsi accéder à un téléphone connecté, lancer des tests et récupérer captures d’écran, journaux et résultats directement dans son environnement de travail.
Les développeurs du projet annoncent par ailleurs plus de 99 % de réussite sur AndroidWorld, un benchmark regroupant 116 tâches réparties sur 20 applications Android. Ce chiffre ne signifie évidemment pas que tous les tests réels seront réussis, ni que l'outil détectera tous les bugs, mais il donne une idée du niveau de fiabilité recherché.
ARTEMIS est avant tout destiné au développement et à l’assurance qualité. Sa mise en place demande un appareil Android avec le débogage USB activé, ou un émulateur compatible, ainsi qu’un environnement de développement configuré et un accès à un modèle d’IA. Sur un smartphone physique, ARTEMIS peut également installer un service d’accessibilité pour faciliter l’analyse de l’interface. Pour les équipes qui testent régulièrement leurs applications, il pourrait à terme transformer une partie des vérifications répétitives en simples consignes à donner à une IA.
- Instructions en langage naturel
- CLI pour tests et benchmarks
- Intégration MCP et SDK Python

articles.title: The Evolution of Commercial Open Source Software
articles.text:
The Evolution of Commercial Open Source Software
Tony Wasserman | 11 November 2026
The Early Days
In the early days of computing, there were no software products. Some computer systems vendors provided mechanisms for their customers to freely distribute applications with their source code, typically through their user groups (e.g, IBM SHARE Library) [1]. Applications were custom-built, developed across many different computer systems using a wide variety of different languages.
The 1964 arrival and subsequent broad adoption of IBM’s System/360 and OS/360 made it feasible for developers to build software products that could be licensed to a large number of buyers. Soon thereafter, Martin Goetz was able to patent a software algorithm and to release Autoflow, the first commercial software product. Those steps led to today’s multi-billion dollar commercial software industry, with vendor-licensed products, accompanied by End User Software Agreements and patents.
Shareware
While vendors focused on enterprises and governments, the arrival of personal computers in the mid-1970s, created a consumer market for software products. In addition to vendor supported products such as Microsoft BASIC, other programs, collectively known as “shareware”, were developed by individuals, with their users asked to make a small donation (under $50 US) to the developer. Some of the most popular applications of this category were PC-Talk, PC-File, PC-Write, and WinRAR, all of which attracted many thousands of users. Shareware remained very popular into the 1990s.
There were many different commercial approaches to shareware. Some applications were released for trial use, and would work for a while, often a month, before asking for payment. Those who paid would receive a code (key) that would allow the program to keep working or perhaps activate some hidden features. Some shareware worked on an honor system, leaving the program operating normally, hoping that users would make a donation to the developer, but not requiring it. There were numerous variations of shareware commercialization, and several services were created to help developers collect payments. Shareware programs were released in binary format, without the source code to modify them or to see how they operated.
Emergence of Open Source
In the late 1970s, the University of California, Berkeley, released binary and source code for BSD Unix on the DEC VAX 11/780, using a new type of source code license. Academic institutions could obtain the software for a distribution fee, while companies had to pay more than $40K for a commercial license from AT&T. BSD Unix was widely adopted in universities, and led to the development and distribution of many applications. My group released several applications in 1980 with BSD licenses, making them early examples of open source software.
In the mid-1980s, though, Richard Stallman created the Free Software Foundation and the GPL license, leading to distribution of his team’s GNU software in both binary and source code formats. When Linux was distributed in the early 1990s, it followed this non-commercial approach, using the GPL license. The concept of “free software” and the success of Linux following its 1992 release led many developers to follow the same approach.
All of the above developments influenced the growth of open source software. The MySQL project, begun in the mid-1990s, used a dual license model, which had the advantage of allowing developers to use the open source license until they were ready to release their product commercially, at which point they had to switch to the commercial license. The code was unchanged, without the additional “open core” components that are common in today’s Commercial OSS (COSS) product. When MySQL was acquired for $1B in 2008, it showed the value of COSS, which made the category attractive to private investors and VCs, an important step in the evolution of COSS.
Evolution of Open Source Business Models
By the early 2000s, following the creation of the OSI and the release of the Open Source Definition, many projects had identified ways to generate revenue from their open source projects. I wrote a paper in 2007, “Building a Business on Open Source Software” [2], that identified different approaches. These included providing support and training services, hosting the software for remote access, commercial enhancement, and integration with other products. These approaches to commercialization remain the primary means by which COSS companies generate revenue, as described in the Monetization section of The State of Commercial Open Source 2026.
It’s valuable to see COSS as just one approach to open source software and to recognize that there remains a very large community of open source users and contributors who work on non-commercial applications, including both community-based development and foundation-sponsored projects. Development processes and team participation in these categories are different from those of COSS and proprietary software products, as described in “Community and Commercial Strategies in Open Source Software” [3], published in 2013. Many of the projects In the former category give little attention to monetization for their work, and volunteer their time and resources. There are more than a billion (!) projects hosted by GitHub, many of which are non-commercial. While it can be difficult for volunteers to contribute to COSS projects, the non-commercial projects are often seeking such help.
Looking Ahead
As the Linux Foundation report describes, the role of AI in COSS is still uncertain, with major questions revolving around the use of proprietary AI coding tools in the development and maintenance of COSS. One can also foresee non-commercial open source software produced by AI tools in addition to the existing contributions of AI coding tools to existing open source projects. These topics are likely to take on growing importance as AI technologies evolve.
In conclusion, the idea of creating a business based on open source software has evolved for decades, going back to the 1960s and the first instances of software being distributed independently of the hardware on which it ran. Today, COSS represents an important segment of software business approaches, though there remain significant questions about the openness of many COSS projects and the licenses under which some of them are distributed.
Tony Wasserman
Software Methods and Tools
References
[1] SHARE (computing). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHARE_(computing), accessed 6 November 2026.
[2] Wasserman, A.I., “Building a Business on Open Source Software” in Petti, C. (ed.), Cases in Technological Entrepreneurship: Converting Ideas into Value. Cheltenham, UK and Northampton, MA, USA: Edward Elgar, 2009, pp. 107-121.
[3] Wasserman, A.I., “Community and Commercial Strategies in Open Source Software”, IT- Information Technology, vol. 55, no. 5 (2013), pp. 181-188.

articles.title: Synology corrige en urgence deux failles de DSM : les versions à installer sur votre NAS — Frandroid
articles.text:
La cybersécurité est devenue un enjeu crucial ces derniers mois. Les failles critiques s’enchainent sur des projets ou des produits très populaires. La dernière en date touche les NAS Synology. Autrement dit, elle touche un objet dont la mission est de stocker les photos de famille, les sauvegardes des PC ou les dossiers d’une PME. On peut en plus souvent y accéder depuis l’extérieur, ce qui en fait une cible de choix pour les pirates. Synology a publié ce mardi 10 novembre un avis de sécurité, référencé Synology-SA-26:19, avec les correctifs de deux failles de DSM.
Deux failles critiques
La faille la plus grave, CVE-2026-76954, se trouve dans l’Auth API, le module de DSM qui gère la connexion des utilisateurs. Il s’agit d’une injection SQL, une technique qui consiste à glisser des commandes dans un champ de saisie pour que la base de données du système les exécute. Synology lui donne 9,8 sur 10 sur l’échelle CVSS, qui sert à noter la gravité des failles, soit le niveau « critique ». Elle ne demande ni identifiant ni action de la victime, et permet de lire ou d’écrire n’importe quel fichier, voire de faire planter le NAS.
La seconde, CVE-2026-85101, touche rsync, le service qui synchronise et sauvegarde des fichiers entre deux machines. Elle contourne l’authentification par un chemin détourné et permet d’écrire n’importe quel fichier, mais seulement d’en lire certains. Synology la classe donc un cran en dessous, en « importante », avec 8,6 sur 10.
Tous les NAS sous DSM 7.2.1 à 7.4 sont concernés
L’avis de Synology vise des versions de DSM et ne cite aucun modèle : 7.4, 7.3, 7.2.2 et 7.2.1. Comme ce système équipe toute la gamme, chaque NAS de la marque qui tourne sur l’une de ces versions sans le dernier correctif est exposé. Surtout, Synology indique qu’aucune mesure de contournement n’existe, donc seule la mise à jour protège le NAS. La marque ne signale pas, à ce stade, d’attaque qui aurait exploité ces failles.
Synology en est à sa deuxième alerte de ce niveau en deux mois. Le 18 septembre, la marque avait déjà corrigé deux failles de DSM notées 9,8, qui permettaient elles aussi de lire ou d’écrire des fichiers à distance. On vous en avait parlé lorsque le rançongiciel C3RB3R a touché des NAS de la marque.
Comment mettre à jour votre NAS Synology
Ouvrez DSM, puis le Panneau de configuration, rubrique Mise à jour et restauration. Vous y voyez la version installée et vous pouvez lancer la mise à jour. Vérifiez que votre NAS atteint au moins la version corrigée de sa branche :
- DSM 7.4 : version 7.4.1-90080-1 ou plus récente
- DSM 7.3 : version 7.3.2-86009-5 ou plus récente
- DSM 7.2.2 : version 7.2.2-72806-10 ou plus récente
- DSM 7.2.1 : version 7.2.1-69057-13 ou plus récente
Synology a publié son avis ce mardi 10 novembre à 10 h 06, heure de Paris, et les versions corrigées sont disponibles depuis. Si vous ne pouvez pas mettre à jour tout de suite, coupez l’accès au NAS depuis Internet en attendant.

articles.title: Ya es oficial: el nuevo router Mini 2 de Starlink ahora promete WiFi vía satélite sin estar conectado a la corriente
articles.text:
El pasado verano, Starlink presentó su nueva antena V5, y hace unas semanas, anunció la siguiente generación de su router, el router 4, cuya principal novedad es que trae a bordo un chipset WiFi 7. Todo indicaba que el siguiente paso de la compañía sería renovar su router de viaje. Y así ha sido.
Starlink ha presentado oficialmente el nuevo router portátil Mini 2, un equipo pensado mantenerse conectado mientras viajas, independientemente de lo remoto que sea tu destino.
Esta nueva generación mantiene el tamaño compacto y el diseño resistente a las inclemencias meteorológicas del router Mini original, pero ahora cuenta con una batería integrada que le permite funcionar sin estar conectado a la corriente.
Con USB- o con batería. El nuevo router Mini 2 de Starlink es la evolución del router Mini que llegó a España hace dos años y que aún sigue a la venta. Esa primera generación ofrece velocidades máximas de descarga superiores a 100 Mbps y funciona en movimiento a una velocidad de hasta 100 km/h (a bordo de una autocaravana, por ejemplo).
La principal novedad de su sucesor es que promete hasta 4,5 horas de conectividad con una sola carga gracias a su batería integrada, que puedes extraer fácilmente para intercambiarla por otra cuando agote su carga. Además, tienes la opción de alimentarlo a través de su puerto USB-C.
WiFi 6 en 60 segundos. Como es resistente a las inclemencias meteorológicas, puedes instalarlo en el exterior siempre que esté mirando al cielo despejado y sin obstrucciones. La propia aplicación Starlink, disponible gratis para iOS y para Android, te muestra en el móvil el lugar de instalación más adecuado según tu ubicación exacta.
Si el router Mini 2 tiene una vista despejada del cielo, Starlink asegura que puedes conectarte a su conexión WiFi 6 en apenas 1 minuto. Cuando no lo uses, puedes guardarlo en su mochila porque tiene unas dimensiones de 263 x 314 x 23,1 mm y un peso total de aproximadamente 1,6 kg con batería y soporte abatible incluidos.
De momento, en Estados Unidos y bajo reserva. Ya se ha abierto el periodo de reserva anticipada por invitación en Estados Unidos con un depósito reembolsable de 100 dólares. Los envíos de esas primeras reservas comenzarán a mediados de diciembre y próximamente llegará a más países.
Su precio, eso sí, no está al alcance de cualquier bolsillo. El nuevo router portátil de Starlink cuesta la friolera de 999 dólares más tasas (a lo que hay que descontar los 100 dólares de la reserva). Lo bueno es que, por ese precio, trae incluido un año entero del plan itinerante ilimitado con datos ilimitados en más de 160 países. Un servicio que está valorado en unos 2.100 dólares.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.text:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert Huber, Franz Giessibl, and Klaus Richter, along with a team at the Max Planck Institute in Hamburg led by Angel Rubio.
Watching Electrons Move at Incredible Speeds
Understanding how matter behaves at the smallest scales is essential for developing the next generation of technology. Advances in clean energy, quantum computing, and powerful electronics for artificial intelligence all depend on knowing how chemical reactions unfold, how light interacts with materials, and how electrons travel through electronic devices.
However, even the sharpest microscopic photographs cannot reveal the full picture. Scientists also need to observe how these processes change over time, effectively creating slow-motion movies of events occurring at the atomic scale.
At RUN, researchers are developing ultrafast microscopes capable of recording the movements of electrons, atoms, and molecules with extraordinary precision in both space and time. About ten years ago, scientists in Regensburg used ultrafast scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the movement of a single molecule across space and time for the first time.
Tracking individual electrons presents an even greater challenge. At these microscopic distances, electrons can move roughly a thousand times faster than atoms and molecules, with important changes taking place over just attoseconds.
To appreciate how extreme these scales are, consider that an atom is approximately ten million times smaller than a millimeter. An attosecond is one-billionth of a billionth of a second. The difference between an attosecond and a second is comparable to the difference between one second and the entire age of the universe.
Making these measurements is especially difficult because electrons do not behave like ordinary objects. Their motion follows the unusual laws of quantum mechanics rather than the familiar rules of classical physics.
Ultrafast Lasers Reveal Quantum Tunneling
To observe electron behavior at these extraordinary speeds, the researchers built a new laser system that provides much finer time resolution than earlier experiments. The system allows them to control and study the quantum motion of individual electrons directly.
In the experiments, carefully timed laser pulses drive electrons from an extremely sharp metal tip toward a silver surface. The distance they travel is only a few atomic diameters.
The researchers detect this movement by measuring the resulting electrical current. To determine exactly when the electrons move, they use two pulses of light separated by a precisely controlled interval.
Simon Maier, the lead author of the paper, explains: "By varying the time interval between the two laser pulses, we can directly observe how the electrons respond."
This approach revealed clear evidence of electron motion occurring on attosecond timescales. It showed that the laser pulses could transfer electrons within these incredibly brief intervals while allowing scientists to observe the process as it happened.
What makes the result particularly remarkable is how the electrons travel. Instead of moving like conventional particles, they behave as quantum waves. This allows them to pass through an energy barrier separating the metal tip from the silver surface, even though classical physics predicts they should not have enough energy to cross it.
This phenomenon, known as quantum tunneling, is somewhat like an object passing through a solid wall without breaking or damaging it.
"Our measurement can be understood as a high-speed camera for the electron wave packets, since you can see at what point in time the tunneling process takes place," explains Katharina Glöckl, a doctoral student and co-author of the publication.
A Surprising 500-Attosecond Delay
To understand the measurements more deeply, researchers working with Prof. Angel Rubio performed sophisticated quantum simulations of the electrons' behavior near the "space-time limit."
Their calculations closely reproduced the experimental findings and uncovered another remarkable detail. The electrons did not respond to the light field instantaneously. Instead, their motion lagged behind it by approximately 500 attoseconds.
At such extreme scales, several fundamental features of quantum physics become important simultaneously.
For example, the researchers found that the laser pulses could not be described entirely by treating light as a wave or entirely by treating it as individual particles called photons. Their effects displayed characteristics of both descriptions. This combination was essential for exploring electron behavior so close to the "space-time limit."
The team also discovered that controlling electron motion over extremely short intervals changes how the electrons are distributed in space. Quantum mechanics describes these electrons using wave packets, which represent how their wave properties extend across different locations.
The relationship between the timing of electron motion and the spatial extent of these wave packets revealed the central limitation behind the discovery.
A Hidden Tradeoff Between Space and Time
Raffael Spachtholz, another co-author of the study, explains: "The more precisely we want to pin down the electron's position in time, the more energy we need to provide. And as a result, the electron wave packet spreads out more spatially."
In other words, improving the precision of an electron's timing comes with a cost. The more tightly researchers define when its motion occurs, the more broadly its quantum wave packet spreads through space.
To examine this relationship experimentally, the team placed a single atom on the surface to confine the electron wave packets to an extremely small region immediately before the laser pulses arrived.
This setup allowed the scientists to directly measure the connection between the electrons' spatial distribution and the timing of their motion.
Importantly, even when the electrons received substantial energy from the laser pulses, their wave packets remained sufficiently localized for microscopy with atomic spatial resolution and attosecond time resolution.
The findings provide experimental insight into a fundamental space-time constraint that scientists had previously only suspected. They also make it possible to systematically investigate how changes in electron motion over time affect the spatial structure of quantum wave functions.
Could Quantum Electronics Become Hundreds of Thousands of Times Faster?
Beyond revealing a new aspect of quantum behavior, the discovery could open the door to technologies that operate on timescales far beyond the capabilities of today's electronics.
One especially promising possibility involves using precisely controlled electron wave packets to influence chemical reactions.
Transferring a single electron to a molecule represents the smallest possible transfer of electric charge. But when that electron is concentrated within an exceptionally small region of space and time, the resulting local peak current density can reach as much as 1 trillion amperes per square centimeter.
Such extreme conditions could give scientists new ways to control chemical bonds and observe how molecules change during reactions.
"In the future, we want to use such wave packets to specifically trigger chemical reactions and observe, on the relevant length and time scales, how chemical bonds can be broken or altered," explains Prof. Jascha Repp enthusiastically.
The implications could extend well beyond chemistry. Greater control over electron motion may eventually help engineers develop electronic devices and quantum information systems that operate at speeds approaching the fundamental limits of electron dynamics.
"In the long term, the insights gained could also contribute to operating electronics and quantum information processing at the intrinsic speed limit of electron motion itself -- hundreds of thousands of times faster than the currently dominant CMOS technology," adds Prof. Rupert Huber.
That possibility remains a long term technological goal rather than an achievement demonstrated in the current experiments. Nevertheless, the findings provide a new foundation for exploring how electrons can be manipulated at the smallest distances and shortest timescales.
For Repp and Huber, the results suggest that the range of potential applications is extraordinarily broad. They believe that future advances in controlling electrons at the space-time limit may ultimately depend more on human creativity than on the constraints imposed by nature.
Story Source:
